A status change reaches logic as `ToLogic::GpuStatus` only while a frame shows a `shader` node; logic keeps it (`Shell::gpu`, for `strand report`) and says each unavailable reason once as a warning and a `strand watch` notice ("GPU unavailable: <reason>; shaders draw nothing (CPU fallback)").

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2: canvas drawing.** `draw: (c) => …` runs in the prop's memo with a `Canvas` record of the node's laid-out size (read as `self.width` is, so render reports it and a resize runs it again, as does any state it reads); the VM records each `Canvas` method call while it runs (`Vm::record_canvas`) and the ops become `Prop::Draw`. Render turns the list into the same `Item::Fill`s boxes use, inside a clip to the box (`strand-render/src/canvas.rs`), so the CPU rasteriser and the GPU lowering draw it alike (`crates/strand-render/tests/gpu.rs::a_canvas_is_drawn_by_the_gpu_like_the_cpu`: worst channel difference 1). Two readings: `c.fill(p)` with no path fills the whole box (the grammar's own example calls `c.fill($accent)` before drawing a line), and a paint that names tokens cannot be resolved on the logic thread, so `strand_scene::canvas::DrawOp` gained `FillThemed(PropValue)` and `StrokeThemed { paint, width }`, which render resolves in the node's token scope as it does a `bg` (DrawOp was `#[non_exhaustive]` for the canvas work). `c.text` is recorded but not drawn yet: text is shaped per node through the text worker, and a canvas needs several layouts per node; that is left open.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2: the `.text` gates and the bar's PSS with the GPU backend linked.** `budgets.rs::the_release_binary_code_stays_within_its_gate` checks the build it was compiled as: 18.5 MiB (19,398,656 B) with the GPU backend, measured at 18,456,983 B; 15 MiB with `--no-default-features`, measured at 15,118,167 B, in a CI step of its own (`budgets` job, and `ci.sh`). The design bar on the real services measured 34,016, 33,731 and 33,888 kB of PSS in three release runs in the container, under the 34 MiB target the budget is stated in (34,816 kB), so neither `opt-level = "s"` for wgpu-core and naga nor section ordering was tried; the test now also asserts that no `libvulkan` is mapped.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2: the hardware leg, run once.** `scripts/container/gpu.sh` on this laptop's Intel GPU (8086:b080, ANV): strand-gpu's 6 tests, render's 6 GPU tests (GPU vs CPU worst channel difference 2 for the rich frame, 1 for the canvas) and `gpu_idle` all pass. On CI's pixman sway ANV's WSI cannot present (no linux-dmabuf), so the promoted panel is attached in `Readback` mode, as the spike found; lavapipe presents there. In release, PSS was 22,049 kB before the GPU, 26,504 and 26,520 kB after the first and second drop: 4,455 kB over the baseline, inside the leg's 6 MiB, of which 2,696 kB is strand's own GPU code paged in and 806 kB libstdc++ (the driver's libraries are unmapped). A debug binary pages in 8.9 MiB of its own code for the same work, so `gpu_idle` checks the baseline only in a release build with `STRAND_GPU_HARDWARE=1`, and reports it otherwise.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review): a presented surface crossfades on the GPU.** Review found that a theme crossfade on a `GpuPresent` surface jumped straight to the new theme: `paint` lowered the frame for `paint_gpu` and then blended the snapshot into the scratch target `paint_gpu` throws away, which also made that never-touched scratch resident. Now the snapshot (still taken by the CPU raster from the old frame's scene, as for any surface whose buffer is not the shown one) is copied once per snapshot into an upload, and the lowered frame draws it in a layer of opacity `1 - w` with the new frame's ops added over it in a `Plus` layer of opacity `w`: exactly `swap::blend`'s `new * w + old * (1 - w)`, done on the GPU. `blend_fade` runs only for surfaces whose pixels are in `target` (CPU and readback). The copy lives for the fade (`GpuState::fades`, dropped at the first frame without one, at a backend switch, with the device or the surface), so a presented crossfade holds the snapshot twice for its few hundred milliseconds; avoiding that would need the snapshot to be an `Arc<Pixmap>` in `swap.rs`, which is not worth a change to the swap's code for a transient (`crates/strand-render/tests/gpu.rs::a_presented_surface_crossfades_on_the_gpu_like_the_cpu`: every frame within the GPU tolerance of the CPU's crossfade frame, and the test fails with 211,176 pixels off on the first frame when the crossfade ops are left out).

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review): every frame and pass is answered.** Review found that the GPU thread dropped a frame without a reply when its size was zero or past the device's `max_texture_dimension_2d`, its surface was not attached, or a texture was missing, and a pass that drew nothing (`Ok(None)`: no size, a bundled pass not built yet) likewise. A presented surface then froze (the host sends the next frame only after `Presented`), a readback surface kept a frame in flight so the CPU drew it for ever with promotion on, and a pass stayed in render's `pending`, which holds the device up. Now `State::frame` draws through `draw_frame`, whose every early return is an error answered as `GpuReply::Failed { surface }` (render takes a surface whose frame fails back to the CPU), a pass that draws nothing is answered `Failed { key }` (render records it as drawn with no pixels until its inputs change), and the host clears a presented surface's frame in flight on `Failed` as on `Presented` (`crates/strand-gpu/tests/frames.rs::frames_and_passes_that_cannot_be_drawn_are_answered`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review): a surface an ending GPU thread holds is released when that thread ends.** Review found a path where a `wl_surface` could go before its swapchain: at `BackendChange::Drop` the host keeps the surfaces still presented as the ending thread's `held` list and forgets the `Gpu`; if the manager then destroyed one of them (`gpu_release`) before the thread had ended, the host saw no running `Gpu` and took it back at once, so the manager destroyed the `wl_surface` while the ending thread could still own its swapchain. The release is now routed (`run/gpu.rs::release_route`): held by an ending thread, it waits for that thread's end, where the held surfaces are taken back anyway; otherwise the running thread is asked, or, with none, it is taken back now. For the same reason a surface an ending thread holds is attached without handles (read back) if render promotes it again before that thread has ended (`run::gpu::host::tests::a_release_waits_for_the_ending_thread_that_holds_the_surface`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review): an unavailable reason is a warning once.** Without a usable adapter, every visible repainting `shader` node makes render ask for the device again once per 30 s (architecture.md: "Render asks again at most once per 30 s while demand lasts"), and each failed start logged `warn!("GPU: …")`, twice a minute for as long as the node showed, though `GpuStatus` and logic's notice were already said once per reason. The retry stays (a driver can be installed, a device can come back), since it is design's rule and costs one short-lived thread per 30 s; the log line is now a warning only when its reason differs from the last one warned of, and a debug line otherwise; a device that came up resets it, so a later failure is said again (`crates/strand-render/tests/gpu.rs::an_unavailable_reason_is_warned_once`). Skipping the retry for reasons that look permanent (`NoAdapter`, `Software`) was not done: the 30 s retry is the documented behaviour, and the reason a user installs a driver is to see shaders without restarting the shell.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review): colour uniforms are premultiplied sRGB, and what of the shader ABI is carried over.** architecture.md's ABI said colour uniforms arrive "premultiplied linear", while a pass renders into a non-sRGB `Bgra8Unorm` texture whose bytes the CPU composites as sRGB (vello_cpu's space, and vello_gpu's in a promoted frame): a file returning `u_tint` painted `#7f3f1f` as `[3, 13, 54]` against the box's `[31, 63, 127]`, and design.md's own example (`shader "aurora.wgsl" { u_tint: $accent }`) would not show `$accent`. Two consistent readings existed: linear in and linear out (an sRGB-encoding store on the pass, a non-sRGB view for vello to sample, and still an error for translucent output, since encoding premultiplied channels is not premultiplying encoded ones), or one space throughout. The second removes a concept: uniforms are packed premultiplied sRGB, the space the output is read in and everything else composites in, so a shader that wants linear-light maths converts itself, as a CSS author does. architecture.md's ABI and `UniformType`'s doc say so, and `gpu_shader.png` was blessed again (its tint is the file's `#f9e2af` now). This is a change to an interface 0c fixed: the integrator should confirm it with the owner, and reverting it is the two lines of `value_floats` and the reference (`crates/strand-render/tests/gpu.rs::a_colour_uniform_paints_like_the_same_bg`, opaque and translucent, within 1 of the CPU's `bg`; `renderer::backend::tests::uniforms_pack_in_buffer_units`). Carried over with the shaders box, which stays unticked: `strand.pointer` is always -1, -1 (render does not yet track the pointer per surface in buffer pixels relative to each pass's box), and `Prop::Uniforms` values are packed as set rather than sprung (the ABI's "from the springing `Prop::Uniforms`"; each entry would spring as its value's type does, which needs per-entry motions in render's prop animation).

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review): a clocked shader on a GPU-drawn surface damages its box every frame.** Rewriting `gpu_idle` to hold the animated panel on screen past 500 ms (review: it never checked that the surface stayed presented) showed it attached in `Present` mode and released about 500 ms later, again and again, while the aurora ran. A promoted surface's passes run in its GPU frames, so no pass pixels come back to change the `shader` node's record as they do on a CPU surface: with only `strand.time` moving, every frame diffed to no damage, which `Promotion::frame` rightly does not count, so the surface looked idle and `Promotion::idle` demoted it (and a readback surface skipped the paint altogether, its frames frozen). Now `Renderer::gpu_clocked_damage` adds the boxes of the clocked passes of a surface the GPU draws to the frame's damage, which promotion reads and which makes a readback surface send the frame. The same run showed the host sending a presented surface's next frame after its `Release` (the thread, which now answers every frame, said "not attached"): a presented surface whose `Release` went out is marked `releasing` and gets no more frames (`crates/strand-render/tests/gpu.rs::a_clocked_shader_on_a_gpu_surface_damages_every_frame`; `crates/strand/tests/gpu_idle.rs::gpu_is_released_when_idle`, which fails on the hold with the damage left out).

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review): `gpu_idle` proves the presented path.** Review found that `gpu_idle` counted any `attached (` line (so a broken WSI falling back to readback passed), never compared presented pixels with the CPU's, had no small shader surface reading back, closed the panel (the `gpu_release` path) instead of hiding it, and was not named as m4-plan names it. It is now `gpu_is_released_when_idle`: panel `Glow` (640×420: a 640×320 clocked shader over a strip with a gradient box, a still shader and text) and panel `Ref` (320×100, the same strip) stay open and `glow.on` shows and hides the shaders. On the lavapipe tier `Glow` must attach in `Present` mode (`STRAND_GPU_HARDWARE=1` also accepts `Readback`, since ANV cannot present on a pixman sway), only `Glow` is attached, and it stays presented for 1.5 s. On grim's screenshot the still shader shows its premultiplied colour over the strip in both panels (red and blue swapped, or straight alpha, would not), which in `Ref` can only come from a pass read back, and `Glow`'s presented strip matches `Ref`'s CPU-drawn one within render's GPU tolerance (6 per channel, 2 % of pixels; 0 pixels past it, worst 3, on lavapipe). Hidden, `Glow` is demoted and `Released` (the demotion path), the thread ends, nothing wakes, both strips are the CPU's again and identical, and PSS across two cycles stays within 3 MiB. The output's background is sway's grey `[63, 63, 63]`, not black, so colours are computed from the screenshot rather than assumed.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review): architecture.md as landed, and the bar's PSS with the GPU linked.** Review found architecture.md still listing `Frame { …, readback: Option<Rect> }` and saying `STRAND_GPU_SOFTWARE=1` was pending, both false on this branch; the `strand-gpu` section now gives `Frame`'s fields as built (`clear`, no `readback`) and says the lavapipe tier sets the variable in CI's env, `run.sh` and `ci.sh`. Review also asked why the design bar reads 33,731–34,016 kB against features.md's 31.2–32.3 MB. The two baselines are different builds, not different environments: features.md's figures (wave4-exitMemory) are the CPU-only build of M3, while m4-gpu-spike measured the GPU-linked build alternately with the CPU build in this same container at a mean of 33.7 MB, about 1.3 MB (+4 %) more, and attributed it (smaps of the `strand` mapping) to relocated `.data.rel.ro` (+129 kB dirty) and `.got`, code pages where LTO mixes hot and cold functions (0.6–0.85 MB together) and 0.3–0.5 MB of mimalloc anon within run-to-run spread; no Vulkan library is mapped. The landed backend's 33.7–34.0 MB is that prediction plus noise, so it was not investigated again; the spike's remedies (section ordering, `opt-level = "s"` for wgpu-core and naga) remain the lever if the bar needs room, and the remaining margin under the 34 MiB target (about 0.8 MiB) is recorded in architecture.md's budgets.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review 2): handles lent for an `Attach` keep the `wl_surface` alive.** Review found that a surface closed between `Promote` and its `Attached` reply (the first promotion waits 100 ms or more for the device) was destroyed normally while the GPU thread could still call `create_surface_unsafe` and `configure` on its `wl_surface`: use-after-free in the WSI, or a reused id. The same held for `BackendChange::Drop` with an `Attach` still queued, since the host only held back surfaces already presented. `State::raw_handles` now takes `&mut self` and lends the surface: until `take_back` a destroy keeps the `wl_surface` and calls `gpu_release`, exactly as for a handed-off surface, while the manager keeps painting and committing it until `hand_off`. The host records which `Attach` carried handles; an `Attached { Readback }` gives a lent surface back at once (the thread dropped its WSI attempt before answering), `Exited` gives back every lent surface, and a dropped thread holds every lent surface until it has ended. A `Release` sent before the `Attached` reply now also makes that reply hand nothing off (it used to hand the surface off and send frames after the `Release`). Reading the rule this way keeps one concept, "the GPU thread has the handles", rather than adding a pending state beside "handed off". Tests: `strand-surface/tests/gpu_handoff.rs::a_surface_destroyed_after_its_handles_were_lent_waits_for_take_back`, `strand run/gpu.rs::a_lent_surface_is_kept_until_the_thread_lets_go`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review 2): still shaders keep their pixels across a device drop.** Review found that the device's idle drop cleared the `shader` nodes' pass results, so the next frame of a CPU surface showing a still shader (an aurora behind a ticking bar clock) drew it transparent and asked for a new pass, starting the device again every minute. The results are CPU pixmaps, not GPU memory: they now stay, and a node asks again only when its inputs change. Test: `strand-render/tests/gpu.rs::a_still_shader_keeps_its_pixels_when_the_device_drops`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review 2): a handed-off surface's geometry goes out as pending state.** Review found that a resize or scale change while presented only reported the size: the viewport destination, `set_buffer_scale` and a popup's window geometry were sent only on the shm path, so the WSI's next commit showed the new buffer in the old rect. `draw_handed_off` now sets them as pending state (the shm path's code moved into `commit.rs::send_geometry`, shared by both). A popup grab's keyboard interactivity is pending state too: `set_grab_keyboard` no longer commits a handed-off layer surface. Tests: `strand-surface/tests/gpu_handoff.rs::a_handed_off_surface_shows_its_new_size_at_the_next_present` (headless sway at 1.5x, the WSI's commit made on the lent handle) and `gpu_handoff.rs::tests::a_popup_grab_does_not_commit_a_handed_off_surface`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review 2): readback pixels of another size are not copied in.** Frames run one behind, so after a resize the first pixels back are the old size; they were copied into the corner of the new buffer and committed as a full frame. That frame is now the CPU's, and the frame sent at the new size is copied in next. Writing its test showed a second bug: from the second GPU frame on, a re-rasterised island (a masked layer) came out blank. vello_gpu writes an upload through the queue but clears a destroyed image's atlas slot in the frame's encoder, so a slot freed and reused in the same frame was cleared after the new pixels landed. The GPU thread now uploads first and destroys retired and replaced images after. Tests: `strand-render/tests/gpu.rs::a_resized_readback_surface_does_not_copy_old_size_pixels`, `strand-gpu/tests/frames.rs::an_upload_in_a_retired_uploads_slot_is_drawn`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-gpu-w2 (review 2): one device per process, also across a drop.** Review found that a promotion right after `BackendChange::Drop` (or `Exited`) spawned a new `Gpu` while the dropped thread was still tearing its device down: two devices for a moment, and under lavapipe two copies of LLVM's state. The host now queues requests while any dropped thread is still ending and starts the next `Gpu` once the last has been joined (it polls them every 50 ms). A release for a surface whose `Attach` is queued is queued with it, so it is never destroyed early. The wait is at most the device's teardown, and promotion never stalls a frame meanwhile because the CPU keeps drawing. Test: `run/gpu.rs::no_thread_starts_while_another_is_ending`.

## m4-effects-paint-w2

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `filter:` and `backdrop:` each take their own functions, checked in `check/effects.rs`.** Both props have the schema's `Filter` type (m4-scene), so the type checker lets `filter: glass()` and `backdrop: bloom(12)` through. design.md spells glass only as `backdrop: glass()` and a backdrop as a blur over your own content, while the colour functions and the bundled passes (`bloom`, `crt`, `chromatic`, `wobble`) work on the node's own subtree. So `backdrop:` takes `blur` and `glass`, and `filter:` takes `blur`, the seven colour functions and the four bundled passes; any other builtin in either is the error `check::misplaced_filter`, with a help naming the right prop. The check looks through `?:`, `match` arms and lists, in props and `when` blocks, since a value the checker cannot see (a `let` of type `Filter`) has no call to judge. Literal knobs that can only be mistakes are `check::effect_range` errors: a negative `blur` or `bloom` radius, and `grain` outside 0..1 (`crates/strand-compiler/src/check/effects.rs` tests).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: group effects are built from props every frame, and the `set_layer_effects` seam is gone.** `crate::effects::group` reads a node's resolved (token-, time- and spring-evaluated) `filter:`, `mask:` and `blend:` when it is flattened and builds its layer: the filter functions in written order, with each run of colour functions composed into one matrix (a `blur` between them splits the run), then the mask, then the blend. Building per frame rather than per diff means a `filter: tint($accent)` follows a theme swap and a `mask: radial(center, 40 * wave(2s))` its clock with no second path, and the effects hash into the node's signature as before. `blend: normal` is no effect. The wave-1 tests in `layers.rs` now set the props (`opacity:` gives the group opacity they set as `Effect::Opacity`; their refs are unchanged), and `tests/effects.rs` draws every function (refs `effects_filters`, `effects_filters_2x`, `effects_blend`, `effects_masks`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: the colour functions' matrices.** design.md names the functions but not their maths. They are the Filter Effects spec's shorthand matrices over straight-alpha sRGB (what CSS does), with Rec. 709 luma weights (0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722) throughout so `grayscale(1)` is exactly `saturate(0)`: `grayscale(a)` and `invert(a)` clamp their amount to 0..1, `saturate`, `brightness` and `contrast` (about mid grey) take any amount from 0, `hue(θ)` keeps luma. `tint(c)`, which CSS lacks, maps each pixel's luma onto `c` (white becomes `c`, black stays black) as strongly as `c`'s alpha, so `tint($accent.alpha(0.5))` is a half-strength tint and the function adds no knob. A radial mask's percentage size (`radial(center, 40%)`, as the snippets write it) is of the distance from its anchor to the box's farthest corner, so `100%` reveals the whole box from any anchor.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: the bundled filters are shader passes, and on the CPU only `bloom` draws.** `filter: bloom(r)`, `crt()`, `chromatic(px)` and `wobble(amp)` become `Effect::Shader` passes with `ShaderInput::Content` and their one length knob as uniform 0 in buffer pixels (`crt` has none), so their reach grows damage as m4-scene fixed and the GPU stream runs them in wave 3. Without a GPU, design.md says bloom "becomes glow" and the shader-only ones draw unfiltered: a bloom layer is an offscreen group (`Layer::cell_local` is false for it) whose pixels are drawn over a copy of themselves blurred with σ = r/3, so the glow ends where the pass's reach does; the other passes push an empty layer (`effects.rs::bundled_filters_fall_back_on_the_cpu`, ref `effects_bundled`). No knob beyond design.md's positional is added, so builtin.schema's declarations stay as 0b landed them.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: the shape library's outlines, and what a shaped box does.** design.md names the shapes (`rect`, `pill`, `circle`, `cookie`, `clover`, `burst`, `flower`, `sunny`, `gem`, `triangle`, `pentagon`, `hexagon`, `heart`) but not their geometry. `rect`, `pill` and `circle` are exact paths (a rounded rect at the box's corner radius, a capsule, an ellipse); the others are 120 points sampled by angle in the box's unit square (`cookie` r = 0.9 + 0.1·cos 9θ, `clover` four lobes, `burst` 12 soft points, `flower` 8 round petals, `sunny` 8 gentle rays, `gem` a diamond with rounded corners, the regular polygons, and a heart by bisection of its implicit curve), each centred and scaled uniformly to fill the box, joined by a Catmull-Rom curve. Every shape having the same 120 points sampled at the same angles is what lets any two morph point by point. A shaped box clips its fill, border, children and content to the outline; its shadow, hit test and `squircle` use the rounded rect at the shape's corner (0 for `rect`, half the shorter side otherwise), since a blurred shadow does not show the difference and hit testing stays a rect test. `mask: shape(name)` cuts a subtree to the same outline in the layer's box (an unknown name is `rect`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `shape:` morphs by a spring on progress, held in the `Animator`.** design.md says a shape change "morphs by spring". The morph is one channel, 0 to 1, on the `shape` prop's transition (`$motion.spatial` by default, `~ instant` snaps, `reduced_motion` snaps); each frame draws the starting outline (the one on screen when the shape changed, a morph in flight included) lerped towards the new one by the progress, so a bouncy spring overshoots and comes back. A spring on progress rather than one per point keeps the morph one motion, equal in time to any other spatial transition. The state lives in `shapes::morph::Morphs`, owned by the `Animator` (`shape_outline`, `forget_shape`), so it shares the animator's forgetting, `busy` (a preview that sees a change asks for a fresh flatten) and frame requests; this is a small edit in S-runtime's `anim/mod.rs` and `flatten/node.rs`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `glow: r` is the shape grown by σ = r/4 and blurred by σ; boxes glow as a shadow, text, icons and images glow their pixels.** design.md gives `glow: 12, $accent.alpha(0.6)` "on boxes, text and icons", "cached as 9-slice or pixmap", and no maths. A plain Gaussian of the shape (CSS's `0 0 12px` shadow) is half strength at the edge and reads as a dim smudge, not a glow, so the shape is grown by σ first and the glow reaches about 4σ = r. A box (every kind but `text`, `icon` and `image`) glows as a shadow with no offset, a spread of σ and a CSS blur of 2σ: the shadow item and its 9-slice cache, under the box and clipped outside it as shadows are. Text, icons and images glow their own pixels: the items they drew are copied into an offscreen group just before them, tinted to the colour (`filter::solid`), blurred by σ and their coverage doubled (a cheap stand-in for growing glyph shapes), which is the cached pixmap the design names; such text gives up its glyph-cell damage, since its glyphs are no longer the last thing drawn. `glow: r` alone glows in the node's colour.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `inner_shadow:` is CSS `inset`, and `rim:` is a one-pixel band following the box.** `inner_shadow` takes the shadow syntax (the schema's `shadow` type), so it means what CSS's `inset` box shadow means: inside the box, the shadow a hole of the box's shape casts, moved by the offset, shrunk by the spread and blurred by blur/2. It is drawn as an even-odd ring (a rect well past the box, minus the moved, shrunk outline) in a blurred offscreen group, clipped to the box, over the background and under the border. `rim: edge, color` ("lit top edge") is the band between the outline and the outline moved one logical pixel (at least one device pixel) in from that edge, clipped to the box, drawn over the border: it follows the corners and thins out around them, as light on a bevel does. Both follow a `shape:`'s outline.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: grain animates at 12 fps, static under `reduced_motion`, and raster sources are built from props.** design.md says both "grain at 12 fps" (the clock list) and "Trivial when static" (the catalogue). Grain is new noise every 12 fps tick, which is what film grain is and what the clock list names; under `reduced_motion` its clock stands still and it is the static grain the catalogue prices. Each device pixel is a grey of hashed lightness at the amount's opacity, over the background and clipped to the box's shape. Its source is built from the resolved props each frame (`effects::raster::built`) and drawn through a new `RasterNodes::pixmap_from`, which keys the pixmap by the source's config too; `effects::raster::rate` gives the clock from the raw props before they resolve (12 fps; when the node's props also read time, its clock runs at refresh and grain keeps its own 12 fps tick, so time-bound props are never held to grain's cap). This replaces the hidden `Renderer::set_raster_source` seam, whose tests now draw grain. `RasterNodes::set` stays, unused for now, for the media stream's sources with state of their own (graph history, spectrum, animated frames). These are small edits in S-runtime's `offscreen.rs`, `flatten/node.rs` and `renderer/mod.rs`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: strokes run clockwise from 12 o'clock inside the box; trim follows the wave.** design.md gives `stroke: 3, $accent { trim: 0, progress; wave: 2, 18px; cap: round }` and no geometry. A stroke follows the box's outline (its `shape:` included) inset by half its width, so it is drawn inside the box as `border:` is and never changes the box's ink. A closed outline starts where it crosses the top of its centre line and runs clockwise, so `trim: 0, progress` fills a progress ring from 12 o'clock as gauges do. `wave: amplitude, wavelength` moves the line along its normal by a sine (a closed line fits a whole number of waves, so it has no seam; an amplitude alone takes the example's 18 px), and `trim` is taken after it, so a trimmed wave keeps its shape. `dash: on, off` and `cap:` go to kurbo's stroker with round joins; the default cap is `butt` (SVG's), and `arc` gauges and wavy meters default to `round` (Material 3's indicators). `trim: to` alone means `0, to`. `stroke`, `trim`, `wave` and `glow` join the props that spring (a stroke's width and solid paint, as a border's), a small edit in S-runtime's `anim/{mod,motion}.rs`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: an `arc`'s `width` is its line's, and its box is square.** design.md's gauge is `arc { value: cpu.usage; sweep: 270deg; width: 4 }`. Read as a box width, that is a 4 px wide gauge, which is not what the line means, and the schema gives the arc no other way to set its line. So on an `arc` (only) `width` is the line width (4 px when not given), and its box is square: `size:`, or `height:`, or 24 px (`Ctx::Square`, as an undecoded image's), a small edit in S-runtime's `layout/style.rs`. The track spans the sweep (270° when not given) with its gap centred at the bottom; a full 360° ring starts at 12 o'clock. The value fills clockwise from the start in `color` (else `$accent`) over a `track` paint (else the foreground at 15 %, a meter's).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: a wavy meter's fill is a static wave that springs flat.** design.md: "Wavy media progress that flattens when paused", `meter media.position { wave: media.playing ? 3 : 0 }`. With a non-zero `wave` the meter's fill is a round-capped line as thick as the meter along its middle, moved by a sine of that amplitude and Material 3's 40 px wavelength (the track stays the flat bar behind it); `wave` springs, so pausing flattens it into the plain pill fill, the same shape at amplitude 0. The wave does not travel: a moving wave would give every playing meter a clock and a repaint every frame, where the design prices the meter as trivial and asks that only what changes repaints.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `backdrop:` is an empty offscreen group of what is drawn behind, under the background.** design.md: `backdrop: blur(16)` is "blur over your own content", "inside a surface", "drawn at quarter scale"; `backdrop: glass()` without a GPU "becomes blur and tint". The scene IR already had the pieces (`ShaderInput::Backdrop`, `Bundled::BackdropBlur`, `Bundled::Glass`), so a backdrop is an effect layer with that one shader pass and no items, clipped to the box's outline and drawn just under its background (so a translucent `bg` tints the blur, as frosted panels are drawn). On the CPU the offscreen cache draws its group from the display list's earlier items over the box grown by the blur's reach (groups still open at the node are left open, their items drawn as they are), at a quarter of the size, blurs it there and scales it back up bilinearly; a blur under 8 device pixels is drawn at half size and under 2 at full size, since a quarter-scale pass would turn it into blocks. Backdrops are drawn after the frame's other offscreen groups, in order, so a filtered group behind one shows filtered. The cache key and the node's damage signature hash the items behind, so a change behind the box repaints it and nothing else. `glass()`'s CPU fallback is a 16 px blur under white at 12 %, a frosted look with no refraction; the GPU version (wave 3, S-gpu) replaces it. The promotion to the GPU above about 0.2 Mpx is wave 3's. Small edits in S-runtime's `layers.rs` (a backdrop is not cell-local), `offscreen.rs` (backdrops drawn last) and `flatten/node.rs`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: the built-in effects and particles are pure functions of `t`, already running at `t = 0`, and hold that frame under `reduced_motion`.** design.md names `effect lightning | sparks | shimmer | ripple | aurora` "with a few named knobs" and `particles { rate; life; sprite: dot(3); glow }` as "CPU sprite blits" under 1,000, but not what they look like. Each is drawn on the CPU as a raster source built from props (its own `color`, else `$accent`; `speed` scales time): lightning a jagged bolt from top to bottom every 1.6 s with one branch, flashing over 0.3 s; sparks bursts of 14 sparks every 1.2 s flying out and falling; shimmer a soft diagonal band sweeping every 1.5 s (capped at 30 fps, as the clock list says); ripple three rings growing from the middle every 2 s; aurora, its CPU fallback, three curtains in the colour and its neighbours on the colour wheel. Particles are born every `1 / rate` seconds at random points, drift at `speed` × 20 px/s and fade in and out over `life`, each one blit of a precomputed `dot` sprite with its `glow`; `rate · life` is capped at 1,000 alive (above it is the GPU's, wave 3). None keeps state between frames: the same `t` draws the same pixels, so a preview, a repaint and a reload agree, and each is already running at `t = 0` (a bolt just struck, the field full), which is the frame `reduced_motion`'s stopped clock shows: "turns off" reads as "stops", as grain's does, rather than "hides". A node's clock now starts only when its raster is drawn inside the clip (the wave-1 special case that counted any visible `effect` as drawn is gone), and `damage.rs`'s idle-effect test became `effect_nodes_run_their_clocks_only_while_drawn`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `letters` goes inside its `text`, and its letters are the drawn glyphs.** decisions.md m4-owner has `letters` animate "the text of its enclosing `text` node", but `text` is a leaf and the checker refused any child (`check::children_not_allowed`), so `text "hi" { letters { … } }` could not be written. `letters` is now a child a leaf `text` may hold, like `popup` and `tooltip` on any element (`check/tree.rs::rendered_child`); any other child is still an error. A `letters` outside a `text` (the snippets fixture's) draws nothing, without an error, so the fixture and its snapshot stay as they are. Render draws such a text one letter at a time: the letters are its laid-out glyphs in visual order (a ligature is one letter and spaces, which draw nothing, are none), `index` counts them from 0 and `count` is how many; the `letters` node's props are resolved once per letter with its `index`, `count` and the text's `t` (the text's clock runs when they read `t`), and its `x`, `y`, `opacity`, `scale`, `rotate` (about the letter's centre) and `color` apply to that letter. The text's layout is shaped once; each letter is a one-glyph copy of it.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: text `fill:` composites onto the glyphs, and `text_stroke:` grows their coverage.** `fill: linear(…)` on text draws the glyphs in an isolated layer and the paint over them source-in, so the gradient spans the text's box (a new `fill` on `Item::Glyphs`, a small edit in S-runtime's `flatten/{mod,hash}.rs` and `raster/draw.rs`). Glyphs are bitmaps, not paths, so `text_stroke: width, paint` cannot be a path stroke: it is a copy of the letters in an offscreen group under them, in the paint's colour (a gradient's first stop), blurred by 1.48 × width and with every pixel over a quarter covered made opaque, which grows the letters by about `width` (a Gaussian's quarter level lies 0.674 σ out) with a soft outer edge. A glow on the same text glows the outlined letters.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `roll: true` rolls the letters that changed, by drawn glyph, along the `roll` prop's transition.** design.md shows `text pct(level) { roll: true }` and calls it trivial but says nothing about which letters move. The renderer compares the old and new layouts glyph by glyph in visual order. A glyph whose slot or position changed rolls: the old one slides up out of the text's box as the new one comes up from below, clipped to the box. Unchanged glyphs stay where they are, so `41%` → `42%` moves only the `2`. If the glyph count changes, every glyph rolls, because a slot-by-slot match would pair digits wrongly. Progress is a one-channel spring on the `roll` entry's transition (`$motion.spatial` by default). `~ instant`, `reduced_motion` and frames with no clock show the new text at once. A change during a roll continues from whichever text is nearer on screen. This adds no concept: the roll is a transition of the text itself.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: what keyframes settings mean, and how stops compose.** design.md gives `keyframes shake { … }` + `play shake`, and the grammar example adds `duration: 300ms`. The checker already allows `duration`, `delay`, `repeat: int`, `alternate` and `easing`. A block with no `duration` plays for 300 ms, the length of the grammar example and of `~ bezier(…)`. `repeat: n` plays it n times. `repeat: 0` or less repeats forever, which needs no new keyword. `easing` (a named curve or `bezier(…)`, linear by default) applies between each pair of stops, as in CSS. Stops are offsets composed with the springs, per architecture.md: `x`, `y` and `rotate` add to the node's own value; `scale` and `opacity` multiply it; every other prop draws the stop's value in place of the node's. A prop missing at the first or last stop starts or ends at the node's own value, so `25% { x: -4 }` alone nudges out and back. The node draws as it is during the delay and after the last run. A tree-level `play` plays once when its node mounts (`seq` 0). Under `reduced_motion`, a finite block does not play and a loop holds still at its start. To key the block by declaration rather than name, the VM now has a `Value::Keyframes(DefId)`. Two files' private `keyframes shake` therefore stay distinct.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `stagger:` numbers the children that enter together.** The schema says `stagger` "delays each child's `enter` this much after the one before" but not which children count. A child the container gained long ago is not "before" a new one. So when the first of a set of children starting their `enter` together is drawn, render numbers those children in child order. Child `i` holds at its enter pose for `i · stagger` and then plays the pose as usual. A later batch counts from 0 again, so a new toast in a staggered column enters at once. One step is capped at 1 s, so a mistyped `stagger: 30s` cannot hide a row for minutes. Only the paint pose is delayed: layout and size springs still place every child at once, so nothing reflows as the children appear. `reduced_motion` shows them all at once, as it does every pose.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: parallax is measured against the surface, the CPU's tilt turns in the plane, and `reduced_motion` turns both off.** design.md gives `parallax: 6px` and `tilt: 8deg`, saying "Parallax trivial; true 3D tilt is GPU". `parallax: d` moves the node up to `d` towards the pointer, scaled by the pointer's offset from the surface's centre (the full `d` at the edges). That way several layers with different `d` move against one another, which is what parallax means. A negative `d` moves the node away from the pointer. `tilt: a` follows the pointer across the node's own box. With no perspective, an affine rotation about the node's X or Y axis only foreshortens it, and at 8° that is about 1 %, which is invisible. So the CPU's 2D tilt turns the node in its plane by up to `a`, towards the side the pointer is on, and the 3D turn stays the GPU's. Both spring along the prop's transition, settle back when the pointer leaves, and apply as paint offsets added to `x`, `y` and `rotate`. `reduced_motion` turns both off, since pointer-driven motion is what that setting asks to stop. Render does not own the `Router`, so the host passes the pointer after each routed event with `Renderer::set_pointer`. A surface with nothing leaning gets no repaint from pointer motion.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: transition masks are clip paths, with pixelate as a blur on the CPU.** design.md lists `transition: wipe(left) | disc | dissolve | pixelate` on `if`, `pages` and image swaps. Its masks are drawn as clips over the node's subtree, which needed no new effect in `strand-scene`. `wipe(edge)` grows from `edge` (`left` by default, read as "from", like `slide(top)`). `disc` grows from the centre until it reaches the corners. `dissolve` reveals 4 px cells in a fixed random order. `pixelate` needs the subtree drawn at low resolution and sampled back up, which only the GPU path can do. On the CPU it draws as a blur that sharpens (12 px to 0) while it fades in. That follows the rule for bundled effects: the CPU fallback keeps the effect's shape without its exact look. A node with `transition:` is revealed as it enters and hidden as it leaves, so a removed node with one now plays out as a ghost, as one with an exit pose already does. A `pages` with `transition:` puts the mask on whichever page draws on top (the later child). If that is the new page, it is revealed over the old. If it is the old page, it is hidden by the complement of the same mask over the new. Either way the swap looks the same, and the old page plays out until the new one is in. Progress springs along the `transition` entry's `~`. The prop itself is a snap, so its default curve is `x`'s, `$motion.spatial`. `reduced_motion` swaps at once. Image swaps (a changed `src`) need the old image kept and are not done yet.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: a shared-element morph starts from the last box drawn with its name, on the same surface only.** design.md says nodes with the same `morph` name "morph into each other across surfaces". m4-plan adds: "Morph across surfaces needs surface origins, else falls back to the enter pose". Render remembers, per name, the box (laid out plus paint offsets) where a node with that name was last drawn, and for 1 s afterwards. A node with that name that enters on the same surface starts over that box. It is moved and scaled separately in each axis about its centre, subtree included, like a FLIP, then springs to its own box along the `morph` entry's `~` (`$motion.spatial` by default). This replaces its enter pose. The node it came from leaves as it would anyway: shared-element morphs move the new element, they do not blend two. Render has no surface origins yet, so a name last drawn on another surface gives nothing to start from, and the node plays its enter pose. That covers the bar pill becoming the media panel for now. Once the surface layer reports where its surfaces sit, the stored box can be moved by the difference between surface origins. `reduced_motion` shows the node in place.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: `merge d` draws a goo field under its children, closing gaps narrower than `d`.** design.md gives `merge 10 { … }` ("children melt together", "via marching squares"), and the schema says "within the given distance". A merge node draws, under its children, a CPU raster of their smooth union. Each child is its drawn box: a rounded rectangle with its paint offsets and springs, taken from the hit boxes once the children are flattened. The boxes are combined by a polynomial smooth minimum of width `2d`, so two boxes `d` apart just meet, and any nearer grow a thicker bridge. The goo takes each child's solid `bg`, blended where they meet. Children without a solid `bg` add no goo. The children still draw on top, so text and icons stay sharp and only the bridges are new. The field is evaluated per pixel rather than contoured by marching squares. On the CPU that is the same work and gives an antialiased edge for free, and marching squares remains the GPU's way. The pixmap is cached by the children's boxes and redrawn only when one moves.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2: an image swap masks the new image in once it is decoded.** For the third place design.md puts transition masks, image swaps, an `image` with `transition:` whose `src` changes keeps the old source and draws it under the new one. The new image comes in through the mask, along the entry's `~`. The mask starts only when the new source is decoded. Until then the old image stays whole, so a slow decode never shows an empty box. When the mask is done, the old source is let go. A node's own `transition:` also masks the image in as it enters and out as it leaves, as for any node. This supersedes the "not done yet" at the end of the transition-mask entry above.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2 (review): a `play` wants frames only while its node is drawn.** design.md says "the frame loop stops when every clock is idle", and a looping `play` is a clock. It used to ask for frames from every laid-out node, before the opacity, scale and clip checks, so a looping spinner under `opacity: 0` (or an ancestor's) kept an idle shell repainting at refresh rate, and a play under a hidden ancestor kept its surface "busy" (no scene-cache reuse) forever. A play now follows the same rule as a node's time clock: it wants frames when the node is drawn, or hidden only by something that follows time, and the props the play itself sets count as following time while it plays (a loop that blinks its own opacity through 0 keeps going; a loop that moves a node, by `x`, `y`, `scale` or `rotate`, keeps going outside its clip, as a time signal there does). A surface counts as busy with a play only if the last painted frame drew it. A hidden play keeps its start, so it resumes in phase when shown, and a fixed-count play that ended while hidden is over (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::a_hidden_or_clipped_loop_wants_no_frames`, `crates/strand-render/src/anim/keyframes.rs::tests::a_play_is_busy_only_while_drawn`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2 (review): an image swap waits for its decode without frames and ends when the decode fails.** A `src` is external input. When the new source failed to decode (a missing or corrupt file), the swap never started its mask, never ended, and asked for a frame every refresh for as long as the image was shown; a slow decode spun frames the whole time too. Now the wait holds the old image and asks for nothing (the decode's arrival repaints the surface, as for any image), and a failed decode ends the swap at once, so the image draws what it would without `transition:` (nothing, as a broken `src` always does) (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::an_image_swap_to_a_broken_source_settles`, `crates/strand-render/src/effects/transition.rs::tests::an_image_swap_waits_without_frames_and_ends_on_a_failed_decode`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2 (review): only a `text` may hold `letters`.** The exemption that lets `text "hi" { letters { … } }` through "takes no children" applied to every leaf, so `icon "x" { letters { … } }`, `meter { letters {} }`, `image` and `input` with a `letters` checked clean and drew nothing. As the letters entry above says, it is now `text` alone; `letters` in any other leaf is `check::children_not_allowed` (`crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::a_text_holds_letters_and_nothing_else`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2 (review): a lone-radius glow is the node's colour everywhere, and a springing glow keeps particles glowing.** Two places disagreed with the glow entry above ("`glow: r` alone glows in the node's colour") once `glow` joined the springs. The spring encoded a lone radius in the inherited colour while flatten drew it at rest in the node's own, so a node with its own `color:` glowed in its parent's colour mid-spring and snapped back; and a box (not a themed kind) drew it in black at rest. Both now take the node's colour: its own `color`, else the inherited one (`anim::motion::glow_color`, also used by keyframes). Particles read `glow` as a number, so the list a spring decodes to dropped their sprite glow to 0 until it settled; they now take the radius from either form (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::a_lone_radius_glow_springs_in_the_nodes_colour`, `crates/strand-render/src/effects/raster.rs::tests::particles_glow_by_radius_alone_or_in_a_list`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2 (review): a solid text `fill` springs; gradients, `filter: blur()` and `blur:` still snap.** m4-plan says the newly drawn props (`stroke`, `fill`, `trim`, `glow`, `blur`, gradients) join `ANIMATED`. `stroke`, `trim`, `wave` and `glow` did, and now a text's solid `fill` does as well, as a colour. A text with no `fill` draws in `color`, so a change from no fill to a fill (or back) has no colour to spring from and snaps (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::a_solid_text_fill_springs`, `anim/tests.rs::values_round_trip_through_channels`). Three stay out, and the reasons are recorded here. `blur:` is not drawn by Strand. It is the compositor's background blur, sent as a region that design.md says is re-sent only when the shape changes, so springing its radius would re-send it every frame, and on the tint fallback it changes nothing a spring could move. `filter: blur(r)` is one function in a filter chain, and a gradient (in `bg`, `fill` or a stroke's paint) is a list of stops. Springing either needs a structured channel encoding (the same kind and the same number of functions or stops at both ends, a snap otherwise), which this wave does not add. So they snap as before, and architecture.md's "Not yet animated" sentence (integrator-owned) should read: gradients, `filter` functions, `mark_color` and `blur:`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2 (review): a staggered child or an image swap never drawn keeps nothing busy.** Undrawn `enter` poses were already dropped after each frame so they keep no frames coming, but staggered children moved out of `enter` into their own starts, and an image swap mid-wipe kept its motion, so a `list { stagger: 30ms }` whose entering rows run past its viewport, or an image hidden by a transparent parent mid-wipe, left the animator busy until those rows' turns came or the image was drawn again (the scene cache was never reused on that surface and a content-sized surface could not shrink). Both now go the way of undrawn enter poses: a staggered child the frame did not draw loses its start and shows at rest when scrolled into view, and a hidden image's swap ends, so it shows its new source at rest when it comes back. Showing them at rest matches what an unseen `enter` already does (`crates/strand-render/src/renderer/tests.rs::a_stagger_past_the_viewport_leaves_nothing_busy`, `crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::an_image_hidden_mid_swap_wants_no_frames`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2 (review): before the GPU path aurora is still and the CPU fallbacks are said, as m4-plan asks.** The built-in effects entry above had aurora's CPU fallback animate at refresh, which departs from m4-plan's acceptance line ("Before the GPU path, particles cap at 1,000 and aurora is static, with a notice") and costs three curtains of `exp`/`sin` per pixel per frame on a large box, which is why design.md says "aurora is GPU". Aurora now has no clock of its own and draws its `t = 0` frame, so its pixmap is drawn once per size (a node whose other props read time keeps the same still pixmap). The notice follows the blur ladder's rung 3: the flattener notes each CPU fallback it draws (a still aurora; particles whose `rate × life` passes 1,000), `Renderer::take_effect_notices` returns each once a run, and the host logs it as a warning and sends it to `strand watch` as `ToLogic::Notice`. It is a runtime notice, not a checker warning: design.md's own `effect aurora` snippet must check with zero warnings, and whether aurora falls back depends on the GPU, which is known only at run time. Wave 3's GPU path takes aurora's animation and drops its notice when a device draws it (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::aurora_is_still_and_cpu_fallbacks_are_noticed_once`, `crates/strand/src/demo/host.rs::tests::effect_fallbacks_are_said_once_as_notices`; `effects_generative_100ms.png` re-blessed, its aurora cell now equal to the `t = 0` frame).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-paint-w2 (review): remembered `morph` boxes are dropped once stale.** Every committed frame remembered each morphing node's box by its `morph:` name, and nothing ever forgot one, so computed names (`morph: "note-" + n.id`, one per notification) grew the map for the life of the process. A box older than a second can start no morph, so it is now dropped: by its own surface's latest frame time (surfaces' clocks may differ), whenever the map has doubled since the last prune and on every tree change, which also drops the boxes of a surface that is gone. The second a replacing node has to start from its predecessor's box is unchanged (`crates/strand-render/src/anim/morph.rs::tests::stale_names_are_dropped`).

## m4-effects-media-w2

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: animated images play through the image store, and their clock is the frames' tick.** design.md asks for `image "spin.gif"` with "frames streamed, not cached whole" and "GIFs at their own rate". An animated image is still an `image` node, so it stays on the image path rather than becoming a CPU raster node: the decode carries the file's `Timeline` (`Decoded::anim`), `ImageKey::frame` names a frame, and the worker (inline offline) keeps a `Player` per image and drawn size that decodes frames one after another from the compressed file onto a canvas at the source's size, starting over when the loop wraps. Its clock comes through `clock::rate`'s raster input (`ImageStore::frame_rate`), so it is capped like any clock, stops while hidden and under `reduced_motion` (which shows frame 0), and only a tick that shows a new frame repaints. The tick is the delays' greatest common divisor (at least 10 ms). A node draws the frame its time shows and asks for the next one, and the store keeps at most those two frames per image and size (the plan's reading), plus the stand-in rules every image has. Players go with the images no frame draws, at most 16 at once (`crates/strand-render/tests/animated.rs`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: how each format's timing and composition is read.** A frame delay under 20 ms (0 included) plays at 100 ms, as browsers do, since such files were made for that. Loop counts are honoured, and a played-out animation keeps its last frame with no clock (an idle shell does no work): a GIF without the NETSCAPE extension plays once and one with count `n` plays `n + 1` times (0 is forever), an APNG plays `num_plays` times, a WebP `ANIM`'s count times. A PNG is animated when it has an `acTL` chunk before its image data, whatever its extension; its default image is a frame only when an `fcTL` precedes it. Timelines are read without decoding pixels (GIF frame headers, APNG `fcTL`, WebP `ANMF` headers). A WebP frame disposed to the background clears to transparent, as libwebp's animation decoder does, since the `ANIM` colour is only a hint; image-webp otherwise ignores the disposal. A still GIF or WebP draws like any image.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: the spectrum is 64 pitch bands from the audio thread, and render picks its bars from them.** A `spectrum`'s `bars` is a render prop that springs and changes without the audio thread hearing of it, so the FFT does not run per bar count: every reading with sound carries `Levels::bins`, 64 bands spaced evenly in pitch from 40 Hz to 16 kHz (the range music and speech fill; a 2,048-point FFT at 48 kHz has a bin every 23 Hz, so the lowest bands take the bin nearest their centre), each the loudest bin in it on a decibel scale from −72 dBFS to full scale. The ring the data thread fills is atomics only, and the FFT runs on the loop thread when a reading goes out, so the realtime thread never allocates or locks, the FFT runs at most once a frame, only while a tap is visible, and never on silence (the meter sends nothing then). Every meter keeps the ring: the peak meters' only consumer is the `spectrum` element (decisions.md, wave4-wm (audio)).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: `graph` and `spectrum` are CPU raster nodes; a spectrum has no clock and is fed only while visible.** A `graph` keeps one sample per physical column, so its clock ticks every `history / columns` (at least 16 ms; it repaints at refresh until its first draw tells it its width) and, as design.md asks, only the new columns are rasterised: the kept pixels shift left and the column the tick adds (and the live one before it) are drawn; the damage is the graph's box, the smallest rectangle a scroll changes. The newest column shows the live value, eased by `smooth`, so a value change between ticks redraws one column and no tick. A gradient `fill` is averaged to one colour (the graph is a column raster, not a path). Under `reduced_motion` its clock stops like every clock, so it stops scrolling. A `spectrum` has no clock at all: it repaints when the binary feeds it bands (`Renderer::feed`), and `Renderer::take_feed_demand` tells the binary which spectra a painted surface drew with pixels, so the audio tap and its FFT run only for visible ones; the binary changes taps only when that list changes. Under `reduced_motion` (design.md: it turns effects off) spectra rest as dots and are not fed. `graph` and `spectrum` draw in the inherited `color` (default `$fg`) like text and symbolic icons do, so they join the themed kinds in `flatten/node.rs`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: a spectrum bar is the loudest band it covers, and the binary taps audio per visible spectrum.** Averaging the 64 bands into fewer bars halved a pure tone (a 1 kHz sine lit about half of a 16-bar spectrum's bar, its neighbours in the same bar quiet), and each band is already the loudest bin in it, so a bar takes the loudest of its bands, which keeps "a tone lights its bar" true at any bar count. The binary keeps one level tap per visible spectrum (`run/feeds.rs`), taken after each paint from `Renderer::take_feed_demand`, with no tap at all for a hidden one; the tap's function runs on the audio thread and only sends the bands over a calloop channel. A spectrum that loses its tap (hidden, removed, or its source no longer a device id) is fed silence on the main thread, so it shows dots rather than stale bars when shown again before its first reading. The hook in `demo/host.rs`'s paint is the same shape as `forward_list_windows`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: what a `#id { … }` block can set, and where an SVG part turns.** A part takes `rotate`, `scale`, `x`, `y`, `opacity` and `fill`, the node props that mean something for one layer of a drawing; `rotate` and `scale` are about the drawing's centre, the reading of "a node turns about its box's centre" for a layer whose box is the whole drawing, which is where a gauge's needle pivots (design.md's example); `x` and `y` are in the SVG's own units, so a part moves with its drawing at any size. `fill` draws every pixel of the layer in one colour with its coverage kept (an SVG filter on the part's wrapper), as symbolic icons take the foreground colour, so gradients and strokes recolour too; the `svg` itself takes `fill` (the whole drawing) and `fit` (as `image`), added to its schema element. Part props spring and read time like any node's (a part reading time gives its `svg` a clock); they are resolved where the `svg` is flattened, since parts have no box of their own. The file is edited as text, not as a usvg tree (whose nodes are read-only): each part's element is wrapped by its byte range in a group of its own, its transform written in its parent's coordinates (the wrapper's absolute transform from one parse), so everything inside the layer keeps its SVG meaning. An SVG is read on the render thread on its first draw (at most 4 MB, once per source): SVGs are small text files, unlike the images the decode worker exists for. `svg_part` lowering gives each `#id` block a node index of its own in the checker.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: Lottie through velato into vello_cpu.** The spike the plan asked for: velato 0.12 with `default-features = false` depends on kurbo 0.13.1 and peniko 0.6.1, the versions vello_cpu 0.3 (vello_common 0.3) uses, and none of vello; its `RenderSink` trait (layers, clips, filled and stroked shapes) maps one to one onto vello_cpu's `RenderContext`, so a `lottie` is a CPU raster node with no second graphics stack and no duplicate crates. Its clock runs at the file's frame rate times `|speed|` (at most 120 fps, then capped like any clock), and the frame is the node's time times `speed` times the frame rate, in whole frames, looping over the file's frames (Lottie players loop by default; a negative speed plays backwards, `speed: 0` holds the first frame with no clock). It is `contain`ed in its box (the schema gives `lottie` no `fit`). The file is read and parsed once per source on the render thread on the first draw (at most 8 MB), before which the node runs one refresh frame; a missing or broken file draws nothing and has no clock. Image layers draw nothing: embedded raster assets would need the image decoders wired into velato's `draw_image`, which no design example needs.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: blurred album art is an `image` in a cached blur group, nothing more.** design.md's `image media.art { fit: cover; filter: blur(30) }` needs no media-specific code: the art decodes at drawn size like any image, and `filter: blur(30)` makes the image a group layer drawn through a 30 px Gaussian into a cached offscreen pixmap (m4-runtime F4), built again only when the art (or the box) changes, while the panel's other content repaints over it. The `filter:` lowering is S-effects-paint's (`renderer`'s effects from props); this stream's test drives the same group through the `set_layer_effects` seam that lowering replaces, so it holds before and after the merge. A blur reaching past the art's edges fades them, as CSS's `blur()` does; `clip: true` on the panel keeps it inside.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: window capture is a process-wide tap, at most 15 fps, scaled down on the protocol thread.** Thumbnails capture through ext-image-copy-capture on the `strand-toplevel` thread, which owns the foreign-toplevel handles a capture source needs. The entry point mirrors the audio taps (`wm::capture::capture_window(id, max, f) -> CaptureTap`) rather than a new service request: a thumbnail is a renderer feed like a spectrum, wanted only while visible, so the binary holds a tap per visible thumbnail and the `wm` service turns the set of taps into `ProtoCmd::Capture` wants. A session asks for the next frame as soon as one arrives, but the compositor answers only when the window changes, so a still window costs nothing; a frame is requested at most 15 times a second (a thumbnail is a preview, and a full-rate copy of every visible window is the cost design.md's budgets rule out). Frames are box-filtered down to cover the thumbnail's drawn size on the protocol thread, so render never receives (or holds) a full-size window. The buffer transform is ignored and the cursor is not painted (`paint_cursors` unset): thumbnails show the window as it is laid out. A failed session retries after a second; a stopped one (its window closed) ends without retry. sway 1.9 has no ext-image-copy-capture, so CI's proof is the fake compositor's implementation of it; the live proof is the compositor matrix.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: a `thumbnail` is fed like a spectrum, at its drawn size rounded up to 64 px, and keeps its last frame while hidden.** `thumbnail w` gets the window's id as its source text (a record's identity), and render asks for its frames through the same demand as spectra (`FeedKind::Thumbnail { window, max }`), so the binary captures exactly the visible thumbnails and no capture runs for a hidden one. The size asked for is the largest physical size it is drawn at on any surface, rounded up to a multiple of 64: a box that animates (a hover scale, a switcher opening) would otherwise start a new capture session every frame, and frames at most 63 px larger than drawn cost little. The frame is drawn by `fit` (`contain` by default, as for `image`), sampled bilinearly, with no clock: each frame repaints the node once. A thumbnail that is hidden keeps its last frame (unlike a spectrum, which rests), so it shows the window at once when shown again while the new capture starts. niri (25.x) offers no ext-image-copy-capture of toplevels, so its thumbnails draw nothing there; the matrix test skips it with a message.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: an animated image's clock wakes at frame changes, not at its delays' common step.** A GIF with delays of 70, 80 and 90 ms has a 10 ms common step, and a clock at that step asked for every refresh frame (each one a full flatten) although only one in five or six showed a new frame. The node's time still moves in that step (`Timeline::tick`), so every frame boundary lands on a tick and `frame_at` stays exact, but the instant the clock asks to be woken is the next frame boundary (`Timeline::until_change`, applied in flattening through `ImageStore::frame_wake`), so the loop wakes once per frame change. A node whose own props read time keeps the plain step, since those props follow the same clock. Test: `animated.rs::the_clock_wakes_only_at_frame_changes` (12 frame changes in a second drawn in at most 14 frames, where the step clock drew 60).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: animated-image players share files and keep within 16 MB together.** A player's canvas has to be at the source's size (frames compose on it), so its memory cannot follow the drawn size the way the image cache does. Players of the same file at other sizes now share the compressed file, a `Restore` disposal hands the saved canvas back instead of keeping a second copy, and the players together keep within `MAX_PLAYER_BYTES` (16 MB: files once each, canvases, the canvas a `Restore` frame saved, and the decoder's frame counted at the canvas's size), dropping the least recently used beyond it. The one being drawn is never dropped, so an animation larger than the budget alone (a 1080p GIF) still plays, by itself; dropping it would only restart its decode on the next frame. Test: `media::animated::tests::players_share_files_and_stay_within_their_bytes`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: the spectrum's FFT is a small radix-2 transform, not realfft.** With this stream's decoders in, the release binary's `.text` was 16.7 MB against the 15 MiB gate (`budgets.rs::the_release_binary_code_stays_within_15_mib`, which design.md's 10–14 MB code budget rests on); rustfft, under realfft, was 846 KB of it with its SIMD kernels and 290 KB without, nearly all its planner's algorithms for sizes the spectrum never asks for. The spectrum runs one 2,048-point transform at most once a frame, so a 60-line in-place radix-2 FFT (`audio::spectrum::Fft`, checked against a direct DFT) does the same work in a few KB; what the bands show (Hann window, 64 bands, dB from −72) is unchanged. design.md's "FFT via realfft" now reads "FFT on the audio thread". Lottie's velato is also built at opt-level "z" (it builds the scene once per animation frame; vello_cpu rasterises at 3), a root `Cargo.toml` change for the integrator. Together they bring `.text` to 15.66 MB, 54 KB under the gate: little room for the other wave-2 streams.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: smaller fixes from the wave-2 review.** A `lottie` with no source (a value not set yet) has no clock, as a broken file has none, instead of repainting at refresh while shown. An `svg` whose document cannot be wrapped (not XML, or a part id usvg rejects once wrapped) is not parsed again on every flatten until its source or part names change. Feed demand is also checked when a surface detaches and when a producer sends, so a spectrum or thumbnail whose surface closed with no paint after stops its producer (`media.rs::demand_drops_without_a_paint`). Capture constraints are gathered until `done` and then cleared, in whatever order the compositor sends them (the fake now sends a resize's formats before its size). An `svg`'s `#id { … }` block takes only `rotate`, `scale`, `x`, `y`, `opacity` and `fill`, what render applies to a layer; any other prop is `check::svg_part_prop` instead of being accepted and ignored. The capture test asserts its frame cap strictly but only that frames keep coming, not how many a loaded machine manages. The end-to-end spectrum test now checks that the tone lifts its own bar (band 34 of 64, bar 8 of 16) and the bars about two octaves away stay low.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: fed media drops what an old tap sent.** A spectrum that lost its tap was fed silence by `sync`, then `fed()` went on to feed the very bands that triggered it, and any still queued, so it held stale bars. A per-node "is it still tapped" check would not cover a node tapped again for another device or window, whose old tap's last sends are still queued. Each tap is now numbered and its sends carry the number; `fed()` syncs the taps and drops anything whose number is not the node's running tap, without a repaint. Test: `run::feeds::tests::a_spectrum_drops_what_its_old_tap_sent`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: a thumbnail's frame belongs to one window.** Nothing ever fed a thumbnail `None`, so a closed window's last frame stayed, and a thumbnail whose source switched to another window showed the old one until (or, with no capture, forever instead of) the new one's first frame. Two changes. First, `capture_window`'s callback takes `Option<&CaptureFrame>`. A tap that the protocol thread served last step, that is missing from the wants now and is still alive, lost its window (the wants list only listed windows), so it is called once with `None`. Second, the thumbnail's render source remembers the window its source named at the last paint and drops its frame when that changes. Doing this in render rather than in `feeds.rs` covers a source changed while the node is hidden (no tap to compare with), and it needs no map of past windows per node that would grow as rows come and go. A hidden thumbnail still keeps its frame. A compositor stopping a session while the window stays listed does not clear the thumbnail: that session is replaced (next paragraph). Tests: `crates/strand-render/tests/thumbnail.rs::a_thumbnail_draws_the_frames_it_is_fed_by_its_fit`, `crates/strand-services/tests/capture.rs`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: a stopped capture session is replaced after RETRY.** A stopped session stayed in the list while a want named its toplevel, which blocked a new one. Dropping it at once would remake a session on a toplevel whose `closed` has not arrived yet, which would stop again in a loop. So a stopped session ends immediately and leaves the list after `RETRY` (1 s). After that, a still-wanted, still-listed toplevel gets a new session; a closed window has left the list by then. The protocol loop wakes for it. The fake compositor gains `Cmd::StopCapture`. Test: `crates/strand-services/tests/capture.rs` (the stop-and-replace step).

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: the player budget never drops a player a live frame draws.** With two large animations on screen (each player about 8–13 MB against the 16 MB `MAX_PLAYER_BYTES`), each `Players::get` evicted the other. The decode worker serves the two in turn, so every frame change re-read a file and decoded it from frame 0. The budget now drops only players that no live frame draws (`Players::with_live`: the worker asks its wanted set; the inline store, whose players are exactly its frames', keeps them all). Players drawn together are kept past the budget. Their memory is bounded by what is on screen, as the image cache's protected frames are. Rebuilding is a CPU cost per tick that grows with the frame count, so it is never the cheaper choice. Test: `media::animated::tests::players_drawn_together_are_kept_past_the_budget`.

**2026-10-09 · m4-effects-media-w2: the live thumbnail proof checks the colour.** `TestWindow::open_filled` paints the test window's buffer with one premultiplied ARGB8888 colour (`open` stays transparent, so other tests are unchanged). The matrix test waits until a frame's centre pixel is within 3 of that colour, read as BGRA, rather than asserting on the first frame. A compositor may capture the toplevel before its first buffer shows. Passed on sway 1.12 and labwc 0.20.2; niri 26.04 offers no toplevel capture, and Hyprland is skipped on the laptop.

## m4-lock-w2

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: what shows the built-in password field.** design.md says "if anything faults, a built-in password field appears" without listing faults. The binary (`run/lock.rs`) shows render's fallback, while a lock is asked for or held, on the first of: logic ended or panicked; a heartbeat unanswered for 3 s (a beat goes 1 s after the last answer, and only while locked, so an unlocked session gains no wakeups); SIGINT or SIGTERM (logic is told to stop and the run ends after the unlock: quitting would leave a lock nobody can release); no committed frame of the lock within 1 s (architecture.md's first-frame deadline); a session locked with no `lock` open (none compiled, or the restart below); the lock's node gone; a runtime fault inside the lock's subtree (its component is frozen, so its field may be dead); the text worker gone; `auth` failing to check a password (`Verdict::Failed`: no helper, a crash, a hang past its timeout, garbage), as opposed to refusing one, which is the lock's own business; and `finished` after `locked`. Once shown the fallback stays until the unlock: going back to config content that just faulted would add a state, not remove one.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: the fallback checks passwords with a client of its own.** A fault in `auth` (its store, its helper, its test environment) must not take the fallback with it, so the fallback runs its own `strand_auth::Client` (the default helper, no test hooks) on a thread of its own, and its token goes through the same channel into `State::unlock` as `auth`'s. Both token paths are wired before `State::enable_session_lock`, in the same function (`Guard::wire`), so no build can take a lock it cannot release. `AuthConfig` gains `failed` (the binary's sink for a check that could not be made) and `client_hook` (how the faults build hands `STRAND_FAULT` to `auth`'s helper only).

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: a strand killed while locked locks again when it starts.** A process that dies while the compositor keeps the session locked (kill -9, an allocation failure, which aborts) leaves the user facing sway's red abandoned-lock screen with no way in. While the compositor says the session is locked the binary keeps a marker, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/strand-<WAYLAND_DISPLAY>.locked`, removed only after an unlock; a strand that starts and finds it locks at once and shows the fallback. A marker left from an old compositor session with the same display name locks a fresh session once: that fails closed, and the user's password clears it.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: the fallback draws without vello, fonts or the text worker.** It is a signed-distance rounded field and dots painted straight into the lock surface's buffer (`strand_render::lock_fallback`), in fixed colours (`#11111b` background, `#1e1e2e` field, `#3b202c` refused), 24 dots at most however long the password; while it shows, the lock's solid outputs take its background colour. Theme tokens were not used: the fallback exists for when the shell's machinery cannot be trusted, and the theme is part of it.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: lock backgrounds are single-pixel buffers, from S-surface's scrim code.** The solid outputs use `crate::solid::solid_buffer` (a `wp_single_pixel_buffer_v1` buffer when the compositor has it, else S-surface's 1×1 shm) scaled by the viewporter, so a lock and a scrim share one code path; `State::lock_solid_is_single_pixel` lets the VM test prove which one sway got. The lock's own buffer object and dispatch are gone.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: one `faults` feature on strand, unified with strand-auth's.** `strand/faults` turns on `strand-auth/faults` (the helper's `auth_crash`, `auth_hang`, `auth_garbage` and `Client::with_test_env`) and the binary's own `STRAND_FAULT` points: `logic_panic`, `logic_hang`, `text_panic`, `lock_no_frame`, `auth_missing` (no helper), and a 3 s `auth` timeout under `auth_hang`. Without the feature each point is an empty inline function and the names are absent from the binary; budgets.rs's `the_binary_holds_no_fault_code` checks the bytes (and the matrix's `the_binary_under_test_holds_the_fault_points` the converse). OOM is played as SIGABRT plus a restart: an allocation failure in Rust aborts, and an address-space limit low enough to fail inside the lock reliably would fail somewhere else first.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: `finished` after `locked` is played in the VM by a Wayland proxy.** sway 1.9 never sends `finished` to a lock it granted, and wave 1 proved the client's answer only against a fake compositor. tests/lock/proxy.rs sits between strand and the VM's sway, forwards every byte and descriptor, learns the lock's object id from the client's requests and, when the test says so, adds one `ext_session_lock_v1.finished` after `locked`. strand's `unlock_and_destroy` and new lock then reach the real sway, which unlocks and locks again, as a compositor that ended the lock would; the test does not assert the session locked in that gap, only that the new lock shows the fallback and takes the right password only.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: the lock idiom submits on Return through `on key`.** auth.schema's example said `input { type: password; on activate { auth.submit(secret) } }`, but the `Router` turns Return into `activate` only for a list's selected row (an input with `nav:`); a plain input gets the Return as `on key`. The VM showed the documented lock never submitting. Changing the Router is S-render's call, so the schema now documents the form that works, `on key(k) { if k.name == "Return" { auth.submit(secret); secret = "" } }`, and Return activating a plain input is left as an open question for the integrator (it would add no concept, only make `activate` mean the same on an input as on a row).

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: wave 1's edits to lock-owned files by other streams stand.** The only one is the M4 wave 1 surface merge giving the lock content `Surface` `blur: None, blur_sent: Some(Vec::new())`, as every layer and popup surface got; a lock surface never sets a blur region and commit.rs's and effect.rs's bare commits skip `Role::Lock`, so nothing changed for the lock.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: `pam_faillock` is proved with a stack of the scenario's own.** The image's `/etc/pam.d/strand` is Ubuntu's plain stack, without `pam_faillock`, and the plan's tier C names it. `faillock.sh` swaps in `deny=3` around `pam_unix`, its tally in a directory the test user owns (the helper runs as that user, not setuid, so the default `/var/run/faillock` is not writable to it), and puts the image's stack back. The test proves the stack works first (the right password unlocks), then that after three wrong passwords the right one is refused by the same helper and by a new one, as `Denied`: a lockout is the stack owner's decision, so it must not show the fallback as a fault would.
