**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: the lock's content is the surface on the lock's node, remembered for the lock session.** A review found that `LockScreen` took a surface as the lock's content only when render's tree called its node a `lock`, while strand-surface keeps the old node after the spec goes during a lock (`spec_gone`) and makes the content again with it when its output goes or focus moves. The new surface then showed nothing and its keys went to the `Router`. The host now remembers the node the content was attached with until the unlock. The review's SIGTERM path does not reach this: logic's unmount at its end sends render no diff, so the node stays in the tree (`sigterm_then_the_contents_output_unplugged_keeps_the_fallback` passes with or without the fix). So the VM plays the node going with a new fault point, `lock_unmount`, which applies the `Remove` logic would send. `lock_unmounted_then_the_contents_output_unplugged_keeps_the_fallback` fails without the fix: the remaining output stays black.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: "the lock's colour" is the `lock` node's `bg`.** architecture.md gives the other outputs "a single-pixel background in the lock's colour" but no definition, and the binary only ever set the fallback's colour and never reset it. While the config's lock shows, the main loop sets the solids to the `lock` node's `bg`, with tokens resolved through the global table and the lock's own `set`. A gradient gives its first stop, and with no `bg` the solids are black. They follow the lock's `when`s (`auth.failed`). Sampling the painted surface was the alternative; it would read whatever the corner happens to draw, and it costs a read on each frame.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: reasons to show the fallback live only while a lock is asked for or held.** An `auth` check that fails while unlocked had made the next healthy lock show the fallback at once. Every main-loop turn with no lock now drops a pending reason. The restart marker follows the same rule: it is removed once no lock is asked for or held, not only after an unlock. A refused lock left the marker behind, and every later start then locked the session. A strand killed with no lock held leaves nothing locked to come back to. This replaces "Only an unlock removes it" in the earlier paragraph.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: the 1 s first-frame deadline is gated with numbers, and a miss is never a functional failure.** strand logs each lock's first frame, measured from the deadline's own start. `a_healthy_lock_draws_its_first_frame_in_time` takes three lock sessions through whichever field shows, then raises `GATE_MISS` at its end if any first frame reached 1 s or the fallback showed for one. `Vm::content()` stops with `GATE_MISS` instead of a plain assertion failure when the fallback took over for a missed first frame, so in the other tests a slow first frame is classed as a timing miss. The VM measured about 610 to 650 ms in a debug build. Most of that is render holding a surface's first frame up to `FIRST_FRAME_TEXT_WAIT` (500 ms) for text, which leaves the deadline little margin; see the open issues.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: password redaction covers current values, by substring, in fault messages.** Logic keeps the current value of each `type: password` input, read from its own diffs and from the `Router`'s writes, as a zeroizing `Password`. It replaces each value with `<redacted>` in the runtime fault messages it logs and sends as watch `fault` events, and in the debug line for a failed write. Older values are not kept: the idiom empties the field on submit, and keeping history would mean more copies of passwords. A one-character password garbles messages that contain that character; that fails safe. An input removed as part of a subtree, not by its own `Remove`, keeps its entry until its slot is reused. That is a few bytes, and in the idiom usually an empty value. The overlay paints no fault text, so it needs no redaction.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: CI lints the faults-only targets and runs the lock VM for every lock file.** The lock-vm paths filter gains run/mod.rs, run/shell.rs, run/logic.rs, strand's Cargo.toml, tests/lock/** and strand-surface's solid.rs and manager/scrim.rs. The lint jobs in ci.yml and scripts/container/ci.sh gain `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features`, which is clean. These are integrator-owned files, so each change is the smallest that does the job.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: strand-surface names the lock's content; the host no longer infers it.** A second review found that remembering the content's node per lock session (the paragraph above) still missed one case: a lock asked for while no output exists, its `lock` gone from render's tree before an output returns (a reload while pending; reloads are not deferred before `Locked`). strand-surface then makes the content with the old node, which render does not know and this lock session never attached, so `LockScreen` took no surface as the content: the first-frame deadline showed the fallback, but nothing painted it and its keys went to the `Router`. `Guard::check` now sets the content each main-loop turn from `State::lock_content()`, pairing it with the node the host saw attached on that surface (the fallback node when none was seen, which shows the fallback as "locked with no `lock` open"). `attached` still takes a surface early when render's tree calls its node a `lock`, so nothing waits a turn in the common case; the remembered node is gone. The VM plays the case with a new fault point, `lock_unmount_unseen`; `lock_unmounted_with_no_output_then_an_output_keeps_the_fallback` and the earlier unplug test both fail without the change (the returning output stays black).

**2026-10-09 · m4-lock-w2: while a password input is mounted, a fault's error that can carry values is redacted whole.** A review found that the substring search above misses a password a config transforms (`secret.upper()`, a slice, an escaped quote) or copies to another state before emptying the field, and those reach the log and watch `fault` events. Finding the faulting expression's reads of the password's state would need the compiler's dependency data and still miss a copy. So while any `type: password` input is mounted, even an emptied one, every runtime fault whose error can carry values (`Error::Failed`, a keyed-collection error) logs and streams as `<what>: <redacted>`. `what` names a prop, handler, state or timer, never a value, and the watch event keeps its `at` location and `frozen`, so the fault can still be found. Errors made only of node ids and names (disposed, cycle, write-in-derived, reentrant, cancelled) keep their text. With no password input mounted, current values are still replaced by substring. In the lock idiom the cost is fault text hidden only while the lock is up. A password copied into state that outlives the input's unmount is the config's own data, and the binary does not track it. For the mounted case this replaces "by substring" in the earlier redaction paragraph.

## m4-lists-w2

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: "Escape did not close the calendar" was the test's keyboard joining the seat too late; the fix is a keyboard there before strand starts.** The intermittent failure of `acceptance.rs::the_bar_and_its_calendar_on_two_outputs` (GitHub run 37983590317 and others) is test-side, and confirmed rather than guessed: the test made its virtual keyboard only after the calendar had opened and pressed Escape 200 ms later. The headless seat has no keyboard until then, so strand learns of one from a `wl_seat.capabilities` event and asks for its `wl_keyboard` only when its main loop next reads the socket; a key sway receives before that request reaches no client and is lost. With the 200 ms sleep removed the test failed five times out of five, and a `WAYLAND_DEBUG` trace of strand showed `capabilities (3)`, `get_keyboard`, `keymap`, `enter` on the bar's layer surface, and no `key` at all; on a loaded runner the 200 ms was sometimes not enough. Nothing in the product can take a key sent before it bound the keyboard, so the product is unchanged. The `Desk` now makes its virtual keyboard after sway is up and before strand connects: strand's own `wl_seat` bind then reports the keyboard and strand requests it while dispatching that first event, ahead of every surface request on the same connection, so by the time `Desk::start_with` has seen a bar painted, sway delivers keys to strand. That is an ordering guarantee rather than a longer sleep, so the test presses Escape with no sleep at all and still asserts exactly what it did (the calendar's pixels gone within 10 s of one Escape). The launcher test uses the same keyboard (it made its own after the desk started, the same latent race). Twenty runs of the test in the container passed, and ten more with six busy-loop processes competing for the CPU.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: the grim proof of smooth 2,000-row scrolling is row continuity between settled shots.** m4-plan names "grim refs once settled" for `demo.rs::the_design_launcher_scrolls_2000_apps`; wave 1 checked the settled shots structurally and left the exit box open. A blessed PNG of one scrolled position would prove one frame; it would say nothing about the rows on either side of it, and a stale or skipped window could still match. The test now reads continuity from grim's pixels instead: after the fast wheel it scrolls sixteen bursts of 16 notches (240 px, exactly five 48 px rows), waits for each to settle with the pointer moved off the list (no row hovered, the cursor outside the compared pixels), and asserts that the list's clip in each screenshot equals the previous screenshot moved up by exactly 240 px wherever the two overlap (at most 0.2% of pixels off by more than 24 per channel; in practice none), that a shift of one more row does not match (so the comparison can tell neighbouring rows apart: their names, icons and comments differ), that eight or more rows fill the list, and that render's `top=` advances by exactly five per burst. The list's clip is found from the shots (the rows that changed between the top and the scrolled shot), and its sides stop 24 px short of the box's rounded corners. Eighty rows pass through the view this way, several of logic's windows, so a row missing, doubled, reordered or drawn at the wrong offset after a window move fails the test. Settling between bursts keeps every compared offset on a whole pixel (in flight a spring sits between pixels and the glyphs' antialiasing differs), and frames in flight stay covered by the per-frame `gaps=` check. With this the exit box is ticked; its other evidence is unchanged.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: the launcher scroll test waits for the box's full width, not only two alike shots.** Under CPU load (six busy loops beside the container) the test failed two runs in eight at "the launcher's box kept its place and size", before any of the new checks: the first settled shot had caught the box at about 0.975 of its size. The launcher's `enter` pose (`scale: 0.96`) is played by the compositor through pose-only commits, which paint no frame, and with strand's main thread starved two shots 150 ms apart could show the pose paused at the same scale, which the structural check (box and row bands alike) took for settled. Settled now also requires the box to measure its declared 600 px at its middle row, the observable end of the pose; ten runs under the same load and ten without passed. The continuity bursts use their own stricter wait (no frame painted between two shots and the list's pixels identical), because a spring's last fraction of a pixel leaves the row bands alike but changes the glyphs' antialiasing (one run in five failed the exact comparison with the structural wait alone).

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: drag and drop matches types by name, and the source's value stays on the logic thread.** architecture.md sends `Prop::Drag` to render as "a `Keyword` naming the type of the dragged value" and `Prop::Accepts` as the type names an element's `on drop` takes. The compiler keeps no expression types past checking, so the name is taken from the value itself when the `drag:` binding runs (a record by its type, an enum by its enum, `text`, `int`, `[Pin]` from a list's first item) and from each `on drop` handler's first parameter as declared (`p: Pin` gives `Pin`, `d: Drop` gives `Drop`, an untyped parameter `any`); both are printed by the checker's own type display, so an alias (`AppId`) is its target (`text`), `path` reads as `text` (they convert both ways), and `T?` as `T`. The value itself never crosses to render: the binding records it per source node (`Ctx::drags`, removed with the node's scope or when no source holds) and `Instance::drag_value` hands it to the drop. An element may have one `on drop` per type (design.md's dock takes `Pin`; the same element can take a `Drop` from a file manager): every handler is registered, and each runs only for a value of its own type, so a `Pin` never reaches a `d: Drop` body. A drop that reorders keyed data (`pins.move(p.app, at)`) is a keyed move, so the row keeps its node and render's FLIP springs it ("reordering springs by key"), with no new node and no enter pose (`instantiate.rs::drag_sources_and_drop_targets_deliver_typed_values`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: the Router owns the drag gesture, and the dragged row is a held paint offset.** design.md gives `drag:` and `on drop` but not the gesture, so it follows the slider's: a press on a `drag:` source is a press until the pointer has moved 6 px (`DRAG_THRESHOLD`; a wobble still clicks), then a drag that ends the press's selection, and its release clicks nothing. The source is drawn at the pointer through the Animator, as a held offset (`Animator::lift`) that the flatten pass paints after its siblings; its box keeps its place, so nothing relayouts while it moves, and letting go turns the held offset into the same FLIP glide a keyed move uses. That is what makes "reordering springs by key" one motion: logic answers `on drop(p, at)` by moving the keyed row in the same turn, and the row springs from where it was let go into its new slot, never from its old one. The target is the innermost node under the pointer (the source itself left out, `Renderer::hit_under`, since it is drawn there) whose `on drop` takes the carried type; `at` is the insertion index among its live children with the source excluded, along the axis the children run, and offset by a windowed `list`'s `row_first`, so it is a global row index logic can use directly. Escape cancels a drag (and does nothing else); with no target the source springs back with no drop. Other programs' drags (`DragEnter` with kinds) only reach a target whose `on drop` takes `Drop`, which is also the only case in which the surface manager accepts the offer (`input.rs::a_drag_past_six_pixels_drops_at_a_global_index`, `escape_cancels_a_drag`, `other_programs_drops_reach_the_target_that_takes_drop`, `a_drag_carried_to_another_surface_drops_there`; `drag.rs`, with the `drag_lift` reference).

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: a drop's arguments are made on the logic thread, and a gone source delivers nothing.** Render sends `NodeEvent::Drop { payload, at }` with the source as a node, because the value is logic's (`Instance::drag_value`); `run/lists.rs::drop_args` turns it into `on drop`'s arguments when the event arrives. If the source unmounted between the release and the event (logic removed it in the same turn), there is no value to hand over and the drop is dropped with a debug line rather than delivered as null, which no typed `p: Pin` could take. Another program's drop becomes builtin.schema's `Drop` record with only the fields its `kind` names filled; `app` is the installed `App` from `apps.all` whose id the drag named, and null when no such app is installed or no `apps` service runs, so a `.desktop` file from an unknown location still arrives as its files (`run::lists::tests::drops_deliver_the_source_value_or_a_drop_record`, `demo::host::tests::drops_are_forwarded_to_logic`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: `wl_data_device` carries only what one surface cannot.** Inside a surface the pointer grab of the press keeps motion coming to the origin, so the Router's drag needs no compositor; the manager starts a `wl_data_device` drag only when the held pointer leaves the surface a drag is in flight on (`SurfaceHost::drag_source`), with the press serial. That keeps the common drag (a reorder in one list) free of protocol round trips and testable offline, and still lets a pin go from a panel to the bar. The source offers one MIME type naming this process and manager, so it is recognised on enter without reading anything (the node travels by identity; another program asking for it gets nothing), and two Strand processes do not mistake each other's drags. Because the pointer leaves the origin surface when the compositor takes over, the source springs back to its box there and no icon follows the pointer: rendering the source into a drag-icon surface would add a second render target per drag for a cosmetic gain, so it is left for later. The compositor never sends the origin the real release of a drag it carries, so when our source is cancelled or finished the manager makes up a left release far outside the origin, which ends the Router's drag with nothing dropped. Other programs' offers are accepted (copy only, never move: a dropped file is not taken away from its file manager) exactly while the Router has a target under the pointer (`SurfaceHost::drop_accepted`), so their cursor shows whether letting go would do anything; files are preferred over text, a `text/uri-list` of only `.desktop` entries is an app (its file name the desktop entry id), and the data is read through calloop, never blocking the main thread, up to 4 MiB. `src/dnd.rs` is included by `manager/mod.rs` as `manager::dnd` so it reaches `State` like the manager's other parts while staying a file of its own (`crates/strand-surface/tests/dnd.rs`).

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: an unread drop cancels its sender, and a dropped offer is always destroyed.** Review found that an offer whose bytes could not be read (no pipe, a read error, more than 4 MiB) was left alive and the Router kept a stale offer, and that a sender that never closed its pipe held a reader for the life of the process. sctk leaves a dropped offer for the client to destroy, so every drop now ends in `end_drop`: read, the offer is finished then destroyed and the host gets `DragDrop`; not read, it is destroyed unfinished and the host gets `DragLeave`. Destroying without `finish` is what the compositor reports to the sender as `cancelled`, which is the truth (a `finish` would tell a sender offering `move` to delete what we never got), so the over-limit case no longer finishes either. Reading gives up after 5 s (`DROP_READ_TIMEOUT`): long enough for any local sender, short enough that a hung one costs nothing lasting. A drop of an offer nobody accepted (wlroots never sends one) ends the same way.

**2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: an `on drop` takes what a call with its parameter would.** Review found that an empty list dragged from a `[Pin]` binding went to render as `[any]` and never met `on drop(p: [Pin], …)`, and that an `int` never met a `float` parameter. The review's proposed fix, the binding's static type from `SourceValue::Chunk`, does not exist: that `Ty` is the prop's schema type, `any` for `drag:`, and the expression's type is dropped in `lower` (another stream's file). The fix keeps the dragged name runtime-derived and widens the targets instead: delivery matches with the checker's `assignable` (an empty list's items are `any`, which fits any list; `int` fits `float`, `length`, `angle`), and `Prop::Accepts` lists every name that fits, so render's name match agrees (`[Pin]` also accepts `[any]`; `float` also `int` and `percent`). **2026-10-09 · m4-lists-w2: only a `list` or a row of `drag:` items holds drop rows.** `drop_index` counted a drop among a target's own children whenever it had any, so a per-item `on drop` on a dock item holding an icon and a label got the pointer's place within its own content (0 or 1) instead of its place in the dock. ## m4-surface-w2

**2026-10-09 · m4-surface-w2: Hyprland's "half-blurred" stripes were the test pattern aliasing with its blur kernel; the layer rule blurs fully.** m4-integration-w1 saw the glass over `strand-Dash` show 2 px black and white stripes at half their contrast (178/229 against 153/255 unblurred) and relaxed the bound to < 230. Read in Hyprland 0.56.2's source (`OpenGL.cpp::blurFramebufferWithDamage`, `blur1.glsl`, `blur2.glsl`), the blur is a dual Kawase of `decoration:blur:size` 8 and `passes` 1 (defaults, which the matrix's config keeps; a layer rule has no size of its own, so `blur: 24` never reaches it): the down pass takes a bilinear centre tap at a 2 px pair's seam plus four diagonal taps 8 source pixels away, and the up pass taps 2 and 4 half-resolution pixels away. With 2 px columns (a 4 px period) every tap lands on the same phase of the stripes, so the down pass blurs nothing and only the up pass's bilinear centre mixes neighbours, 3:1, which leaves exactly a quarter and three quarters of white behind the glass: the observed 64 and 191 under the 40 % the glass lets through. A model of the two passes in the scratchpad reproduces 0.25/0.75 for 2 px stripes and gives 3 px stripes (a 6 px period, not a divisor of the offsets) under 4 % of their contrast, 5 px 12 %, noise 28 %. So ignore_alpha (0.6 glass over 0.5), the blur region (none is sent for this surface; the rule blurs the whole surface), xray and new_optimizations (the background layer is in the cached blur, which is what we want blurred) are not involved, and nothing in `strand compositor-rules` changes. The test now paints 3 px stripes and asks for a contrast under 60 of the unblurred 306 (about 12 expected after Hyprland's contrast 0.89 and noise), which a rule that does nothing or blurs by half cannot meet. A user's real wallpaper has no 4 px period, so they never saw the alias.

**2026-10-09 · m4-surface-w2: what a surface delegates of its pose, and in whose terms.** design.md: "Surface-level fades and scales cost no repaint: opacity via `wp_alpha_modifier_v1`, scale via viewporter, small moves via layer-shell margins". Compositors arrange a layer surface by the size it asked for and draw the surface from that box's top-left corner (wlroots' `wlr_scene_layer_surface_v1_configure`, smithay's layer map and Hyprland all take the requested size), so a smaller viewport destination shrinks towards the top-left whatever the anchor, and a margin moves a surface only from an edge it is anchored to (a centred axis ignores margins; a stretched one would change size). So `SurfacePose` is in the surface's own terms (scale keeps the top-left corner, the offset moves it; strand-scene's doc said "about the anchored side", which no compositor does) and render (`strand_render::pose`, over the root's resolved props, so it reads the same `anchor`/`attach` placement does) delegates only what lands exactly: opacity on every surface but a `lock`; x or y on a `panel` or `osd` anchored on one side of that axis; scale only when both axes are, with the move that keeps the box's centre (render scales about it) folded into the offset. A `bar`'s margin counts into its exclusive zone, so a bar delegates only opacity (moving it would reflow the windows every frame); a `popup` only opacity (the positioner places it; the plan's "popup x/y always repaint", and its scale for the same reason). The rest of a pose is painted as before, which composes with the delegated part since opacity, translation and a centre-keeping scale commute. A root's static `opacity`, `x`, `y` or `scale` is delegated too, not only a motion: the result is the same picture, and deciding by "is it moving" would switch between two paths mid-animation for nothing. The input region stays the box in surface coordinates, so during a delegated scale the pointer is hit-tested against the unscaled box for the pose's few frames. The pose comes from the frame the manager just painted (`Flattened::pose`), so a frame that drew nothing still carries the springs' new values to a bare commit; `set_compositor_poses` follows `CompositorCaps::delegates_poses` (alpha modifier and viewporter) in the binary's host. Proof: `strand-render/tests/surface_poses.rs` (offline: the content paints once, at rest, PNG `surface_pose_at_rest`; later frames have no damage while the pose rises; a centred panel delegates only its fade; off, everything repaints), `strand-surface/tests/fake.rs::poses_go_to_the_compositor_without_buffers` and `::a_pose_offset_moves_the_margins_and_survives_a_reconfigure` (the multiplier, destination and margins per commit, one buffer), and on real compositors `compositor_matrix.rs::surfaces_meet_the_live_compositor` (a panel held at half opacity and half size about its centre shows white at half over the wallpaper inside the half-size box and the wallpaper around it), which runs only on the matrix (sway 1.9 has no alpha modifier).

**2026-10-09 · m4-surface-w2: while the GPU presents a surface, its pose is painted; the GPU branch wires it.** architecture.md ("Surface hand-off") paints poses into GPU frames. `strand-surface`'s `gpu_handoff.rs` and render's `Renderer::backend` are S-gpu's and not on this branch, so this stream gives them the two seams: `State::clear_pose(surface)` sets the identity pose as pending state without committing (the next present commits it), for `hand_off` to call; and render's delegation, which needs one more condition at merge, `self.backend(surface) != Backend::GpuPresent` in `Renderer::delegated_pose` and in the flatten hook (`extras.compositor_poses` per surface), so the GPU frames carry the pose. Listed for the integrator.

**2026-10-09 · m4-surface-w2: submenus open to the side their `anchor:` names; the tray's click point is the pressed node's bottom-left corner on its output.** design.md says only that popups "are anchored xdg\_popups that nest, which is how tray menus work". A menu's submenu opens beside its row, not under it, so a popup whose parent is a popup now opens to the side: right by default, left for `anchor: left` (or a left corner), above for `anchor: top` and below for `anchor: bottom`, with the compositor flipping it in x when it does not fit (`FlipX`, sliding in y). Beside its row it is level with the row's top and grows down (`Anchor::TopRight` with `Gravity::BottomRight`, mirrored for left; `PopupConfig::aligned`), at the usual gap (6, or the margin on the side it opens towards). This reuses `anchor:`, which a popup accepted and ignored, instead of adding a prop. `attach:` still names the touching side and centres the popup, and a popup in a bar or panel ignores `anchor:` as before. The wave-1 sway test's nested menu now opens to the right, and its configure proves it (`sway.rs::popups_nest_under_their_anchors_and_close_on_click_away`: origin (86, 62), then (84, 62) to the left after a reposition; `placement::tests::submenus_open_to_the_side_their_anchor_names`). For the tray, `Activate`, `SecondaryActivate` and `ContextMenu` took (0, 0) (m3's "Click positions are not passed yet"). That paragraph promised optional `x`/`y` on the schema's actions, but a shell author has no coordinates to pass, so the reading that removes a concept wins: the host records the point on every press (`strand_services::tray::set_click_point`, a process-wide atomic the actions read when they run) and the actions keep their signatures. The point is the bottom-left corner of the innermost node pressed (the icon), not the pointer: an app placing a menu of its own (Qt on XWayland, an X11 tray proxy) puts the menu's top-left corner there, and its toolkit flips the menu up from a bottom bar. The plan's reading is followed: the corner is in output-logical coordinates, not global layout coordinates. Wayland clients cannot place by them anyway, and the SNI spec's "screen coordinates" are the output's for a one-output session. To give the host that corner, the surface manager reports where each surface lies on its output through a new no-op-default hook, `SurfaceHost::surface_placed`. A layer surface's position is derived as compositors arrange one of its size over the whole output, because exclusive zones of other clients are not known, so a panel beside a bar is off by the bar's zone. A popup's position comes from its configure. Proof: `strand-services/tests/tray.rs::the_tray_is_the_watcher_when_there_is_none` (the mock app records `Activate at 1830,36` and `SecondaryActivate at -4,1052`), `strand/src/demo/host.rs::a_press_sets_the_tray_click_point`, and the sway test's origins.

**2026-10-09 · m4-surface-w2: a tray menu is a recursive component over the DBusMenu model, a `list` takes `focus: true`, and a late keyboard leave no longer closes a regrabbed popup.** The tray menu needs no new syntax. The fixture (`crates/strand/tests/fixtures/tray_menu.strand`) is design.md's tray loop with a component per icon: `state open` bound `open: <-> open` on the menu's popup, so Escape and click-away close it. `on change item.menu.opened { open = item.menu.opened }` opens it after `item.menu.open()` (and after `activate()` on a menu-only item) and closes it when an entry is chosen, and `on hide { item.menu.close() }` tells the app. A recursive `Menu` component lists `item.menu.items`, and each row holds its submenu's popup (`open: <-> sub`, `on show { e.open() }`, `Menu e.children`). The compiler mounts a recursive component lazily and a closed popup's content is unmounted, so depth costs nothing until opened. A row resets `sub` when the menu closes, so a reopened menu shows no stale submenu. Two gaps showed. First, the Router walks a focused `list` with the keys (S-lists' hooks: Down/Up select, Right opens the selected row's submenu, Left closes a nested one, Return activates), but the schema let only `input` take `focus: true`, so a menu with no text field could not get the keys. `focus: bool` is now a prop of `list` too, which reuses the prop instead of adding a concept (strand-compiler's `builtin.schema`, one line, for that stream to review). Second, a menu reopened after an entry was chosen closed at once. When the first menu closed, the bar gave its grab's `exclusive` back for `none`, and sway sent the matching `wl_keyboard.leave` only with its next keyboard change, the enter of the new grab, after the new popup had taken the keys. That leave reached the new popup, and focus loss closed it. The manager now remembers a layer surface that released a grab while it had focus (`State::releasing`). A leave that comes for it while a new grab holds the keyboard does not reach the grabbing popup, and the enter that follows hands the keys back. Proof: `tray_menu.rs::tray_menus_nest_walk_and_choose` (the reopened menu stays and Escape closes it).

**2026-10-09 · m4-surface-w2: a leave that may be the late one is held to the end of its dispatch, not dropped.** Review found that `State::releasing` outlived its purpose on a compositor that keeps a layer surface focused when it gives `exclusive` back and owes no leave: the next grab came with no leave or enter, and the next real focus loss (a lock, another exclusive surface) was then taken for the late leave, so the grabbing popup was never told and its `open` stayed true. A leave cannot be told stale from real when it arrives; what tells them apart is whether an enter for the same surface follows it, and sway sends both in one flush. So a leave that comes for a `releasing` surface while a new grab holds the keyboard is now held (`State::held_leave`) until the dispatch that brought it ends (a calloop idle). An enter for that surface in between makes it stale, and the popup keeps the keys. Without one, the popup gets its `KeyboardLeave` then. `releasing` is also dropped when its surface is destroyed. The fake compositor gained a seat keyboard whose focus tests move (`Cmd::KeyboardEnter`, `KeyboardLeave`, `Key`) and an `xdg_wm_base` for popups, so the case no real compositor in CI shows is tested: `fake.rs::a_grabbing_popup_loses_the_keyboard_after_an_earlier_release` covers both orders.

**2026-10-09 · m4-surface-w2: under a delegated scale the manager maps regions, input and popup anchors through the pose.** Review found that a delegated scale left everything in surface-local coordinates at their at-rest values. With a viewport destination of s × size, a surface's local coordinates are the destination's (wlroots and smithay size the surface by it), so the pointer arrives in them and the compositor reads the opaque, input and blur regions in them. A panel at `scale: 0.9` therefore claimed a box about 10 % too large as opaque (over its own rounded corners and shadow, which a culling compositor then leaves undrawn), took clicks on a box past its drawn one, and was hit-tested at the wrong node. The earlier paragraph's "for the pose's few frames" was wrong: a root's static `scale` is delegated for good. The fix is in the manager, which owns the protocol coordinates. Render keeps reporting regions of the content at rest, and the manager maps them by the destination over the logical size (`Surface::pose_factor`). The opaque region is rounded inwards, so it never claims a pixel the content does not cover. The input and blur regions are rounded to the nearest pixel, so the bands down a rounded corner stay edge to edge, at most half a pixel past the shape. A popup's anchor rect is mapped by its parent's factor when it is positioned. Pointer and drag positions are divided back before the host sees them (`State::send_input`). A pose's new scale sends the input region with its commit, and a frame that drew nothing now also carries a blur region that moved. Two alternatives were rejected. Requiring scale 1 for the opaque region drops the claim for good on a static scale and leaves input and blur wrong. Delegating scale only while it moves needs render to know whether a spring is moving, and switches paths at the settle; the earlier paragraph rejected that, and mapping makes it unnecessary. A static scale above 1 stays delegated. Painted, a root larger than its surface is cut off at the surface's edge (the buffer is the box plus its overhang). The compositor shows all of it, softened by the upscale. The author asked for that size, and only this path shows it whole. A popup open while its parent's scale animates keeps the place it was given until it is repositioned; the popup itself is a surface of its own and is not scaled. **2026-10-10 · m4-integration-w2: promotion's idle rule waits for the attach and for a presented frame, and GPU replies wake render.** The full local suite failed `gpu_idle.rs::gpu_is_released_when_idle` in 2 of 4 runs: "Glow went back to the CPU while its shader animated". The debug log showed `Glow` released while the device was still starting. The idle rule demotes a promoted surface that has not painted for 500 ms. Its clock was the last CPU frame before the device start, and the start (naga and llvmpipe compiling for hundreds of ms under load) stalled the loop past that window, so the surface was demoted before its first GPU frame, then promoted again. Three changes in render and the run loop (gpu stream code, fixed here because the merged load exposed it): (1) the idle rule applies only to a surface the GPU draws (`Surf::idles`: attached, no presented frame in flight), and `gpu_wake` leaves the others out so the loop does not spin on a past wake; (2) the attach (`set_backend` to a GPU backend) and each presented frame's `Presented` restart the idle window (`Promotion::shown`); (3) `run::gpu` runs render's update and asks for frames after any reply other than `Presented`. The third surfaced once (1) and (2) kept the renderer's timer from firing every 500 ms: `Ref`'s still shader pass came back, its node was marked dirty, and nothing asked for the CPU surface's frame, because the GPU ping's handler did nothing and the repaint had depended on that incidental timer. ## m4-effects-finish

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: Return activates a plain `input`.** m4-lock-w2 found that the documented lock (`input { type: password; on activate { auth.submit(secret) } }`, as `grammar_examples.strand` also writes it) never submitted, because the `Router` turned Return into `activate` only for a `nav:` list's selected row, and left Return activating a plain input to the integrator. It adds no concept, only makes `activate` mean on an input what it means on a row ("it was chosen"), so the `Router` now sends `activate` to a focused `input` that has no `nav:` list when Return or KP_Enter is pressed, after `on key` hears the key, and the key edits no text. An input with `nav:` still activates its list's row. `grammar_examples.strand` is now right as written, auth.schema's example goes back to `on activate { auth.submit(secret); secret = "" }`, and builtin.schema's `on activate` says so; the `on key` form keeps working (`crates/strand-render/tests/input.rs::return_activates_a_plain_input`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: a node's first frame starts at its props' values.** `Renderer::apply` records every animatable prop logic sets on a shown surface as a touch with the value it replaced, so that the change springs from there; the props of the diff that creates a node replaced nothing (`None`), and the node's first frame sprang each of them from its default (a red box faded in from transparent, an `x: 4` slid in from 0), on top of or instead of its enter pose. design.md says `enter {}` is where a node animates in from, so only the pose's props move: the Animator now ignores a node's touches on the frame it enters (writes made before it was ever drawn have no value on screen to start from) and springs only its enter pose. `effects_stagger.png` is re-blessed: its boxes now fade in by their pose's opacity alone instead of also springing their colour from transparent (`crates/strand-render/tests/motion.rs::a_created_node_starts_at_its_values`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: a shared morph a preview sees start begins on the painted frame.** `Renderer::update` flattens a dirty surface at its last painted frame's time before the next paint (the preview), and the shared-element morph started there: its starting delta was the remembered box minus the new node's box with its ancestors' paint offsets as they were a frame earlier, and that one-frame-old offset stayed in the whole morph (inside a parent whose `x` springs, the node started a few pixels off the box it morphs from). Shapes and rolls already leave their start to the painted frame; the morph now does the same: a preview marks the node pending (it plays no enter pose, and `busy` asks the paint for a fresh flatten), and the painted frame starts the morph from the boxes and offsets of its own time. A pending node that frame did not draw shows at rest, as an unseen enter pose does (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::a_preview_leaves_a_shared_morph_to_the_painted_frame`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: `jelly` stretches a dragged node along its motion, by its own speed, on a wobbling spring.** design.md gives "Jelly and squash while dragging (vector content) | `jelly: 0.4` | Trivial" and nothing more. A node with `jelly: a` that a drag holds (its lift), or that springs back from one (the glide home), is drawn stretched by `1 + s` along the way it moves and squashed by `1 / (1 + s)` across it, so its area is kept, about its centre and as a transform of its subtree, so vector content stays sharp and costs nothing. `s` is `a` times its speed over 1,500 px/s, at most `a` (`jelly` itself is clamped to 0..1). The speed is the node's drawn offset between painted frames, smoothed, rather than the `Router`'s pointer velocity (architecture.md lists `DragView::velocity` for jelly): render does not own the `Router`, the drawn offset also covers the glide home, which the pointer does not, and frames at fixed timestamps then give the same jelly every run. The deformation springs (the `jelly` entry's `~`, else `spring(300, 0.35)`, underdamped so it wobbles) as a vector holding its amount at twice its axis's angle: motion either way stretches the same axis, and the spring overshooting through zero is a squash along it, so a sudden stop rings out squash-stretch, which is what jelly looks like. A node neither held nor moving keeps no state; `reduced_motion` and frames with no clock show it undeformed (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::jelly_stretches_a_dragged_node_and_wobbles_out`, ref `effects_jelly.png`; `crates/strand-render/src/effects/jelly.rs::tests`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: the rice acceptance, and what "only while music plays" covers.** `crates/strand-compiler/tests/render.rs::rice_now_renders_at_fixed_times` compiles design.md's rice (`rice_now.strand`) with the design theme into a bar, plays music on the mock host with a generated album cover and a fed spectrum, and paints it at fixed times (refs `rice_now_0ms`, `rice_now_500ms`, `rice_now_1000ms`): the squircle pill, its conic border, the cookie cover turning at 20°/s, the mirrored spectrum and the breathing glow; every frame's damage stays inside the pill and its glow's reach. design.md says "only the pill's own pixels repaint, and only while music plays". The first half holds. The second holds for what the snippet makes conditional (the cover's turn, the glow and the spectrum, which the binary feeds silence when paused), but the snippet's own `border: 1.5, conic(from: t * 40deg, …)` reads `t` unconditionally, so the border keeps turning, and the pill keeps its clock, while paused; the test asserts that reading rather than changing the design's snippet. A shell that wants the pill still when paused writes `media.playing ? t * 40deg : 0deg`.

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: a `spectrum` or `graph` with no size is 64 × 24.** Both had no content size, so design.md's `spectrum audio.sink { bars: 24; width: 72; … }` in the rice's row (which centres its children) laid out 0 px tall and drew nothing, and `graph cpu.usage { history: 60s }` with no size would draw nothing anywhere but a stretching column. Like `arc` (24 px square) and an image (16 px), they now have a small default: 64 × 24 when `size` is not set and `width` or `height` is missing, the side that is set winning. A fully sized one keeps no content size, so existing layouts are unchanged (a small edit in S-runtime's `layout/style.rs`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: a shared-element morph crosses surfaces on one output, by the surfaces' origins.** design.md's morph is "across surfaces, so the bar's media pill becomes the media panel"; m4-effects-paint-w2 left it to one surface because render had no surface origins, and m4-plan reads "Morph across surfaces needs surface origins, else falls back to the enter pose". The surface manager already says where each surface's buffer lies on its output (`SurfaceHost::surface_placed`, m4-surface-w2, used for the tray's click point), and the host knows each surface's monitor from `surface_attached` and `surface_entered`. The host now hands both to render (`Renderer::set_surface_origin`; a popup, attached with no monitor, takes its parent surface's output), and a node entering with a `morph` name last drawn on another surface starts over that box moved by the difference of the two origins, when both are known and on the same output (the monitor's identity, so per-monitor bars never morph into another monitor's panel). Origins are looked up when the morph starts, not when the box was drawn, so a bar at rest whose cached frame never flattens again still counts. Without origins, or across outputs, the node plays its enter pose as before. Layer origins ignore other surfaces' exclusive zones (origin.rs says so), so a panel anchored beside a bar can start a zone's width off on that axis; that is the placement's own limit (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::a_shared_morph_crosses_surfaces_on_one_output`, ref `effects_morph_across.png`; `crates/strand/src/demo/host.rs::tests::surfaces_are_placed_on_their_outputs_for_render`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: `pixelate` is a true mosaic on the CPU too.** This supersedes the m4-effects-paint-w2 note that drew `pixelate` as a sharpening blur because "only the GPU path can" draw a subtree at low resolution. The CPU can do that with the offscreen-group machinery the blurs already use. The masked subtree is drawn whole into its group pixmap, and each square cell of `(1 − p) · 12` logical px (aligned to the node's box corner, so the grid does not crawl as damage changes) becomes the average of its pixels. That is exactly the drawing at one sample per cell, box-filtered, then sampled back up by nearest neighbour. The cells shrink to 1 px, the plain drawing, as the node fades in at opacity `p`. The mosaic is a field on render's own `Layer` (`mosaic: Option<u16>`), not a new `strand_scene::Effect`, because only render builds it (from `transition:`). The GPU path uploads the same CPU-drawn group, like any offscreen group. Its cost is one pass over the group's pixels, cheaper than the blur it replaces (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::pixelate_draws_a_mosaic_that_refines`, ref `effects_pixelate.png`; `crates/strand-render/src/offscreen.rs::tests::mosaic_averages_each_cell_from_its_phase`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: goo is contoured by marching squares.** design.md says goo merge is "Ok, via marching squares", and m4-effects-paint-w2 evaluated the field at every pixel instead. The goo raster now samples the field and its colour at the corners of a 2 px grid. It finds each cell edge's zero crossing by linear interpolation, and takes the cell's outline from those crossings: one segment, or two for a saddle, joined or split by the sign at the cell's centre. Each pixel's coverage is its signed distance to its cell's outline, antialiased over one pixel, and its colour is the corners' colours interpolated bilinearly. The field is evaluated once per grid corner, a quarter as often as before, which is what makes it "Ok" on the CPU. The grid is 2 px rather than a coarser 4 so a bridge appears once it is about a pixel thick, rather than popping in at 4. The drawing agrees with the field everywhere more than a pixel from the outline (`crates/strand-render/src/effects/goo.rs::tests::marching_squares_follow_the_field`), and `effects_goo.png` was re-blessed with no visible change.

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: the CPU's tilt stays 2D, as design.md says.** design.md's GPU section says that without a usable GPU "tilt stays 2D", and the catalogue says "true 3D tilt is GPU". So the in-plane turn of m4-effects-paint-w2 is the specified CPU version, not an approximation of it. The paint-w2 note records why it turns in the plane: with no perspective, a turn about the X or Y axis only foreshortens, by about 1 % at 8°. A CPU perspective warp would mean resampling the node's pixels through a homography every frame the pointer moves, which is the work the design gives the GPU. The 3D tilt belongs to the "Bundled GPU effects (8)" box, whose WGSL has not landed (`strand-gpu/src/pass.rs`: "Bundled passes are drawn by their CPU versions until their WGSL lands"). It is not part of this stream, and the Effects catalogue's "parallax/tilt" counts the CPU version (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::parallax_and_tilt_follow_the_pointer`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: a backdrop inside an offscreen ancestor shows what is behind it.** Offscreen groups were drawn inner first, with backdrops last. So an ancestor drawn whole (for a `filter: blur` or a colour matrix around a `backdrop:` node) took the backdrop's group before it had pixels, and the backdrop showed nothing. The groups are now drawn in order of where each one ends in the display list. That puts every group after the groups nested in it, and a backdrop (an empty group) after the groups closed before it, which it shows. It also puts the backdrop before the groups still open around it, which then draw its pixels with their own content and filter them together. What the backdrop reads is unchanged: the surface's content behind it, with the ancestors' earlier items drawn as they are, because their groups are still open there (`crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::a_backdrop_inside_a_filtered_ancestor_shows_what_is_behind`, ref `effects_backdrop_nested.png`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: `svg` and `lottie` files are read on the image worker, and Lottie image layers draw.** Both media sources read and parsed their files inside `RasterSource::state`, which runs during flatten on the render thread. design.md keeps file IO off that thread, as images already were. The image decode worker now also takes file jobs. A source asks through `RasterProps::files` (`ImageStore::load_file`, keyed by kind and source). The worker runs the read and parse, stores the result, and wakes the loop. The render loop then marks every surface dirty (`files_arrived`), and the source takes the result the next time it is flattened. A source changes once in a while, so a full re-flatten is cheaper than tracking which surface shows which file, and damage still repaints only what changed. While a read is in flight the node draws nothing and has no clock. Before, a Lottie that was not loaded yet asked for refresh frames, which would now spin while it waits. Inline backends (tests, offline renders) still run the job at once. The worker keeps at most 64 results that no source has taken, so a source that changed mid-read leaves nothing behind for long. A Lottie's image assets are decoded in the same job, at their authored size. They can be PNG or JPEG, either a base64 `data:` URL (decoded by a small base64 reader rather than a new dependency) or a file next to the animation, at `u` + `p` relative to its directory. Remote URLs are not fetched. Velato's renderer then draws them in image layers through `RenderSink::draw_image`, clipped to the authored box. An asset that cannot be read or decoded draws nothing, as before (`crates/strand-render/tests/lottie.rs::image_layers_draw_embedded_and_neighbouring_assets`, ref `lottie_images.png`; `::the_file_is_read_on_the_image_worker`; `crates/strand-render/tests/svg.rs::the_file_is_read_on_the_image_worker`; `crates/strand-render/src/image.rs::tests::file_jobs_run_on_the_worker_and_are_taken_once`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: thumbnails turn frames upright, leave the pointer out, and the matrix checks the window's colour again.** ext-image-copy-capture-v1 sends each frame's `transform` before `ready`. The capture used to ignore it, so a window drawn with a rotated or flipped buffer would have shown in its buffer's orientation. `wm::capture::upright` now applies its inverse before scaling, reading it as a `wl_surface` buffer transform: rotations are counter-clockwise, and a flip about the vertical axis comes first. The fake compositor sends a transform when asked (`Cmd::TransformToplevel`), and fills the buffer so that the upright image is known. Sessions keep `Options::empty()`: without `paint_cursors` the protocol leaves the pointer out, which suits a thumbnail of a window, and no cursor sessions are made. The module docs now say so instead of "the cursor is not painted". The tests' `TestWindow` filled a 64×64 buffer whatever its tile, so on Hyprland the frame's centre fell outside the buffer, and m4-integration-w2 loosened the matrix test to "the colour anywhere in the frame". The window now fills the size its compositor configures (each side its own where the configure leaves it 0), as a real client does. The test again asks for the window's colour at the frame's centre. That passes on sway (a 28×16 frame) and labwc (16×16) in `matrix.sh`, with niri skipped (it offers no toplevel capture), and the full matrix passes on all three with the filling window. Hyprland cannot start here without a KMS card, so CI's vkms run is its proof (`crates/strand-services/src/wm/capture.rs::tests::frames_are_turned_upright`, `crates/strand-services/tests/capture.rs::transformed_frames_come_upright`, `crates/strand/tests/compositor_matrix.rs::a_window_is_captured_for_its_thumbnail`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: "only the ring repaints", and what "multiple outlines" is.** design.md gives gradient borders with an animated angle the cost "Trivial; only the ring repaints". Until now a border whose `conic(from: t * 60deg, …)` turned damaged its node's whole box every frame, and with it everything drawn inside. A node whose border runs along its box (no `shape:`) now hashes the border apart from the rest of what it draws. Its damage record keeps the four strips the ring lies in, each as wide as the larger of the border and the corner radius plus 2 px for antialiasing. When only the border changed, in the same place, the frame damages those strips and nothing else, the same way a text change damages only its changed glyphs. A shaped node's border follows its outline anywhere in the box, so it keeps whole-box damage. The catalogue row also says "multiple outlines", but no syntax for it appears anywhere in design.md, and `border:` takes one width and paint. Rather than add a list-valued `border:` (a new concept), several outlines are written the way the rest of the language composes: a box's `border:` together with its `stroke:` (dash, trim, wave) and `rim`, or nested boxes that each have their own border (`crates/strand-render/tests/damage.rs::a_turning_gradient_border_repaints_only_its_ring`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: the Effects catalogue box is ticked.** Each row of design.md's catalogue tables now has a proving test, listed in features.md: the Effects catalogue box (paint-w2's and media's evidence, plus this stream's jelly, cross-surface morph, pixelate, marching-squares goo, ring damage, nested backdrop, Lottie images, worker file reads and upright thumbnails) and, for the rows other boxes own, the shapes and paint box (radii, squircle, gradients, dither), the scrims box (scrim, concave fillets) and the album-art evidence. Some rows have GPU halves, which stay open in their own boxes and do not hold this one back: `backdrop: blur()`'s promotion to the GPU and the compositor's blur belong to the Blur ladder box, and true 3D tilt, aurora on the GPU and particles above 1,000 to the Bundled GPU effects box.

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: multiple outlines, corrected and proved.** The ring paragraph above says several outlines are "a box's `border:` together with its `stroke:` (dash, trim, wave) and `rim`". A `stroke:` is drawn inside the box as a border is, along the same outer edge, so a stroke and a border of the same width are one outline, the later one on top. Two concentric outlines come from a `stroke:` narrower than the `border:` it lies over (a 2 px pink stroke over a 6 px blue border shows 2 px of pink, then 4 px of blue), with a `rim` lighting their top; separated rings come from nested boxes, each with its own border. A reviewer found no test proved either; `crates/strand-render/tests/effects.rs::multiple_outlines_compose_from_border_stroke_rim_and_nesting` (refs `effects_outlines.png`, `effects_outlines_2x.png`) now draws both and checks each band's colour.

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: the rice's paused half is in design.md, and its ring is what repaints.** The rice paragraph above kept design.md's "only while music plays" and let the test assert the opposite, which CLAUDE.md does not allow: the docs win unless they change in the same commit. The snippet is the design's, so the sentence under it changes instead, to what the snippet does: "Only the pill's own pixels repaint; when the music stops, the cover, spectrum and glow go still, and only the turning border's ring repaints." That needed the ring to be small enough to tell apart on a pill. The ring's strips were four bands each as wide as the corner radius, which on a `radius: full` pill covers the whole box, so its border fell back to whole-box damage. The strips are now two columns as wide as the corners reach (a squircle's 1.6 × its radius, capped at half the side) and, between them, two rows as tall as the border, each 2 px more for antialiasing: a pill's round ends and its border rows. The rice test now asserts that every paused frame damages something, nothing past the pill and nothing over its middle, where the spectrum rests (`crates/strand-compiler/tests/render.rs::rice_now_renders_at_fixed_times`; the pill case of `crates/strand-render/tests/damage.rs::a_turning_gradient_border_repaints_only_its_ring`, whose partial repaints add up to a full paint).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: a Lottie's image assets have a pixel budget.** Assets were decoded at their authored `w`/`h`, up to 4096² (64 MiB) each, with no cap on their number, and kept as long as the source stays. So a downloaded file with a few large, or many tiny-but-claiming-large, `data:` assets could hold hundreds of MB in a 24 px node, against design.md's ~30 MB bar. Each asset is now decoded at most 1,024 px on its longer side, and a file's assets together at most 1 Mi pixels (4 MiB): when their capped sizes add up to more, all are shrunk alike to fit, and any whose size is not authored take what is left, in id order. Each is drawn scaled to its authored box, so only sharpness changes, and only for assets larger than a shell would show. Decoding at the drawn size instead was not done: the file is loaded once per source on the worker, before any node size is known, and the same source can be drawn at several sizes (`crates/strand-render/src/media/lottie.rs::tests::assets_are_decoded_within_the_budget`, `crates/strand-render/tests/lottie.rs::a_large_asset_is_decoded_small_and_drawn_over_its_box`). (Superseded 2026-10-10: decisions.md m4-owner-docs, "a Lottie's image assets are bounded as images are".)

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: jelly's speed is smoothed by time, and a held node at rest wants no frames.** The jelly paragraph's smoothed speed moved half way to each frame's speed per painted frame, so the same drag stretched less at 60 Hz than at 144 Hz while it built up, and the smoothing's time constant followed frame pacing. Each frame now moves it `1 − e^(−dt/τ)` of the way, τ = 24 ms (half way at 60 Hz, as before, so `effects_jelly.png` moved by at most 4 levels and was re-blessed). "The same jelly every run" still needs the same frame times, as any spring does. A held node that stops moving keeps its state (the drag goes on), but no longer keeps `Animator::busy` true, so its surface's cached frame is reused until the drag moves it again (`crates/strand-render/src/effects/jelly.rs::tests::the_stretch_does_not_depend_on_the_refresh_rate`, `::a_held_node_at_rest_wants_no_frames`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-effects-finish: a popup's output follows its parent.** The cross-surface morph paragraph has a popup take its parent's output once, when the popup is placed. A popup placed before its parent got no origin and never got one, and one whose parent moved to another monitor kept the old output. Render now keeps what the host placed (each surface's own output, `None` for a popup, and its position), and resolves every surface's output from its nearest placed ancestor surface whenever any surface is placed, moves or goes (`crates/strand/src/demo/host.rs::tests::surfaces_are_placed_on_their_outputs_for_render` now places the popup first and moves the parent).

## m4-gpu-effects

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: the bundled effects run on the file-shader pipeline, with four `vec4` uniforms each.** design.md names eight bundled GPU effects and m4-owner their spellings; nothing fixed how their WGSL meets the GPU thread. Each is now a synthetic `ShaderCode` (path `bundled:<name>`, `strand-gpu/src/bundled.rs`) with uniforms `u0`–`u3` at `@group(1)` bindings 0–3, run by the same pipeline, prelude and caches as a `.wgsl` file, so the bundled effects add no second pass path and no second ABI. `ShaderPass::uniforms` fills them in order (missing floats are zero), slot 0's first float being the reach where an effect has one (`Bundled::reach`). Layouts: `bloom` u0 = (radius px, strength); `chromatic` u0.x = offset px; `crt` none; `wobble` u0 = (amplitude px, wavelength px, period s); `tilt` u0 = (pitch, yaw) radians; `glass` u0 = (refraction px, corner radius px, dispersion, frost px); `backdrop_blur` u0.x = σ px; `aurora` u0–u2 the three curtains' straight colours, u3.x speed. Two effects are not one fragment pass: `backdrop_blur` is two steps (across, then down, `PassFrame::then`), and `particles` is an instanced sprite pipeline of its own (below). A `PassFrame` now carries its input pixels (`input`, the CPU raster's byte order, which is `Bgra8Unorm`'s, so they upload as they are) and the steps after it (`then`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: the knobs, one optional knob at most per function.** builtin.schema now declares `bloom(radius: length, strength: float = 1)`, `crt()`, `chromatic(offset: length)`, `wobble(amplitude: length)` and `glass(refraction: length = 12)`, with their docs. The compiler drops a defaulted argument the call leaves out from the value it sends, which shifts every later argument, so only a trailing optional knob reaches render where it was written; each function has at most one. Fixed by design rather than knobs: wobble's wavelength (40 logical px) and period (2 s), glass's dispersion (0.3 of its refraction) and frost (1.5 logical px), CRT's curvature and scanline pitch (every 3 logical px). `crates/strand-compiler/tests/scene_catalogue.rs::bundled_effects_have_their_spelling` checks the new arities and `tests/instantiate.rs::bundled_effect_knobs_reach_the_scene` that the knobs arrive.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: what each effect looks like.** design.md lists the effects by name only, so each was given the look its name usually means, kept simple and resolution-independent (lengths are logical pixels × scale). Bloom: a 64-tap golden-angle Gaussian (σ = radius / 3) of the parts whose straight luma passes a soft knee (0.2–0.7), times `strength`, screened over the input; luma rather than the brightest channel, since a saturated blue would otherwise bloom like white. Chromatic: red from a copy `offset` to the left, blue from one to the right, green in place. CRT: barrel distortion (k = 0.06) with the corners cut round, a 0.6 px colour fringe, scanlines every 3 px (80–100 % brightness) and a vignette. Wobble: rows displaced sideways by a sine of `amplitude`, wavelength and period, travelling with time. Tilt: the card turned in perspective (the eye 2.5 × its longer side away) and scaled to fit its box, so its reach stays zero. Glass: a rounded-box SDF of the box with its corner radius; inside, the backdrop is bent towards the rim by up to `refraction` (the convex rim's `e²`), red and blue bent ±0.3 of that apart (dispersion), lightly frosted (9 taps of 1.5 px) and tinted 6 % white, with a fresnel rim (0.35·e³) and a highlight under the pointer (a Gaussian of 0.35 × its shorter side, plus the rim facing the pointer). Aurora: the CPU fallback's formula ported exactly to WGSL with `t` running, so the GPU's frame at `t = 0` is the CPU's still. Backdrop blur: a separable Gaussian at full resolution. Particles: the CPU's own particles (the same births, positions and alphas, `Particles::gpu_uniforms`), each one instance of the same `Sprite::dot` coverage, so only the cap differs.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: particles above 1,000 are the GPU's up to 50,000 alive.** design.md says "Under 1,000: CPU sprite blits; above: GPU", with no upper bound. A pass's instance buffer is 12 bytes a particle, so 50,000 alive (600 KB, from the CPU's same 10,000 births a second cap) is the GPU's limit (`GPU_MAX_ALIVE`); the positions are computed on the CPU each frame, which keeps the field a pure function of `t` exactly as the CPU draws it and spares a compute pipeline.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: where a pass's pixels go.** A node's own pass (a `shader` node, aurora, particles past the cap) keeps the shader path: its pixels are the node's `Item::Raster`, and on a promoted surface it runs in the GPU frame. A layer's bundled passes (`filter:`'s bloom, CRT, chromatic, wobble, and the 3-D tilt; `backdrop: glass()`; a large `backdrop: blur()`) read the layer's group or what is behind it, which render rasterises on the CPU when it asks (after drawing the frame's offscreen groups), so they are always `Pass` requests read back, on either backend, and their pixels become the layer's offscreen group (`Layer::gpu`, which makes the layer an offscreen group and hashes into its node's damage signature). A filter layer's CPU blur and colour matrix apply before its bundled passes, whatever the written order: the CPU's own filters are one offscreen step and splitting them around a GPU pass would cost a second readback for an order nobody writes differently. Pixels are used when their key is the want's, or (a frame behind, as a clocked pass's are) when the last ones are of the same size; otherwise the CPU fallback draws.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: an effect asks for the GPU only while it shows.** design.md: "each starts GPU only while visible". A bundled effect's pass want is made only while its node shows: inside its ancestors' clip and the surface (a node scrolled or placed out of view, or on a hidden surface, asks nothing). The wants are what start the device and keep it in use; when the last goes, the device drops 30 s later (`renderer/promote.rs`, the one idle rule). This applies to `shader` nodes too, which used to ask while clipped out. Wants are made whatever the device's state, so a failed device is retried after 30 s as the shader path already did. `crates/strand-render/tests/gpu_effects.rs::bundled_effects_start_the_gpu_only_while_visible` runs each of bloom, CRT, chromatic, wobble, glass, aurora and particles out of view (nothing asked, the device unused), in view (asked, up), out again (no demand) and past the idle window (`BackendChange::Drop`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: GPU forms, fallbacks and their notices.** Render now knows whether a GPU can draw (`GpuStatus` not `Unavailable`, in a `gpu` build). Then aurora runs a clock (its CPU fallback stays still until the GPU's pixels come), `filter: wobble()` follows time, and the aurora and particle notices are not said: they were for the user without a GPU, and saying them while a device starts would say them on every GPU machine's first frame. Without one (refused, failed, or a build without `gpu`) everything is as before, so `tests/effects.rs::aurora_is_still_and_cpu_fallbacks_are_noticed_once` now delivers an `Unavailable` reply first. `tilt:` turns in 3-D only once the GPU has answered for the node (any pixels under its filter slot): until then it turns in 2-D, as on the CPU, and asks for a one-pixel tilt pass that starts the device, so a renderer whose device never comes up (and every CPU test) keeps the 2-D tilt rather than drawing the card flat. The lean now springs four channels (offset, and the turn across and down the box); the CPU uses the first turn as its `rotate`, the GPU both as yaw and pitch.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: glass reads its box, a large blur reads 3σ past it, and "large" is 0.2 Mpx of box.** design.md puts the GPU's backdrop blur "above about 0.2 Mpx". A `backdrop: blur()` is the GPU's when its box is at least 200,000 buffer pixels; its pass reads what is behind the box grown by 3σ (clipped to the surface) and its pixels cover that region, under the box's clip. Glass reads only its box (it samples past its edge by clamping), so its pixels are the box. Smaller blurs stay the quarter-scale CPU blur, which costs less than a readback at those sizes. `tests/gpu_effects.rs::a_large_backdrop_blur_is_the_gpus`.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: a shader's pointer follows the pointer.** `strand.pointer` was always (-1, -1): render now passes the pointer in buffer pixels relative to the pass's box (through the node's transform), or (-1, -1) off the surface or outside the box, only to code that reads it (so other passes' keys do not change with every motion), and to glass's highlight. A surface showing such a pass repaints on pointer motion, as one with a lean does (`tests/gpu_effects.rs::a_shader_follows_the_pointer`, `::glass_is_drawn_by_the_gpu_and_follows_the_pointer`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: shader uniforms spring.** design.md: a `u_*` uniform animates like any prop. `Prop::Uniforms` joined render's animated props: each entry's numbers (a number, a px or percentage length, an angle, a colour's four channels, a list's items) spring channel by channel on the effects curve, and a value of another shape (another name, another kind, a duration or bool, which have no motion) snaps. `anim/tests.rs::shader_uniforms_spring_between_values_of_one_shape`, `tests/gpu_effects.rs::shader_uniforms_spring`.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: `c.text` draws.** m4-gpu-w2 left canvas text recorded but not drawn because text is shaped per node. A node already has several texts (`TextSpec::part`: a `segmented`'s labels), so each text op of a canvas is one: part 1 + its index among the canvas's text ops (at most 254, the rest are not drawn), shaped by the text worker in the node's font and colour (a canvas now takes the themed font and colour, as text does) and drawn as `Item::Glyphs` with its first baseline starting at the op's point, in order with the shapes and clipped to the box. Until its layout is back a text draws nothing, as any text does. `crates/strand-render/src/canvas.rs::tests::texts_are_drawn_in_order_at_their_baseline_in_the_box`, `tests/canvas.rs::a_canvas_draws_its_texts` (refs `canvas_text.png`, `canvas_text_2x.png`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: `STRAND_GPU_IDLE_MS` stays a test hook.** `strand run` reads it to shorten the 30 s idle (`gpu_idle.rs` needs a cycle in seconds); it is documented in architecture.md's `strand-gpu` section as a test hook and nowhere a user reads, and a shell has no way to set it. Making it a setting would add a concept design.md does not have.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: the budgets after the effects.** Measured in the container on this branch, release builds: the default build's `.text` is 18,878,215 bytes (gate 19,398,656; 46 KB more than m4-integration-w2's 18,831,751), the CPU-only build's 15,521,415 bytes (gate 15,728,640; 9 KB more than 15,512,455, all of it canvas text, the uniform springs and the lean's extra channel, since every GPU-only path in render is behind `#[cfg(feature = "gpu")]`), and the design bar on the real services 33,628 kB PSS (target 34,816 kB, ceiling 38,912 kB). No budget, gate or target changed and none needed code moved; the CPU core's margin is now 207 KB.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: two fallback tests make their GPU unavailable.** `strand-render/tests/effects.rs::aurora_is_still_and_cpu_fallbacks_are_noticed_once` and `strand/src/demo/host.rs::tests::effect_fallbacks_are_said_once_as_notices` test the notices of a user with no GPU; in a `gpu` build a renderer that has heard nothing yet may still get one, so each now delivers a `GpuReply::Unavailable` first. The host test lives outside S-gpu's files and was changed for that reason only.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): a failed bundled pass draws its CPU version.** A pass that fails on a working device (`GpuReply::Failed` with its key: over the device's texture size, a driver's compile error, a readback error) was recorded as one transparent pixel, which every bundled effect then took as its pixels: a filter layer drew a one-pixel group, glass and a large blur a one-pixel backdrop, aurora and particles nothing, with no notice and until the want's key changed. A failure is now recorded as such (`ShaderResults::failed`): it still keeps the want from being asked again while its inputs stay, and a `shader` node still draws nothing (it has no CPU version), but `ShaderResults::usable` never offers it, so a bundled effect draws the CPU version design.md gives it (bloom a glow, glass blur and tint, the others unfiltered, aurora still, particles capped). A tilt turns in 3-D only after a filter pass of its node gave pixels (`ShaderResults::answered`) and while its last one did not fail; once one failed it turns in 2-D and asks for no warm-up pass until the node goes. `tests/gpu_effects.rs::a_failed_bundled_pass_draws_its_cpu_version` (each of bloom, CRT, chromatic, wobble, glass, a large blur, aurora and particles: the frame after the failure is the CPU's, and nothing is asked again), `::a_tilt_whose_pass_fails_stays_2d`. Both run without a device: the test answers the passes.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): a pass's pixels are held only while a frame wants them.** Results were pruned only when their node left the tree, and not at all for a surface whose frame wanted nothing, so a hidden glass, a large blur (at least 800 KB, several MB at 1440p), a filter layer or a tilt at rest kept its full-resolution read-back pixels as long as the node existed. Each result now records the surface that asked for it, and every frame of a surface drops that surface's results its wants no longer name (before the early return when it wants nothing); a surface that goes away drops its results at the next tick. A failure's record (a shared one-pixel pixmap) stays while its node does, so it is not asked again. These pixels are not counted in the offscreen groups' 4 MB: design.md's 4 MB is the CPU's cache of groups it rasterised, while these are a pass's output held only while the effect shows, like a `shader` node's pixels, and they belong to the GPU path's own cost (design.md's +20–40 MB while promoted). A pixmap per showing effect is the floor for drawing it at all; what was wrong was keeping it after. `Renderer::gpu_pass_bytes` (tests) and `::bundled_effects_start_the_gpu_only_while_visible` check it is non-zero while each effect shows and zero once hidden. `strand/tests/gpu_idle.rs`'s promoted panel now carries a `filter: bloom(8)` box while `on`, so its PSS-across-cycles check (3 MiB) runs the layer readback path too.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): a tilt's warm-up pass waits until the node shows.** The one-pixel pass that starts the device for a 3-D tilt was asked whenever the lean turned, before the visibility check, and the lean turns with the pointer anywhere on the surface: a tilt clipped out (a row scrolled out of a clipping list) started the device, and retried every 30 s without one. It is now asked only while the node shows, the same test every other effect uses. `::bundled_effects_start_the_gpu_only_while_visible` now covers all eight (the tilt, with the pointer on the bar, and the large backdrop blur added) plus a `.wgsl` noise field, each hidden both off the bar and clipped out by an ancestor's `clip` while on it. Two harness changes keep it independent of wall-clock pacing: render's `set_promotion(false)` (tests) keeps the 1300 px surface the large blur needs on the CPU however long its frames take, and the idle window is shortened only after the visible phase, so a slow frame cannot drop the device mid-test. Both were latent in the earlier version (the large blur test promoted once in a loaded run).

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): "aurora and noise fields" is one item, aurora bundled and a noise field a `.wgsl` shader.** design.md:524 lists "aurora and noise fields" as one of the eight but gives a noise field no spelling: the built-in effects are `lightning | sparks | shimmer | ripple | aurora` (design.md:510), the filters and backdrops without a node of their own are named (bloom, crt, chromatic, wobble, glass), and `noise(x)` is a time signal for props, not a node. Inventing `effect noise` or `filter: noise()` would add a concept the design does not have. So the item is read as aurora, which is the bundled shader (`effect aurora`, a field of curtains moving with `t`), plus noise fields written as `.wgsl` shaders, which "use the same path" (design.md:524): drawn by the GPU, started only while visible, released 30 s after. The visibility test runs a time-reading noise-field shader beside the eight. If the owner wants a bundled noise field with its own spelling, that is a design.md change first.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): files outside S-gpu's ownership.** m4-plan gives S-gpu `promote.rs`, `canvas.rs` and `renderer/backend.rs` in strand-render, yet wave 3 has it land "the 8 bundled effects with S-effects' CPU fallbacks", and the effects meet the CPU where the flattener and the fallbacks are. An earlier report on this branch said only two files outside its crates changed; that was wrong. This branch changes, in S-runtime's files: `flatten/{mod,node,hash}.rs` (pass wants made while a node shows, the tilt's 3-D switch), the new `flatten/gpu.rs` (the bundled wants and drawing their pixels), `layers.rs` (`Layer::gpu`), `offscreen.rs` (a GPU layer's pixels used as its group; `render_group`'s bundled flag and `rasterise` split out), `renderer/{frame,wake}.rs` (one argument), `renderer/{mod,layout_pass}.rs` (`gpu_ok`, the GPU hooks), `anim/{mod,motion}.rs` (uniforms spring, the lean's four channels); in S-effects' files: `effects/{mod,lean,particles}.rs` (the knobs, the tilt pass, the lean's channels, particles' GPU uniforms), one-line changes in `effects/{builtin,light,transition}.rs`, `anim/keyframes.rs` and `backdrop.rs`, and the new `effects/gpu.rs`; in the compiler, `builtin.schema`'s bundled knobs and their tests; and `strand/src/demo/host.rs` (recorded above). Each change is the smallest seam the effect needed, and none changes the behaviour of the owner's code without a GPU (the CPU-only build's tests are unchanged apart from the two fallback tests above). S-effects is also active in wave 3, so these files may conflict at merge: the integrator should merge S-effects first and have this branch rebased, with S-runtime and S-effects reviewing the hunks in their files.
