## m5-core

**2026-10-10 · m5-core: the 0a interfaces land as inert code (wave 0b).** `strand_core::ipc` holds the protocol's types and JSON-line codec (`Request` with every M5 command, `parse`, `parse_m5`, `encode`, `VERSION`, `MAX_LINE`, `DBUS_NAME`, the answer helpers) and the `IpcRequests` channel with its `Reply`/`ReplyFuture` one-shot; the binary's `ipc.rs` became `ipc/{mod, server, cli, describe}.rs` over it; `Shell::request` dispatches to `run/request/*.rs`, one module per command (the existing reload, reset, set, mock and watch moved there unchanged; the get, toggle, call, clear, report and inspect modules are empty until their streams fill them); `strand` is a library with the binary over it; `ActionCtx` reaches every `ServiceHost`; the `Renderer` has inert inspect and `frame_summary` stubs; `Suggestion` has a `title`; the logic loop drains the request channel; `tests/m5.rs` has its eight empty stream modules; the snapshot hop's types exist. No answer a socket client hears changes, malformed requests included (next paragraph), and nothing feeds the request channel outside the run tests until S-ipc's D-Bus front end. Release `.text` measured in the container (budgets.rs's gate test, `--release`), before → after: CPU-only 15,657,671 → 15,670,215 B (+12,544), GPU 19,041,095 → 19,049,607 B (+8,512); both inside their gates, but not within 0b's 1 KB bound, and paid for by no allocation yet (last paragraph). The tree-sitter package does not exist yet, so the root `Cargo.toml` gains no member; S-lsp adds it with the package (or asks the integrator).

**2026-10-10 · m5-core: `parse` reads only the commands the shell serves; M5's fields are read by `parse_m5`.** The first cut of 0b had `ipc::parse` read every M5 command and the stub modules answer them "unknown command". That kept well-formed requests' answers, but it changed three things an M4 client could hear: a `reset` with both `path` and `node` (M4 reset the path and ignored the node) was refused, a `reset` with only a `node` heard "not served by this shell yet" instead of "`reset` needs a `path`", and a malformed `get`, `toggle`, `clear`, `call` or `inspect.*` heard the codec's "`toggle` needs `path`" instead of "unknown command". It also cost about 5 KB of `.text` for commands nothing serves (measured: 15,677,127 → 15,672,071 B in a `cargo build --release --no-default-features` binary). So `parse` reads M4's commands exactly as M4 did, field for field, and answers any other `cmd` "unknown command `x`"; M5's field reading is `parse_m5(cmd, &v)` in the same file, tested (every variant round-trips through `encode`, `parse_m5`), and unused by `parse` until a stream adds its arm (`"get" | "toggle" => return parse_m5(cmd, &v)`) with its handler and its `Shell::request` arm. Streams still share one codec. Each adds one `parse` arm, a one-line merge, which is cheaper than paying for the unserved commands. The dispatch's unserved variants share one arm that answers `strand_core::ipc::unknown`, which a `Request` built on another thread (the request channel) still reaches. architecture.md says so (0a had `parse` read every command). When S-inspect serves `reset{node}` it decides how a `reset` with both fields reads; `parse_m5("reset")` reads only the node, and if the both-fields case becomes a refusal, that is a change for M4 clients which S-inspect records.

**2026-10-10 · m5-core: wire forms the 0a text left open.** A node id (`inspect.node{id}`, `inspect.highlight{id}`, `reset{node}`) and `inspect.dump`'s `surface` are opaque strings: the inspector passes back what its own answers spelled, and S-inspect picks the spelling without a protocol change. `call`'s `args` are a list of strings read by the action parameters' types, as `set`'s value is read by the cell's type, so the CLI and D-Bus send the same thing. `reset{node}` is its own variant, `Request::ResetNode`. Every string field except `set`'s value and `call`'s args is non-empty. An empty one encodes, but it does not parse back: a field the command needs is refused, and an optional one (`inspect.dump`'s `surface`, `inspect.highlight`'s `id`) reads as absent. `Request`'s doc says so and `empty_strings_do_not_round_trip_except_set_values` pins it; `encode` does not refuse them, since it returns a line, not a `Result`, and the D-Bus front end builds its own requests and checks its own arguments.

**2026-10-10 · m5-core: the request channel is the logic loop's, handed out through `Live::requests_to`.** The channel's wake is the sleeper's ping, which only the logic thread has, so `logic()` makes the channel and drains it after each sleep, beside the socket (a send pings the loop awake, so no extra calloop source and no polling). A clone of the sender goes to `Live::requests_to` when given: the run test `requests_from_another_thread_are_answered_by_the_logic_loop` uses it, and S-ipc hands its own clone to `strand_services::ipc_bus`. Calls are answered through the same dispatch as the socket's (`Caller::Socket` or `Caller::Bus`). `reload` (whose answer waits for its load, keyed by socket client) and `watch` (a `Changed` signal on D-Bus) are answered as unknown from the channel until S-ipc serves them there. A `Reply` dropped unanswered completes with a refusal, so a D-Bus caller never hangs.

**2026-10-10 · m5-core: the snapshot hop lands as types, not a channel.** `ToMain::Snapshot { kind, reply: SnapshotId }`, `SnapshotKind::{Report, Pick, Layout { node }}` and `ToLogic::Snapshot(Snapshot { reply, data })`, with the snapshot as the JSON its IPC answer carries (main builds it from its own state between frames; logic only forwards it). A second logic→main calloop channel, wired with nothing sending on it, would add `.text` for no behaviour, against 0b's 1 KB bound; the first stream that sends one (S-tools' `report` or S-inspect's layouts) wires the channel, and the other reuses it. The types carry `allow(dead_code)` until then.

**2026-10-10 · m5-core: the library's shape.** `lib.rs` holds the whole module tree, private as before; the binary reaches it through a hidden `strand::cli` facade (`check`, `fmt`, the IPC commands, `compositor_rules`, `demo`, `run`, `trim`, `LogConfig`, `default_dir`), so no module becomes public API before S-plugins designs `Shell::builder`. `main.rs` keeps `#[global_allocator]` and the `NO_THP` constructor: a `#[used]` constructor in an rlib is not guaranteed to reach the link in unoptimised builds. `lib.rs` repeats both under `cfg(test)`, so the unit tests, which moved with the modules into the library's harness, still run on mimalloc with THP off (`mimalloc_is_the_test_harness_allocator`, `transparent_huge_pages_are_off_in_the_test_harness`). `run::trim` became `pub` for the facade.

**2026-10-10 · m5-core: `ActionCtx` is the last parameter, and the services do not take it yet.** `ServiceHost::action(rt, target, name, args, ctx)`; the VM passes `ActionCtx::default()` (no input, invocation 0), `SchemaHost` records it in `ActionCall::ctx` (asserted in instantiate.rs's input-handler test), the composite host forwards it, and the store and custom hosts ignore it. strand-services' `DynService::action` is unchanged: carrying the context into the services' ordering queue is S-platform's design, inside the crates it owns.

**2026-10-10 · m5-core: 0b costs 12,544 B of CPU-only `.text` (8,512 B GPU), not the 1 KB the plan bounded it by, and no allocation pays for it; it needs the integrator's or the owner's acceptance before it merges.** The 1 KB bound assumed inert code compiles to nothing. Most of 0b is reachable: `encode` covers every variant (the CLI's `request` calls it), the dispatch has its arms, the logic loop drains the request channel and answers through `Reply`, and `ActionCtx` is passed to every action. I diffed symbols (`nm -S`) of `cargo build --release --no-default-features` binaries. The first cut cost +35 KB; four changes brought it to +12.5 KB. (1) The codec's functions are `#[inline]`, so they are built in the binary's crate at its opt-level `s` and reuse its `serde_json` instantiations, instead of a second, opt-level-3 copy in strand-core: −12 KB, because `Value`'s deserializer and `BTreeMap` insert had been duplicated. (2) `encode` builds one `Map` instead of a `json!` per variant. (3) The request channel is a `Mutex<Vec<IpcCall>>` instead of `std::sync::mpsc`, whose generic channel code cost about 2 KB (architecture.md updated); (2) and (3) together saved 6 KB. (4) `parse` no longer reads the unserved commands (previous paragraph): −5 KB. Building the tree without the library split measured about 3.9 KB smaller. The split itself changes LLVM's inlining across the shell: pairs like `Shell::after_step` −14 KB / `Shell::apply` +11 KB, and `live::run` folded into the worker's thread closure. No attribute removes that reliably; `#[inline]` on the `cli` facade's targets made it 20 KB worse, so I did not keep it. The rest, about 8.6 KB, is new reachable code, about 2.6 KB of it the request channel and `Reply` (`strand_core::ipc`'s symbols). **Who pays:** the plan's ledger ("Ledger and allocations") gives all 230,000 B to named streams plus the integrator's 42 KB review-fix reserve, and 0b has no line, so the provisional gate's headroom does not cover it. My proposal: the request channel and `Reply` (about 2.6 KB) come out of S-ipc's D-Bus front-end allocation (40 KB), since that is the plumbing it would otherwise write, and the rest (about 9.9 KB) comes out of the integrator's reserve (about 24% of it), or the owner says otherwise. The GPU build's +8,512 B is the same code (its inlining differs). It belongs to the same lines, not to the GPU-only 40 KB, which is for outline, flash and `report`'s GPU section. Getting under 1 KB would mean leaving the lib split, or the request channel's drain, out of 0b. The plan put both there so streams never rebase across them, and that trade is the integrator's or the owner's, not this stream's.

## m5-size

**2026-10-10 · m5-size: `scripts/size-report.sh` and the M5 size baseline.** The report builds the two gated binaries exactly as budgets.rs's gate does (`cargo test --release -p strand [--no-default-features] --test budgets --no-run`, fat LTO), so its `.text` is the gate's figure, and breaks `.text` down by crate and by symbol: symbols in the `.text` section (readelf, by section index), demangled with c++filt and charged to the crate their path names (`<T as Trait>::f` to T's crate unless T is a std or primitive type, generic std code such as drop glue and sorts to the first non-std crate in its type arguments; `[c]` for symbols with no Rust path, `[unattributed]` for bytes no symbol covers). It uses only binutils and awk (mawk in the image), so the Dockerfile and ci.yml are unchanged; `scripts/test-size-report.sh` tests the attribution rule. Fat LTO charges inlined code to its caller, so the breakdown says where bytes sit, not what each crate costs exactly. Baseline at ea3079e (docs/size-baseline.md): CPU-only 15,657,671 B and GPU 19,041,095 B, equal to m4-owner-3's merged figures. Largest crates (CPU-only): strand_compiler 2,116,739, strand_services 1,983,039, strand_render 1,187,801, strand_core 948,562, zbus 533,985, strand 521,863, hashbrown 494,872. Two findings drive the reclaims below: `jpeg_decoder` and `image_webp` are each instantiated twice, once for strand-theme's `BufReader<&mut File>` and once for strand-render's in-memory cursors (about 44 KB and 45 KB of duplicate decoder code), and `image`'s glue in strand-theme is about 10.5 KB. Q8: `strand fmt` costs 27,729 B (`strand::fmt::run` 21,293 plus `strand_compiler::fmt` 6,436), under the 40 KB at which the plan would offer moving it, so it stays in `strand`.

**2026-10-10 · m5-size reclaim 1: strand-theme decodes WebP wallpapers with `image-webp` directly, without `image`.** `image` 0.25.10 (feature `webp`) leaves strand-theme's runtime `[dependencies]`; `image-webp` 0.2.4, already linked by strand-render and already built at opt "z", takes its place, so only `image`'s `DynamicImage`, `decoder_to_vec` and error glue leave the binary. The decode is the same: the header checks (`MAX_PIXELS`, `WEBP_BYTES_PER_PIXEL` × pixels within `FULL_FRAME_BYTES`) run before anything is allocated, which made `image::Limits`' `max_alloc` (the frame's 3 or 4 bytes per pixel, always under the bound) redundant; the frame is allocated at `output_buffer_size()` and read with `read_image`, as `image`'s wrapper does, RGB or RGBA by `has_alpha()`, then `malloc_trim`. `image` stays a dev-dependency for the tests' encoders. Measured with `scripts/size-report.sh`: CPU-only 15,657,671 → 15,648,071 B (−9,600), GPU 19,041,095 → 19,030,727 B (−10,368). No timing gate decodes a WebP (theme_swap_bench's wallpaper is a PNG, and the quantiser runs off the logic thread), and no opt-level changed, so the timing benches were not rerun for it. Tests: strand-theme's suite unchanged and green, plus `a_lossless_webp_seeds_as_the_same_png_does` (an RGB and an RGBA lossless WebP each seed exactly as the same pixels in a PNG). Review fix: the first cut formatted image-webp's errors directly, which dropped `image`'s "Format error decoding WebP: " prefix from a corrupt wallpaper's error and reworded IO errors ("IO Error: …"); `webp_err` now words them as `image`'s `from_webp_decode` did (an IO error as itself, anything else after the prefix), so the reclaim changes no message, and `a_corrupt_webp_keeps_its_error_wording` holds it.

**2026-10-10 · m5-size reclaim 2 (withdrawn): resvg, tiny-skia and tiny-skia-path stay at the release default, opt 3.** The first cut built them at "z" (−117,440 B CPU-only, −117,120 B GPU) on the reason that an SVG is rasterised once per source and drawn size on the decode worker. That holds for icons and image SVGs (strand-render's image.rs) but not for bindable SVG (media/svg.rs, design.md "SVG with bindable layers"): its parts' props resolve every frame, springs and `time` included, and each change re-parses the wrapped text with usvg and redraws it with resvg and tiny-skia on the render path (offscreen.rs, when `state()` changes), so `#needle { rotate: level * 270deg }` under a spring rasterises every animation frame. Design.md rates the feature "Trivial" (under 0.1 ms a frame for a 300 × 40 region), and the three timing benches cited for the first cut draw no SVG, so they could not show it was behaviour-neutral (Q7). Measured with the new ignored test `svg_frame_cost` (strand-render tests/svg.rs: a 300 × 40 meter whose needle's `rotate` reads `time`, 2,000 frames after 100 warm-up, minus the same scene with the part still; `--profile timing`, four builds run interleaved, four to six rounds each in the container): the per-frame redraw costs about 210 µs with the three crates at "z" (202–215), 126 µs at "s" (124–128) and 56 µs at opt 3 (55–58), so "z" made it about 3.7 times slower and over the "Trivial" bound, where opt 3 keeps it under. The reclaim is withdrawn; Cargo.toml says why in its place, and budgets.rs's `RELEASE_OPT_LEVELS` loses the three entries. The review's second point (the first cut's timing runs were single and non-interleaved against a busier baseline) falls with it. Also measured, not taken (outside this stream's scope): usvg, svgtypes and simplecss at opt 3 instead of their "z" (m4-integration-w2) would save another 5 µs a redraw (about 51 µs), at a size cost not measured.

**2026-10-10 · m5-size reclaim 3: miette, strand-introspect, freedesktop-desktop-entry, pipewire and libspa go from opt "s" to "z"; blake3 and roxmltree stay where they were.** The five run at event rates off every timing gate: miette renders diagnostics, strand-introspect parses D-Bus introspection for custom services, freedesktop-desktop-entry parses `.desktop` files for the apps service, pipewire and libspa run on PipeWire's thread. Not taken: **blake3 at "z"** made both binaries larger (+2,048 B CPU-only, +2,368 B GPU; the hashing is its SIMD assembly, and "z" only changes the Rust glue's inlining), and **roxmltree at "z"** (−8,768 B more) because fontique parses fontconfig's XML with it, which may sit on the reload path, and Q7 allows no size opt-level on a gated path. Timing: the laptop's reload bench is bimodal under load (token p95 about 17.5 ms with the portal clause near 1.8 ms, or about 20.5 ms with it near 4 ms, whole runs at a time), which made single runs misleading (the roxmltree run first looked like a 3 ms regression). Five interleaved rounds of `reload_latency` (`--profile timing`, 50 rounds, two runs each) on reclaim 2's tree and on this one landed in the same state pairwise (rounds 3–5 both about 20.5 / 4.2 ms, round 1 both about 17.6 / 1.9 ms), so this reclaim shows no regression beyond that noise; theme_swap_bench and list_scroll_bench were unchanged. GitHub's `timing` job decides whether it stays.

The largest candidate the report found is not behaviour-neutral within the crate boundaries, so it is offered, not taken: `jpeg_decoder::Decoder::decode_internal` and `image_webp`'s decoder are each built twice, once for strand-theme's `BufReader<&mut File>` and once for strand-render's in-memory cursors (about 44 KB + 45 KB). **2026-10-10 · m5-infra spike 1: headless sway renders with GLES2 and with Vulkan on the render node alone, and both offer linux-dmabuf; the M4 fallback to pixman was the tests' own sway, not the GPU.** `spikes/gpu-compositor/run.sh` runs `inside.sh` in run.sh's image with only `/dev/dri/renderD128` and the hardware ICD (gpu.sh's arrangement; no `/dev/dri/card*`, no host socket) and starts a private headless sway three times, keeping each `sway.log`. On the laptop's Intel PTL GPU (8086:b080, Mesa 25.2.8 from noble-updates, sway 1.9 / wlroots 0.17): `WLR_RENDERER=gles2` with `WLR_RENDER_DRM_DEVICE=/dev/dri/renderD128` starts on EGL's `iris` driver (EGL 1.5, `EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import_modifiers`), advertises `zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1`, and `vkcube-wayland` on ANV presents 60 frames to it; `WLR_RENDERER=vulkan` starts on ANV ("only experimental", wlroots says), advertises linux-dmabuf, and vkcube presents too; `pixman` starts, offers no linux-dmabuf, and vkcube aborts in `demo_init_vk_swapchain`, which is m4-gpu-spike's finding. So nothing falls back on this machine: `gpu-session.sh` has always started its sway on GLES2, but every test that starts its own sway (gpu_idle.rs among them) pins `WLR_RENDERER=pixman` without the render node, and that sway is what the promoted panel was attached to, in `Readback` mode (m4-report, m4-gpu-w2). `gpu-session.sh` now tries GLES2, then Vulkan, then pixman, exports the renderer that started as `STRAND_GPU_SWAY_RENDERER`, and keeps the sway log in `GPU_SWAY_LOG` (default `target/container/gpu-session-sway.log`). sway 1.9 segfaults while shutting down after SIGTERM in these runs (after "Destroying output"); every result above was read before that, and the tests already start a sway per test.

**2026-10-10 · m5-infra spike 2: the prebuilt tree-sitter CLI 0.27.0 generates from grammar.js without node.** `spikes/tree-sitter-cli/run.sh` fetches `tree-sitter-linux-x64.gz` of v0.27.0 (released 2026-08-30; 0.27.1 of 2026-10-08 is too new to pin), checks its sha256 (`20a1f39ec1c45f2211492dcb8881c802b643b554bb196869a29ac3778277fa77`, the digest GitHub lists for the asset, pinned in the Dockerfile, ci.yml and the spike) and runs it in run.sh's image, which has no node, deno or bun. A plain `tree-sitter generate` fails ("Failed to run `node`"); `tree-sitter generate --js-runtime native` evaluates `grammar.js` with the CLI's built-in QuickJS and writes `src/parser.c`, `grammar.json` and `node-types.json`; `generate src/grammar.json` needs no JS at all; generation is deterministic (two runs, identical `parser.c`), the parser is ABI 15 (the `tree-sitter` crate must be 0.25 or newer), and `tree-sitter parse` builds and runs it with the image's cc. The same grammar generated with node (a `node:22-trixie-slim` container: the binary needs glibc 2.39, which bookworm's 2.36 lacks) gives byte-identical `grammar.json`, `parser.c` and `node-types.json`. So the plan's fallback (CI checks `parser.c` against a committed `grammar.json` only, a developer regenerating `grammar.json` with node) is not needed: CI regenerates everything from `grammar.js`, which also catches a stale `grammar.json`.

Tests: `scripts/container/test-check-tree-sitter.sh` (a toy grammar: fresh files pass; a hand-edited `parser.c`, an edited `grammar.js` without regenerating and a missing `grammar.json` fail; a fake CLI of another version is refused; the Dockerfile's and ci.yml's version and sha256 agree, and ci.yml names the sha256 once). CI's lint job and `run.sh ci`'s lint steps now also run the CI scripts' own tests (`test-gate-misses.sh`, `test-check-tree-sitter.sh`, `test-ledger.sh`, `test-gpu-measure.sh`), which no job ran before.

**2026-10-10 · m5-infra spike 3: sway 1.9 issues an xdg-activation token for a layer surface and a click's serial, and honours it; a launched window gets focus on sway whatever its token.** `spikes/xdg-activation` (its own `[workspace]`; wayland-client 0.31.15, wayland-protocols 0.32.13 staging, wayland-protocols-wlr 0.3.12) maps toplevels A then B (B focused) on a private headless sway in run.sh's image, maps a 200×40 top-layer surface with no keyboard interactivity, clicks it with a `zwlr_virtual_pointer_v1` (headless sway has no pointer capability until one exists), asks `xdg_activation_v1` for a token with the click's serial, the seat and the layer surface, and activates A with it; each scenario in a fresh sway, under sway's default `focus_on_window_activation` (urgent) and under `focus`. Results: a token with the layer surface's valid serial makes A urgent (default) or focuses it (`focus`); with the serial off by 1000 sway still sends a token string but ignores the activation (no urgency, no focus); a token with no serial or surface is honoured only as urgency, even under `focus`; a new toplevel C mapped and then activated with a valid token is focused, but sway 1.9 focuses a newly mapped window on the focused workspace anyway, so on sway a launch does not tell a honoured token from none. So S-platform's container tests can use real sway for "a token comes from the clicked layer surface" and for "an existing window is activated (urgent / focused)", and the launch's focus check stays in `matrix.sh` on the compositors where it discriminates, as the plan says.

One root also shows on several surfaces (a bar per output), so a node has no single surface to name. Of the two fixes offered, a root→surface map sent to logic adds a message and a concept; dropping the surface removes one, so `Highlight(Option<NodeId>)` and `Layout { node }` it is, and main resolves the node with the new `Renderer::surfaces_of(node)` (the surfaces attached at the nearest surface root at or above it: every output's for a bar, a popup's own for a node inside it, none when nothing shows it). `set_highlight` takes `Option<NodeId>` and outlines it on each; a layout snapshot answers `node_layout(surface, node)` for each. `surfaces_of` is real code, not a stub (strand-render's own state answers it), and nothing in the binary calls it yet. architecture.md's snapshot-hop and strand-render paragraphs and m5-plan say so. The reading most consistent with m5-owner Q14 ("never a dropped or reordered action"): the VM numbers every handler invocation from 1, with input or without, the number lives in the frame for the whole run, only `input` is cleared at the first `await`, and 0 (`ActionCtx::default()`) is an action outside any handler, unordered; the queue is one on the services thread, keyed by invocation, shared by every service. architecture.md, m5-plan's 0a bullet and `strand_core::ActionCtx`'s doc say so. Text only; S-platform implements it in wave 2.

**2026-10-10 · m5-w0-harden (third round): plugins get the binary's allocator and THP setting from `strand::process_setup!()`.** `main.rs` declared `#[global_allocator]` (mimalloc) and the priority-100 `.init_array` `NO_THP` constructor, and `lib.rs` repeated both under `cfg(test)` only, so a plugin binary built on `strand::Shell::builder()` would run on the system allocator with THP on, and the plugin contract ("copy `[profile.release]` ... or the PSS figures do not hold") was wrong as written: wave3-pixels' 55 MB against about 25 MB is that case. A library's `#[used]` constructor is not guaranteed to reach the linking binary, so the library cannot do it alone; `strand::process_setup!()` (a `macro_rules!`, with its names behind a hidden `strand::__process`) declares both statics at the invoker's crate root, and `main.rs`, `lib.rs` under `cfg(test)` and a new `tests/m5/process_setup.rs` all invoke it, so there is one copy of the setup. The contract in architecture.md and m5-plan's S-plugins now requires a plugin to invoke it (and `plugin_hello` to). CPU-only `.text` unchanged at 15,635,975 B (budgets.rs's gate test in the container; ledger half `CPU-only 15,635,975 (Δ -21,696 vs 15,657,671; gate 15,859,712)`). Tests: `tests/m5.rs`'s `process_setup::a_linking_binary_allocates_with_mimalloc` and `a_linking_binary_runs_with_thp_off`; main.rs's and lib.rs's existing allocator and THP tests now run through the macro.

## m5-speed-profile

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-profile: the release profile's opt-levels re-chosen for speed, and how they were measured.** The owner's policy of 2026-10-10 puts speed first when the trade is sensible, with binary and memory gates catching accidental growth rather than forcing speed trade-offs. The size-first opt-levels (wave4-exitMemory, m4-integration-w2, m4-effects-media-w2) were surveyed crate by crate (P1–P31, the M5 speed survey) and every override on a path a person waits on was measured. Method: release builds (fat LTO, one codegen unit) in the container, the same flags as the shipped binary; each variant's bench binary copied out and run against the baseline in interleaved rounds (the order alternating each round), pinned to one performance core (`taskset -c 3`: the laptop's P-, E- and LP-E-cores otherwise mix frame times by ±20%), 10 rounds unless stated; figures are the minimum over the rounds of each run's median, with the paired win count. For each dependency change the control workloads, those that never run the changed crate (list scrolling for the image decoders, the decodes for material-colors), stayed within ±1%. The change to `strand` has no control workload, because its link-time pass reaches every crate (theme swaps moved −1.5%). It was judged instead on the paired wins (10 of 10 for list scrolling) and on an effect of −19 to −26%, many times the spread between rounds of one binary: unchanged workloads such as the calloop wake and the settings parse varied by under 2% across the 10 rounds of m5-speed-input. The benches run through strand's new `speed-bench` feature (`crates/strand/src/speed.rs`), which links strand-render's list_scroll_bench, theme_swap_bench, motion and svg tests into `strand`'s own library test, plus new measurements where none existed: image decodes at drawn size, the wallpaper seed, a `material(seed:)` solve, launcher search per keystroke, a Lottie's frames and first show, and the system fonts' first lookup. The library's own integration tests could not show the largest effect (m5-speed-strand), because each links in its own crate's session. Run with `scripts/container/run.sh cargo test --release -p strand --no-default-features --features speed-bench --lib speed:: -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`. `[profile.timing]` keeps `lto = false` for the gates' build time (P5); its comment now points at the feature as the way to time the shipped LTO. Baseline: laptop/m5-w0 at 27e2660, CPU-only `.text` 15,638,727 B and GPU 19,029,447 B as `cargo build --release` binaries (the per-change deltas below use these). Measured by budgets.rs's gate test, the ledger's method, the baseline profile gives 15,635,975 B and 19,015,687 B; this tree's crates/strand/Cargo.toml is used for both, so only the profile differs. Result by the gate test, after the review round (calloop and xkeysym back at "s", m5-speed-input): CPU-only **17,958,935 B** and GPU **21,854,807 B**, so +2,322,960 B (+14.9%) and +2,839,120 B (+14.9%). The first commit measured 17,965,143 and 21,862,167 B. Both builds are over their current gates (15,859,712 and 19,398,656 B). The brief leaves the gate constants to the integrator, so m5-speed-gates gives the proposed values with their reasons. **The GPU build's speed was not measured.** Every speed figure here is from the CPU-only build (`--no-default-features`). The GPU build is the default in every installed build, and it takes its +2,839,120 B and about +2 MB PSS on those figures. They should carry over: the CPU raster path, text, layout, decoding and dispatch are the same code, and GPU promotion is only for sustained large damage. The exception is Wayland: the GPU build uses libwayland's C backend (`client_system`), so m5-speed-input's dispatch gain is the CPU-only build's. The design bar's PSS on the real services went from 32,641 to 34,684 kB (CPU-only) and from 34,222 to 36,282 kB (GPU), about +2 MB of resident code: the GPU build is now over the 34,816 kB warning target, still under the 38,912 kB ceiling. These laptop figures are from the first commit; the review round's 6–7 KB of code is below their noise. GitHub's budgets job measured the first commit (run 38125161409, 9890c54): the GPU design bar on the real services is **37,817 kB** (35,659 kB at `94fe372`, so +2,158 kB). That is over the 34,816 kB target and 1,095 kB under the 38,912 kB ceiling. The full shell's bar is 38,843 kB and its OSD peak 54,753 kB, under design.md's 59–64 MB. m5-speed-gates proposes the memory re-base. The full shell measured 44,273 kB (CPU-only; 42,121 before) and 43,848 kB (GPU; 41,799 before) with 4 desktop entries. budgets.rs: `RELEASE_OPT_LEVELS` lists the 20 size overrides kept. The new `RELEASE_SPEED_CRATES` fails the same test if any of the 23 speed crates gets a size override back (checked: an added `velato = "z"` fails it). Since the review round, `sized_speed_crates` also fails on a `[profile.release] opt-level` or a wildcard `[profile.release.package."*"] opt-level` other than 3. The profile-wide level reaches `strand`, and through it the whole fat-LTO pass; the wildcard reaches every dependency without an override. `a_size_level_reaching_a_speed_crate_is_caught` checks it on each form ("s", 2, a quoted `"*"`, a single-quoted value, a trailing comment) and passes on explicit 3s. and the `.text` gate's message says a deliberate speed choice re-bases the gate with its measured reason instead of "code at event rates belongs at s or z". Each change follows, with the speed and size it was taken for.

## m5-speed-strand

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-strand: `strand` goes from opt "s" to 3, because fat LTO optimises the whole binary at the linking crate's level (P6 and the survey's Finding 0).** rustc runs the fat-LTO pass pipeline in the session of the crate that links the binary, with that session's opt-level: with `strand` at "s" the link-time pass over the merged module ran LLVM's Os LTO pipeline (inlining at the optimise-for-size threshold, no loop or SLP vectorisation of what it inlines) for render, text, layout, vello_cpu, skrifa and every other crate, whatever their own level. The per-crate opt 3 held only for each crate's own pre-link pass. The measurement confirms it: on top of the dependency changes below (strand at "s" → 3, nothing else changed), list scrolling's frame work went from 927 to 737 µs at 60 Hz (−21%, 10 of 10 rounds) and from 888 to 700 µs at 144 Hz (−21%), the launcher's opening animation from 1.90 to 1.41 ms a frame (−26%), a Lottie frame from 1,116 to 901 µs (−19%), an animated bindable SVG frame from 118 to 96 µs (−19%) and a still one from 59 to 47 µs (−20%), a lossless WebP decode −12%, a GIF frame −4%, a crossfade at buffer age 2 −9%, the `set { }` scope swaps −3 to −6% and the theme swaps −1.5%. None of these run strand's own code; it is all the link-time pass. Size: +1,940,928 B CPU-only and +2,452,224 B GPU, of which only part is strand's own code; the rest is cross-crate inlining in render and the GPU crates. Opt 2 was measured as the cheaper reading: it saved 196,672 B CPU-only and 431,744 B GPU against 3 but was slower everywhere (list scroll +11–14%, SVG +13–21%, Lottie frame +15%, launcher +11%), so 3 is taken. Splitting strand's cold glue into a library built for size, with the binary in a crate of its own at 3, would recover some of the size but moves a crate boundary (architecture.md) and the budgets test's `CARGO_BIN_EXE_strand`; not done here. Reload latency (bench::reload_latency_to_the_presented_frame, 4 interleaved rounds of 20 edits, not pinned) moved from 21.2 to 20.8 ms token p95, 21.2 to 20.7 ms markup p95 and 4.5 to 4.0 ms portal → painted (baseline and result both missed the advisory headless break on the laptop, as before): reload waits on the pipeline, not on this code.

## m5-speed-input

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-input: wayland-client, wayland-backend and smithay-client-toolkit go to 3; calloop and xkeysym stay at "s" (P15, P16, P21), measured in the review round.** The first commit took all five to 3 without a measurement. The review round added `speed::input_dispatch_cost`, in the shipped LTO session. A fake compositor on a socket pair answers 32 `wl_display.sync` requests with 64 events (`wl_callback.done` and `wl_display.delete_id`), all arriving in one read, as a burst of pointer motion does; only the client's side is timed. The test also times 32 messages through a calloop channel with the dispatch that drains them (the main ↔ logic wake), and 153 keysym names through xkeysym (a key press's name). Two release builds, CPU-only, interleaved 10 rounds on `taskset -c 3`: this profile against one with the five crates at "s". Wayland went from 18.0 to 13.7 µs per burst (−24%, 10 of 10 rounds). That is 0.21 µs an event against 0.28 µs: small next to a frame, but the cost of every event at up to 1 kHz pointer rates. The calloop wake measured 6.8 µs in both builds (0 of 10). The keysym names measured 0.3 µs in both, about 2 ns a name. The settings parse in the same runs (a control: toml_edit is at "s" in both) was 13.3 µs in both. So calloop and xkeysym go back to "s", which saves 6,208 B CPU-only and 7,360 B GPU (17,965,143 → 17,958,935 and 21,862,167 → 21,854,807 B). wayland-client and wayland-backend stay at 3 on the measured gain. smithay-client-toolkit stays at 3 without a figure of its own: its seat, pointer and keyboard handlers sit between the backend and strand's on the same per-event path, and opt 3 is the release default for a clearly hot path. In the GPU build the wire parse is libwayland's C (`client_system`), so this gain is the CPU-only build's; the Rust side of dispatch (proxy lookup, the event queue, sctk) is in both. The three crates cost about +15 KB CPU-only and +21 KB GPU at 3: the first commit's +21,184 / +28,480 B for five, less the 6,208 / 7,360 B measured for the two.

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-gates: the proposed `.text` and memory gates after the speed profile, for the integrator.** The review found that the first commit left the branch red, failing the budgets job's two `.text` steps (run 38125161409), with no new gate recorded. The brief for this work says the integrator sets the gate constants, so `TEXT_GATE_CPU`, `TEXT_GATE_GPU` and the PSS constants are unchanged here and the branch stays red on those steps until the integrator applies them. These are the proposals, computed with the plan's own rules. The speed profile is a **re-base**, not M5 spend, and every M5 allocation and the reserve are unchanged. The re-base is +2,322,960 B CPU-only and +2,839,120 B GPU (m5-speed-profile, gate-test figures against the same tree's baseline profile). **CPU-only gate: 18,219,008 B** (278 × 64 KiB). That is m5-plan's rule (the lowered baseline 15,620,615 B, plus the re-base, plus the 230,000 B allocation, rounded up to 64 KiB) applied to 18,173,575 B. It is 260,073 B over this tree's 17,958,935 B, of which 214,640 B is the allocations left and 45,433 B is rounding no stream may spend. **GPU gate: 22,282,240 B** (340 × 64 KiB, 21.25 MiB): 18.5 MiB plus the GPU re-base, rounded up. That is 427,433 B over 21,854,807 B, the same structure as before (the 230 KB, the GPU's own 40 KB and the rest). **Ledger reading** (m5-plan, "How size is measured"): Δ stays against M4's 15,657,671 / 19,041,095 B, so spend is Δ + 37,056 − 2,322,960 = **Δ − 2,285,904** CPU-only and Δ + 37,376 − 2,839,120 = **Δ − 2,801,744** GPU. This tree reads Δ +2,301,264 (spend 15,360 B, as before) and Δ +2,813,712 GPU (spend 11,968 B). **Memory**: the two-monitor design bar's 34,816 kB target and 38,912 kB ceiling (design.md, "Testing") were set for a size-built binary. The speed profile adds about 2 MB of resident code by choice: +2,060 kB on the laptop and +2,158 kB on GitHub. That leaves CI 1,095 kB under the ceiling for all of M5's waves 1 and later, so the ceiling would fail on unrelated work. The proposal raises both by 2 MiB, to a **36,864 kB target and a 40,960 kB ceiling**. That puts GitHub's 37,817 kB 3,143 kB under the ceiling again, about the margin it had before (3,253 kB at `94fe372`), and it still catches accidental growth. The policy says runtime memory is not sacred, and strand stays a tenth of quickshell's ~400–500 MB. The full shell's design.md 59–64 MB is not touched (54,753 kB peak). handoff.md calls the memory gates owner-confirmed and says agents do not change them (wave4-core). ## m5-speed-caches

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-caches: the paint cache, offscreen groups and image cache are sized for speed, not memory.** Under the owner's policy of 2026-10-10 (speed wins where the trade is sensible; runtime memory is not sacred; gates catch accidental bloat), the cache budgets that M0–M4 shrank for memory are raised: `PAINT_CACHE_BYTES` 4 → 32 MB and `MAX_ENTRY_BYTES` 2 → 16 MB (`strand-render/src/cache.rs`), `OFFSCREEN_BYTES` 4 → 32 MB (`offscreen.rs`), `IMAGE_CACHE_BYTES` 6 → 32 MB (`image.rs`) and, with it, `MAX_PLAYER_BYTES` 16 → 32 MB (`media/animated.rs`). design.md's "about 4 MB" (cached offscreen groups) and "6 MB LRU" (images) now read 32 MB, and architecture.md's paint-cache, image and offscreen paragraphs follow. Measured with a new ignored bench, `crates/strand-render/tests/cache_bench.rs` (`--profile timing`, base and new test binaries run interleaved, three rounds, in the container): a 2× launcher (600 × 460 logical, 1332 × 1116 px with its shadow's overhang; a gradient card with a 48 px shadow) repainted whole every frame (the fallback where the compositor cannot fade or scale the surface itself, a resize, an age-0 buffer; see the review paragraph below for the paths users hit) took 39.4–40.2 ms a frame with the 2 MB entry limit (the gradient dithered cell by cell and the shadow drawn directly on every paint, 0 kB cached) and takes 6.5–7.8 ms (8,542 kB cached); a blurred group of 1400 × 1000 px repainted whole took 123.8–126.0 ms a frame over the 4 MB offscreen budget (210 group draws in 210 frames) and takes 7.9–8.8 ms (one draw, 6,164 kB kept). A launcher of 300 apps at 2× (256 px PNG icons drawn at 96 px, 36 kB each) scrolled through, closed and opened again re-decoded all 300 icons with the 6 MB cache (300–336 ms of decodes, about 1.0–1.1 ms each, so a reopened launcher's first rows popped in late) and re-decodes none with 32 MB (`images.rs::a_reopened_launcher_decodes_no_icon_again`, run in both builds: 300 and 0). The player budget was not measured on its own (no bench shows a dropped player coming back); it moves with the image cache so that animations re-shown later are not decoded from frame 0 again. Tests that pinned the old figures now derive theirs from the constants (`images.rs::the_image_cache_holds_its_budget`, `image.rs`'s LRU test, `layers.rs::offscreen_groups_are_reused_bounded_and_freed_when_idle`, the player tests at 1300 and 1500 px) and `paint.rs::large_gradients_are_dithered_too` uses a 2700 × 1600 gradient (over the 16 MB entry limit, its band bound scaled with it).

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-caches: a stopped frame loop keeps what its frames did not use, for 30 s.** The wave3-pixels fixer r1 rule freed every paint-cache entry and offscreen group no frame of a run of paints used as soon as the frame loop stopped. With the larger entries above, a closed 2× launcher opened again rebuilt its shadow on its first frame and its gradient on its second: 48.1–53.0 ms, then 18.8–20.7 ms, before 6.0–6.6 ms frames (base, 2 MB entries, nothing cached: 39.4–40.2 ms every frame). The stop-time trim is gone (`Renderer::burst`, `Raster/PaintCache/Offscreen::trim_unused_since`), and `IDLE_FREE` goes from 10 s to 30 s, the GPU device's idle time: entries unused for that long are freed at the next paint or wake, still never at a wake of their own, so the M0 rule of no wakeup between minute ticks is untouched. The reopened launcher's first frame now takes 7.0–8.5 ms (`cache_bench.rs::reopen_first_frame_cost`). design.md's "freed when idle" holds with "idle" meaning 30 s unused; a shell with no clock keeps them until its next wake of any kind, which the owner's policy allows (memory, not a runtime cap). Test: `paint.rs::shadows_no_frame_used_go_once_idle` (kept when the loop stops, freed by the first paint after the idle time, rebuilt pixel for pixel).

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-caches (review): an entry over 2 MB is built only by a second frame that repaints all of it, and the launcher's real paths are measured.** The review found two faults. First, the 16 MB entry limit made a cold launcher open slower: its first frame built the shadow pixmap, and design.md says surface-level fades and scales cost no repaint (`wp_alpha_modifier_v1`, viewporter), so on most compositors a launcher opened more than `IDLE_FREE` after it closed paints exactly one whole frame and then partial frames. Second, the bench above measured only whole repaints. Now `PaintCache::shadow_in` and `gradient_in` take whether the frame repaints the entry's whole on-surface extent (`Raster::prepare`: a damage rect set that covers it). An entry up to `EAGER_ENTRY_BYTES` (2 MB, the old limit) keeps the old rule: a shadow is built at first sight, a gradient on a second frame's use. A larger one is built only when a second frame repaints all of it. Until then the raster draws it directly over the part each frame shows (gradients cell by cell, shadows through their clip). The GPU backend's `shadow` still builds at first sight, since its frames are whole and count no frames. The seen record lives `IDLE_FREE`, so a launcher reopened within 30 s builds on that reopen and draws from the cache on later ones. The new `cache_bench.rs::launcher_open_cost` measures the path users feel: the 2× launcher with nothing cached, one whole first frame, then eight keystrokes, each changing the eight result rows (only they repaint); then the same launcher reopened within the idle time. Base (`laptop/m5-w0`), the first speed commit (`16bb169`) and this change were built from the same bench file and run interleaved, four rounds, `--profile timing`, in the container. Cold open, first frame: base 36.8–40.0 ms, 16bb169 51.0–52.1 ms, now 37.6–39.7 ms. Mean typing frame: 3.73–4.09, 2.23–2.29 and 3.76–4.00 ms. Open plus eight keys: 66.6–72.7, 68.8–70.4 and 67.7–71.7 ms. A cold open is now as fast as base; 16bb169's first frame was 13 ms slower. Reopened within 30 s: the first reopen costs the same in base and now (36.6–41.4 against 36.7–41.7 ms; 16bb169 49.1–52.7 ms), and so does the second, which builds both entries in its whole frame (36.8–42.5 against 36.4–41.6 ms). ## m5-speed-thp

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-thp: THP stays off except for the largest pixel buffers, where the kernel allows it.** C1 of the speed survey. THP for the whole process stays off: it cost about 55 MB of PSS against 25–32 MB (wave3-pixels, wave4-exitMemory), and the render benches run with THP fully on and fully off (a `prctl` wrapper around the same test binary, glibc's allocator, interleaved, three rounds) differ by only a few percent per frame (4K crossfade blend 3.28–3.38 ms on, 3.42–3.60 ms off). The cold case differs a lot: the first 4K crossfade of a run, whose 33 MB snapshot is fresh memory, took 3.5–5.6 ms with THP and 14.5–15.9 ms without. So `strand_services::child::thp_off` now asks for `PR_SET_THP_DISABLE` with `PR_THP_DISABLE_EXCEPT_ADVISED` (Linux 6.18; the plain flag on older kernels, as before), and `strand_render::hugepage` advises `MADV_HUGEPAGE` on buffers of at least 8 MiB before they are first written (a crossfade's snapshot; see the review paragraph below for what changed). mimalloc does not override the flag (its own `prctl` runs only when `PR_GET_THP_DISABLE` reads 0), and `restore_in_child` gives children the exact inherited setting, the new flag included. Measured with the wrapper set to the new mode against fully off, same binary, four rounds: the 4K crossfade's worst (first) swap 3.6–5.3 ms against 14.0–23.5 ms, its median and blend frames unchanged (2.29–2.81 against 2.35–2.63 ms; 3.08–3.67 against 3.37–3.62 ms per blend). No bar, toast or icon buffer reaches 8 MiB, so the bar's memory has no huge page (budgets.rs and demo.rs still read `AnonHugePages: 0 kB`). `THP_enabled:` in `/proc/<pid>/status` reads 1 in the new mode, and main.rs's tests ask `prctl`. CI's runner kernels fall back to the old behaviour. `.text`: GPU +512 B, CPU-only +448 B (the first version).

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-thp (review): the snapshot is its own mapping, kept as one spare, and the advice goes with it.** The review found three faults in the first version. (1) Advising the cache and offscreen pixmaps did nothing at fault time: vello_common's `Pixmap::new` writes every element (`vec![PremulRgba8::from_u32(0); n]`, no zeroed-alloc path for a user struct), so the pages were already small when `advise` ran. All that was left was khugepaged collapsing them later. (2) `MADV_HUGEPAGE` sets `VM_HUGEPAGE` on the address range, not on the allocation. mimalloc serves 8–16 MiB objects from ordinary segments and reuses them after a free, so heap blocks handed out later in that range (including the shadow's scratch buffer, freed at once) could become huge-page backed: the PSS bloat THP-off exists to prevent. (3) No test read huge pages after a crossfade. Now: the cache, offscreen and scratch advice is gone (no benefit was measured for it). `strand_render::hugepage::HugeBuf` replaces `advise`: a buffer of at least 8 MiB on Linux is its own anonymous `mmap`, 2 MiB aligned and advised before its first write, and it never touches the heap. The crossfade snapshot (`swap.rs`) is a `HugeBuf`. Unmapping on every drop made every crossfade fault its 33 MB in again: medians 14.0–15.2 ms with THP off and 3.3–3.8 ms in the new mode, against 2.3–2.6 ms when 16bb169's heap reused the freed block. So a dropped mapping is kept as the one spare. The next snapshot of the same mapped size reuses it with its pages in (copied over in full, or cleared when it must start from zero). `hugepage::trim_idle`, called with the paint cache's trims (every paint and wake, never a wake of its own), unmaps the spare once it has been unused for `IDLE_FREE`, advice and all, and a buffer of another size replaces it. `theme_swap_bench.rs::a_4k_surface_crossfade_is_measured`, 16bb169's and this change's binaries interleaved, each under a `prctl` wrapper in the new mode and fully off, four rounds. Round 1 ran while another session built, so these are rounds 2–4. New mode: median 2.35–2.67 ms (age 1) and 2.54–2.59 ms (age 2) against 2.43–2.48 and 2.70–2.78 ms; worst (first) swap 3.2–4.8 ms against 4.5–5.5 ms. Fully off (CI's kernels): medians 2.45–2.53 and 2.51–2.61 ms against 2.55–3.05 and 2.62–2.68 ms; worst 11.8–15.5 ms against 13.8–15.5 ms. Blend per frame unchanged (3.39–3.62 against 3.48–3.69 ms). Tests: `hugepage.rs::large_buffers_are_their_own_aligned_mapping` (aligned mapping, spare reused and cleared, unmapped by the trim); `main.rs::thp_stays_on_only_for_advised_buffers` now reads the buffer's own VMA in `/proc/self/smaps` (at least 16 MiB of a written 32 MB `HugeBuf` huge), so the allocator's state cannot flake it. After the spare is trimmed it checks that the mapping is gone and that 32 MB of small heap blocks, written, leave the process with `AnonHugePages: 0`. demo.rs's `assert_thp_off` again requires `THP_enabled: 0` where the kernel lacks `PR_THP_DISABLE_EXCEPT_ADVISED` (asked in a throwaway child's `pre_exec`) and 1 where it has it, besides the resident huge pages. budgets.rs's full-shell runs above read `AnonHugePages: 0 kB`.

## m5-speed-gpu-drop

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-gpu-drop: what a promotion after the device dropped costs; `DROP_AFTER` stays 30 s.** C10 of the speed survey. `crates/strand-gpu/tests/start_cost.rs` (ignored, `--profile timing`) times the GPU thread and device starting with a surface attached, the first frame (vello_gpu's pipelines built) and a second frame, four times in one process. On the laptop's Intel GPU (ANV, `scripts/container/gpu.sh`): 109.8 ms to start the first time and 22.2–25.1 ms after, first frames 5.6–7.2 ms, second frames 0.7–0.9 ms. On lavapipe: 74.9–119.0 ms to start, a 168 ms first frame the first time and 7.5–8.2 ms after. All of it runs on the GPU thread while the CPU keeps drawing, so a re-promotion delays the switch by about 30 ms past promotion's 500 ms window and stalls no frame. Keeping pipelines across drops would save nothing measurable, since Mesa's in-process shader cache already brings later first frames down to about 7 ms. The 30 s drop stays (design.md; holding the device costs 20–40 MB and changing it is the owner's call).

## m5-speed-policy

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed-policy: deliberate speed reverts are charged to the gate, not to the ledger.** m5-owner Q7 ("reclaims are behaviour-neutral only"; no opt-level cut on a gated hot path) and m5-plan's rule that a stream "never raises an opt-level on a hot path to make room" were written when size came first. Under the owner's policy of 2026-10-10 a revert made for speed (a cache sized back up, a slower algorithm kept for `.text` replaced, an opt-level raised on a hot path) is not a stream's spend: it lands with its measured speed gain and its `.text` cost, and the integrator raises the gate by that recorded, judged amount instead of taking it from the 230 KB allocation. Behaviour-neutral reclaims stay as Q7 says. m5-plan's Ground rules now say so. The rest of the code-level survey stays as it is: the wallpaper decode's bounds (C16: the 1/8 JPEG decode is also the faster one), the palette memo (C17), the glyph atlas, notification history and Lottie asset bounds (C18, bounds against hostile input), promotion's 500 ms rule (C11, a design rule), the radix-2 FFT (C9: one 2,048-point transform at most per frame, off the render thread; realfft would cost 290–846 KB), the IPC codec, sway adapter and image-webp choices (C13–C15, no speed effect), the duplicated JPEG and WebP decoders (C12, size only, left to the size stream), and the feature cuts that cited `.text` (C19, features rather than speed, the owner's call).

**2026-10-11 · m5-speed: the paint's idle trim reads its clock before the frame touches its entries.** GitHub's test job at `31da659` (run 38128685562) failed `strand-render/tests/paint.rs::shadows_no_frame_used_go_once_idle` (329,168 B expected after the full repaint, 292,704 B kept): the flake speed-code saw once locally. `Raster::paint` ran `prepare` (which builds and touches the frame's entries) and only then read `Instant::now()` for `trim_idle`, so on a slow runner an entry the frame built early was already older than the test's 20 ms idle time and was freed by the same paint. The clock is now read before `prepare`; `trim_idle` measures with `saturating_duration_since`, so anything touched after it is never idle. `cache.rs::entries_touched_after_the_trim_clock_stay` holds that. In production the idle time is 30 s, so the race needed a 30 s frame; the fix is for correctness of the rule, not a user-visible change. ## m5-open-spectrum

**2026-10-11 · m5-open-spectrum: a diff retargets the fed nodes' producers, so a resting spectrum follows its device without a frame.** Root cause of `wm_audio_shells.rs::a_test_tone_lifts_a_spectrum_bar` failing on GitHub (runs 38065740030, 38076927579, 38116737469), not an audio-thread race. The feed taps (`run/feeds.rs`) were synced only after a paint (`Host::painted`), a surface detach and a producer's send. A spectrum's source is `audio.sink`'s id as text, which reads 0 until the `audio` service publishes its first state, so when the bar's first frame comes before that, the spectrum is tapped for device 0, which matches no PipeWire node, and no meter starts. When the real id arrives, logic's diff changes only the spectrum's `source`. A resting spectrum draws the same dots for any device, so `Renderer::update` finds the records unchanged and clears the surface's dirty flag; no frame follows, `painted` never runs, and the tap stays on device 0 for good (nothing else repaints a static bar). That matches the failures' detail: no `audio: a meter reads device` line and `strand-levels missing, hearing []`. The `reading the default metadata again` line in run 38116737469 is incidental (it was absent in 38076927579). Locally PipeWire usually answers before the first frame, so the test passed; on a slower runner the order flips. Reproduced deterministically in the container by sleeping 3 s before the audio service's loop started (a temporary, uncommitted hook): the unfixed tree failed with the GitHub signature exactly, and the fixed tree passed in 3.4 s. Fix: `Host::apply_diff` (what `demo::apply` now calls) syncs the feeds after every diff, so `take_feed_demand` sees the new source at once. It reads the last frame's records, so a node a diff hides or moves still changes its producer at the next paint, as before. The fix is in product code; the test was right. `demo/host.rs::a_resting_spectrum_follows_its_device_without_a_frame` checks that no frame follows the source change and that the tap moves to the new device; it fails without the sync.

**2026-10-11 · m5-open-budgets: the hardware GPU leg's leak tripwire is growth between cycles; the after-drop bounds are backstops.** `PRESENTED_SLACK_KB` (12 MiB after the first cycle's drop) was a weak tripwire: the presented leg's residue spread 4.6–8.1 MiB, so a small leak hid in the spread and a bad run neared the bound. Seventeen runs of `gpu_idle.rs` on renderD128 (`gpu.sh`, release, three or four cycles each, thirteen presenting with `STRAND_GPU_PRESENT=1` and four reading back; some with temporary per-mapping diagnostics) show where it comes from. Presenting, the first cycle left **4,726–8,506 kB** over the pre-GPU baseline in thirteen runs (up to 8,833 kB after a later cycle); reading back, 4,611–6,123 kB in four (up to 7,466 kB after a later cycle), so the readback leg's 6 MiB was 21 kB from failing. The residue is the same parts each time: strand's own GPU code paged in (1.8–2.0 MB), mimalloc's pages (1.84 MB), libstdc++ (0.5–0.6 MB) and anonymous memory (2.8–3.6 MB), most of it one glibc arena of Mesa's (a 64 MiB-aligned heap of about 7.4 MB, Mesa allocating with glibc while Rust uses mimalloc). The `malloc_trim` after the GPU thread ends returns that arena's free pages only as its fragmentation allows, so its resident part sits at about 0.3 or 2.2–3.0 MB and moves by 2–2.7 MiB between cycles in some runs (+1,960, +2,048, +2,100, −2,053, −2,742 kB) and between runs. Timing is not a source: PSS read 1, 3 and 6 s after each drop was flat but for one transient +457 kB that settled within 3 s; the huge-page spare (`hugepage.rs`) is never made here (only the 4K crossfade uses it); no growth across cycles otherwise (36–66 kB after the second, then flat within 4 kB, but for one readback run's third cycle, +531 kB over its second). So: the hardware leg runs three cycles by default (`HARDWARE_CYCLES`; `STRAND_GPU_IDLE_CYCLES` still overrides, at least two), and every later cycle's PSS after the drop must be within **4 MiB** of the first (`PSS_SLACK_KB`, raised from 3 MiB for the arena's 2.7 MiB swing and applied to lavapipe too, which measured −116 kB). That is the leak tripwire: what the first cycle leaves is paid once, a leaked device (20–40 MB) trips it on the second cycle, and a leaked swapchain (640×420, about 3.2 MB) by the third. The absolute bounds become backstops checked after every cycle: **16 MiB presenting** (`PRESENTED_SLACK_KB`, about 7 MiB over the worst) and **12 MiB reading back** (`HARDWARE_SLACK_KB`, about 4.7 MiB over the worst), both still under what a device held past the drop leaves. The final code passed its presented and readback runs (the lavapipe leg, `run.sh` in debug, passed at 3 MiB with −116 kB). `scripts/gpu-measure.sh` prints the 16 MiB backstop (not run). architecture.md's hardware-leg paragraph, features.md's GPU boxes and handoff.md's open item 1 say so.

## m5-open-reload

**2026-10-11 · m5-open-reload: why `reload_latency` misses on the laptop: the CPU idles down between edits; the gate is right, and the last-good cache write leaves the reload path.** handoff.md's open note (token p95 about 20–21 ms headless against a break near 19.9 ms; GitHub passes) named the power state as an unconfirmed cause. It is now confirmed, by experiment rather than inference. Machine: Intel Core Ultra X7 358H, 16 CPUs (0–3 P-cores at 4.7–4.8 GHz, 4–11 E-cores at 3.7, 12–15 low-power E-cores at 3.3), on AC, `powersave` governor, `balance_performance` energy preference, `balanced` platform profile, idle states down to C10; load 3.5–7 from the owner's desktop and other agents. All runs `STRAND_LATENCY_ROUNDS=50 cargo test --profile timing -p strand --lib bench::reload_latency_to_the_presented_frame` in the container at `2fedfa2`. (1) **Pinning changes nothing.** Twelve interleaved runs, `taskset` on all CPUs, the P-cores, the E-cores and the low-power E-cores: token p95 20.6 / 20.4 / 20.2, 19.6 / 20.7 / 20.9, 20.2 / 20.0 / 20.1 and 21.0 / 20.6 / 21.2 ms; 11 of 12 missed. Hybrid scheduling is not the cause. (2) **One busy core elsewhere fixes it.** The bench on CPUs 0–14 with a shell busy loop alone on CPU 15 (which the test never uses), interleaved with the same run without it, three each: with the loop 17.9 / 18.1 / 18.0 ms, all passing (the sampled clocks of CPUs 0–4 and 8 averaged 1,630 / 1,568 / 1,613 MHz over the run); without it 21.0 / 20.7 / 20.7 ms, all missing (726 / 873 / 783 MHz). A loop that adds no work to the test's CPUs can only help by keeping the package out of deep idle and its clocks up, so the miss is the power state between edits: the bench idles 250 ms between saves, and each save's few milliseconds of work start on cold, slow cores. This is also why earlier laptop runs passed under heavy load (laptop-decisions, m5-size reclaim 3's "bimodal under load") and why GitHub's always-on runners pass. (3) **Where the time goes**, from a temporary patch (not committed) printing `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` at each hand-off, token edits, median idle → with the loop: save → inotify read 0.16 → 0.09 ms; the coalesce to the batch 15.23 → 15.16; watcher → worker awake 0.07 → 0.03; compile 0.78 → 0.41; worker → logic awake 0.07 → 0.04; commit (`Instance::reload`) 0.88 → 0.47; logic → main thread 0.05 → 0.02; `Renderer::apply` 0.89 → 0.41; applied → painted 1.43 → 0.52; painted → presented 0.39 → 0.21; total 20.0 → 17.5 (p95 21.0 → 17.9). The only fixed wait is design.md's 15 ms coalesce, the same in both modes; thread wakes are under 0.1 ms; every stage of CPU work takes about twice as long when idle (about 4.5 ms against 2.1 ms in all). Nothing sleeps or polls in the path. (4) **The gate stays.** The monitor model (35 ms at p95 with a uniform vblank) leaves about 4.5 ms of work after the 15 ms coalesce; the laptop does it in 2.1 ms when its clocks are up and GitHub passes, so the gate is not mis-specified, and design.md's budget is a product promise on a user's machine, which is not at 700 MHz while someone types. The container suite's timing steps stay advisory on the laptop (laptop-open); `STRAND_STRICT_TIMING=1` runs passed there with a busy loop on a core of its own beside them. (5) **A real cost found on the way: the last-good cache write was on the reload path.** `Loader::commit` wrote the cache (read the manifest, a temporary directory, the files, two renames, a removal) before the compiler worker sent the build to the logic thread. The bench passed no cache, so it never saw this; `strand run` always has one. Timed in the traced worker with the cache on btrfs (the owner's `~/.cache`): 0.50 ms median, 0.60 p95, per reload. Now `commit` only marks the sources unstored, and `Loader::store_cache` (architecture.md's loader paragraph) writes them; the worker calls it after sending each build, and once at the start of its thread for the boot's commit (off the shell's start too). Before → after, interleaved, three runs each with the cache on btrfs, idle CPU: the worker's wake → build sent 1.25 / 1.27 ms → 0.79 / 0.77 / 0.76 ms; token total median 20.56 / 20.59 ms → 20.18 / 20.11 / 20.00 ms, p95 21.19 / 21.13 ms → 20.93 / 20.47 / 20.67 ms (the first before run, which ran partly with its clocks up, median 17.8 ms, is left out). It does not by itself pass the idle laptop: what is left is the power state. The bench now runs the worker with a cache, as `strand run` does (on `/dev/shm`, beside the config), so a write back on the path would show in it. Tests: `crates/strand-compiler/tests/loader.rs::the_cache_is_written_by_store_cache_after_the_commit` (a commit writes nothing; `store_cache` writes once, then nothing until the next commit) and `crates/strand/src/live.rs::a_reload_is_sent_before_its_sources_are_cached` (the cached manifest is made a FIFO, so a store blocks in its first read: the build must arrive while it is blocked; with the store moved back before the send the test fails after its 10 s wait). After the change, the step itself (`--lib reload_latency`, both tests): idle, token p95 20.6 / 20.3 ms headless against breaks of 20.1 / 19.8 (missed), `reload_latency_meets_its_budget` 19.4 / 20.1 ms (passed); with the busy loop on CPU 15, 17.9 ms against 19.6 (passed) and 17.3 ms. Not taken: further cuts in strand-render (a token edit's `SetTokens` marks every surface for layout; its apply is 0.89 ms against a markup edit's 0.52 when idle, and the paint after it is no slower than a markup edit's, so the most it could save is about 0.4 ms) and the compiler (0.8 ms for a whole-program compile): neither would close a 2.4 ms gap made by the clock.

Each is placed at the first level whose build needs it, by design.md's test, "does it remove a concept, or add one?": a construct that is another face of one a level already teaches goes there, and one that adds a concept no build of that level needs waits for the level that does. Levels 1–3 build design.md's bar (a) exactly (m5-owner Q15), so everything bar (a) writes is at level 3 or below. **2026-10-11 · m5-docs: what spec.md freezes beyond syntax.** Q5 freezes "syntax" and "builtin schema entries" but does not say whether diagnostics, numbers or the CLI are part of the language. spec.md reads it by design.md's principle that the language is what a program means: diagnostic codes and message wording are not frozen (they are how errors are reported, and freezing them would turn every better message into a 2.0 change), but which programs are accepted is: a program accepted in 1.x stays accepted with the same meaning, while a program rejected may become accepted when a rule is added. Numbers that change what a program does (15 ms coalesce, 250 ms overlay delay and settings write delay, 30 writes per second, 30 s monitor retention, 4 px query hysteresis, 5 s service stop) are frozen; performance targets and memory budgets are not. CLI commands, flags and paths are frozen only where spec.md section 13 names them (`get`, `set`, `toggle`, `call`, `clear`, `watch`, `reload`, the path spellings, the D-Bus name with its may-change caveat), since everything else is tooling that M5 is still building.

The guide's strand-check test (`every_guide_block_checks`) settles (3) and (4) when it lands; it needs a build slot and is not part of this commit. (Amended 2026-10-11, m5-docs review round 1: (1) landed with S-tools and S-palette and is checked; (3) and (4) are settled by tests, below; (2) stays prose.)
