**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 1): the control centre shows the power profile and does not set it, because the checker rejects writes to a config service's `rw` field.** Written step by step, `control.strand`'s `on click { ppd.profile = p }` failed with `check::read_only` ("cannot assign this"). `check/expr.rs` `rw_root` walks to the service's `Def` and asks `writable_place`, which accepts `State` and `Settings` and returns `NotWritable::Other` for `DefKind::Service`, so no `rw` field of a `service … from …` can be assigned or bound with `<->`. design.md ("Service fields are writable only where the service marks them `rw`") and the runtime (`strand/src/services/custom.rs`: "an `rw` field written (`ppd.profile = "performance"`, `<-> ppd.profile`) is an item write") both mean it to work. The checker is strand-compiler's, outside this stream, so it is reported rather than changed: the proposed fix is one arm in `rw_root`, `ExprKind::Def(d) if matches!(self.defs[d.0 as usize].kind, DefKind::Service(_)) => return Ok(())`, with a checker test and a runtime test that the write reaches the `custom` store. Until it lands, the Power tile lists the three profiles and highlights the one in use, which keeps the `for … key p` loop the section teaches, and the prose says that the assignment is rejected today. When the fix lands, the tile's buttons come back with `on click { ppd.profile = p }`, and `every_guide_block_checks` will check them.

**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 1): every pin draws one icon.** The dock's inner `for app in apps.all.filter(…)` drew nothing for an uninstalled pin, but `on drop`'s `at` counts the row's drawn children with the dragged one left out (strand-render `input.rs` `drop_index`), while `pins.move(k, at)` counts pins, so a hidden pin before the drop point put the dragged one a place off. The pin now reads `let app = apps.all.find(a => a.id == p.app)` and always draws one `image`, `app?.icon ?? "application-x-executable"`, faded while `app == null`; `app?.launch()` does nothing then. A reader can also see a missing pin and right-click it away, which the old dock did not allow. `the_guide_dock_reorders_every_pin_and_keeps_the_order` boots with Nautilus missing, pushes foot, drops firefox at 2 and expects `[org.gnome.Nautilus, foot, firefox]`, before and after a restart; against the old block it fails at the icon count (1 drawn for 2 pins). (Amended 2026-10-11, m5-docs review round 3: the counts agree along one dock; a drop on another monitor's dock counts that dock's own icon for the pin, below.)

**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 1): `temps` reads one chip.** `= temp1_input` is the first `temp1_input` in `sensors -j`'s output, found depth first over keys in sorted order (serde_json without `preserve_order`), so `acpitz-acpi-0` or `amdgpu-pci-*` came before the CPU's chip. The command is now `["sensors", "-j", "coretemp-*"]`, Intel's CPU driver, whose `temp1_input` is `Package id 0`; the prose says to write `"k10temp-*"` on AMD (`Tctl` is its `temp1_input`), to run `sensors` to see the chip names, and that with no such chip the service fails and `temps.cpu` stays `0`. A key path cannot name the chip instead: `coretemp-isa-0000` is not an identifier, and a string key is one segment. Nothing in the container has those chips, so this is not tested. (Amended 2026-10-11, m5-docs review round 2: the service does not fail, below.)

**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 1): locking before sleep waits.** Level 4 now gives `swayidle -w before-sleep 'strand set lock.locked true && sleep 1'`: without `-w` swayidle lets the machine suspend as soon as the command starts, and `strand set` returns when the cell is written, not when the compositor grants `ext-session-lock`, so the unlocked desktop could show on resume. No command waits for the grant today (`lock_shown()` follows the compositor's `Locked`, but nothing reports it to the command line); a `strand set` that waits for it would be S-ipc's, and the pause stands in until then.

**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 2): level 5's `from file` reads `/etc/hostname`, and the page states the `key=value` limit.** `service os from file "/etc/os-release" { name: text = PRETTY_NAME }` failed on real systems. strand-services' `Document::parse` (`custom.rs`) reads a file as pairs only when every non-blank line is a pair whose key has no whitespace. openSUSE Tumbleweed's `# VERSION="…"` line therefore made the whole file `Document::Text`, and every field reads that text whole. The parser also strips double quotes only, so a `PRETTY_NAME='…'` kept its quotes. Comment handling is not the guide's to fix: custom.rs belongs to strand-services, and the request to read `#` comment lines and single quotes as os-release(5) defines them goes to its owner. The step instead reads a file the parser handles on every system: `service host from file "/etc/hostname" { name: text }`, one word read whole, and the header shows `host.name`. The prose says what the parser does, including the limit (pairs only when every line is a pair, double quotes only) and why the step avoids os-release. `the_guide_file_services_read_one_value` parses a sample of each file a level-5 `from file` reads with `Document::parse` (openSUSE's os-release with its comment, and a one-word hostname). It requires every field to read one value with no newline and no quote; against the old block it fails with the whole os-release text. `the_guide_states_the_pairs_limit` pins the limit the page states, so if strand-services lifts the limit, the test fails and the page changes with it. (Amended 2026-10-11, m5-docs review round 3: it reads `/proc/sys/kernel/hostname`, below.)

**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 2): a missing sensor chip is a warning on stderr, not a failed service.** Round 1's prose said that with no chip of that name "the service fails, says so in `strand watch`". It does neither. For a non-zero exit, `poll_command` (strand-services `custom.rs`) logs ``log::warn!("`{}` failed ({status})")`` and returns `None`; `run_poll` skips that update and polls again without returning an error. `strand watch` sends config warnings, host notices and `file` notices, never a service's poll failures. Level 5 now says that `sensors` fails every 5 s and `temps.cpu` stays `0`. It also says that nothing marks the service failed or reaches `strand watch`, and that the only trace is a `strand: WARN strand_services::custom: ...` line in the terminal running `strand run` (level 1 has the reader keep one open). Whether a poll command that keeps failing should reach `strand watch` is for strand-services and S-ipc to decide, not the guide; this round only makes the page true. The change is prose about another crate's behaviour, so it has no test here.

**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 2): the component-token override is resolved, not just shown.** Round 1 said `the_guide_control_centre_overrides_a_component_token` settles unverified item (4), "a `set` override beats a component token's default" (spec.md 9.4). The test read only the SceneMirror's text, and that text would not change if render stopped reading a node's `tokens=` level for dotted component names, or if each `Tile` instance gained its own inner level that shadowed the row's. The test now resolves every tile's `pad: $Tile.pad` the way strand-render's flatten does (`TokenScope` over the global table, then each ancestor's `Prop::Tokens`, nearest last). It asserts that a tile under the row resolves to `$space.2`'s value and every other tile to `$space.3`'s, and that the two values differ. strand-dev gains `strand-scene` and `strand-services` as dev-dependencies for this test and the `from file` one above.

**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 3): a drop on another monitor's dock lands one place on when it passes that dock's copy of the pin; the page says so, and the fix is strand-render's.** A dock is a `bar`, so there is one on each monitor, each drawing every pin. A drag that leaves its surface is handed to the compositor (`Router`, `PointerLeave` sets `handed`), and a `DragDrop` on another surface places it with `drop_target_at`/`drop_index` there. `drop_index` (`input.rs`) leaves out only the dragged source node, which is on the first dock, so the second dock counts its own icon for the same pin; `pins.move` takes the pin out before it inserts, so a drop past that icon is one too high (pins `[firefox, nautilus, foot]`, firefox dropped on DP-2 between Files and Foot: `at` 2, order `[nautilus, foot, firefox]`). Along one dock the counts agree, and a drop before the other dock's copy is right. No config can tell the two cases apart (`on drop` hears the pin and `at`, not where the drag began), and moving the dock to one monitor drops the design's "a `bar` is on every monitor" default, so the guide keeps its dock on every monitor, with design.md's `on drop(p: Pin, at: int) { pins.move(p.app, at) }`, and its prose states the limit ("dropped past that dock's own icon for the same pin, it lands one place further on"). `the_guide_dock_drops_where_the_pointer_is` (`crates/strand-dev/tests/guide.rs`) drives the guide's dock on two mock monitors through `strand_render::Router` over a laid-out `Renderer` (strand-render and strand-text become strand-dev dev-dependencies), replacing the hand-written `at` the round-1 test passed: along DP-1 the drop is exact, across to DP-2 before the copy it is exact, and past it the order is the off-by-one one; when render is fixed that assertion fails and the page changes with it. Proposed for strand-render's owner (no interface change): `drop_index` also leaves out, on a surface other than the drag's origin, a row that is the same `for` item as the source on another instance of the same surface (the same key under the same `for`, which the scene does not carry today and logic would have to mark, for example a `Prop::DragKey` set beside `Prop::Drag`); or logic, mapping `DropPayload::Node` back to its value in `run/lists.rs` `drop_args`, lowers `at` by one when the target's `for` holds the same key before `at`. Either is an architecture.md change to the drag-and-drop bullet ("`at` a global row index" gains "with every copy of the dragged item left out"), so it is reported, not made.

**2026-10-11 · m5-docs (review round 3): level 5's `host` reads `/proc/sys/kernel/hostname`.** Round 2's `/etc/hostname` is not one word on every system: hostname(5) allows `#` comment lines, which `Document::parse` keeps in the text every field reads whole, and its `?`/`$` tokens are expanded only when the name is applied; and the file may be absent (Fedora leaves the static hostname unset), which `run_file` reads as no document, every field `Null`, a blank header. The kernel's `/proc/sys/kernel/hostname` always exists and holds the one name the machine runs under, as strand-services' own `system` service reads it first (`system.rs` `hostname`). It is a regular file with no inotify events, so the page says a rename shows once the service starts again (on restart, or after nothing has read it for a few seconds) instead of "it follows the file". `the_guide_host_service_reads_the_kernels_name` runs the page's `host` declaration through `strand_services::Services` on the real file (the watch arms on procfs and the field reads the kernel's name, one line) and shows that a commented `/etc/hostname` reads its comment; `FILE_SAMPLES` holds the new path.

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs (wave 3): `docs/reference/` is generated from the schemas, committed, and checked current.** `strand-dev reference [dir]` (`crates/strand-dev/src/reference.rs`) writes six pages from `Schema::builtin_with` of every builtin service's schema text and the entries' `///` docs: `README.md` (the index and counts), `elements.md` (each element's props with types, defaults and docs, its events, and where it may appear: a surface, no children, only directly inside another), `services.md`, `types.md` (records, enums, aliases, opaque types), `functions.md` and `tokens.md` (the 62 palette roles and the 25 base tokens). Plugin schema files in `$XDG_DATA_HOME` are never read, so the pages are the same on every machine; a plugin's own entries are its author's to document. The pages are committed, not built at publish time, so a reader of the repository sees them and a schema change shows up in review as a page diff: `reference::tests::the_reference_is_current` regenerates into memory and fails on any difference with the command that fixes it, `every_schema_entry_is_on_a_page` fails on an entry with an empty doc cell, and `writing_removes_pages_no_longer_generated` keeps the directory to exactly the generated pages. The guide's README and architecture.md's `strand-dev` section point at it.

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs (wave 3): the ladder test, and the constructs taught in prose.** `crates/strand-dev/tests/ladder.rs` applies every guide step in page order, compiles the config, walks the HIR of the file each step wrote, and names every construct it meets (an HIR node the walk cannot name fails the test, so a new construct is placed before the guide uses it). `no_guide_block_uses_a_construct_above_its_level` holds design.md's rule; `each_construct_is_taught_at_its_level` holds the levels in order: a construct's first step is at its own level, never later, since a later first use means its placement is wrong. Seven constructs are placed at a level whose build does not write them, and the test accepts them only when that level's page names them in inline code: `else` and `exit` (level 3, first written in level 4's lock screen and toasts), `@reset` (level 4, one attribute shown inline rather than a step that prints the file twice more), `canvas`, a shader and SVG layer selectors (level 5's escape hatches, which need a reader's own `.wgsl` or layered SVG, or whose paint order is not pinned), and `service from listen` (level 5; its useful commands are compositor-specific). Writing them as steps instead would add files no build needs, which adds concepts to a page rather than removing them. `the_ladder_is_the_guides_table` holds the test's table to the guide README's rows, and `the_walk_finds_constructs_above_a_level` proves the walk catches a level-3 construct in a level-2 block.

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs (wave 3): the freeze review.** The four points the draft spec marked unverified are settled by the code and pinned by `crates/strand-dev/tests/spec.rs`, and spec.md says "frozen". (1) Section 7.1: a bare number where a length is expected is logical pixels, the same as `px`; where an angle is expected it is degrees; where a duration is expected it is a load error, so `stagger: 2` never means 2 ms or 2 s (`a_bare_number_for_a_length_is_logical_pixels`, and the end of `mixed_unit_comparisons`). (2) Section 7.2: an ordering comparison takes two plain numbers, two values of one kind, a length, angle or percentage beside a plain number (which takes its unit), or a length beside a percentage; a duration compares only with a duration (`1s < 500ms` is accepted, `1s < 2` is not), and lengths, angles and durations never mix (`mixed_unit_comparisons`, eight accepted and five rejected with `check::type_mismatch`). A length beside a percentage compares the numbers as written, since a comparison has no size to resolve the percentage against; this is recorded as the frozen behaviour rather than tightened, because the checker accepts it today and rejecting it would break a config that checks. (3) Section 10.4: `@reset` resets its cell on every reload that commits the declaration with the attribute, whether the edit was to its file or another, and the cell is kept again once the attribute is removed (`at_reset_resets_on_every_reload_that_keeps_it`); level 4's prose says to take it out after one save. (4) Section 11: a settings file that does not exist gives every field its default and reading it creates nothing (`a_missing_settings_file_gives_every_default`).

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs (wave 3): the newcomer test, and what each step's reload is predicted to keep.** `crates/strand/tests/m5/newcomer.rs::the_guide_builds_bar_a_on_two_outputs` is the newcomer exit's automated layer. It runs `strand new` in an empty `$HOME` (the guide's first block must be the file it writes), `strand run` with no directory on a headless sway with acceptance.rs's two outputs and `STRAND_MOCK=acceptance`, and `strand watch --json`; then it saves each of levels 1 to 3's twelve later steps over its file in place. After each it requires the save's `reload` event committing that file with no diagnostics, `strand check` with no diagnostic, the kept and reset cells the identity rules predict (`PREDICTED`), and each output's bar against `crates/strand/tests/refs/newcomer/stepNN_headless{1,2}.png`; last it clicks the clock and matches the calendar. The prediction: levels 1 and 2 declare no `state`, so nothing is kept or reset; level 3's `clock.strand` and the `bar.strand` that first places `Clock` add `Clock.open` on each bar, which is new, not kept; every later save keeps both `Clock.open` cells (the closed calendar's `month` is not mounted) and resets nothing. `strand watch` names a kept cell by component and cell (`Clock.open`), once per instance, not by its monitor; the test compares the sorted lists. The references were made with `STRAND_UPDATE_REFS=1` on the mock's frozen clock and title (the owner's ruling for deterministic pictures) and each was looked at. The test takes about 21 s in the container against a 120 s budget, checked once at its end with the `timing gate missed` marker, so `gate-misses.sh` treats a slow machine's miss as advisory.

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs (wave 3): the agent proxy scores what the shell shows.** `docs/guide/target-checklist.md` lists nine items for bar (a) (`bar-per-output`, `dots`, `title`, `clock`, `calendar`, `volume`, `battery`, `tray`, `themed`), and `score` in newcomer.rs checks each against the inspector's `inspect.dump` on the acceptance mock: monitors are told apart by the bar instance's identity, never by output name, and no item depends on file names, component names or layout, so any honest build of the bar passes. A pixel comparison would fail every bar laid out differently from the guide's. The newcomer test scores the guide's own result and requires 9/9, which proves the scorer on a known good bar; the hello bar scores 3/9 (bars, title and battery text). `scripts/agent-proxy/` holds the harness: `prepare.sh` makes a workspace with the guide (without the checklist), an empty config directory, a `strand` limited to `check`, `fmt` and `new` through the container, and the prompt; `run.sh` starts a session a person chooses with `AGENT_PROXY_CMD`; `score.sh` runs the ignored `agent_proxy_score` test on the result and prints the minutes since `prepare.sh`. The harness was exercised end to end with the guide's own files (9/9); no model session has been run, since a rehearsal is a person's to start (m5-plan: advisory, first cut under time pressure).

## m5-docs3

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs3 (review round 1 of S-docs' wave 3): `strand-dev reference` writes only into a reference directory.** `reference::write` removed every `.md` in the directory it was given that it did not generate, so `strand-dev reference docs` would have deleted design.md, spec.md and the rest, and `strand-dev reference .` README.md and CLAUDE.md. It now reads every `.md` there first and, when one does not open with the generated note's first line (`<!-- Generated by `strand-dev reference` …`), refuses with `InvalidInput` ("not a reference directory: …; nothing was written") before removing or writing anything; it removes only generated pages that are no longer generated. Every page opens with the note (`every_page_opens_with_the_generated_note`), so a run over its own output is never refused. The default directory is relative (`docs/reference`, meant from the repository's root), so with no directory named `strand-dev reference` now fails when `./docs/reference` does not exist instead of making a stray one (crates/strand-dev/src/reference.rs::tests::writing_refuses_a_directory_with_hand_written_pages, crates/strand-dev/tests/reference_cli.rs).

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs3: lengths in different units compare as written, and spec.md says so.** The freeze review's 7.2 said "two values of the same kind" compare, and its test never tried `ch`: the checker types `px`, `ch` and `%` all as `length`, and the VM's `compare` compares the numbers and ignores the unit (lowering normalises `s` to `ms` but keeps `ch` and `%` as their own units), so `2ch < 10px` checks clean and is true although 2ch is wider than 10px in any text font. Two readings: reject a comparison that mixes length units, or state the behaviour. Rejecting needs the unit in the type (the checker's `Ty::LENGTH` carries none, and a `ch` read through a `let` loses it), a strand-compiler change outside S-docs, and a load error added later would break configs that check today; the draft already fixed the same rule for a length beside a percentage ("compared as written, a percentage is not resolved against a size"), and a comparison has no font to resolve a `ch` against, as it has no size for a percentage. So spec.md 7.2 now says two lengths in different units (`px`, `ch`, a percentage) compare their numbers as written, with `2ch < 10px` as the example; a lint that warns on the mix stays possible under the compatibility policy, since a warning breaks nothing (crates/strand-dev/tests/spec.rs::lengths_in_different_units_compare_as_written: four mixes check clean, and the running shell shows `2ch < 10px` true and `30px < 2ch` false).

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs3: spec.md is reviewed for the freeze, not frozen; the freeze is the integrator's closing commit.** m5-plan puts the freeze at the last commit of wave 3, after every stream that could add a schema entry, and the Waves table and handoff.md's Closing give "the freeze text" to the integrator; S-platform and S-inspect are still in flight. So spec.md's status line no longer says "frozen": it says the freeze review settled every open point, each with a test, and that the freeze is wave 3's last commit, after which the compatibility process applies. This amends m5-docs' "the freeze review" paragraph ("spec.md says 'frozen'"); the settled points stand. features.md's Docs box stays ticked (the spec is written and reviewed); "language spec frozen" is the Exit line's box, the integrator's.

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs3: the bare-number tests check values, not only silence.** `a_bare_number_for_an_angle_is_degrees` paints a bar with a rotated box through strand-render's offline renderer and requires `rotate: 45` to paint the same pixels as `rotate: 45deg` and different ones from `rotate: 0` and `rotate: 90deg` (the scene keeps `45` as a number and `45deg` as an angle, and render reads a number as degrees, so only the pixels pin the frozen-to-be "it is degrees"). `mixed_unit_comparisons` requires `stagger: 2`'s one diagnostic to be `check::type_mismatch`, not merely some diagnostic (crates/strand-dev/tests/spec.rs).

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs3: the proxy's `strand` acts on its own config, and the session has no compositor.** `prepare.sh`'s `bin/strand` ran strand through `scripts/container/run.sh`, which starts in the checkout's root with `HOME=/tmp/home`, so `strand new` wrote into a throwaway container home and a relative path resolved against the checkout, not where the session stood. The workspace now has `home/`, whose `.config/strand` is a link to `config/`, and the wrapper runs strand with `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` there, in the caller's directory (refusing one outside the checkout, which the container cannot see): `bin/strand new` writes `config/bar.strand`, and a bare `bin/strand check` checks `config/` (run by hand: `new`, `check`, `check config` and `check ../config` from `guide/`). Deviation from m5-plan, recorded: the plan says the proxy "works in the container with two headless outputs"; here the session gets no compositor (`strand run` is refused, and PROMPT.md says so) and the two headless outputs are the scorer's, since running a shell on the proxy's behalf would need a compositor per session for no gain in what is scored.

**2026-10-12 · m5-docs3: the newcomer test's 120 s budget is strict, and the scorer depends on no layout.** m5-docs said the budget's miss is advisory because it carries the `timing gate missed` marker, but only ci.sh's timing steps consult `gate-misses.sh`, and the test runs in the strict `cargo test --workspace` step (the `test` job). The plan's budget is a gate on the test itself ("the whole test runs in 120 s or less in the container"), measured at about 21 s, so it stays strict: the claim is corrected here, not the step; the marker stays, so a miss reads as a time miss, and `gate-misses.sh` names newcomer.rs among the markers' owners with a note that its miss fails (`the_gate_miss_marker_is_the_one_the_container_suite_reads`). The scorer opened the calendar with one click at the top centre of `HEADLESS-1` and counted dots as numeric-keyed nodes with a `radius`, so a correct bar with its clock at the right, or with glyph dots, lost items, against m5-docs' "no item depends on … layout". Now every item but the calendar is scored on a dump taken before any click (a click may focus a workspace or mute the speaker), the dots are the distinct numeric keys on each monitor however they are drawn, and `open_calendar` clicks along `HEADLESS-1`'s bar (the top centre first, then outwards every 40 px, on four rows) until a dump shows the calendar, closing any other popup a click opened; the inspector's dump carries no node rectangles, so the clock cannot be found from it. `the_scorer_passes_a_bar_laid_out_otherwise` runs the guide's bar with the clock moved to the end section and the dots as `text "●"`, and scores 9/9 with the calendar opened away from the top centre (crates/strand/tests/m5/newcomer.rs; docs/guide/target-checklist.md follows).

## m5-plugins

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: the plugin builder's public surface is four items.** design.md says only that a service is a `#[service]` struct whose schema drives checking, hovers and docs; Q18 fixes `strand::Shell::builder().service::<S>().run()`, git-only and unstable. The interface (architecture.md, "Plugin builder", accepted by the integrator) makes exactly that public: `Shell`, `Shell::builder`, `Builder::service` and `Builder::run`, beside `process_setup!` and the hidden `cli` and `__process`. The module tree stays private, errors are printed rather than exported, and nothing configures the shell from Rust (no config path, no hooks, no host access): a plugin adds services and nothing else, which keeps the unstable surface small enough not to churn (m5-plan Risk 14). `strand` does not re-export `strand-services`: the `#[service]`, `Store`, `Data` and `Call` derives emit `::strand_services` paths, so a plugin must name that crate itself, from the same git URL and rev as `strand` (cargo unifies them; a mismatched rev is a compile error on the `Service` bound, not a runtime one). A `crate = …` override in strand-services-macros would let a plugin depend on `strand` alone, but it changes a crate S-plugins does not own and saves one Cargo line, so it is not taken in M5.

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: a plugin binary is the whole `strand` command line, so `main.rs`'s dispatch moves into the library (accepted by the integrator, 2026-10-11).** A plugin replaces `strand` in the user's session, so it must answer `run`, `check`, `fmt`, `watch`, `reload`, `get`, `set`, `toggle`, `call` and the rest as `strand` does; written twice, the two command lines would drift, and the idle hooks `main` installs (`set_idle_hook(cli::trim)` for text and images) would be the first thing a plugin forgot. So `Builder::run` is the dispatch, `COMMANDS` and `main`'s body, moved to `src/entry.rs`, and `main.rs` becomes `process_setup!()` plus `Shell::builder().run()`: `strand` is a plugin with no extra services, which removes a concept rather than adding one. It changes 0a's interface text ("`main.rs` keeps `main` and the COMMANDS table"), and the integrator accepted it; 0a now says so. Timing: one pure-move commit at the wave 1 → 2 boundary, after S-ipc's `get`/`toggle`/`call`/`clear` arms merge and before S-tools adds `new`, `export` and `report`, so no stream rebases a half-moved file; S-plugins writes it and the integrator merges it (amended 2026-10-11, m5-integration-w2: the integrator wrote it as `laptop/m5-w2`'s first commit). Moving a file does not move its ownership: m5-plan gives S-ipc the COMMANDS table, so after the move `entry.rs`'s COMMANDS rows and dispatch arms are a shared dispatch point (m5-plan's strand list, beside `Shell::request`'s arms): S-ipc keeps the table and its own rows, S-tools changes the existing `new`, `export` and `report` rows and adds their dispatch arms (amended 2026-10-11, m5-integration-w1: the rows already exist, answering "not implemented yet (M5)", and the D-Bus front end is `ipc_bus.rs`, not this table), each as one-line entries the integrator merges, and S-plugins owns only `src/plugin.rs` and `entry.rs`'s one call into it. m5-plan's Streams table and per-file lists record this, and give S-plugins `strand-compiler/src/schema/plugins.rs` (below), a new file no other stream touches. The allocator and THP tests stay in `main.rs` (they test the binary). Not taken: a plugin `run()` that serves only `run`, `check` and `--write-schemas` (a plugin shell that cannot answer `strand call` from its own binary, and a second CLI to keep in step).

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: how a plugin service registers and is served.** `service::<S>()` records function pointers (`S::NAME`, `S::schema`, and a `register` that calls `Services::register::<S>` and returns `Client::dynamic()`), so the generic code is monomorphised only in a plugin binary. `run` validates the list (a builtin's name or a name registered twice is `DuplicateService`; a name that is not `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*` is `BadName`, checked before it becomes a file name; then each linked text must apply over the builtin and the earlier linked texts, else `Schema { service, errors }`) and fails every subcommand on it before anything runs, then stores it once in a private process-wide `OnceLock` through `plugin::install(slot, list)`, which takes the slot as a parameter and refuses one already set. Both readers of it, `services::schema()` (already a process-wide `OnceLock`) and `Real::start`, read it after `run` has set it; were `schema()` ever read first, it would initialise the extras empty and `run`'s install would fail, which a unit test pins (against a local `OnceLock` passed to `install`) rather than a code path tolerating. Each reader has a pure twin that takes the list, `services::schema_with(extras, files) -> Served` (the schema, and each file-declared service no linked store serves with its file's path) and `Real::start_with(…, extras, served)`, which `schema()` (through `served()`) and `Real::start` call with the process-wide lists; `Real` keeps its `Served`, and `Real::set_text` resolves names in it through `set_text_with(schema, …)`, the twin of the free `set_text`, so unit tests never set or read process state the shared lib test binary's other tests have already initialised (`schema()` is read by rules, check, live and run's tests, in any order). `Real::start_with` registers the extras right after `Builtin::register` (unchanged, as m5-plan requires) and adds each to the `Composite` as a `StoreHost`, the same as a builtin, and `Real` keeps them beside `builtin`; `shutdown` already disposes every store, extras included. So reads, writes, events, actions, `fn` and async methods and the D-Bus front end reach a plugin service through the existing `Composite` name routing. Two paths do not route by `Composite` alone: `Real::set_text` (`strand set`) and S-ipc's `Shell::run_action` (`strand call`, `run/request/call.rs` on laptop/m5-ipc) each find the service to `acquire` and to `wait_ready_of(SET_WAIT)` with `builtin.all()`, so for a plugin service nobody reads they would skip the acquire and the first-read wait. Both switch to one lookup, `Real::served(name)` (builtins, then extras); the `call.rs` line is S-ipc's file and lands with S-plugins' wave-2 PR as a one-line entry S-ipc reviews. The miss matters differently on the two paths (see "the second review" below): for `set` a relative write is computed before the first read and then overwritten, which a unit test catches; for `call` it is not observable, since an action is fire-and-forget and `with_run` starts the service and queues the action behind its start either way, so the lookup there keeps `call` returning after the first read as `set` does and no `strand call` test claims to catch it. A no-code `service hello from …` in a config meets the same name rule as one naming a builtin. A plugin service runs on the shared current-thread runtime, or its own thread with `#[service(thread)]`, under the same lifecycle (lazy start, 5 s stop).

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: one schema rule for `strand check`, `strand run` and the LSP, plugin files included (the stock `strand run` reading the files: accepted by the integrator, 2026-10-11).** Q18 says only that the plugin binary writes the files outside the watched config dir, so the LSP never loads plugin code; m5-plan's S-plugins section and architecture.md's 0a paragraph say the files reach `strand check` and the LSP. Neither says whether the stock binary's `strand run` reads them. It does: today all three check against one schema (`Schema::builtin_with(&schemas())`, "for `strand check`, `strand run` and the LSP alike"), and a config that `strand check` passes but `strand run` refuses as an unknown name would break that. The order is the builtin texts, the linked plugin texts in `service` order, then the files in file-name order, skipping a file whose stem names a linked service (code wins: in a plugin binary its own services never depend on what is on disk). Each text goes through `Schema::extend`, which is atomic, so a bad or colliding file is skipped with a warning naming it (printed by `strand check`, logged by `strand run`, `eprintln!`ed by `strand-dev lsp` as its schema load is today) and never stops a shell booting (design.md, "keep the last good tree"). The fingerprint chains every applied text, so the last-good cache follows the files; a cache written by the plugin binary and one written by `strand` differ whenever their schemas do, which only costs a cold compile. A service declared by a file but served by no linked store answers reads at its schema's defaults through the `SchemaHost` fallback, as unserved names already do; writes, calls and actions on it are refused with the notice's text (below, "the second review"). When the config reads it, the shell raises one notice naming the file and telling the user to run the plugin binary or remove the file; a silent bar of defaults would be the worse failure. The notice is tied to the read, not to the file: a thin `UnservedHost` sits in the `Composite` under that name, raising the notice on its first `acquire` and resolving it (`resolved: true`) on its last `release`, both through `Services::report`, so a leftover file from a plugin the user tried once raises nothing for a config that never mentions it (a log line at start says the file is there). `Real::start` runs before any config is compiled, so it cannot decide this itself. When a plugin binary finds its own service's file differing from its linked text it logs that the file is stale. Files are read once per process (both `schema()`s are `OnceLock`s); the LSP and a running shell see new files after a restart, which is when a rebuilt plugin binary takes effect anyway. Re-reading on change is left out: it would put plugin schemas on the reload path for a case that needs a new binary.

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: `--write-schemas` and the schemas directory (invented CLI surface, m5-plan Ground rules).** Q18 names the flag and `$XDG_DATA_HOME/strand/schemas/`; the rest is chosen here. The flag is top-level (`my-shell --write-schemas`, like `--version`), takes no directory (tests set `XDG_DATA_HOME`; one fewer spelling to freeze), writes the registered services' schemas only (the builtins are compiled into every `strand` and `strand-dev`), and exits. The directory is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/strand/schemas/` when that variable is absolute, else `$HOME/.local/share/strand/schemas/` (the XDG rule `live.rs`'s font directories already follow), created as needed; neither is `NoDataDir`. One file per service, `<name>.schema`: a header line `// strand plugin schema, written by <exe> --write-schemas; do not edit` (a schema comment, so the file is plain schema text; `<exe>` is defined below), then `S::schema()` verbatim; written to `.<name>.schema.tmp` and renamed, so an LSP starting meanwhile reads the old file or the new one. It also removes `.schema` files whose header names the same binary and whose service it no longer registers (a renamed or dropped service), and never touches another binary's files. The binary's identity is `<exe>`, `std::env::current_exe()` canonicalised: a name (argv[0]'s file name, the package name) would let two projects that both build a `my-shell`, the guide's own example name, remove each other's files, and argv[0] as typed would differ between `./target/release/my-shell` and the installed one. The path errs the other way: a service dropped while the `target/` build wrote its file is not removed by the installed binary, so `--write-schemas` lists such files (another path's header, a name this binary does not register) as "left alone" with their writer, and the read-tied notice above names them if a config still reads them. When `current_exe()` fails the header says `unknown` and nothing is removed. It prints each path written or removed. `strand --write-schemas` writes nothing and says so (exit 0). The reader takes `*.schema` but dotfiles, regular files only (symlinks followed, FIFOs and devices refused, as the theme importers refuse them), at most 1 MiB, UTF-8; a missing directory is no plugins. Reading and applying live in one place, a new `strand_compiler::schema::plugins` module (`dir`, `load`, `apply`), because both the binary and `strand-dev` link strand-compiler and a skip rule written twice could disagree between `strand check` and the LSP; strand-services-schema stays the builtin texts.

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: `--write-schemas` refuses an undocumented plugin schema; the rest of the errors.** design.md generates hovers and docs from service schemas, and the builtin schema and every builtin service text are held to `Schema::undocumented()` being empty. A plugin's text is held to the same at write time: `Undocumented { service, entries }` lists what lacks a `///` doc and writes nothing, so a plugin cannot put hover-less names into the LSP. `strand check` does not apply the rule to files it reads (a hand-edited file still checks configs). The other errors: `Schema { service, errors }` (the text does not apply over the builtin and earlier plugin texts; also checked by `run` before any subcommand, so a plugin never boots on a text that does not apply), `Write { path, error }`, `NoDataDir`, and the two registration errors above. `DuplicateService`, `BadName` and `Schema` fail every subcommand before it runs (architecture.md's Errors bullet says the same). They are one private enum, printed as `<binary>: <error>` with a failing exit code; none is a panic, and no path that reads the files can fail the shell.

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: `Builder::run` checks the process setup it cannot do itself.** A library cannot install a global allocator or a constructor in the binary that links it (m5-w0-harden), so a plugin that forgets `strand::process_setup!()` runs on the system allocator with THP on, and its PSS is about twice the bar's figure. `run` checks once, before dispatch, that a fresh heap block is mimalloc's (`mi_is_in_heap_region`, already linked) and that THP is off for the process (`transparent_huge_pages_are_disabled`), and prints a warning naming the macro if not. It warns rather than refuses: the plugin still works, and the check costs two calls. The verdict is a pure `setup_warning(mimalloc, thp_off)` over the two probes, so its polarity is a unit test on all four inputs. A binary test of the THP half must undo inheritance first: `PR_SET_THP_DISABLE` survives fork and exec, and the m5 test binary runs `process_setup!` itself, so a child it spawns starts with THP off whether or not its own constructor ran. The tests therefore spawn plugin binaries with THP turned back on (`prctl(PR_SET_THP_DISABLE, 0)` in `pre_exec`), and a second example, `plugin_bare` (`Shell::builder().run()` with no services and no macro), shows the warning appearing. The guide's plugin page (S-plugins, under S-docs' layout) states the contract: invoke the macro at the crate root; copy the workspace's `[profile.release]` (`lto = "fat"`, `codegen-units = 1`) and every `[profile.release.package.*]` override; and leave the plugin's own crate at the release default opt-level 3, because fat LTO runs the whole program at the linking crate's level (m5-speed-strand), so a plugin built at "s" or "z" would slow the render path. A test compares the guide's profile block with the root `Cargo.toml`'s, so the page cannot drift.

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: size and speed.** m5-plan budgets "about 0 in `strand`". It is not quite 0: the stock binary now holds the schema-file reader and applier, the `--write-schemas` writer, the builder's validation and the process-setup check. Estimated at 4–8 KB of CPU-only `.text`, charged to the plugins line of m5-plan's ledger (8 KB; amended 2026-10-11, m5-integration-w1: first "charged to the reserve", which no longer pays for it) and confirmed by the ledger in wave 2; nothing generic is instantiated in `strand` (the extras list is empty and `service::<S>` is never called), and the CLI move is a move. A plugin binary's size is `strand`'s plus its services' and is not gated. Speed: the extra cost on `strand`'s boot is one `opendir` of a usually missing directory when the schema is first built, and with files, one `Schema::extend` each (the builtin texts already take the same path); nothing touches the reload path, the frame loop or a service call, since an extra is the same `Rc<dyn DynService>` behind the same `Composite` lookup as a builtin. A plugin's PSS matches `strand`'s plus its service when the profile and macro contract is kept, which is why `run` checks it.

**2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: the second review: what the lookup can be tested by, refusing on an unserved file, and the watch order.** Six findings against the notes, all taken. (1) `strand call`'s lookup cannot be caught by a `strand call`: `Client::act` answers once `Msg::Action` is queued and `with_run` starts a stopped service and queues the action behind its start, so whatever a service does about "not ready" never reaches the answer, and the action runs after the start with or without the acquire. `plugin_hello`'s `ready` field and refusing `greet` are dropped (they tested nothing), the second-instance call is dropped, and architecture.md no longer says a skipped wait "fails visibly". `run_action` still uses `Real::served`, so `call` returns after the first read as `set` does and there is one lookup, not two; the miss that is observable, `set`'s relative write before the first read, is a unit test. Not taken: making actions answer (a strand-services change to every action's path, for no user-visible gain over the fire-and-forget design). (2) A service declared only by a leftover file now refuses writes, calls and actions in `UnservedHost` with the notice's text: `resolve_call` and `set_text` accept the name once the file is in the schema, `Real::served` finds nothing to acquire, and `SchemaHost::action` returns `Ok` after doing nothing, so `strand call hello.greet` would have answered success where before the file it was refused as unknown, the silent-defaults failure the notice exists to prevent. Reads stay at defaults, so a bar still boots. (3) Service notices reach only the watchers connected when they are taken, and `watch_request` replays warnings and host notices, not them; the notice raised by a boot's mount is taken on the first loop step, before a watcher can connect. Replaying active service notices would change S-ipc's `watch.rs` and every service's notices, not just this one, so it is not taken here; the test boots on a config that does not read `hello`, connects `strand watch`, then reloads the read in, as `dbus_shells.rs`'s conflict test does. (4) The diagnostic that takes the rows away is `ServiceDiagnostic`'s existing `resolved: true`, raised through `Services::report`; there is no `cleared` field and no strand-services change. (5) The extras get seams: `plugin::install(slot, list)` over a passed `OnceLock`, `services::schema_with(extras, files)` and `Real::start_with(…, extras)`, which the process-wide `schema()` and `Real::start` (signature unchanged) call; a unit test that set the process-wide extras would leak into every other test's `Real::start` and depend on whether `schema()` was already initialised. (6) `plugin_hello` is described once, the same in architecture.md's "Examples" and the tests paragraph: `greeting`, a writable `count` its first read sets to 41, and a `greet` that always acts.

(1) `Real::set_text` and the free `set_text` resolved the service and its fields in the process-wide `schema()`, so a unit test's extra, defined only in the schema the test built, was "nothing is exported" before anything was written, and the twins did not reach the code they were added to test. `set_text_with(schema, host, rt, types, path, text)` is the pure twin; the free `set_text` passes `schema()` (callers unchanged) and `Real::set_text` passes the schema `Real` was started with. Building it changed eight things. (1) The fallback does not answer an unknown name: `SchemaHost::new` creates cells only for `Schema::builtin()`'s services, so "reads go to the fallback" read nothing for a file-declared service (a runtime error, "`hello` has no field `greeting`"). `Real::start_with` now declares each unserved service on the fallback through the existing `ServiceHost::declare` (a `CustomService` with no fields, which `SchemaHost` takes as "cells at the record's defaults"), and `UnservedHost` reads through it. No strand-compiler change. (2) Every service in the bare builtin schema is `provisional`, and some stay so in `strand` (`clock`, `calendar`, `screens`; `audio` without PipeWire), so a file or a plugin text declaring one would have replaced the builtin's stub instead of failing as "declared twice". `plugins::apply` skips such a file with a warning ("it redeclares a builtin service") and `run` refuses such a text as `Schema`; a plugin service named like a builtin was already `DuplicateService`. (4) `apply` extends with the file's text without its header line (`plugins::body`; `plugins::header` writes it), so the fingerprint, and the compile cache, do not change with the writer's path; the stale check compares the same body with the linked text. (5) `PluginError` has a seventh variant, `ReadEarly` (the list was read before `run` installed it: the `OnceLock` case the notes pin with a unit test), printed like the rest. The schema-file reader and `schema_with` are `#[cold] #[inline(never)]` (they run once per process). (7) `strand::Builder` is exported beside `strand::Shell` (`Shell::builder()` returns it, so the type must be nameable); the hidden `cli` module no longer re-exports `entry::main`, which `Builder::run` now calls. **2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: review round 2: the mock reads plugin services at their defaults.** One finding, taken. File-declared services got fallback cells and an `UnservedHost` only in `Real::start_with`, and under `STRAND_MOCK` (`desktop` or `acceptance`) `run/logic.rs` builds no `Real`, so the shell ran on the bare `SchemaHost`, which has cells only for `Schema::builtin()`'s names, while the compile still checked against `served().schema`: a config reading `hello.greeting` with `hello.schema` present passed `strand check` and then failed its mount with "`hello` has no field `greeting`". Decided here: the mock raises no service notice for a file's service and does not refuse its writes or calls. The mock stands in for every service (a builtin's store does not run under it either), it has no `Services` to report a notice through, and a plugin's own service, which the binary does serve, reads the same defaults under it, so a notice saying "this binary does not serve it" would separate two cases the mock treats alike. The info line names the file. Tests: `services::tests::plugins::the_mock_reads_plugin_services_at_their_defaults` (a file's service and a linked extra mounted on the schema host alone, read at their defaults) and `tests/m5/plugin.rs::the_mock_reads_plugin_schemas` (the stock `strand run` under `STRAND_MOCK=desktop` with `hello.schema` boots a config reading `hello` and reads `0` and `""`). **2026-10-11 · m5-plugins: review round 3: an unserved file service refuses its items' actions and writes too.** One finding, taken. `Real::start_with` added each `UnservedHost` with no item records, so `Composite::route_item` sent an item action or item write on a record the file's service hands out (`let g = hello.main` then `g.poke()`, `g` read at its defaults) to the fallback `SchemaHost`, whose `action` simulates and answers `Ok`: the click did nothing and nothing was refused, while `hello.greet()` was refused with the file's path, contradicting the second review's item 2. `start_with` now passes the records the service hands out as the `UnservedHost`'s `items`: its own record and every record its fields, event parameters and method results reach, transitively, less those the builtin schema declares (their items are a builtin store's, or the fallback's mock simulation) and those a store already serves (a plugin's own, or an earlier file's), so no record is claimed twice. The reachability rather than "the records the file's text declares" keeps `Served`'s shape: which records a file added is not recorded in it, and a record a file declares but its service never hands out has no items to act on. `UnservedHost` already refused `write_item` and item `action` with the notice's text. Test: `services::tests::plugins::an_unserved_file_service_refuses_item_actions` (a `Greeter` record with `action poke()` reached through `hello.main`; it failed at the action's `unwrap_err` without the fix). Proposed architecture.md text ("The served schema", not edited here): "…behind a thin strand-local `UnservedHost` that `Real::start_with` adds to the `Composite` under that name, with the records it hands out that neither the builtin schema declares nor a store serves as its items, one for each entry…".

## m5-tools

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: `strand export` writes palette roles only, one table per target, and never invents a colour.** *(Superseded 2026-10-11 by the owner's decision below, m5-tools "Strand ships no app mappings": there are no per-app targets. What still holds: no colour is invented for a key the palette lacks, colours are opaque `#rrggbb` unless an expression makes them translucent, and `-o` writes through `write_atomic`.)* design.md says the export "writes the same palette for the rest of the desktop" (Wallpaper palettes) and that the palette is the Material 3 role schema, 1:1 (Token model). So each target key below takes exactly one of the 49 roles (`strand_theme::Role`, role.rs:40–90), by Strand name, at the role's opaque sRGB value written as `#rrggbb` (the precision of the persisted palette, palette.rs:90–100; `Partial::fill` makes every role opaque, palette.rs:243). No base or component token is exported (`$fg.muted`, `$surface.hi` are Strand's derivations, not the palette), no runtime token overlay either (`strand set $accent …` is a live experiment the overlay says how to `clear`; the export writes what the theme file resolves to), and no key gets a colour the palette lacks: where a target wants a colour Material 3 has no role for (GTK's success and warning, a terminal's 16 ANSI colours), the key is not written and the target's own value stands. Deriving those would add a concept (a second derivation table with hues the theme never chose) and would recolour meaning: programs print errors in ANSI red and successes in green, and a Material palette holds one hue family plus `error`. Keys are written in the tables' order, one per line, under a one-line comment naming the palette's `source` and `dark`/`light`, so the golden files (`crates/strand-theme/tests/export.rs`, catppuccin-mocha) are stable. The writer is pure (`Palette` → `String` in `strand-theme/src/export.rs`); `-o <file>` goes through `strand_theme::writer::write_atomic` (writer.rs:38), not the queued `FileWriter`, since the command exits right after. Each file is meant to be included by the user's own config (kitty `include`, GTK `@import`, Hyprland `require`/`source`), which Strand never edits.

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: `gtk` writes libadwaita's named colours with `@define-color`.** *(Superseded 2026-10-11, m5-tools "Strand ships no app mappings": Strand ships no GTK mapping. The libadwaita 1.10 finding, that `@define-color` still drives its `--x-color` variables, is kept as a fact a user's own template can rely on.)* One file serves GTK 4 with libadwaita and GTK 3 (adw-gtk3 and apps' own CSS read the same names). `@define-color` rather than libadwaita 1.6's `--x-color` variables, because libadwaita still defines its colours that way and binds each variable to the named colour: the stylesheet in the owner's libadwaita 1.10.0 (read from `/usr/lib/libadwaita-1.so`'s strings) has `--window-bg-color: @window_bg_color` and the same for every key below, so a user `gtk.css` (provider priority USER) redefining the name recolours the widgets, while a `:root { --x: … }` block would be a parse error on every GTK 3 start. **2026-10-11 · m5-tools: `hyprland` writes Lua by default and hyprlang with `--classic`, as `strand compositor-rules` does.** *(Superseded 2026-10-11, m5-tools "Strand ships no app mappings": Strand ships no Hyprland mapping, so no `--classic` for `export` either; whether a user's template writes Lua or hyprlang is the user's choice.)* Hyprland 0.55 moved its configuration to Lua and deprecated hyprlang (wave4-exit-ci, laptop-resilience; the owner runs 0.56.2, `hyprctl -j version`), while older releases read only hyprlang, and one file cannot be both. m4-surface-w1 already settled this for `strand compositor-rules`: Lua by default, `--classic` for hyprlang (rules.rs:277–282). The export takes the same flag rather than a new target name or version detection (a pure writer does not ask the running compositor). Lua form: one `hl.config({ … })` call with nested tables (`general = { col = { active_border = "rgb(rrggbb)", … } }`, the shape of `/usr/share/hypr/hyprland.lua`), for `require("strand")` from the user's config. Classic form: `general { col.active_border = rgb(rrggbb) … }` blocks, for `source =`. Window and group borders map onto M3's colour families. Plain windows take the accent. Groups are a second kind of active window, so they take the secondary family. A locked group, or a window that refuses grouping, is a third state, so it takes the tertiary family (locked groups the strong roles, the refusing windows' borders the container ones). The groupbar's text sits on the groupbar's fill, so it takes each fill's `on_` role. The shadow keeps Hyprland's default opacity (`0xee`) in the palette's `shadow` colour, since an opaque shadow would be harsher than the default, and the palette's alpha is always 1.

| `general.col.nogroup_border_active` | `tertiary` | |
| `general.col.nogroup_border` | `tertiary_container` | |
| `group.col.border_active` | `secondary` | |

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: Strand ships no app mappings (owner).** *(Holds in its principle; its "two generic outputs" and declared outputs are replaced 2026-10-11 by m5-tools "the owner-approved theming design".)* The owner's decision, in substance: Strand must be flexible enough to carry rich palettes into many applications and formats, theme switches included, but Strand itself maintains no first-party app themes or mappings: no kitty, ghostty, GTK, Hyprland or Zed, neither as code nor as shipped templates. It is decided from first principles, not modelled on anyone's dotfiles. This replaces the four per-app paragraphs above. `strand export gtk | kitty | hyprland` becomes two generic outputs: `strand export json` (the palette as data) and `strand export --template <file>` (any text format, its holes filled with Strand token expressions). A config can also declare outputs that are re-rendered whenever the theme changes. The paragraphs below set out each part. The principle test holds: each per-app table was a concept Strand would have to keep up to date with someone else's release; a template is the user's, and the only thing Strand adds is the expression language it already has.

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: a palette keeps every named colour of its source, as `$palette.<name>`, beside the roles.** *(Superseded 2026-10-11 by m5-tools "the owner-approved theming design": extras are snake_case, read only in templates and `file` text, persisted as `extra` lines, and 13 hue roles join the schema.)* design.md's palette is the Material 3 role schema, 1:1, which every importer fills, and "one table derives any role they lack" (Token model). That stays exactly as it is: the 49 roles (role.rs:40–90) are still filled by each importer's own mapping, else by `Partial::fill`'s derivation table (palette.rs:225–360), and nothing else feeds a role. What changes is that an importer no longer drops the rest of its source. A `Palette` also carries its source's named colours, its *extras*, in source order:
- Catppuccin: its 26 names (`CATPPUCCIN_NAMES`, import.rs:159, `rosewater` … `crust`).
- base16: `base00`–`base0F`; base24: `base00`–`base17`.
- matugen: every colour key that is not one of the 49 roles under its M3 name (`source_color`, for one).
- W3C design tokens: every colour token, its group path kept as segments.
- `material(seed:)`, `material(image:)` and the built-in palette: `source_color`, the seed or the colour the quantiser chose.

The palette's identity is its existing `source` string (`catppuccin:mocha`, `wallpaper`, `built-in`, palette.rs:45–50) and its `dark` flag. An extra is read as `$palette.<name>` (`$palette.mauve`, `$palette.base0D`), with the source's spelling kept where it is a valid identifier, so a name copied from the scheme's own documentation works. In a segment, any character other than a letter, digit or `_` becomes `_`. Two names that become the same are an import error naming both. Every extra lives under the one `$palette` namespace so that it can never shadow a role or a base token, now or when a later importer brings a name like `surface` or `space`; `$palette` becomes a reserved token name (`override` of it is an error). Extras relate to roles only through the importer's mapping: Catppuccin's `mauve` is both `$accent` (the default accent) and `$palette.mauve`, and changing the accent (`catppuccin:mocha:blue`) changes the role, never the extra. In a swap, extras are palette roots like the roles: an extra both palettes have springs in OKLab, and one only one side has appears or disappears at once. The contrast guard does not touch extras (it solves declared text/background pairs, which are tokens). Which extras exist depends on the palette at run time, so reading one that is absent gives null, which `??` replaces (`$palette.green ?? $tertiary`). In a template, an absent extra without `??` is an error (next paragraphs). In the shell, it is a diagnostic once per name and palette, and the prop keeps its default. `strand check` checks extra names only when `use palette` is a single literal `import(…)`. The persisted palette (`palettes/palette`) gains `palette.<name> #rrggbb` lines, and a file without them reads as before (`Palette::from_text` ignores lines it does not know, palette.rs:104–127).

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: `strand export json` writes the palette as data.** *(Superseded 2026-10-11 by m5-tools "the owner-approved theming design": the JSON also carries `source`, the 62 roles and every resolved token.)* One JSON object: `{"name": <source or null>, "variant": "dark" | "light", "roles": {<49 Strand role names in schema order>: "#rrggbb"}, "extras": {<names in source order>: "#rrggbb"}}`. It is pretty-printed with two spaces and ends with a newline, so a golden file is stable. Roles are keyed by their Strand names only (one name per thing; a consumer that wants M3 names maps them, and `Role::m3` is documented). Every role and extra is opaque (`Partial::fill`, palette.rs:243). It writes the palette alone, never base or component tokens: the owner asked for the palette as data, and anything derived from it is what templates are for. Output goes to stdout or `-o <file>` (Q16), the latter through `writer::write_atomic` (writer.rs:38).

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: `strand export --template <file>`: the holes are Strand token expressions, and there is no filter syntax.** *(Superseded 2026-10-11 by m5-tools "the owner-approved theming design": the holes and the `{{ "{{" }}` escape stay; the value formats become `hex(…)`/`argb(…)` and the channel methods `.red()`/`.green()`/`.blue()`/`.opacity()` (review fix round 3: this note first said "channel fields", the form the integrator's ruling dropped); how every other kind of value is written, in a hole and in `export json`, is restated in "template expressions and formats", review round 3.)* A template is any text file. `{{ expr }}` is a hole, and `expr` is an ordinary Strand expression (grammar.md, Expressions) over the theme only: token paths and their methods (`$accent`, `$fg.muted`, `$accent.alpha(0.4)`, `$surface.mix($fg, 8%)`), extras (`$palette.mauve`), literals (colours, numbers with units, strings), colour functions (`oklch(from $surface, l: l + 0.12)`), arithmetic, `?:` and `??`. A name that is not a token (a `state`, a `let`, a service field, a `fn`) is an error saying that a template reads the theme only, so a rendered template depends on nothing but the token table. Whitespace inside the braces is free, and a hole may span lines. The hole ends at the first `}}` outside a string literal. There is no escape syntax: a literal `{{` is written `{{ "{{" }}`, using the language's own string literal, and a `}}` outside a hole is plain text. **How a value is written:**
- A colour is `#rrggbb` when opaque and `#rrggbbaa` otherwise (CSS Color 4).
- A number is written in its shortest form (no fraction when whole, at most 4 decimals).
- A length is written as CSS writes it (`14px`).
- A string is written as is.
- Fonts, shadows, springs and other composite values are an error naming the type.

Other notations come from methods, which design.md already makes the way to extend token paths ("adding methods later never breaks token names"). Six template-only methods: `hex()` (`rrggbb`, no `#`, alpha dropped), `hex_alpha()` (the alpha as two hex digits), `red()`, `green()` and `blue()` (0–255) and `opacity()` (0–1). With them, `rgba({{ $accent.hex() }}{{ $accent.hex_alpha() }})`, `0x{{ $accent.hex_alpha() }}{{ $accent.hex() }}` and `rgb({{ $fg.red() }}, {{ $fg.green() }}, {{ $fg.blue() }})` are all plain template text. These methods are template-only (a prop never needs a colour as text), so the render thread's colour-valued method set (`TokenMethod`, strand-scene tokens.rs:34) is unchanged. **Errors:**
- The cases: an unclosed `{{`, a syntax error, an unknown token (with a did-you-mean over the roles, base and component tokens and this palette's extras), a non-token name, and a value that cannot be written as text.
- Each is a diagnostic with the template's `file:line:col` and a caret, rendered as `strand check` renders, so the template file is added to the `SourceMap`.
- Every error in the file is reported, not only the first. The exit status is non-zero, and nothing is written: the whole output is rendered into memory first, so neither stdout nor `-o` gets a partial file.

Output goes to stdout or `-o <file>` (atomic, `write_atomic`).

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: where `strand export` reads the theme.** *(Superseded in part 2026-10-11 by m5-tools "the owner-approved theming design": the CLI asks the running shell over IPC first, so the paragraph after the bullets no longer holds, and `json` now reads the whole token table too. The mount the bullets define holds: it is the offline fallback for every export, restated in m5-tools "the CLI", step 2 (review fix).)* `json` needs a palette and keeps the source order confirmed above: the persisted palette (now with extras and identity), else the offline solve, else `strand export: no palette: run strand once, or fix the theme` with its cause. A template needs a whole token table (base and component tokens, overlays), so it is rendered against an offline mount of the config, made as follows:
- The config is compiled as `strand check` compiles it (check.rs:112, :161). A compile error is the error, since the template needs the config's base tokens.
- It is mounted with the deterministic `SchemaHost`, `system` seeded from `palettes/system`.
- Settings files are read, `persist` cells are read without writing, and the token overlay file of S-ipc's `strand set` (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/strand/tokens.toml`) is applied. Nothing is written.
- The palette root is pinned to the persisted palette when there is one, so a wallpaper palette is not quantised again and the palette on screen wins. Otherwise the solve's palette is used, through the no-fallback accessor below; otherwise the error.

The CLI does not ask a running shell over IPC. Every input the running shell's token table depends on is on disk (config, persisted cells, settings, overlays, palette, the portal's kept values), so the offline mount reproduces it. The exception is a token set chosen by a live service field, which is rare. A user who needs the exact live table declares an output (next paragraph), which the running shell renders itself. This keeps one CLI path and no new IPC request.

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: outputs re-rendered on theme change are declared with `export template "<file>" to "<file>" [run [<argv>]]`.** *(Superseded 2026-10-11 by m5-tools "the owner-approved theming design": the `file` element replaces this item.)* *(Amended 2026-10-13 by m6-w2-language "declared actions", the owner's ruling: its "no handler action that ... runs a command" no longer holds; a handler runs a command through a declared `action`, never a general statement.)* A top-level item, the CLI's `strand export --template T -o F` written into the config:
```
export template "colors.css.tmpl" to "~/.local/share/my-site/colors.css"
export template "term.tmpl" to "~/.cache/term-colors" run ["term-reload", "--all"]
permit exec "term-reload"
```
*Grammar:* `kw:export kw:template STRING kw:to STRING ( kw:run expr )?`, at the top level only. `template`, `to` and `run` are contextual after `export`, so `export state` and `export let` are unchanged. *Paths* are string literals, resolved as settings files are (`~/` from `$HOME`, absolute as is, relative to the config directory; `Storage::resolve`, instantiate/mod.rs:672–681). Literal paths keep the set of files Strand writes static: `strand check` can list it, and two outputs naming the same target are a load error. *The command* is an argv list, never a shell line. Its program must be allowed by `permit exec`, the rule `from poll` and `from listen` already follow (grammar.md, Services and permits), so no config runs anything it did not permit. *The template file* is watched with the config, as `shader` files and `import()` files are. Editing it re-renders, and its errors are load errors with its own `file:line:col`. *When:* the rendered text is a memo over the token table. It is re-rendered when the table's target changes: a config edit, `look`, a portal dark/light or accent change, a new wallpaper palette, `strand set` on a token, `strand clear`. A swap's spring frames are not renders, since the logic thread holds the target and the render thread only animates toward it. The file is written only when the text differs from what Strand last wrote, and at boot only when it differs from the file's current content. So a reload that changes nothing writes nothing and runs nothing, and a theme edited while Strand was stopped is caught up at boot. Writes go off the logic thread through a `FileWriter`-style queue: atomic, latest content per path wins, so a burst of `strand set`s coalesces without a timer. The command runs after its write lands, never twice at once for one output; if a newer write landed while it ran, it runs once more after. A failed write, a command that cannot start or exits non-zero, or a template that fails at render time (an extra the new palette lacks) is logged and becomes a `strand watch` notice naming the output. On a failed render the old file stays, and the next theme change retries. These failures are not an overlay notice, since the shell itself is fine. *Overlays count.* A template is evaluated against the token table, and design.md puts overlays in it ("runtime overlay > file > default", Who wins), so the other programs show what the shell shows, and `strand clear` takes them back too. Excluding overlays would need a second token table that exists nowhere else. The CLI applies the overlay file as well (above), so the CLI and a declared output agree. *Why not `on change` plus an action:* `on change` never fires at boot (design.md, "Events and time"), but an output must be brought up to date at boot. The language also has no handler action that writes a file or runs a command; adding both as general handler statements would be two new side-effect primitives that any handler could aim at any path, a larger concept that would weaken "never writes into another program's config unless asked". A declaration keeps every written path visible and checkable, and reuses `export`'s meaning ("make this reachable outside the shell") and `permit exec`. The user names every target, so writing it is being asked. It belongs on the learning ladder at level 5, beside `tokens` (S-docs places it).

**2026-10-11 · m5-tools: harmonised hues: no new roles; a `harmonize` token method instead (recommendation for the owner).** *(Superseded 2026-10-11 by m5-tools "the owner-approved theming design": 13 hue roles, derived by harmonising when the source has none.)* A wallpaper Material palette has one hue family plus `error`, and a template for a terminal or an editor wants a green or a yellow. Adding roles (`success`, `warning`, ANSI hues) would break design.md's "mapping 1:1 onto Material 3 system roles". M3 itself treats such colours as an app's *custom colours*, harmonised toward the source colour, not as system roles. New roles would also force every importer to fill them or the derivation table to invent them: Catppuccin's real `green` would be overwritten by a guess, and for a wallpaper palette the "fixed hue" to harmonise from would be a constant Strand picks, a first-party mapping on a smaller scale. Recommended instead: one token method, `.harmonize(toward)`, which rotates the colour's HCT hue toward `toward`'s by up to 15° and keeps its chroma and tone, as material-colors' `harmonize` does (the crate is already a dependency at 0.5.0). The user picks the hue once in their own tokens, `tokens base { hue.green: #3fb950; success: $hue.green.harmonize($accent) }` (a raw hex is allowed in tokens; the lint is for props), or from an extra when the palette has one: `$palette.green ?? $hue.green`. A template then writes `{{ $success }}`. As a derived token, it re-resolves with the accent, so it follows wallpaper and theme switches. It is a `TokenMethod` the render thread evaluates during a swap: one HCT round trip per such token per frame, microseconds against the about-100-operation token graph.
