## m6-flakes

**2026-10-12 · m6-flakes: a dropped image request that a frame wants again is sent again.** `budgets.rs::the_full_shell_on_the_real_services_is_measured` failed once on CI with the launcher showing no marked icon past its wait (handoff.md, Deferred work). Traced in the container, the launcher's frames want the marked icons, then want none of them (the next flatten, within the same millisecond), then want them again about 30 ms later. The image worker drops a request that no frame wants when it reaches it (`None`, with no wake), and that happened to `mark-001` and `mark-002` at their drawn size in 8 of 10 traced runs on two loaded cores. It is harmless when the render loop polls the drop before it flattens again, which forgets the key so the next frame asks for it. A loop that polled just before the drop was queued, and then flattened, saw the key still in flight and did not ask for it. Nothing was ever polled for it afterwards, and the surface drew without the icon until something else repainted it, which is the CI symptom. The worker now wakes the render loop for a drop too, and `ImageStore::poll` sends a dropped key again when a frame wants it. A drop is the rare case (a frame stopped wanting a queued key), so the wake costs nothing at idle. The alternative, sending a key again from `want` once it had left the wanted set while in flight, needs counting jobs per key to tell a stale result from the fresh one, for the same outcome. `strand-render`'s `image::tests::a_dropped_request_wanted_again_is_decoded` sets up the ordering. The worker is held by a file job while the frame wants `k` and then wants nothing; after the drop the frame wants `k` again before the loop polls. The test fails without the wake (no wake for the drop) and without the second send (no wake ever brings `k`). The end-to-end failure did not reproduce: delays injected into the worker and the render loop moved the ordering elsewhere, and old code passed 5 runs with each. That the launcher's wanted set flips, which this race needs, is traced, as above. With the fix the test passed 15 of 15 runs on two cores with three busy loops and 15 of 15 unloaded (release, as CI's budgets job runs it).

**2026-10-12 · m6-flakes: the watcher test stamps its writes ahead of the clock.** `strand-watch` `core.rs::tests::a_file_rewritten_without_pause_is_read_within_max_delay` failed once on CI with "read before `max_delay`" (run 37874718084). The watcher puts off reading a file modified less than the 15 ms quiet period before the read, judged by the file's modification time against the wall clock. The test wrote with the time of writing, so a runner that kept the test thread off the CPU for 15 ms between its write and the flush made the file look settled. The early read was correct, and the test's assumption was wrong. A sleep of twice the quiet period between the first write and its flush reproduces the failure every time. Each write is now stamped 900 ms ahead (`File::set_modified`): a clock stepped back, within `MTIME_SKEW` (1 s), which the watcher counts as fresh. The file stays "just written" whatever the scheduler does, and the first round keeps the stall on purpose. Unchanged product code; 60 of 60 runs on one core with three busy loops and 60 of 60 on two cores. The old test passed 60 of 60 under the same load, so the stall is the reproduction that counts.

The stale key, dropped as unwanted in the launcher's want-none-want gap, fell through: forgotten, nothing arrived, nothing repainted, and the theme change's repaint had skipped it as pending. The exclusion bought nothing. A dropped key has no old-theme result to throw away, and the worker's `load_with` resolves the theme when it runs, so a key sent again is looked up in the new one. That is the product working as designed, and a starved runner (a python-dbusmock answering late during 100 reloads) would have failed the test for it. The bus monitor now also records when each connection first spoke, when each `Introspect` was sent and when its answer came (by reply serial and destination). A connection between the probes is explained only when it sent nothing but `Hello` and `Introspect`, and an older connection's `Introspect` sent at least 1.9 s before it (the 2 s deadline runs from the question, a moment before the call) was unanswered or answered no sooner than that. Anything else still fails, so the old per-question shape (a new connection per refresh on a healthy bus) still fails. The test asserts the monitor saw an answer whenever it saw an `Introspect`, so a monitor that missed answers cannot explain every connection; it prints the reconnects. `reloads.rs::a_reconnect_after_an_unanswered_introspect_is_explained` checks the classification on recorded events: connections made after a prompt answer are unexplained, a reconnect after an unanswered or 2.5 s answer is explained, and one that did more than introspect is not. **2026-10-12 · m6-flakes (review): the idle window's start is read just before its snapshot.** The window checked `seconds_into_minute()` and only then read the minute and took its snapshots, so a stall of several seconds between the two could start the window at :00–:02 of the next minute, inside the tick's frame and trims, with the minute the same at both ends. One clock read now gives the minute and second right before the snapshot. The window is taken again (at most three times, as before) if it began before :02 or the minute changed by its end. **2026-10-12 · m6-flakes (review 2): the reloads test explains a reconnect by the bus's order and one late call each.** The classifier in "the reloads test explains `strand-introspect`'s reconnect" above had three gaps. First, it judged lateness from the monitor's timestamps against a 100 ms margin (1.9 s). Both stamps are taken when the test's monitor task reaches each message, and `strand-introspect`'s deadline starts before the connection lookup and the write, so on a starved runner a call strand gave up on could measure 1.88 s, and its real reconnect failed the test. Second, one late or unseen `Introspect` from any older connection explained every later connection that only introspected, and the guard asserted only that some answer was seen, not what that paragraph claimed. Third, the immediate retry after a call fails with no answer starts milliseconds after the call, under the 1.9 s gap the classifier required, though that paragraph named it as tolerated. The monitor now numbers every message in the bus's order. A call counts as dropped when its connection never spoke after it (order, not time) and it went unanswered, or its answer came at least half of `TIMEOUT` (1 s) after it. Every connection that only says `Hello` and `Introspect` must start after a distinct dropped call from an older connection, matched to the earliest one, so each dropped call explains one reconnect. There is no gap between the call and the reconnect, which covers the immediate retry. Half the timeout is a guess too, but a healthy bus answers in milliseconds, so the per-question shape still fails, and the margin is about 1 s of scheduling skew instead of 100 ms. A timing-free test of "late" was considered: strand closes a timed-out connection before the answer, while a per-question connection closes after it. It was not used: when the dropped connection's socket closes depends on when `strand-introspect`'s current-thread runtime next runs its tasks (possibly not until the next refresh, not verified), and a reader descheduled past the answer reverses the order anyway, the same scheduling question again. The guard is now the claim that paragraph made, restricted to connections that spoke again: the test fails on any `Introspect` the monitor saw no answer to whose connection then sent something else, since a monitor that misses answers would make a kept connection look dropped. `reloads.rs::a_reconnect_after_an_unanswered_introspect_is_explained` now covers an unanswered call with a reconnect 5 ms later, a 1.88 s answer, a second per-question connection after one dropped call (unexplained), and a late call whose connection asked again (it explains nothing, and when unanswered the guard reports it). It fails with the 1.9 s threshold back, without the one-to-one match, and without the "never spoke again" condition. Runs: 2 of 2 unloaded (0 refreshes, 0 reconnects) and 3 of 3 on two cores with three busy loops (1 refresh answered, 0 reconnects each).

**2026-10-12 · m6-flakes (review 3): `strand-introspect` logs its drops, and the reloads test explains a reconnect by that log, with nothing timed.** Review 2's classifier still decided "late" from the monitor's stamps (an answer at least half of `TIMEOUT` after its call). Those stamps are taken when the test's monitor task reads each message, on a one-worker runtime, and zbus queues messages without dropping any. A monitor stalled past a late answer reads the call and the answer back to back and measures a gap near zero. So the skew has no bound, not "about 1 s" as that paragraph said, and a real timeout reconnect could still fail the test. Separately, `Shared::properties` bounds the connect by the same deadline, so a reconnect whose handshake runs past it leaves a connection that said only `Hello` (or that the monitor saw nothing from) and never asked, which the classifier reported as unexplained. Neither the bus nor the monitor can tell, without timing, a connection strand gave up on from one closed after its answer: both look like `Hello`, `Introspect`, answer. Only strand knows, so `strand-introspect` now says so. `Shared::forget` logs `dropped its connection :1.N to the bus (why)` at `warn`, with the connection's unique name, and a connect that runs past the deadline logs `gave up connecting to the bus (no answer within 2s)`. Both are written before the next question connects again. That is worth having anyway: a bus that stops answering was silent before. The reloads test reads strand's log (`STRAND_LOG=info`). A connection between the probes is explained only when it sent nothing but `Hello` and `Introspect` (at least one message) and is numbered after a connection the log names, one reconnect per drop, the earliest it can. The bus numbers connections in order, so this is still the bus's order. A connection that never asked is explained the same way, and while the log has connects given up on, each such connection becomes a drop that explains one later reconnect. The monitor's timestamps, answers and "last word" order are gone, and so is review 2's guard on unanswered calls, which existed only because unanswered calls explained connections; with a stalled monitor at the end it was a latent flake of its own. The per-question shape still fails: no drop is logged. Injected by not keeping the connection, the test fails ("strand's sockets changed by reload 93 … 0 drops in strand-introspect's log"). Provoking real drops (`TTL` set to 1 s locally, and the ppd mock stopped with `SIGSTOP` for 8 s at 5, 7 or 9 s) showed the purpose was not met before this either. The per-reload socket check failed on the reconnect's new socket in 2 of 3 runs, before the bus check ran. A socket change is now allowed up to the number of drops logged since the baseline: at most one socket opened and one closed per drop, the dropped one perhaps not closed yet (`sockets_explained`). With both changes, the same injection passed 3 of 3: one reconnect explained in each of two runs (`named: {15}` and `{15, 24}`), and none in the third. Review 2's classifier fails both review scenarios on recorded events: a dropped call whose late answer the monitor read 1 ms after it ("left: [(10, [Hello, Introspect])]"), and a `Hello`-only reconnect ("left: [(10, [Hello])]"). `reloads.rs::a_reconnect_after_a_logged_drop_is_explained` replaces `a_reconnect_after_an_unanswered_introspect_is_explained`. It covers a reconnect after a logged drop, a second per-question connection after one drop (unexplained), a drop that names a later connection (it explains nothing before it), a connection that did more than introspect, and a `Hello`-only connection after a drop followed by another reconnect, which is explained only when the log has the connect given up on. `reloads.rs::a_socket_replaced_after_a_logged_drop_is_explained` covers the socket allowance. `strand-introspect`'s `a_question_that_times_out_does_not_wait_for_another_callers_connect` now asserts both log lines and fails without them ("the dropped connection is not logged: []"). The docs follow. features.md's box no longer says "ordered by the bus rather than by timestamps" of a test that still timed its calls, and it says a run may see no refresh at all. The first reloads paragraph above said "one refresh is seen per run" from the runs then, and review 2's unloaded runs saw none. architecture.md names the two log lines (and the crate's dependency on `log`), and handoff.md's CI entry follows. Runs: 2 of 2 unloaded and 3 of 3 on two cores with three busy loops, each with 1 refresh and 0 reconnects.

**2026-10-12 · m6-integration-w1 (integrator sweep, sweep-1 and sweep-2): a hidden row's `drag:` values are evaluated from its item, so spec.md 6.7's limit is gone, not narrowed.** S-edges left `Instance::drop_at` guessing what each row's `drag:` value is of its item from the mounted rows (the item, its key or one field, the same for all) and spec.md 6.7 with a narrower "known limit of the implementation", while features.md's box and m6-edges' heading said the limit was removed; the owner had asked for `at` to be exact. Now `drop_at` asks, for each of the first `before` items, what that row would drag if it were mounted: `ListWindow` keeps the `for`'s body, binding, scope and instance prefix (`mount::probe::RowProbe`), and `Ctx::probe_row` walks the row in a scope of its own, disposed after, as mounting walks it: elements (each `drag:` source by its last `when` that holds, else its own; a source whose value fails holds none, as mounted), `if` and `match` branches, components with their parameters bound as `mount_component` binds them and their slots, a `for` inside an element that does not hold rows, and the boundaries render's `copy` keeps (a nested `list` or an element holding a `for`'s rows contributes only its own content). The row's `let`s are plain memos and its `state`s read the cell the row keeps while scrolled out (`keep_row_cells`, found by the key the mounted row used, never taken) or else their initial value; nothing reaches the scene, the registry or the services. Two things a row never laid out cannot know are recorded, not limits of the meaning: a `when` on its laid-out size reads 0 (as a mounted row does before its first layout), and a `let` awaiting a service method is not fetched. The cost is one walk per hidden row on a drop, which is a user action. spec.md 6.7's "known limit" sentence is replaced by what the rows not mounted are judged by; a bug fix under spec.md 14 (no syntax, schema or meaning changes: the meaning is the one 6.7 states). Proved by `crates/strand/src/run/lists.rs::tests::a_hidden_copy_is_found_whatever_the_row_drags` (a `Grab` built from the item, a nested field `p.meta.id`, a `when`'s, a `let`'s, a `state`'s, a component's, a kept `state` changed while mounted and scrolled out, and the probe leaving that cell in place), which fails with `at` 43 for "a value built from the item" on the S-edges code; the earlier tests (`a_hidden_copy_is_one_by_renders_test`, `a_drop_leaves_out_a_copy_render_could_not_see`, `crates/strand-compiler/tests/render.rs::a_drop_on_a_scrolled_windowed_list_is_exact`) pass unchanged. architecture.md's drag-and-drop bullet, features.md's box and handoff.md's known limit follow; the m6-edges paragraph is annotated where it says the narrower limit stays.

**2026-10-12 · m6-integration-w1 (verification): the compositor matrix's "the wallpaper never showed" was the launch test's app outliving its test.** GitHub's `compositors` job failed `surfaces_meet_the_live_compositor` on niri in 7 of 13 runs since 17:08 UTC (2 in about 40 during M5), across branches with unrelated code and identical packages. Every failing run's niri leg took 64.5–64.6 s against 8.9–9.9 s for a passing one, and in every one the next stores test's boot line still showed the window `strand-activated` / "launched" (in none of the passing ones). The new failure record (`matrix-<kind>-surfaces-no-wallpaper.png`, the pixel, the surfaces and the compositor's windows and layers) caught it on this branch (run 38313012428): `(320, 540)` read `[127, 200, 255]`, the test window's light blue, and `niri msg windows` listed "launched" (pid 1432) as a 628×704 tile over the left half, the `strand-Wall` layer showing on the right. `a_launched_app_is_activated_with_its_token` wrote `done` and removed the helper's directory within the helper's 20 ms poll, so the helper often never saw `done` and kept its window mapped for its 60 s wait. The same leak failed sway's `the_stores_report_the_live_compositor` once ("never: closed", run 38285415946). Strand was never at fault, so the fix is in the test. The helper writes its pid with its env, and a `Launched` guard says `done`, waits for that pid to exit and only then removes the directory. The guard kills the app after `PATIENCE`, and it also runs when the test panics. The test then waits until the compositor shows no window, and the helper's wait gives up as soon as its directory is gone. With the fix (`5fc576e`) the compositors job passed all four compositors 10 times in a row on GitHub (runs 38313500275 twice, 38313506857 twice, 38313514110, 38313520931, 38314895371, 38314903251, 38314911205 and 38314918416; niri's leg 8.9–9.9 s in each), and `scripts/container/matrix.sh` passed here, along with `MATRIX_LOOP=10` on niri and sway (0 of 10 failed on each). Why the rate rose on 2026-10-12 is not known; the race depends on how quickly `drop(bar)` returns on the runner (crates/strand/tests/compositor_matrix.rs::a_launched_app_is_activated_with_its_token, ::surfaces_meet_the_live_compositor).

**2026-10-12 · m6-integration-w1 (verification): `strand report`'s "not two painted bars" was a real scale bug: a surface made just before its output's scale changed kept the old scale.** `m5::report::every_section_is_reported_and_the_json_round_trips` failed in 6 of the last 120 GitHub CI runs (38211145613, 38212608204, 38217127812, 38285415946, 38291508165, 38314903251; run 38314918416 passed), and every dump has the same shape: HEADLESS-2 at scale 2.0 and 960×540 logical, its bar 960×32 with one frame drawn at scale 1.0, and no later frame. The test runs `swaymsg create_output` and then `output HEADLESS-2 scale 2` at once, so strand sometimes creates the bar between the two commands. sway 1.9 (`surface_update_outputs` in `sway/desktop/surface.c`) sends `wp_fractional_scale_v1.preferred_scale` and `wl_surface.preferred_buffer_scale` when a layer surface is made, and on an output scale change it sends them again only to surfaces that `output_for_each_surface` reaches. That walk skips a surface with no buffer yet, and mapping one sends nothing. So a bar that sway saw made at scale 1 but not mapped when the scale changed got 960 logical from its configure and never got 2.0. strand kept the scale from creation, and a monitor scaled by kanshi right after a hotplug would show the same blurry bar. `scale_change_before_the_first_frame` in strand-surface's sway tests makes it happen every time: the bar is created, a `roundtrip` lets sway answer without strand dispatching, and then the output's scale is set to 2. Without the fix it failed 20 of 20 on both scale paths (logical 960, buffer 960×36, scale 120). The fix is in strand-surface: when an output's geometry changes, each surface on that output that the compositor has not shown a frame of yet (no presentation, discard or frame callback) takes its scale from the output again, as it did at creation (`rescale_unshown_on`). A preference the compositor sends later still wins, and a surface the compositor has shown keeps trusting it alone. Evidence: the two new tests passed 50 of 50, `cargo test -p strand-surface` and `cargo test -p strand` pass, the report test passed 100 of 100 and the sway scale and hotplug tests 20 of 20 in the container. The CI race itself was not reproduced here (the old report test passed 200 of 200 unloaded); the deterministic test reproduces its exact dump (crates/strand-surface/tests/sway.rs::a_scale_set_before_the_first_frame_is_kept, ::a_scale_set_before_the_first_frame_is_kept_on_the_integer_path).

**2026-10-12 · m6-integration-w1 (verification): the nightly fuzzer's "the overlay opened with no notice and nothing held back for 250 ms" was the check taking a held save for the fix.** Nightly run 38313001306 (job 115022936574; seed 38313001306) failed `random_edits_through_five_save_styles` at step 4318 (retype), InPlace, with "held 129.85 ms on the logic thread". It was the only such failure in the 17 nightly runs since 2026-10-06 and in the 120 failed CI runs since 2026-10-10. The seed reproduces it here on the same step in all six pipelines (4,400 edits on four cores loaded with busy loops), so the cause is the edit sequence, not a slow runner. A broken save left `store.strand` with a syntax error. The retype step then saved `bar.strand` alone first (a partial save), which was held back behind that error with the same diagnostic, so the overlay's 250 ms ran on. The rest came after the test's 50 ms watch, and the overlay opened 252–267 ms after the broken load, before the commit, as design.md's "errors that survive 250 ms of quiet" says it should. Strand was not at fault. The round-3 check (2026-10-06) began the hold's end at any save's start (`saving()`), so it took the partial save's start for the fix's and estimated 145–151 ms (130 ms on the runner). The fix is in the check. The logic thread now reports when it applied each load (a `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local, `run::LOADS_APPLIED`, sent in `Shell::apply` with the same instant the overlay's quiet period starts from). The fuzzer judges the hold on that timeline exactly, from the held load to the load that commits (or to now, if none has yet). It needs the full 250 ms (`overlay::QUIET`), where the round-3 estimate allowed 200, and a failure now says how each load got from its save to the logic thread. The seeded run passes with the new check. `a_save_held_back_behind_a_broken_one_does_not_end_its_hold` is the same case in miniature: under the round-3 check it measured 115 ms against 384 ms on the logic thread. It passed 10 of 10 on loaded cores, and so did 10 runs of 400 edits each with random seeds (crates/strand/src/fuzz.rs::random_edits_through_five_save_styles, ::a_save_held_back_behind_a_broken_one_does_not_end_its_hold).

Handlers and `id:` on a call are its root element's (m6-w2-language, "handlers and `id:` on a component call are its root element's"), and that covers the case the owner hit: an island component reports its hover through `Island id: isl { … }` and `isl.hover`, and the tray menu's rows switch the menu through a handler on each row's call, which runs in the caller's scope. State that two places need lives in the caller, which passes it down as an ordinary read-only parameter and changes it from a handler on the call. A parameter mode would add a concept for a case real testing has not hit, and "does it remove a concept, or add one?" counts against it. So parameters stay read-only (spec.md 5.2), assigning one stays a load error (spec.md 8.3), `<->` on a call stays `check::two_way_prop`, and a component still cannot expose the state of an element that is not its root. Nothing changes in the language, the code or spec.md. The question is revisited only if real testing hits a component that must write its caller's state from inside itself. `<->` parameters then land in a later wave with that component as the test, and under spec.md 14 they would only give a meaning to programs rejected today. owner-testing.md marks gap 6 fixed for the owner's case, with the rest declined for now (crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_calls_handlers_and_id_are_its_root_elements, ::a_calls_id_and_screen_reach_its_hover_popup).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner: the default `$motion.spatial` is spring(3000, 0.75), the owner's ruling on bug 2 (owner-testing.md).** The owner took option (b) of m6-w2-surface's proposal "a snappier default `$motion.spatial`" (2026-10-13). spring(700, 0.9) reached half way at 60 ms and 90% at 129 ms, where Quickshell's 200 ms OutBack does at 26 and 60 ms. spring(3000, 0.75) is half way at 27 ms and 90% at 51 ms, overshoots by 2.84% (`exp(-ζπ/√(1-ζ²))`), and is within 0.2% of rest at 141 ms. Option (a), keeping the spring and having the guide teach overrides, leaves every shell with the motion the owner found slow. Option (c), spring(1600, 1) as `$motion.effects` uses, is still twice as slow to 90% (97 ms). Option (b) matches OutBack's pace with a small bounce and stays a spring, so an interrupted hover keeps its velocity; it closes the gap without adding a concept. design.md fixes the value, so its theme changes in this commit, and so does every copy: the compiler's design fixture and its snapshots, the guide's level 5, strand-theme's built-in theme and its export golden, `strand_scene::motion::SPATIAL`, and the doc comments that cite it (`strand-dev reference` regenerates functions.md). `$motion.effects` and `$motion.bouncy` are unchanged. The owner accepted a visible cost. Whatever moves or resizes along the default passes its place by up to 2.84% and comes back once. A `pages` slide across 120 px shows up to 4 px of background at its far edge for a frame or two, and a toast entering 420 px from the right passes its place by up to 12 px. The overshoot also exposed a render bug. A list's drawn scroll offset followed its spring only while it moved more than 0.01 px a frame, and an overshooting spring crosses its target fast enough that its last frame before settling can land 0.00024 px short; the drawn offset then never reached the target. Now, once a scroll is at rest, its drawn offset lands on the target exactly (`ScrollState::unapplied`, in `layout/list.rs`, used by `renderer/lists.rs`); `motion.rs::wheel_steps_spring_the_offset` proves it unchanged. Re-blessed, each a frame mid-spring that the faster spring moves and nothing else, each viewed against the old reference: `motion_springs` (the filmstrip), `effects_morph`, `effects_morph_shared`, `effects_morph_across`, `effects_roll`, `effects_transitions`, `effects_pixelate`, `effects_image_swap` and `graph_history`. The effects references described as "partway", "mid" or "on its way" are now taken two refreshes in (64% of the way), not at 64–80 ms, where the new spring has already landed. Assertions rewritten for the new pace or the overshoot, each keeping its intent:

- `strand-render/tests/motion.rs::springs_sampled_at_fixed_timestamps_match_reference`: "never moves back" becomes `assert_springs_to`, which checks the value ends on the target, passes it by no more than the analytic peak (2.84% plus 0.2%, and a pixel of rounding), and turns back at most once.
- `::retargeting_mid_flight_keeps_velocity`: retargeted two refreshes in (64% of the way), not five, by when the new spring has landed.
- `::keyed_reorder_glides_to_new_slots`: the first frame is within the spring's first refresh (26% of 48 px, at most 13 px), not under 12 px, and the glide follows `assert_springs_to`.
- `::enter_and_exit_poses_and_siblings_slide_to_fill_the_gap`: the enter moves on every frame up to the second and is still short of its place there (89% three refreshes in), not up to the fifth.
- `::token_swaps_glide_and_popin_scales`: popin's first frame is within the spring's first refresh (scale 0.63, at most 13 of 20 px), and mid-flight is checked one refresh later, not three.
- `::a_leaving_toast_lets_the_next_slide_up_in_a_content_sized_panel`: each step is at most the spring's largest advance in one refresh (38% of the 62 px slot, 24 px), not 12 px.
- `::a_centred_panel_keeps_its_rows_in_place_as_it_grows`: the first frame is within the spring's first refresh of the row's 12 px move (at least −19), not at least −16.
- `::a_lone_toast_enters_with_its_panel_and_leaves_before_it_closes`: the exit is read on row 2, since the toast's height collapses on the same spring and leaves row 15 after one frame.
- `::pages_slide_by_source_order`: the new page may stop short of the clip by the overshoot (4 px), and its edge follows `assert_springs_to`.
- `strand-render/tests/effects.rs::a_pages_transition_wipes_one_page_over_the_other` and `::transition_masks_reveal_and_hide`: mid-wipe and the closing masks are two refreshes in, not four.
- `::a_shared_morph_starts_from_the_named_box`: the first frame is checked where the spring puts it, 26% of the way from the pill (pixel 54, 30), not over the pill itself.
- `strand-scene/src/motion.rs::tests::retargeting_keeps_velocity`: interrupted at 25 ms (half way), not 60 ms (97%), and the position is compared within 1e-4, since f32 rounds the new displacement.
- `strand/tests/acceptance.rs::toasts_arrive_stack_slide_and_leave`: the 2 px "never backwards" tolerance becomes the overshoot bound (12 px, turning back once). The slide in and the slide up are read by time from the first shot and from the click, not counted: one shot off its place within 200 or 400 ms, and at rest from 400 or 600 ms. Grim's shots come slower than the spring's 52 ms to 90%, so the old count of two caught frames failed in every release run. The hovered toast's band is read once settled, since the first shot showing it can catch it entering and put the pointer elsewhere; the `toasts_hover` reference is unchanged.

The new default is proven by crates/strand-scene/src/motion.rs::tests::the_default_spatial_spring_is_snappy and crates/strand-theme/src/defaults.rs::tests::the_built_in_theme_resolves_every_base_token. owner-testing.md marks bug 2 fixed; the owner judges the feel on their session.

## m6-w2-services

S-services' M6 wave-2 stream on `laptop/m6-w2-services`: the owner's hands-on findings (docs/owner-testing.md, read from the main checkout) that are services' to fix. Code comments that cite m6-w2-services point here.

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-services: a workspace that does not exist yet is switched to, `workspaces.focus(target)` (Gaps 2).** `ws.focus()` needs a `Workspace`, and Hyprland makes a workspace only when it is switched to, so an empty persistent slot could not be clicked. The service gains one action, `workspaces.focus(target: int | text)`: an `int` is the workspace's number, the same on every compositor, and a `text` its name. It adds a call, not a concept: it is `ws.focus()` for a workspace the shell can name but not hold, and the union keeps it one action rather than `focus_id`/`focus_name`. Each adapter makes what its compositor makes on switching. A number (`WmAction::FocusWorkspaceNumber`): Hyprland's workspace of that id, its numbered workspaces' ids being their numbers (`dispatch workspace 4`); sway's `workspace number 4` (the workspace whose name starts with 4, made when none does); niri's fourth workspace of the focused output (`{"Index": 4}`, as `niri msg action focus-workspace 4`; past the last is niri's own empty one); the standard protocols a listed workspace named by the number. A negative number on sway is a configured workspace's id of the adapter's own (Gaps 3, below), so a slot's `id` still reaches it; zero and other negative numbers name no workspace. A name: Hyprland's `name:<name>` (a number by number, never `special:`); sway's `workspace "<name>"`, which sway makes on its assigned output; niri's named workspace (`{"Name": …}`, a number that names none being the n-th of the focused output), since niri cannot make a workspace by name; the standard protocols switch only to a workspace they list. The review (M1) asked for one meaning of a number: the first version took an `int` as a workspace's id, which is the number on Hyprland but sway's internal container id and niri's own id, so `workspaces.focus(4)` meant three things. Anything else fails as `UnknownWorkspace` or the new `UnknownWorkspaceName`, logged like every action's failure. `ws.focus()` on a Hyprland id no workspace has used to answer `UnknownWorkspace` and now makes it; nothing in the language could reach that path before (only listed workspaces had items), so no program changes meaning (spec.md 14). A float is not a workspace number: the checker types the argument `int | text`, and the language stream's fix of integer list literals (gaps 12) makes a bar's `[1, 2, 3]` an `[int]`. The service still takes a whole float as the number, as defensive handling of a value the checker does not pass, not as a documented form (review M2). The compiler's provisional `workspaces` stub declares the new members, additive under spec.md 14 (`crates/strand-services/src/wm/hyprland.rs::tests::named_switches_make_what_hyprland_makes`, `::dispatches_name_the_target`, `crates/strand-services/src/wm/niri.rs::tests::actions_are_niri_requests`, `crates/strand-services/src/wm/sway.rs::tests::assigned_workspaces_are_configured_and_made_by_switching`, `crates/strand-services/tests/hyprland.rs::configured_and_named_workspaces_are_switched_to_and_made`, `crates/strand-services/tests/sway.rs::sway_config_assignments_are_configured_workspaces` (a number made and focused by `workspace number`, a slot by its negative id, 0 refused, on real sway 1.9), `crates/strand-services/tests/niri.rs::the_stores_follow_niri` (a number sent as `{"Index": n}`), `crates/strand-services/tests/wm_services.rs::the_compositor_stores_follow_hyprland`, `crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::workspace_and_window_members_check`).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-services: persistent workspaces are a list of their own, `workspaces.configured`, placed by `workspaces.slots(screen)` (Gaps 3).** Hyprland's workspace rules say which workspaces belong on which monitor before they exist, and the owner's bar shows them all. Two shapes were weighed. (a) Put them in `workspaces.all` with a new `exists: bool`: every existing reader of `all` (a dot per workspace, `count`, `on(screen)`) would start showing workspaces that are not there, which changes `all`'s meaning, against spec.md 14, and every `Workspace` would carry a field that is true everywhere else. (b) A list of their own, records of the same `Workspace` type: `all` keeps its meaning, a slot is an ordinary `Workspace` (empty, inactive, unfocused) whose `ws.focus()` makes it, and when the compositor makes it, it leaves `configured` and appears in `all` under the same id on Hyprland. (b) was taken, with one `fn`, `workspaces.slots(screen)`, since merging and ordering two lists is beyond the language's thin list helpers (gaps 11): the screen's workspaces and its slots, by number, then the rest in order. The number is the id on Hyprland (where a workspace renamed `4: web` is still 4, and a named workspace's negative id puts it with the rest), the number the name starts with elsewhere (review minor 11). What counts as configured: on Hyprland a numbered rule (`workspace = 4, monitor:DP-1`, or `monitor:desc:…` by description prefix) for a monitor that is on, read from `j/workspacerules` at connection and on `configreloaded` (a reply that does not parse is no rules, never a degradation; a named rule makes no slot, because its id exists only once Hyprland makes it, and a selector such as `r[1-5]` names no one workspace); on sway, the main config's top-level `workspace <name> output <outputs…>` lines from `get_config` (with `set $var` expanded, quotes, continued lines; blocks and comments skipped; not included files, which `get_config` does not send), on the first of its outputs that is active (the outputs read at the start, on `reload` and on every `output` event, so a hotplug moves the slots; review minor 12), and with ids of the adapter's own (`-(n + 1)`) since sway gives a workspace an id only once made; niri has none, because its named workspaces always exist and are in `all`. sway makes the first workspace assigned to an output when the output comes, so that one is never a slot (`tests/sway.rs`). (`crates/strand-services/src/wm/hyprland.rs::tests::numbered_rules_are_configured_workspaces`, `crates/strand-services/src/wm/sway.rs::tests::assignments_are_read_from_the_config`, `::assigned_workspaces_are_configured_and_made_by_switching`, `::an_output_event_reads_the_outputs_again`, `crates/strand-services/src/wm/service.rs::tests::slots_follow_the_compositors_numbers`, `crates/strand-services/tests/hyprland.rs::configured_and_named_workspaces_are_switched_to_and_made`, `::hyprland_adapter_follows_replayed_traffic`, `::the_hub_shares_one_adapter_between_stores` (a late subscriber gets the slots in the replay), `crates/strand-services/tests/sway.rs::sway_config_assignments_are_configured_workspaces` (real sway 1.9), `crates/strand-services/tests/wm_services.rs::the_compositor_stores_follow_hyprland`.)

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-services: a window is linked to its desktop entry, `win.app`, and draws its icon (Bugs 3, gaps 9).** `Window.icon` was the raw app id "until the apps service resolves desktop entries", which nothing did, so Spotify (`Spotify`, XWayland) and Chromium (`Chromium-browser`) drew no icon, and a bar mapping windows to categories had to match `apps.all` by hand. The compositor service now reads the listed desktop entries (`apps::AppIndex`, the same reading as `apps.all`, on the blocking pool at its start and again whenever the `apps` service's sources or the icon theme change, `apps::changed`; one read at a time, a change during a read marking it to read once more) and finds each window's entry from its app id, the first rule that matches winning: the entry's id; the same ignoring case (`Spotify`); its `StartupWMClass` ignoring case; the last part of a reverse-DNS id (`org.gnome.Nautilus` for `nautilus`, or the app id's last part for an entry named by it); the entry's name ignoring case; and last the longest dash-separated head of the app id that is an entry's id (`chromium` for `Chromium-browser`, the class some Chromium builds give their XWayland windows). The icon is the entry's when the theme has it, else the app id's when the theme has that (as written, then lowercased), else the entry's fallback icon, else the app id as before. The link is a new field, `Window.app: App?` (the same `App` record `apps.all` lists, so `win.app?.categories` gives a category glyph): one field rather than a second record or a `fn`, so it adds a link, not a concept. Only listed entries link (a `NoDisplay` entry is not an app the shell shows). `icon` changing from the raw app id to the entry's icon is a bug fix under spec.md 14: the schema documented it as "an icon name for its app", and the raw id was the stated stopgap; `app` is additive, and the compiler's `Window` stub declares it. The first version held the state back until the first read, so a slow desktop-entry directory delayed the bar's workspaces and windows (review minor 10); the compositor's state is now published at once, a window showing its app id and no app until its lookup lands. The lookups run on the blocking pool too, one batch of app ids at a time, each id's result kept until the entries are read again (an older result standing until the newer one lands), and the state is patched with the icons and apps when a batch lands, so a window flips once from its app id to its entry's icon, a moment after the compositor is read (`crates/strand-services/tests/apps.rs::windows_find_their_desktop_entries`, `crates/strand-services/tests/wm_services.rs::windows_are_linked_to_their_apps`, `::windows_are_published_before_the_desktop_entries_are_read`, with a FIFO for a desktop entry that blocks its read until the test lets it go). Since a link can land at any moment after the state, the compositor-service tests link windows to no desktop entry and no icon theme (`tests/common::no_desktop_entries`, set by `Collector::new`, `wm_services`'s `serial()` and the idle test) unless a test sets its own: a GitHub runner's Firefox entry linked the replayed `firefox` window inside `niri_adapter_follows_replayed_traffic`'s quiet window (run 38512677814), where the container, with no such entry, passed. A link that changes nothing is never published, so with no entries no late batch can come.

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-services: `media.position` is writable, and writing it seeks (gaps 13).** A scrubber needs to seek; the choices were a writable field or a `seek(fraction)` action. The field is writable (`position: float rw`): a slider already binds `<-> brightness.level` and `<-> audio.sink.volume`, so `slider { value: <-> media.position }` is a scrubber with nothing new to learn, where an action would be a second name for the same number (it removes a concept rather than adding one). `position` stays the fraction 0 to 1 (`elapsed` stays read-only: one writable place per quantity). The service seeks the active player with MPRIS `SetPosition(trackid, µs)` when the track names an `mpris:trackid` other than `NoTrack`, else `Seek(offset)` from where it is now (players without track ids accept only that), in a task of its own; the position is fixed at the target at once and answers the write, so a dragged scrubber does not jump back, the player's `Seeked` confirms or corrects it, and a failed call asks the position again. A player whose `CanSeek` is false, a track of unknown or zero length, and a value that is not a number keep the place (the write answers with the current position). Adding `rw` is additive under spec.md 14 (a program that compiled still does; one that assigned `media.position` was a `check::read_only` error and now seeks) (`crates/strand-services/tests/media.rs::writing_the_position_seeks_the_player`, whose halfway seek goes to a player that sends no `Seeked`, so the position comes from the write alone, `crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::media_position_is_a_scrubber`).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-services: the `network` service over iwd where NetworkManager does not run (gaps 15).** The owner runs iwd alone (device `wlan0`), so `network` was offline. The service now has two backends behind the one schema, and no new concept in the language: NetworkManager whenever it owns its name (it may itself drive iwd, and it is still D-Bus activated when nothing runs), iwd (`net.connman.iwd`) when only iwd does; either appearing or going ends the body's backend and chooses again, in the same body (no restart, joins in flight reported as failed as a NetworkManager restart already reports them). iwd is followed, never started: `Daemon::watch` follows a name without activation, since activating iwd beside a NetworkManager that runs wpa_supplicant would fight it for the device. The mapping: `wifi` is the station-mode `Device`'s `Powered` (written there); `connected` is the `Station`'s `State` `connected` or `roaming` (iwd knows only Wi-Fi, so a wired-only machine under iwd reads not connected; the schema says so); `ssid` is the `ConnectedNetwork`'s `Name`; `strength` comes from a signal level agent this process serves (`RegisterSignalLevelAgent` with 5 dBm steps from -50 to -90: iwd tells when the signal crosses one, so nothing is polled, where NetworkManager's access point `Strength` is a signalled property too), read first from `GetOrderedNetworks` when a network is joined, on NetworkManager's scale (-100 dBm is 0, -50 is 1); `access_points` is `GetOrderedNetworks` (one entry per name, the strongest) re-read when a scan ends, with `Scan` asked only while a visible reader reads them, as over NetworkManager; `secure` is a `psk` or `wep` network. Joining is `Network.Connect` in a task of its own; `connect_with(password)` holds the password for the passphrase agent this process registers, which iwd asks only for a network it does not know (iwd then keeps the passphrase, as NetworkManager keeps a profile). The refusals are NetworkManager's (`refusal`): an open network takes no password, an 802.1X one joins only once iwd knows it. The review's minors fixed: every call to iwd carries `NO_AUTO_START` (`iwd::call`), so a call that reaches the bus after iwd exited is refused rather than starting it; both agents answer only iwd's current unique name, so a password goes to iwd alone and no other peer sets the strength; `connect_with` on a network iwd knows forgets it first (`KnownNetwork.Forget`), so the new password replaces the kept one rather than being ignored; a registration iwd refuses is tried once per iwd and, for the signal level agent, once per station, not on every signal; the level is dropped when the station goes or comes (a power cycle), not kept from the last network; joins in flight when NetworkManager takes over fail with "NetworkManager took over", and a join whose task ends without answering fails too; and the NetworkManager backend chooses again when iwd turns out to own its name once the backend has subscribed to iwd's name, closing a boot race that left `network` offline until a daemon changed (no deterministic test: the window is between two bus calls). Tested against a zbus iwd on a private bus, since python-dbusmock has no iwd template (`crates/strand-services/tests/network_iwd.rs::network_follows_iwd_where_networkmanager_is_absent`, `::a_refused_signal_agent_is_asked_once`, `crates/strand-services/src/network/iwd.rs::tests`, with `::iwd_is_never_started_by_a_call` on a bus where iwd is activatable, `::a_new_password_for_a_known_network_forgets_it_first`, `::a_station_coming_or_going_drops_the_level`).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-services: a builtin `session` service over logind (gaps 1's power menu, gaps 17).** The coordinator added it to this stream at the owner's request (first-party services for common shell needs). `session` serves logind (`org.freedesktop.login1`): `can_suspend`, `can_hibernate`, `can_reboot` and `can_power_off` from `CanSuspend` and the others (`yes` and `challenge` are true, since polkit then asks for a password; `no` and `na` false), asked at the start and again when logind restarts, since they are methods logind signals no change of; the actions `suspend()`, `hibernate()`, `reboot()` and `power_off()` (logind's `Suspend`, `Hibernate`, `Reboot`, `PowerOff`, `interactive` true so polkit may ask), `lock()` (`LockSession`) and `log_out()` (`TerminateSession`), the last two on this process's own session, found by `GetSession("auto")` (the caller's session, else the user's graphical one, so a shell started by a systemd user unit still finds it); each call is a task of its own, and a failure is `failed(action, error)`, as `network.failed` and `bluetooth.failed` report theirs. One member beyond the coordinator's list: `event lock_requested`, logind's `Lock` signal on that session. Without it `session.lock()` would do nothing visible in a shell whose lock is its own `lock { open: <-> locked }` (Strand listened to logind nowhere); with it `on session.lock_requested { locked = true }` makes `session.lock()`, `loginctl lock-session` and an idle daemon's lock command all reach the shell's own lock, which removes the need for `strand set lock.locked true` in the idle daemon rather than adding a second way. Hibernate is an action even where `can_hibernate` is false: logind refuses it and `failed` says so, which a menu that greys the button never sees. `lock()` and `log_out()` are bounded at 120 s; the power actions are not, because polkit's dialog may stay open as long as the user leaves it and logind acts once it is answered, so a bound would report `failed` for an action that then happens (review minor 13; the schema says a power action fails only on logind's refusal). Tested with python-dbusmock's `logind` template, the session given an id other than `auto` (`c2`, which `GetSession("auto")` names) so lock and log out are seen to go by the id logind answers (`crates/strand-services/tests/session.rs::session_reads_logind_and_acts_through_it`, `crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::session_is_a_power_menu`).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-services: a config service named like a builtin one shadows it, with a warning (the owner's ruling).** Spec.md 4.2 made a config `service` named like a builtin one `check::redeclared` (decisions.md m5-docs, review round 3), so adding the builtin `session` would reject a config that declared its own `service session`, while spec.md 14 says a program accepted in 1.x stays accepted. Two readings went to the owner: (a) adding a builtin service counts as an addition under 14's second bullet and such a config renames its service, or (b) a config service shadows a builtin one, with a warning as a `let` or `state` gets, so every name in the prelude behaves alike and 14 holds without exceptions. The owner ruled (b) (review of `laptop/m6-w2-services`, B1). The language stream implements it in strand-compiler (`declare_global`) with the spec.md 4.2 edit; this stream does not touch the compiler, and `session` ships as it is. `crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::session_is_a_power_menu` still asserts today's `check::redeclared` in its second assertion on this branch; the integrator flips it to the shadowing warning at merge.

## m6-w2-language

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-language: `after T while c` is one-shot, said in its first sentence (owner testing, Docs 1).** The owner wrote a hover popup's close delay as `after 200ms while !over { pop = "" }`; it closed the first popup and never again, because the timer runs once per mount, as spec.md 8.4 said, but its wording ("runs once, after `c` has held for a total of `T`") reads like a grace timer that re-arms. Nothing changes meaning, so this is a wording fix under spec.md 14 (no syntax removed or changed): spec.md 8.4 now opens with "is one-shot: it runs at most once per mount of the node or component it is written in (once for the program at the top level)", says the count pauses and is not reset when `c` turns false, that the timer is done once its body has run and `c` turning false and true again never re-arms it, and names the idiom for a delay that runs each time a condition ends: `on change c after T { if !c { … } }`. The guide's level 4 says the same where it teaches `after … while` (the toast) and shows the idiom in a plain block (not a step; every construct in it is level 4 or below). A test pins both behaviours side by side (crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::after_while_is_one_shot_and_the_grace_idiom_runs_each_time).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-language: whole numbers stay `int`s through `?:` and `match` (owner testing, Gaps 12).** `fn rules(name: text) -> [int] { let r = match name { "DP-8" => [1, 2, 3, 4], _ => [] }; r }` was a type error: a whole-number literal is an `int` only where something asks for one or where it is the whole value of an untyped declaration (`state xs = [1, 2]`, decisions.md "whole numbers are ints"), and a `match` or `?:` around the list hid it, so the local `r` was a `[float]`. The shape that rule reads (`whole_shape`) now goes through `?:` and `match` when every branch has the same shape, an empty list fitting any list shape (`c ? 1 : []` is no shape). Nothing else changes: such a `state` is pinned to `float` by a fraction written to it, as before, through the same widening; and since an `int` (or `[int]`) is accepted wherever a `float` is, no program that was accepted reads differently. The other reading, making every whole literal an `int` wherever nothing asks, was not taken: an untyped `state s = c ? 1 : 2` that a handler writes `0.5` would then need the widening the declaration rule already gives, and that rule is what this extends. Under spec.md 14 this only accepts programs that were rejected; spec.md 5.3 says so (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::whole_numbers_stay_ints_through_match_and_ternaries). *Amended the same day:* a `for` over a literal list of whole numbers (`for w in [1, 2, 3] key w`) loops over `int`s too, as the iterable gets the same shape an untyped `let` does; the services stream's `workspaces.focus(target: int | text)` is called with such a `w` (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::a_looped_whole_number_list_gives_ints). *Corrected after review:* "no program that was accepted reads differently" was wrong as first written: with `int`s reaching further, four programs that loaded on `main` became type errors, because a fraction later written to a value derived from them had nothing to widen: an untyped `state size = w` from such a loop, then `size = size / 2`; a component's inferred parameter fed `[4, 8]`'s items, its `state r = n` then `r += 0.5`; `state marks = big ? [10, 20] : []` then `marks.push(2.5)`; and `let sizes = wide ? [20, 30] : [10, 20]`, `state cur = sizes[0]`, `cur = cur * 1.5`. The widening rule now covers what the extension reaches: an untyped `state` whose first value is whole (an `int` or `[int]`, whatever expression gives it) is widened by a fraction written to it as a literal-initialised one is, the widening following the value back through the declarations it came from; and a `push` or `insert` of a fraction into a whole list widens the list as an item write does. So each of the four loads and means what it did on `main` (a `float`), while a value nothing writes a fraction to stays an `int` (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::whole_number_values_widen_where_fractions_are_written).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-language: dates order (owner testing, Gaps 16).** `d.date < clock.today` was a type error (`<` needs numbers), so trimming a calendar's trailing week took `d.date.add(months: 1).month_start() == clock.today.month_start()`. Two builtin `Date`s now order by time: the checker accepts `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` between two values of the schema's `Date` record (a config's own `type Date` is not it), and the VM already compared records field by field, which for a `Date` (year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute) is time order; a date without a time of day (`hour` null) comes before every time on that day, as null orders first. Only `Date` is ordered, not records in general: a record of several fields has no order a reader would guess. A load error becomes a meaning, which spec.md 14 allows; spec.md 7.2 says so (crates/strand-compiler/tests/vm.rs::dates_order).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-language: `+` on texts, `distinct` and `sum` (owner testing, Gaps 11).** The owner's bar deduplicated glyphs with a `find` per item, built text with `join("", a, b)`, and built the workspace indicator's offset from `count`s. Three additions, each removing a workaround rather than adding a concept: `+` between two `text`s joins them, and `s += "x"` on a `text` place appends (both were load errors; `+` between a text and anything else stays one, its help naming both fixes); `xs.distinct()` keeps the first of each equal item in order (structural equality, as `==` and `contains` use; keys are kept, it is not one of the incremental view steps); `xs.sum()` adds a list of numbers of one unit, and `xs.sum(x => …)` adds what the function gives for each item, `0` for no items, null items skipped, a non-number a load error. `+` on text is not a mini-language in strings (design.md's "Bad" table): it is the operator that already exists, given to the one other type where a reader expects it. `distinct` and `sum` are list methods, which are schema entries (spec.md 1, 14: added, never changed); spec.md 7.2 names `+` on texts (crates/strand-compiler/tests/vm.rs::text_plus_distinct_and_sum). *Corrected after review:* "`0` for no items" held for numbers without a unit only; an empty list of durations summed to the whole `0`, not `0ms`. The lowering adds the zero of the sum's type, so no items is `0ms`, `0%` or `0.0` as the type says (the same test).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-language: `dur(d, clock: true)` (owner testing, Gaps 14).** `dur` writes `45 s`, `12 min`, `2 h 5 min`, right for a battery and wrong for a track's `1:23 / 3:45`. `dur` gains a named parameter, `clock: bool = false`; with `clock: true` it writes `m:ss` under an hour and `h:mm:ss` from an hour, seconds rounded down as a player's clock counts them. A parameter with a default on a builtin function is a schema addition (spec.md 14): every call that was accepted means what it did. A separate function (`clock(d)`) or a strftime-like duration format was not taken: the first adds a name for one variant of an existing one, the second a mini-language in a string. `media.position` is a fraction, so a track's elapsed time is `(media.length ?? 0s) * media.position`, which the reference's `dur` entry and this test show (crates/strand-compiler/tests/vm.rs::dur_has_a_clock_form).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-language: declared actions, the owner's ruling (owner testing, Gaps 1).** A handler could not run a command: no power menu, no compositor dispatch, no "open settings", and a `from dbus` service exposed properties only, so even logind's `Suspend` was out of reach. The owner ruled (2026-10-13) that shells must be this flexible, with first-party services for the common needs and two general fallbacks, which this implements. It amends m5-tools "outputs re-rendered on theme change …", whose *Why not `on change` plus an action* said the language has no handler action that runs a command and that adding one as a general handler statement would be a larger concept: the ruling keeps that concern by making the command a declaration, not a statement. (1) *A top-level `action name(params) [command]`.* The command is a list literal of text literals and the action's parameters only, its program a literal allowed by `permit exec`, so every program a config can run is written where it is declared, and `strand check` lists each command with its parameters (`dispatch(ws: int) runs: hyprctl dispatch workspace {ws}`); the language server shows the same on hover. A parameter needs a type (`text`, `path`, `int`, `float`, `bool` or an enum: a value with one text form) and no default, and is exactly one argument as `text` shows it, never split and never read by a shell. A handler calls it as a function, so it is checked as one (arity, types) and, as every action call, only in a handler (`check::action_in_binding`). The VM queues the request; the logic loop takes the queue after each tick's diff and starts each command on a thread of its own (64 KiB stack) that waits for it: detached in its own process group, stdin and stdout on `/dev/null`, stderr strand's log, without strand's activation token, with the huge-page setting strand inherited restored. Logic never waits on a fork. A failure to start or a non-zero exit is logged and becomes a `strand watch` notice naming the action, as a `file`'s `run` failing does, and not an overlay notice, since the shell is fine. Not taken: a shell line (`action x "cmd $arg"`), which needs quoting rules and lets a title with a `;` run something; an argv computed from any expression, which would hide what can run from `strand check`; a general `exec(...)` builtin, a second way to run things with no list. (2) *A `from dbus` service's `action name(params) = Method`.* It is a method on the service record, so `ppd.hold("performance", "game", "strand")` is an ordinary service action call: lowered as one, routed by the composite host to the custom service, which calls the method with a timeout and logs a failure as builtin services' actions do. The method is checked against introspection beside the properties (`check::dbus_method` with a did-you-mean, another number of arguments; `check::dbus_type` per argument: `int` to any integer signature or `d`, `float` to `d`, `text`/`path` to `s` or `o`, an enum to `s`, `bool` to `b`, `[text]` to `as`). Another source's block declaring one is `check::misplaced`. Under spec.md 14 this only adds: `action` starts an item only before a name (`action: text` in a service block is still a field, and a top-level `action` followed by a name was a syntax error before), so every program accepted before means what it did. spec.md 5.7 is new, 3 and 8.3 name it; grammar.md gains the keyword and the `action` and `method_action` productions; the tree-sitter grammar and its highlights follow; design.md's no-code services and learning ladder, and the guide's level 5 (in prose, since an action's command is the reader's own), name it; the reference is generated from the builtin schemas and has no entry for a declaration (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::actions_are_checked_like_calls_and_against_permit_exec, ::dbus_actions_are_checked_against_introspection; crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_declared_action_asks_for_its_command_with_whole_arguments; crates/strand/src/run/exec.rs::tests::a_command_runs_with_its_arguments_whole; crates/strand/src/check.rs::tests::actions_are_listed_and_checked_against_permit_exec; crates/strand/tests/services.rs::a_click_runs_a_declared_actions_command; crates/strand-services/tests/custom.rs::a_dbus_declarations_actions_call_its_methods). *Corrected after review:* "never read by a shell" overstated it: no shell stands between strand and the program, but the program reads its arguments its own way, so `["sh", "-c", cmd]` runs `cmd`'s value as a script and an argument starting with `-` may be read as an option. spec.md 5.7 and the guide say so, and a parameter right after a shell's `-c` (`sh`, `bash`, `dash`, `zsh` and the like, `-c` alone or among short options) is the warning `check::shell_script`, whose help shows the script written out with the value as `$1`. A command `permit exec` refuses now keeps no argv, as any other refused command, so nothing can run it. An action runs at most once at a time, with one re-run queued (the latest call's arguments), as a `file`'s `run` is, so a command that hangs holds one thread however often it is clicked. A `from dbus` action's method call is a task of its own, never awaited in the service's loop, and waits for the daemon's answer however long it takes, as the `session` service's power actions do: the method may be one polkit asks a password for, and only the daemon's error is a refusal. An enum argument is sent as the daemon spells it (as a field write is: `power_saver` as `power-saver` once read so), and a methods introspection that fails is the warning `check::dbus_unchecked` on the actions (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::refused_commands_keep_no_argv_and_shell_scripts_are_warned_about, ::unread_methods_leave_actions_unchecked_with_a_warning; crates/strand/src/run/exec.rs::tests::an_action_runs_once_at_a_time_with_one_rerun_queued, ::a_command_runs_in_a_process_group_of_its_own; crates/strand/src/run/tests.rs::a_failing_actions_command_is_a_watch_notice; crates/strand/src/services/custom.rs::tests::the_introspector_answers_methods_as_the_bus_does; crates/strand/src/services/mod.rs::tests::custom_services::the_design_ppd_service_on_a_mock_power_profiles_daemon).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-language: a config `service` named like a builtin one shadows it, the owner's ruling.** A config's `service battery from …` was the load error `check::redeclared` ("two services under one name would be ambiguous", spec.md 4.2). The owner ruled that it shadows the builtin within the config instead, with the `check::shadows_builtin` warning a `let` or `state` hiding a name gets. The reason is spec.md 14: a release that adds a builtin service (wave 2's `session`, next wave's monitor configuration) must not stop a config that declared a service of that name from loading. Nothing is ambiguous once the config's own wins: a name resolves to the config's global before the builtin services (as it already did for other globals), and the runtime's `Composite` host now routes a declared custom service before the builtin member of the same name, so reads, writes and actions reach the config's. The builtin's fields are hidden with it (`battery.percent` is an unknown field there). A component or surface named like a builtin element stays an error, since elements resolve before components and the component could never be placed. Under spec.md 14 this only accepts programs that were rejected; spec.md 4.2 says so. The services branch's `checker.rs::session_is_a_power_menu` still expects the old error in its second assertion; the integrator flips it at merge (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::a_config_service_shadows_a_builtin_one, crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_config_service_named_like_a_builtin_is_the_one_read, crates/strand/src/services/mod.rs::tests::custom_services::a_config_service_shadows_the_builtin_of_its_name). *Completed after review:* shadowing is the config's alone, so the runtime's own reads by name never reach a config service: the default palette's `system.dark`, `accent` and `contrast`, the other mode's `system.dark`, `system.reduced_motion`, and the `screens.all` and `screens.focused` that mount bars go through `ServiceHost::read_builtin`, `sources_builtin`, `acquire_builtin` and `release_builtin` (architecture.md), so `service system from poll …` keeps the palette and `service screens from …` keeps the bars. `on battery.changed` resolves the event against the config's service first, as a read does (an event it does not declare is `check::unknown_event`), and `strand call battery.boost 3` resolves against the running config's services before the builtins, so it runs the config's action. The composite host remembers which host took each hold, so a reload that adds (or removes) a shadow releases the hold where it was taken; the fallback host (`SchemaHost`) moves a shadowed builtin's cells aside while the config's service is declared and restores them when that service stops (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::a_config_services_events_shadow_the_builtins, crates/strand-compiler/tests/reload.rs::a_shadowing_service_leaves_the_runtimes_reads_and_stops_on_reload, crates/strand/src/services/mod.rs::tests::custom_services::the_runtimes_own_reads_go_to_the_builtin_services, ::a_reload_adding_a_shadow_lets_go_of_the_builtin, crates/strand/src/ipc/call.rs::tests::a_config_service_is_the_one_called).

The reading that removes a concept: a component whose tree is one element *is* that element where it is called, so handlers and `id:` in a call's block mean what they mean in an element's block, about the root. Handlers run in the caller's scope (they write the caller's state, which is what the tray's row components needed: `Row r { on click { menu = r.submenu } }`) and are checked against the root element's events; a call whose root is another component's call reaches the element at the bottom. Where the tree is not one element (an `if`, `for`, `match` or `slot` at its top, or two elements) there is nothing to be about, and either stays a load error that names the fix. Alternatives not taken: forwarding handlers to a component-declared target (adds a declaration form), and making every call a wrapper node (adds a scene node to every call and changes layout). The runtime shares the call's element state with the root (`Env::adopt_node`), so `c.hover` is the root's hover, and attaches the handlers to the root's scene node after it mounts. Under spec.md 14 this only accepts what was rejected; a component with an `id` parameter keeps taking `id:` as its argument. spec.md 5.2 says so (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::handlers_on_a_call_are_its_root_elements, crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_calls_handlers_and_id_are_its_root_elements).

A component takes it when it reads `screen` or calls a component that does (closed over the call graph after checking), and each call passes the `screen` in scope there (the bar's, a `Screen` local, or the calling component's own). A call where there is none (a `panel`, a top-level `popup`) is the load error `check::no_screen` at the call, naming both fixes. Only components that read it pay for it. The owner ruled, for components, types, enums and `fn`s: (1) a file that declares a name and uses it gets its own declaration; (2) a file without its own gets the single declaration elsewhere, exactly as before; (3) where two or more other files declare it, a bare use is a load error at the use (`check::ambiguous_name`) that names every declaring file, labels each declaration and offers `file.Name` as a fix per file (a file whose name is not an identifier is told to rename, as exports already require). `file.Name` reuses the form exports use and parses and checks wherever a bare name stands: a component call (`tray.Row e { … }`, the `.` touching both names; a touching `(`, `[`, `.`, `?.` or assignment after it keeps the old "statement in a tree" error), a type (`x: tray.Item?`), a constructor (`tray.Item(a: 1)`), an enum and its variants in values and patterns (`tray.Kind.dark`), and a `fn` call (`tray.fmt(x)`); it is read as the file's declaration only where `tray` names a file of the config, nothing in scope is called `tray`, and the file declares no `state` or `let` of that name, so `file.name` exports read as before. Surfaces, services, actions, token sets and keyframes stay unique across the config (they are identified by name at runtime or by the CLI), any kind stays unique within one file, and a component, type, enum or `fn` named like one of those is still `check::redeclared`. The owner's condition was clear feedback, so `strand check` and the language server put a note (`check::same_name`, the new `Severity::Note`: not an error or a warning, the LSP's Information) at each declaration of a shared name, listing the other files and explaining rules 1 to 3; a load never reports it, so the reload overlay stays quiet. `strand check`'s summary counts notes apart (", 2 notes"). Hover and go-to-definition follow the checker's resolution (rule 1 before rule 2, a qualified name to its file), and hover on a shared name says which file it came from and which others declare it. Downstream, a shared name is shown and kept as `file.Name`: shared types and enums in the type table (messages, and reload carrying a value over by type name), a shared component's lowered name (reload identity, state paths such as `a.Row.open`, the inspector), and a shared component's `tokens { }` under `$file.Name.…` so two components' tokens never collide (a unique component's stay at `$Name.…`). An ambiguous use checks on with the first declaration as a stand-in, so one mistake is one error. Alternatives not taken: per-file namespaces with imports (adds a concept; spec.md has no import and the guide says so) and making the last-loaded declaration win (silent and order-dependent). Under spec.md 14 this only accepts programs that were load errors before (`check::redeclared` across files for these four kinds), and every program that loads today resolves exactly as before: with every name unique, rules 1 and 2 give the one declaration, rule 3 never applies, and the qualified forms are new syntax that was an error (an unknown element or name). **2026-10-14 · m6-w2-language: the same name in two files, corrected after review.** The coordinator's review of the first cut found one blocker, five majors and eight minors; each is fixed here, and four statements of the paragraph above no longer hold. *(1, blocker) An ambiguous use is one error and no stand-in.* "An ambiguous use checks on with the first declaration as a stand-in" was wrong twice: inside an overloaded builtin's arguments (`radial(f(), $fg)`, `material(f())`) each overload attempt checked the argument again and restored the reported-error set but not the separate ambiguity set, so the error vanished and the program loaded with `a.strand`'s `f`; and with a stand-in, a constructor whose fields differ between the two files gave a cascade of field errors against the first. The ambiguity is now deduplicated through the reported set the overload attempts restore, and an ambiguous use is an error expression (`Ty::Error` in a type, an error pattern in a pattern), so one mistake is exactly one error. *(2) A name becoming shared costs the unedited file nothing.* With the display name `a.Row` doubling as the key, adding `b.strand` with its own `Row` and `Item` re-keyed `a`'s cells, its value types and its persisted paths, and a reload reset them. Keys are now stable whatever is shared: a component's cells and reload identity by `lower::Program::owner_key` (`module.Name`, always), a cell's type by `TypeTable::stable` (a config type is always written `file.Name` there), and reload's value translation by home file and name (`RecordDef::same_record`, `EnumDef::same_enum`); the type table no longer renames a shared type, it marks it (`ty::Home { file, shared }`) and only display adds the file. Persisted paths keep their readable form (`Row.open` while unique, `a.Row.open` while shared), so they move: a live reload hands the value to the new path and removes the old one after the old instance has gone (its last write with it), and a cold boot migrates from the other form (`instantiate::mount::moved_path`, `migrate_persisted`): while shared it reads the bare path only when no other same-named component has a `state` of that name (it could be theirs), while unique the qualified path wins as the newer. A migrated value that differs from its old default is stamped with today's default, so a "kept over new default" notice that would have shown on that boot is not shown. A component or type whose name is unique before and after keeps its state when it moves to another file, as it always has (the reload fuzzer's "component moved" step): reload identity takes a moved component's body by its name when exactly one file declares it on each side, its cells are found under the old file's key (`Ctx::moved_from`), a cell's type is unchanged when either its stable or its shown form is (`reload::CellTy`), and values translate between two unshared types of one name whatever their files. A shared one moved is a new declaration (its key names the file), so its state starts from its defaults; keying by name alone would merge two files' `Row`s. *(3) The rules count only what a position takes.* "A use resolves by three rules" counted every declaration of the name, so two `component Workspace`s hid the builtin `Workspace` type and a `type Item` beside a `component Item` made `x: Item` ambiguous. Each use now asks for a kind (`check::names::Want`): a type position takes types and enums, an element components, a call `fn`s and types, a variant enums, a plain value anything. Rules 1 to 3 run over the accepted declarations only; with none, the name falls through to the builtins as before. A name declared once still resolves to its one declaration whatever the position, so no program that loaded reads differently. *(4) Component tokens follow rules 1 and 2.* The first cut required `$a.Row.gap` everywhere a `Row` was shared, which made `$Row.gap` inside `a`'s own `Row` an error and broke a theme's `override Row.gap` as soon as a second `Row` appeared, even one without tokens. Now a read of `$Row.…` and a set's `override Row.…` resolve over the same-named components that have `tokens { }`: the file's own (which covers inside the component), else the only one; where two or more other files' have tokens, the read is `check::ambiguous_name` naming them, with `$a.Row.gap` fixes when the key spells the whole path. A template reads tokens by full path at run time, so it writes `$a.Row.gap`; spec.md 4.2 says so. *(5) One stem in two directories.* `bar/row.strand` and `menu/row.strand` both declaring a shared name made every `row.Name` fix unusable; it is now the load error `check::file_name` at the later declaration asking to rename one, as two exporting files of one stem already were, and no fix, note or hover offers `row.Name` (`check::names::nameable`). *(6) Completion follows the rules.* A component call's props, parameters and slot are the component the checker resolved at the call (`program.refs` at the kind's span, as navigation does), else by the rules with the call's qualifier (`ctx::Call`); the element list offers each component as the file would write it, bare where the file's own or the only one, `file.Name` otherwise, never a bare name that would be ambiguous. *Minors.* (7) is (1). (8) A file whose name is no identifier is never offered as `my-row.Row`, in the error, the note or hover; they say to rename the file. (9) The inspector names a shared component's scope `b.Row` (`owner_name`), and the token write-back takes `component b.Row` as the `Row` in the file of stem `b`, the path `b.Row.gap` as `gap` in it. (10) A builtin type's or schema enum's name is never a file qualifier, so an `Edge.strand` does not change `Edge.top`. (11) A qualifier that is a name in scope, a service or a value keeps the parser's "statement in a tree" error (`n.expire 3`) rather than "no file `n`". (12) The tree-sitter grammar's `tray.Row` is lexed by its scanner by the compiler's rule (`.` touching both names, no touching `(`, `[`, `.`, `?.` or assignment after), so both parsers agree on each case. (13) The guide's paragraph quotes the full help, says how tokens read, that adding the second declaration can make another file's bare use an error while a running shell's reload holds the new file back, and that the editor shows the note; a test keeps the quote true. In an element and a type, `q.Name` is file `q`'s declaration whenever that file declares a component, type, enum or `fn` `Name` and no local or file-level name `q` is in scope (`Checker::file_for_name`): a service, value or builtin type cannot be placed or used as a type, so nothing is ambiguous. Where the form still cannot be written, nothing offers it: the ambiguity error asks per use (`Checker::qualified_reaches`, by the position), and the note and hover read `hir::Program::unqualifiable` (`can_qualify`), the stems whose `stem.name` an expression reads as something else, filled by the checker; their help says "`battery.percent` already means something else, so rename `battery.strand` to name it so".
