Now a call's cells are taken from the one old file that declared a component of that name and no longer does (`Ctx::moved_from`, and `take_parked_moved` for a bar parked across the reload), and reload identity gives the remaining declaration's body the cut one's identity, through the token diff between the cut file's old text and the new file's (`Identity::take_over_moved_bodies`), so a list item's `state` inside the component survives too. A kept cell whose persisted path changed form carries its live value to the new path and the old path is removed after the old instance goes; the path is never guessed from the program on a reload. The limit that remains is stated in spec.md 4.2: a call that comes to name another file's declaration while the one it named still exists (pasting into the calling file) starts from its defaults, as calling a different component does. *(3)* A settings field compares its type by `CellTy::same` across a reload: `SettingsSlot::types` remembers the string the handle holds and passes it again when the type is the same, so a unique enum moved to another file keeps its field with no "type changed" notice, and later reloads compare against what the handle holds. *(4)* `migrate_persisted` runs only on a fresh mount (no cell carried and no reload in progress): the live value is authoritative on a reload, and a reload makes no synchronous per-instance write. *(5)* When the newer copy (`prefer`) holds its default, an older copy at the target path is removed so it never comes back in its place. *(6)* is in (2). *(7)* The token write-back splits `component a.Row` at its last `.`. *(8)* spec.md 4.2 states what a reload keeps and its limits instead of the broader claim. Under spec.md 14 the corrections accept programs the first two cuts rejected (`tray.Row` in an element or a type beside the `tray` service) and keep every reading a program had on `main` (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::every_offered_fix_compiles_whatever_the_files_are_named; crates/strand-compiler/tests/reload.rs::a_component_pasted_then_cut_keeps_its_state, ::a_settings_field_of_a_moved_enum_keeps_its_value, ::a_name_becoming_shared_keeps_the_unedited_files_state, ::a_newer_default_value_replaces_an_older_copy_on_a_cold_boot, ::a_parked_bar_keeps_a_moved_components_state).

**2026-10-14 · m6-w2-language: the same name in two files, third review.** Two fixes. *Paste-then-cut only.* `Identity::take_over_moved_bodies` handed the remaining declaration the deleted one's body identity whenever a name went from two files to one, so undoing a paste (deleting the pasted copy), deleting one of two components both in use, or renaming one of them beside the other reset the survivor's own list items' `state`. The skeleton walk now counts each component's calls by file and name (`Identity::calls`), and a body is taken over only in the paste-then-cut shape: the survivor had no calls in the old program (a fresh copy) and the cut one had some. *`self` and node names.* A file named `self.strand` (or `hover.strand` and the other node names) made `self.width` a read of the file: `file_for_name` and the member-expression branch now skip `self` and the node names, which are read before any file-level name, so such a file changes nothing (spec.md 14). The member branch's export read (`theme.look`) had the same gap on `main` (`self.width` beside a `self.strand` read the file's exports); it is closed too (crates/strand-compiler/tests/reload.rs::undoing_a_paste_keeps_the_originals_state, ::deleting_one_of_two_components_in_use_keeps_the_others_state, ::a_rename_beside_a_same_named_component_keeps_its_state, ::a_component_pasted_then_cut_keeps_its_state; crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::a_file_named_self_is_not_a_qualifier).

## m6-w2-surface

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-surface: a squircle corner with no room to ease in rounds towards the circle (owner-testing.md bug 4).** wave3-pixels (p3) made each `corners: squircle` corner a quintic superellipse quadrant reaching 1.6 × the radius along both edges, capped at half the shorter side. Where the cap bites, the quintic curve was squeezed into the room a circle of that radius has, so `radius: 20` on a 40 px bar (and design.md's rice, `radius: full; corners: squircle`, which design.md calls "a squircle pill") drew nearly square ends: 3 px in along the corner's diagonal was filled where the pill's is background. The exponent now falls linearly with the reach the cap leaves, from 5 at the full 1.6 × radius to 2 (a circle) at a reach of only the radius, so a corner of half the side is the pill a round corner draws, and an uncapped corner is unchanged. This keeps p3's claim that the squircle stays within a pixel or so of the circular hit shape and shadow, which the capped corners broke by several pixels. No syntax changes; it is a drawing fix under spec.md 14, since what `squircle` means (smooth corners of that radius) is kept and a pill-ended box is what the radius asks for. The capped squircles of `paint_corners` (50 px wide, radius 20) and the rice pill's refs were blessed again (crates/strand-render/tests/paint.rs::a_squircle_bar_of_half_its_height_is_a_pill, ::corners_per_corner_full_and_squircle; crates/strand-compiler/tests/render.rs::rice_now_renders_at_fixed_times).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-surface: a text's line box stays CSS's `normal`; the room above the capitals is the font's (owner-testing.md bug 5).** The owner saw an island's first line about 18 px below its top edge at `pad: 12` and asked whether Strand's line box differs from Qt's. It does not, for that font. Strand's line box (parley's default, `MetricsRelative(1.0)`) is CSS's `line-height: normal`: the font's ascent, descent and line gap (OS/2 typo metrics when the font sets USE_TYPO_METRICS, hhea otherwise), with ascent and descent rounded and half the gap above the first baseline, floored, as Chrome does. Qt's text line is ascent plus descent, without the gap. The owner's JetBrains Mono Nerd Font has ascent 1020, descent 300 and gap 0 per 1000 units in every table, so the two put the baseline at the same place: at 18 px, 18 px below the line's top, with the capitals (cap height 730) starting about 5 px into the line. 12 px of padding then shows about 17 px above the capitals, as measured. The owner's Quickshell calendar puts its 13 px title in a row beside an 18 px Material Symbols icon, which fills its own line box nearly to the top (ascent 1056 of 960, glyphs to 960), and centres the text in that row, so its top edge reads as tighter. Nothing changes. Trimming the line box to the capitals is CSS's `text-box-trim`/`text-box-edge: cap alphabetic`. It would be a new prop and a concept every text's box would carry, so it is not added. Uneven padding (`pad: 10, 16, 14, 16`, as the test config does) is the idiom. The guide's padding examples could say so; that is left to the docs stream. A test pins the convention: Liberation Sans, whose gap of 67 shows the difference from Qt (crates/strand-render/tests/layout.rs::a_text_line_box_is_css_normal).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-surface: a layer surface's buffer stays inside the edges it is anchored to, and a popup grabs only for the press that opened it (owner-testing.md bug 1).** The owner saw hover islands open on the neighbouring monitor, or away from their item, on four Hyprland monitors. A headless sway with two outputs (1280 × 720 at scale 1 and 1920 × 1080 at 1.5 beside it) and a virtual pointer walking the owner's floating bar, its items, their islands and the other output places every island under its item, on its own output, at full size, and keeps it open across the gap, so sway is right as it was. The cause is Hyprland's: `CPopup::reposition` (src/desktop/view/Popup.cpp) constrains a popup to the monitor `MonitorQueryCore::closestTo` finds at the parent layer surface's origin, where sway takes the layer's own output. Strand grew a layer surface by its shadow's reach on every side and moved its margins out by as much, so a bar anchored to the top, left and right edges had its buffer's origin up to 37 px past its output's top-left corner. On a monitor with a neighbour to its left, that origin lies on the neighbour (or nearest it), and Hyprland slid the islands onto it. Render now caps the overhang on each side a surface is anchored to at its margin there (`specs.rs`, `within_edges`): a bar by its edge and the two beside it, a panel or OSD by its `anchor` (a panel's `attach` taking its place). The buffer's origin is then always on its own output, and the margin on an anchored side is never negative. The shadow lost on those sides would have been drawn off the output, or onto the neighbour, which no compositor shows. Whether this fixes the owner's Hyprland is pending the owner's run on his monitors: the container has no Hyprland with several outputs, so the cause is read from Hyprland's source and only the placement is tested. The owner's bar's buffer goes from 2570 × 62 to 2560 × 59 on HEADLESS-2 in the acceptance run, and the `headless2` refs of the acceptance and newcomer tests were blessed again: they differ by about 1 px at the bar's right end and in its right-side content, a rounding improvement. The suspected grab is the second half. A popup grabbed with the serial of the seat's last press within `GRAB_WINDOW` (500 ms), so an island a hover opened within half a second of a click grabbed and took the keyboard. A popup now grabs by its cause, not by when or where it opens. Logic stamps each scene diff with the press that caused it (`SceneDiff::press`, `run::PressCause`): the last press among the events and two-way writes it handled since its last step (`ToLogic::Event`'s and `ToLogic::Write`'s `input`), which a hover change or an input-less write handled after it does not take away, else, on the step after the services reported a change, the press of the last action a handler ran with one (`Composite::action_press`), up to `GRAB_WINDOW` after it, so a menu a service opens in answer to the click (a tray menu's `opened`) is still the click's however the pointer moved meanwhile. The host marks each popup a diff creates or opens with that press (`demo::popup_causes`, `State::set_popup_cause`), and its surface grabs only when that press is the seat's last and within `GRAB_WINDOW`. A popup a hover, timer or IPC opened is marked with none and never grabs, however soon after a click; a click's menu grabs however far the pointer moved before its surface was made. A popup inside a parent popup with no grab takes none either, as xdg-shell requires (a grabbing popup's parent is a toplevel, a layer surface or a grabbing popup). The first version's `GRAB_SLOP` (a press stopped counting once the pointer moved 8 px from it) is removed: deciding by distance failed a click-opened menu the pointer had moved away from before it showed. spec.md 5.1 now says when a popup takes the keyboard. Neither change touches syntax or a prop's meaning (spec.md 14): both are where Strand puts a surface and when it grabs (crates/strand-render/tests/layout.rs::a_layer_surface_buffer_stays_inside_its_anchored_edges; crates/strand-surface/tests/render.rs::shadowed_layer_surfaces_stay_inside_their_anchored_edges; crates/strand/tests/hover_popups.rs::hover_islands_open_under_their_items_on_mixed_scale_outputs; crates/strand-surface/tests/sway.rs::a_popup_grabs_only_for_the_press_that_opened_it; crates/strand/src/run/tests.rs::a_diff_carries_the_press_whose_handlers_made_it).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-surface: `trigger: hover` gives a popup's open state to the pointer, with `delay`, `grace` and `p.open`; the owner's ruling (owner-testing.md gap 4).** The owner's islands needed an `id:` on every popup, a state and a hand-written grace (`on change over after 200ms`), because the pointer moving from a bar item onto its island unhovered the item, and an `if hover { popup { … } }` closed its own popup on the way to it. This branch first held every popup's anchor hovered, then (reviewed) only a `hover: keep` popup's. The owner ruled (2026-10-13) for neither: `hover` keeps its meaning, and the popup itself says what opens it. `popup` gains `trigger: open | hover` (default `open`, today's behaviour), `delay: duration` and `grace: duration`, schema entries with no new syntax, and `Node` gains `open: bool`; under spec.md 14 this only adds. spec.md 6.3 states the rule. With `trigger: hover` Strand owns the open state: the input router opens the popup while the pointer is on its anchor (after `delay`), keeps it while the pointer is on the anchor or on anything opened from it, popups nested in it included, or while a press that went down there is held (a slider's drag), and closes it `grace` after (default `HOVER_GRACE`, 200 ms, Quickshell's and the owner's figure). It writes the popup's `open` as two-way writes go (`Intent::Write`, `ToLogic::Write`), and logic keeps it in the node's `open` signal (`NodeState::open`, which `Instance::write` sets for such a popup), so the body mounts and the `enter` and `exit` poses play as for any popup. One `trigger: hover` popup is open from a surface at a time: opening one closes the other at once, with no grace overlap, so the pointer going straight from item to item swaps the islands. It never grabs, and a popup opened from inside it does not either (review minor 7: no grab under a parent popup without one). `open:` beside `trigger: hover`, a `trigger` that is not a written variant or sits in a `when`, and `delay` or `grace` without `trigger: hover` are load errors naming the conflict (`check::hover_popup_open`, `check::popup_trigger`, `check::hover_popup_prop`). `delay` defaults to none: `hover` styles change at once, and a tooltip's 600 ms (`TOOLTIP_DELAY`) is for an incidental hint, while a hover island is what the element is for; a config that sweeps the pointer along a bar of islands can set `delay: 150ms`. `p.open` reads any popup's open state through its `id:`: true from the moment it opens until it closes, as its exit pose starts, mirroring `open:` on an `open:` popup and the router's writes on a `trigger: hover` one. It does not wait for the exit pose to finish. The open state is logic's own and changes at once, with no report back from render; an anchor styled `when p.open` then springs back while the popup plays its exit, the two moving together rather than one after the other. Popups without `trigger: hover` open and close exactly as on `main`, and tooltips are untouched. Their grab follows the cause rule of the bug 1 paragraph above, which differs from `main` in one way: a popup a hover, a timer or IPC opened within 500 ms of a press no longer grabs (on `main` any popup opened within `GRAB_WINDOW` of the seat's last press grabbed). `main`'s spec.md said nothing of grabs, the no-grab class and its accepted deviation (features.md) already existed for popups opened late, and no syntax or schema entry changes meaning, so spec.md 14 allows it; spec.md 5.1 now states the one rule. Pick mode opens nothing and ends the graces. Because the router now knows which popups are one surface's hover islands, it is the base for gap 5's travelling island. The idiom is `popup { trigger: hover; … }` in the item, and level 3 of the guide shows it after the volume slider's `if hover`, with `when popout.open`. The router times delays and graces (`Router::next_wake`, `Router::tick`) and wakes the loop through the renderer's timer (`Renderer::set_input_wake`, set again after each settle, which forgets removed popups). The host ticks the router before each `Renderer::update` and as a surface detaches, as architecture.md's Router hooks now say (crates/strand-render/tests/input.rs::a_hover_popup_opens_on_its_anchor_and_closes_after_the_grace, ::going_straight_from_a_to_b_swaps_the_popups_with_no_overlap, ::a_nested_hover_popup_keeps_the_one_it_opened_from, ::a_drag_that_leaves_the_popup_keeps_it_open, ::a_hover_popup_waits_for_its_delay, ::a_hover_popup_takes_its_own_grace, ::a_popup_without_trigger_hover_is_left_to_the_program, ::pick_mode_ends_the_hover_graces; crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::the_router_opens_a_hover_popup, ::an_anchor_reads_its_popups_open; crates/strand-compiler/src/check/surfaces.rs::tests::a_hover_popup_takes_no_open; crates/strand/src/demo/host.rs::tests::the_router_opens_hover_popups_through_logic, ::settling_a_removed_graced_node_drops_its_wake; crates/strand-surface/tests/sway.rs::a_popup_grabs_only_for_the_press_that_opened_it; crates/strand/tests/hover_popups.rs::hover_trigger_islands_need_no_wiring, ::going_straight_from_item_to_item_swaps_the_islands).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-surface: the owner's animations measured at scale 1.5; what feels slow is the pose and the spring, not the frame rate (owner-testing.md bug 2).** All figures are warm medians in the container, `--profile timing`, the CPU raster path on the laptop's CPU (crates/strand-render/tests/owner_motion.rs, three rounds).

- The owner's floating bar is 3840 × 125 physical pixels at 1.5. It paints whole in 4.6 ms, and in 11.6–13.9 ms when a second buffer is painted whole as its shadow is cached. That happens only at boot, on a resize or on a scale change: a new buffer is given a copy of the newest frame (`shm.rs`, `adopt_newest`), so an animation never starts from an unknown buffer.
- The workspace pill's move (`x ~ ease(out_back, 200ms)`) takes 12 frames (200 ms), at 0.16–0.18 ms a frame (worst 0.16–0.24 ms), with damage 1.6% of the buffer. After the paint cache went idle and freed its shadow, the first frame is 0.23–0.34 ms.
- An island (567 × 284 at 1.5) paints its first frame in 3 ms and each frame of its enter in 1.25 ms (worst 1.27 ms).

None of these is near a 16.7 ms refresh, so there was no raster cost to fix. Two causes of the owner's impression did turn up, neither a frame-rate problem. First, the test config writes `enter { opacity: 0; scale: 0.9 }` on the card inside each island's always-mounted `popup { open: … }`. The card mounts once at boot, and spec.md 6.6's `enter` plays on mount, so the islands pop open with no animation at all. Quickshell animates them. The pose goes on the `popup` itself, which as a surface plays it each time it opens (16 frames, at rest after 10, 167 ms). Alternatively the popup takes `trigger: hover` (above), which mounts the card with each open. Strand is right; this is a config trap the guide could name. Second, `$motion.spatial`, spring(700, 0.9), starts slowly from rest. It reaches half its way at 61 ms and 90% at 129 ms, and it overshoots only 0.2%. Quickshell's 200 ms OutBack (Qt's, or CSS's `cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1)`) reaches half at 26 ms and 90% at 60 ms and overshoots 9%. Over the first 100 ms the spring covers about half the distance per frame, which reads as less snappy whatever the frame rate. The owner can match Quickshell today with `set { $motion.spatial: spring(3000, 0.75) }` in the bar (the token takes a spring; `strand check` rejects a curve there), or with `~ ease(out_back, 200ms)` per prop, as the pill already does. Changing the default is proposed below. The GPU build's promotion of these surfaces and Hyprland's own pacing cannot be measured in the container; the owner's `strand report` (paint p50, p95 and p99 per surface) would show the first, and nothing here suggests the CPU path needs it (crates/strand-render/tests/owner_motion.rs::the_owners_bar_and_island_at_one_and_a_half).

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-surface, proposed for the owner's review, option (b) taken by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-14 (m6-owner): a snappier default `$motion.spatial` (owner-testing.md bug 2).** The default spring is a theme default that design.md fixes. Changing it moves every shell's motion and every motion reference, so it is the owner's call; nothing is changed. Options:

- (a) Keep spring(700, 0.9) and have the guide show `~ ease(out_back, 200ms)` and a stiffer `$motion.spatial` override.
- (b) spring(3000, 0.75): half way at 27 ms, 90% at 52 ms, 2.8% overshoot, settled within 0.2% at 142 ms. That is OutBack's pace with a small bounce, still a spring, so retargeting mid-motion keeps its velocity.
- (c) spring(1600, 1.0), which `$motion.effects` already uses: half at 42 ms, 90% at 98 ms, no overshoot.

Recommendation: (b). It removes the gap the owner felt without adding a concept, and a spring keeps the property curves lack: an interrupted hover keeps its momentum. The cost is re-blessing the motion references, and the 2.8% overshoot shows on size springs as well as moves.

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-surface, proposed for the owner's review, option (a) taken by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-14 (below): one island that travels between items (owner-testing.md gap 5).** Quickshell's popout is one surface whose island slides and resizes from item to item. A Strand `popup` anchors to the element it is written in, and xdg-shell repositions a popup at once, never by animation, so a sliding island has to be one surface that draws the island moving inside it. What is missing is a way to say where it should be: no expression can read where an element sits. This does not fall out cheaply. It needs a compiler schema entry, logic's layout facts and a render read, so it is designed here and not built. Options:

- (a) **An element's laid-out box, read by its id**: `vol.box` (x, y, width, height in its surface's logical pixels), as `self.width` already reads the enclosing node's size for container queries, and as `name.hover` reads another node's boolean. The island is then a single `popup` anchored to the bar (or a top panel on the bar's output) as wide as the bar, holding `box { x: (pop == "volume" ? vol.box.x : bri.box.x) - 140 ~ $motion.spatial; width: … }`. Logic already receives laid-out sizes as layout facts (`ToLogic::Size`, `Renderer::take_layout_facts`), and positions would ride the same channel and settle one frame later, as container queries do. This adds schema entries and no syntax, which spec.md 14 allows in 1.x.
- (b) **A popup anchor that is a value**: `popup { anchor: vol }`, repositioned as its anchor changes. It moves at once (xdg_popup.reposition), so it does not slide, and it makes element references values, a new concept.
- (c) **A built-in travelling popout element**: an element that takes its children's popups and morphs one surface between them. It is the most direct, but it is a new element with its own rules that copies Quickshell's widget.

Recommendation: (a). It is the smallest construct, a read of something every element already has. It also serves other uses (a tooltip-like hint placed by hand, a drag indicator), and the shared-element `morph` already tracks boxes across surfaces on one output (`Renderer` surface origins), so render has the data. If it is taken, the owner's islands become one popup. `trigger: hover` (above) is the base for it either way: the router knows which popups are one surface's hover islands.

**2026-10-13 · m6-w2-surface: a press keeps its cause through input-less messages and service answers; the router's open popups follow logic (review r2).** `SceneDiff::press` was the last message's: each event or write set it, to `None` when it had no input, and a hover change cleared it, so a click followed in the same drain by an input-less write lost its grab, and a tray menu whose `opened` answer came after the pointer left the icon opened without one, which `main` (any popup within `GRAB_WINDOW` of the seat's last press grabbed) did not do. The press now has two causes, kept apart from messages without one (`run::PressCause`). The last press among the messages handled since the last step stamps that step's diff, whatever came after it in the drain; the next step starts with none. A handler's action carries its press already (`ActionCtx::input`); the composite host remembers the last one with its time (`Composite::action_press`), and the step after the services report a change carries it while it is within `GRAB_WINDOW`. Correlating each answer with its action exactly would need every service to echo the action's context back; the window, and the host's check that the press is still the seat's last, bound a wrong attribution as `main` did, and only for the step that hands over service reports. A step per pressed message was the other way to keep causes apart: it would have kept a hover change in the click's drain from sharing the click's press, at the cost of a scene diff (and a frame) per press message and a restructured loop; a hover-opened popup sharing a click's drain grabbing is what `main` did for any popup within 500 ms of a press, so the drain rule was taken. The router's map of open `trigger: hover` popups now follows logic (`Router::observe`): its own writes coming back, late and in order, change nothing, and any other `open` logic sends is logic's own (a reload remounting the popup open or closed), which the router takes on; a popup a reload makes the program's (`trigger` gone) is dropped and never written again. A click away on such a popup's surface, which is how `popup_done` reaches the router, closes it in logic too, so the surface the compositor dismissed is not left open in logic, and it opens again only once the pointer has left its anchor (no reopen loop under a pointer that stays). Delays and graces are added with `checked_add`: one too long for the clock never comes due rather than panicking. Leaving pick mode hit-tests the pointer again, so the hover and the popup under it come back at once instead of the grace closing it. The `pressed` chains were dropped from the router's "where the pointer is": a held press keeps its chain hovered, so they added nothing (crates/strand/src/run/tests.rs::a_press_keeps_its_cause_through_input_less_messages, ::a_hover_between_a_click_and_its_menu_keeps_the_press; crates/strand/src/services/mod.rs::tests::a_pressed_action_is_remembered_for_its_answer; crates/strand/tests/tray_menu.rs::tray_menus_nest_walk_and_choose; crates/strand-render/tests/input.rs::the_routers_open_popups_follow_logics_diffs, ::popup_done_closes_a_hover_popup_until_the_pointer_comes_back, ::a_huge_delay_or_grace_never_comes_due, ::pick_mode_ending_rebuilds_the_hover_under_the_pointer, ::a_drag_that_leaves_the_popup_keeps_it_open; crates/strand/tests/hover_popups.rs::going_straight_from_item_to_item_swaps_the_islands).

**2026-10-14 · m6-w2-surface: an element's laid-out box, `id.box`, and conditional ids, the owner's ruling on gap 5 (spec.md 14: it only adds).** The owner dropped the `popup { group: … }` island built after the gap 5 proposal (never committed) and ruled for its option (a), the general primitive: `id.box` reads a node's laid-out box. The schema gains `record Rect { x, y, width, height }` and `Node.box: Rect`, and an `id:` inside a `when` block, which loaded before and did nothing (a silent no-op; this sentence said "a load error", corrected by the review entry below), now names the node while the condition holds where its name means nothing else. Both only add, as spec.md 14 allows in 1.x, and spec.md 6.3 and 6.7 say so. The decisions in it:

- **The origin is the top-left of the node's surface's box**, in logical pixels, as laid out, without paint offsets, transforms or poses. It is the frame render lays the node out in. It is the same at every output scale (each output's bar is its own instance; `strand-render/tests/boxes.rs::boxes_are_logical_on_mixed_scale_outputs`). It needs no compositor placement. Leaving out the node's own `x` is what lets `x:` follow a box at all. A popup's own box is where it sits in its parent surface's box, from where the surface manager placed both (`Renderer::set_surface_origin`). So `it.box.x - pop.box.x` is a bar item's left edge in the popup's frame, which is how an island in a popup lines up with a bar item. A bar, panel, OSD or lock is at 0, 0: where the compositor put it on the output is nothing a shell lays out against.
- **Loops: one frame late, and the checker allows only what cannot loop.** (Superseded by the box-dependency graph in the review entry below: these three kinds could still loop through two bindings.) The box is a layout fact, as `self.width` is: render reports the boxes of watched nodes after layout (`Prop::Watch` `box`, `Renderer::take_layout_facts` now gives a `LogicalRect`), logic sets them (`Instance::set_box`), and its diff applies at the next layout. A node's first box holds the frame, as a query's change does, so the first frame already shows its value. That alone would not stop a width that follows the row it widens from chasing itself a frame at a time. Allowing only paint props would forbid the owner's island its width, which resizes per item. So `check::box_layout_loop` (`check/boxes.rs`) allows a value that depends on a box, through `let`s, `state`s that handlers set from it or under it, `fn`s, component parameters (per call) and `for` bindings, to set three kinds of prop. The first is paint props on any element but a surface. The second is any prop of an element on another surface: one surface's layout never moves another's content, and a popup's own box counts as on both its surfaces, since its size and anchor place it. The third is the layout props of an element with a constant `place: absolute` that the box is neither of nor inside: taffy lays an absolute element out after its parent and gives no other box its size. Anything else is an error, and so is an `if`, `for` or `match` on a box of its own surface, since it mounts there. A box read through a node passed as a value is placed nowhere and may drive paint only. The other options were rejected. Applying it a frame late alone, with no check, settles some programs and oscillates others, and nothing tells the author which. Paint only rejects the ruling's own example.
- **The first box snaps, later boxes spring.** A binding that read a box not yet reported (all zeros) sends its next value without its transition (`BootRead`), so an island or indicator appears in place instead of sliding in from 0, 0. Every later change springs with the binding's `~`. A box only goes to logic when it changes, so a settled shell does no work for it (`boxes.rs::a_settled_box_wakes_nothing`).
- **Conditional ids, for the workspace indicator.** The owner's indicator is an absolute box in the workspace row following the current workspace. The current workspace is one copy of a `for`, and an `id:` in a `for` body names each copy: read outside the `for`, it named none. `for n in ids key n { box { when n == current { id: cur } } }` names the copy whose condition holds (the last to start holding when several do; while none does, a node never laid out, zeros). It is a signal in the component's scope that the copies' `when` effects set and that an unmounting copy clears. Each node it may name has its box reported, so a value following `cur.box` travels from one known box to the next. **The spec's `x: row.box.x` is written `x: cur.box.x - ws.box.x`.** The literal form cannot hold: `.box` is in the surface's frame, and an absolute box's `x` is from its parent. Making `.box` parent-relative would give each reader a different frame and make the island, which reads across surfaces, impossible. The one subtraction reads both numbers from layout, so no offset is computed by hand (`boxes.rs::the_workspace_indicator_follows_the_current_box`, where the row's padding, gaps and a leading spacer are never written in the indicator).
- **The island's popup is sized explicitly from its anchor's box** (`width: pill.box.width + 16`), not by a new size-to-anchor prop. It is a box on another surface, so the check allows it, and it adds no construct. The popup draws nothing itself, so it takes input only in the boxes of its top-level elements that drew (`Painter::input_region`, which the surface manager applies at each commit: `sync_painted_input`), and the pointer passes through the rest of its width. A popup whose root draws (a `bg`, a border, a shadow) keeps the manager's whole-box region. Popups written before this draw a card at top level, so their region is the card's box as before. Only a popup with no background whose top-level elements leave gaps between them now passes those gaps through.

**2026-10-14 · m6-w2-surface: the review of 66c2f03 — `.box` can never loop, conditional ids keep today's programs, and the island's popup alone lets its gaps through.** The review found holes in the entry above; the owner's intent is that `.box` can never loop, so the rule is narrowed to that:

- **A box-dependency graph replaces the three kinds** (`check/boxes.rs`). Two absolutes each sized from the other's box, and a bar item and a popup's content each sized from the other's, passed every kind alone and relaid out every frame. Now each binding that depends on a box is an edge from the boxes it reads to the boxes it can move, and every cycle through a `.box` read is refused (`check::box_layout_loop`), its message naming the path (`` `a.box` → `width` of `b` → `b.box` → `width` of `a` → `a.box` ``) and each other binding on it labelled. What a binding moves: paint props nothing (a box is laid out before paint offsets; on a surface its effects, corners and `open` too, so a surface's paint props may now follow a box, which the first cut's docs claimed and its code refused); the layout props of an element that is always `place: absolute` (no `when` or pose changes `place`; the first cut read only the static prop) its box and those inside it, on its own surface (a popup inside it moves, its content does not); any other layout prop, `if`, `for`, `match`, `pages`' `current` (it mounts by value), a `segmented`'s `options` (now in `Prop::affects_layout`), a `set { $token }` and a `when { id: }`'s condition every box on their surface, a popup's own box included (its size and anchor place it); a surface's own props also the popups opened from it; a component's or file's tokens every box. The categories stay as the graph's edges; a cycle of one edge is the first cut's refusal, so every program it refused is still refused. `n.width` and `n.height` of another node are the same frame-late fact as `n.box` and are followed too, but they loaded on `main` before `.box` existed, and spec.md 14 holds with no exception: a cycle with no `.box` read on it, only sizes, is a warning, `check::size_loop`, naming its path the same way (`` `b`'s size → `text` → `b`'s size ``), and the program loads with the meaning it had (`text b.width > 10 ? "wide" : "narrow"` beside `b`, which `instantiate.rs::only_measured_nodes_are_watched` writes, as on `main`). A cycle with a `.box` read anywhere on it stays an error, whatever sizes are on it too; the search tracks, per box reached, whether a `.box` edge was crossed, and reports a sizes-only path only when no boxed one closes. `.width` on a node passed as a value is not followed (it loaded too); `.box` on one still counts as any box. A first cut of this review entry refused size loops as errors; the coordinator ruled that out (2026-10-14, "only add"). An element's own size in its own props stays a container query (spec.md 6.3: hysteresis), so `when self.width < 300 { … }` still loads.
- **A conditional id's conditions taint `name.box` and every read of the name** (which node it names follows them), and a `when { id: }` whose condition reads a box of its own surface is refused like an `if`: the flip-flop, `when n == (cur.box.x > 10 ? 1 : 2) { id: cur }`, renamed the other copy each frame with no layout at all.
- **`when c { id: x }` keeps its old meaning wherever binding `x` would change a program that loads today (spec.md 14).** It loaded and did nothing before. The name now becomes a conditional id only where it means nothing else at that body: not a plain `id:` there, a name in scope (a parameter, a `state` or `let` of the body, an element's scope name), a declaration of the config, a builtin (service, value, function, node boolean), any enum variant or a file. Otherwise the `when`'s `id:` does nothing, as before, with a warning (`check::conditional_id_ignored`) that says what the name already is. The first cut made a plain `id: x` beside `when … { id: x }` an error, which broke such programs.
- **Only a `trigger: hover` popup lets its gaps through (spec.md 14).** The first cut gave every popup that draws nothing itself a region of its top-level elements' boxes, which changed what existing `open:` popups do with a click in a gap between two cards. The pass-through is part of the new hover popup only (`Renderer::input_region` reads `SurfaceSpec::hover_trigger`); every other popup takes clicks in its gaps exactly as on `main`. A `blur` or `backdrop` draws for this, on the root (the whole box) and on a top-level element (its box).
- **A popup's own box stays right when its parent moves.** The surface manager keeps each popup's configure position (`Role::Popup::at`) and places it again whenever its parent's origin changes (an exclusive zone, its output, its pose's margins) or the parent is first placed, telling the host; a parent with no origin leaves the popup with none. Render reports a popup's box when facts are next taken rather than at each origin (`placed_dirty`), so a parent and its popup moving together report one box and never a stale one between, and a popup whose parent is not placed reports none rather than one at 0, 0. A popup's first place holds its frame for logic's answer, as a first box does.
- **A shadowed island does not resize its popup as it travels.** The overhang an absolute element's shadow asks for followed its `x`, so each frame of the travel changed the popup's overhang, its buffer and its place. On a `trigger: hover` popup, an absolute element that `x` or `y` moves now asks for the reach at whichever edge of the popup it may touch (`layout/mod.rs`), constant while it moves inside. Other surfaces keep the reach at the element's place (a static badge on a panel keeps its buffer), since only the popup is placed by its overhang, and so does an `open:` popup, whose buffer stays as on `main` (spec.md 14; the third review, below).
- **Smaller ones.** A conditional id keeps its holders in order (`NodeState::hold`): it names the last to start holding, and the one before when that stops, never depending on effect order. The elements it may name are measured only for what is read through it (`Program::alias_watch`: `.box`, `.width`/`.height`, or passed as a value); a name read for its booleans measures nothing. The runtime and the checker use the schema's `Rect` and `Node` (`TypeTable::find_schema_record`), so a config's own `type Rect` or `type Node` cannot change what `.box` or `self` is.

**2026-10-14 · m6-w2-surface: the third review of the box graph (c9e6907).** One blocker and four minors, each fixed. (1) Inherited values reach into popups, but a binding's reach stopped at a popup's own box: a `set { $space.2: chip.box.width > 60 ? 4px : 48px }` on a bar's row, read by a row inside a popup that holds `chip`, relaid `chip` out every frame and loaded. Render inherits `set`, `font`, `weight` and a surface's own props into the surfaces nested in what they set and lays those out again, so the rule is now the simplest sound one: whatever moves a popup's own box moves every box on that popup, and so on through popups inside it (`check/boxes.rs::moves`, a closure over the surfaces each binding moves). It covers a popup's `width: $space.2 * 4` read through an ancestor's token, an `if` mounting a `set`, a surface's own `weight`, an element's `font` and popups inside popups; each is in the negative corpus. It refuses more than it must (a bar item's layout prop moves what an open popup holds, which only an inherited value would), but only programs that read a box in a popup from what lays out its parent, which `.box` made possible: nothing that loaded on `main`. (2) The dependences settle until nothing changes rather than for 64 rounds: the sets only grow and are finite, and a chain of 100 `let`s took one round each. (3) A service field a handler writes (`brightness.level = r.box.width / 1000`) carries what it was written from to every read of the field, as a `state` does. (4) A `bar`'s size, `edge`, `margin`, `open` and `screens` change its exclusive zone, which places and sizes every layer surface on its output, so they move the boxes of every `bar`, `panel` and `osd` (which output is not known statically: all of them), and so does whatever lays out a bar with no `width`, `height` or `size` (its content is its thickness). Panels and OSDs reserve no zone (`SurfaceSpec::exclusive_zone`), so their size moves only themselves. (5) The travelling-island shadow reservation applies only to `trigger: hover` popups (the bullet above), so no `open:` popup's buffer differs from `main`'s. spec.md 6.3 and the module doc of `check/boxes.rs` say all of this. Tests: `strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::inherited_values_reach_nested_popups` and the negative corpus's `box_layout_loop.strand` (25 refusals, with the review's program and its five variants), `::a_long_let_chain_is_followed_to_its_end`, `::a_service_field_written_from_a_box_is_followed`, `::a_bars_exclusive_zone_moves_the_other_layer_surfaces` (two bars through a state, a bar sized by its content; a bar's paint and a panel's size still load); `strand-render/tests/boxes.rs::an_open_popups_shadow_overhang_is_mains`. With the closure, `a_box_loop_through_several_bindings_is_refused` finds the bar-item-and-popup loop by its shorter path, and `a_conditional_ids_condition_is_followed` refuses each condition that picks the name too, since renaming on the bar reaches the popup it holds.

Neither stream tested these pairs, so `crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::file_stems_and_shared_names_meet_ids_and_boxes` and `crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::same_named_components_keep_their_own_conditional_ids` do; both passed with no code change. docs/owner-testing.md marks gap 5 fixed (`id.box`, the travelling island as one `trigger: hover` popup, with its tests) and its header names `15a0de7`; every test it cites exists (crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::file_stems_and_shared_names_meet_ids_and_boxes, crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::same_named_components_keep_their_own_conditional_ids).

## m6-owner-fixes

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a travelling island stays on its output on Hyprland (owner-testing.md bug 6).** On the owner's Hyprland 0.56.2 the travelling island of `target/try/qs/strand/shell.strand` ran off the right edge under the rightmost status items. Two causes, both found by reading Hyprland's source (v0.56.2, efb5099) and tracing headless sway. First, Strand changed the popup mid-travel: the island's springs (`spring(3000, 0.75)` underdamps) carry it a pixel or two past the popup's box as it reaches an edge, and layout took the shadow reach from where it was drawn, so the hover popup's overhang went from 37 to 38 or 39 px and back. That changes `PopupConfig`, and the manager repositions the popup (`xdg_popup.reposition`) on `xdg_wm_base` 3 and later, or makes it again below that (sway 1.9 offers version 2). Second, Hyprland gets that reposition wrong: `CXDGPopupResource::applyPositioning` (`src/protocols/XDGShell.cpp:93-96`) moves the monitor's constraint box by the popup's own window-geometry offset (`m_surface->m_pending.geometry.pos()`, the overhang) before sliding, so a repositioned popup with a 37 px overhang slides to 33 px past the right edge (37, less the 4 px padding of `getPosition`). At creation the window geometry is not set yet and the slide is right, which is why a fresh island first opened on screen. The island, clamped inside the popup by `island.box` as the config intends, followed the popup off the edge. Fixes, neither changing what a config means: (a) layout takes a moving island's shadow reach in a `trigger: hover` popup as if the island were inside the popup's box (`layout/mod.rs`), so an overshoot is clipped rather than resizing the popup, as the m6-w2-surface review meant ("the overhang does not follow where the island is drawn"); (b) the surface manager moves a popup's box inside its parent's output along its anchor's edge itself, through the positioner's offset (`placement::popup_shift`, from the parent's place and the output's logical place), and still asks for slide and flip for what it cannot know (another client's exclusive zone, a posed parent). A configure elsewhere than asked counts in `Stats::popups_moved`. Hyprland's offset still moves a repositioned popup at an output's *left* edge right by its overhang plus 4 px; that keeps it on screen and `.box` reports where it is, so nothing more is done. The proposal of 2026-10-14 to take a popup's anchor from the surface it opens on and key placed boxes per surface is not built: each monitor's `bar` is an instance of its own (spec.md 5.1), so a popup's parent node has one surface and the per-node keys are right; the case left is a popup in a `screens: all` panel, whose instances share a node, and its `.box` reads the panel last placed (crates/strand-render/tests/boxes.rs::an_island_overshooting_the_popups_edge_keeps_it_still, crates/strand-surface/tests/sway.rs::a_popup_at_an_outputs_edge_is_placed_inside_it, crates/strand-surface/src/placement.rs::tests::a_popup_is_shifted_inside_its_output, crates/strand/tests/hover_popups.rs::the_travelling_island_stays_on_its_output_at_the_right_edge).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a closing surface's last commit keeps its exit's pose (owner-testing.md bug 7).** The owner's precise report: going from the Slack tray icon to the clock, once the Slack menu has gone and the calendar island is up, the menu "flickers in and out once briefly". Cause, Strand's: with the alpha modifier (Hyprland) a closing popup's exit is a delegated pose, and the surface manager sets the pose the renderer reports right after each paint with that frame's commit (`manager/commit.rs`, `Painter::surface_pose`). The renderer reported the pose of its cached flatten, and the frame that ends a closing pose also drops the content kept for it (`process_finished`, `drop_closing_content`), which clears that cache for the next frame; so the last frame reported no pose, and the manager sent the rest pose (multiplier 1, and the viewport's full size where the scale is delegated) with the last commit before the popup was destroyed. Hyprland applies a multiplier on commit (`src/protocols/AlphaModifier.cpp`) and, unmapping the popup, snapshots it at that alpha and fades the snapshot out with `fadePopupsOut` (`src/desktop/view/Popup.cpp:270-278`, `src/render/Renderer.cpp:3171`; the owner's `fade`, about 300 ms): the whole menu came back and faded. Fix, which changes no meaning: `Renderer::delegated_pose` reports the pose of the last painted frame, kept apart from the cache (`SurfaceState::posed`), so the pose that rides a frame's commit is that frame's, whatever its end invalidates for the next one. It touched every delegated closing pose whose content unmounts on close (popups, and panels), on any compositor with the alpha modifier; sway 1.9 has none, so the exit is painted there and it never showed. On headless sway the other suspects were ruled out: the menu is not opened again (made once, gone once), draws nothing after its exit, and content that changes as it closes (as the tray's does when `item.menu.close()` makes the app send its menu again) is not drawn: the exit plays over what it last showed. The first reading of bug 7 (the islands' cross-fade under Hyprland's popup fades) was wrong, and its proposal to skip `exit` and `enter` on a hover hand-off is withdrawn (crates/strand-render/tests/surface_poses.rs::a_closing_popups_last_frame_keeps_its_exit_pose, crates/strand/tests/hover_popups.rs::a_tray_menu_left_for_the_island_goes_once, ::a_hover_hand_off_draws_nothing_new_on_the_old_island).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes (bug 8): an `image`'s, `svg`'s or `lottie`'s relative file is under the config directory, made absolute by instantiate; a literal one that is not there is a `check::missing_file` warning.** The owner's `svg "dot.svg"` and `image "dot.svg"` beside `bar.strand` drew nothing while the same file by absolute path drew, and `strand check` was clean: render's `image::resolve` and `image::read_local` took a relative source as `PathBuf::from(src)`, the process's directory, where every other path in the language (settings files, service files, shaders, templates, `material(image:)`) is under the config directory, and design.md and guide level 5 write `svg "gauge.svg"`. Two places could resolve it: render, handed the config directory, or the compiler, which knows it (`Storage::config_dir`) and already resolves every other config path. The compiler does: instantiate rewrites the value of an `image`'s, `svg`'s or `lottie`'s `source` prop, literal or computed, through `check::assets::local_source`, so the scene carries an absolute path and render keeps one meaning for a path (what it is handed), with no new renderer interface, its decode cache keyed by the real file, and a lottie's own assets found beside it as before. `~/`, absolute paths, `file://` and other URLs, and icon names are left as written. Which `image` sources are files is the one rule render already drew by, moved from `image::is_icon` to `strand_scene::source_is_file` (both crates depend on strand-scene; strand-icons stays dependency-free and the compiler gains no edge to it), so the compiler's rewrite and check never take an icon name for a path. A module in a subdirectory resolves against the config directory too, as a shader does, not its own file's directory. The check (`check::assets::check`) stats each literal source, an `image`'s only when `source_is_file`, and warns with the full path it looked at; it touches the disk, so `strand check` and the LSP run it beside `check::files::templates`, and `strand run`'s loader does not. Local files are not watched: editing `dot.svg` while the shell runs is not drawn until render reads the file again (a restart; an `image` also at a new drawn size), as before; design.md names shaders, settings and wallpapers as live, not images, so no new watch is added for them (crates/strand-compiler/tests/render.rs::relative_media_paths_are_under_the_config_directory, crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::a_missing_literal_file_is_a_warning, strand-compiler `check::assets::tests::relative_local_sources_go_under_the_config_dir`).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes (the owner's ruling (2026-10-14)): a config `icons/` folder is looked in before the icon theme for every icon name.** Custom SVGs beside the shell work as drop-in icons, and the same name falls back to the system theme on a machine without them. Where the folder sits in the chain: `strand_icons::candidates` gives pairs, the name and its other `-symbolic` variant, from the name asked for to its most generic fallback (`network-wireless-signal-good`, `network-wireless-signal`, …); for each pair `resolve` tries the folder (the name, then the variant) and then the theme (`lookup` of the name, then the variant, each through the theme's parents, `hicolor` and the base directories), and only then the next pair. So "my file wins" for the plain name and its `-symbolic` variant (`icon "wifi"` draws `icons/wifi.svg`, else `icons/wifi-symbolic.svg`, before the theme's `wifi`), while a theme icon of a more specific name still wins over a generic file in the folder (`network.svg` there does not hide the theme's `network-wireless`); putting the folder's every candidate before the theme's first would let one generic file shadow a whole family. Files: `<name>.svg`, else `<name>.png`, in the folder itself (no subfolders, no sizes; an SVG is drawn at the box's size and a PNG scaled); the folder is listed once per `strand_icons::generation`. Tinting: a folder file is recoloured by `color` (the scope's `$fg` unless set) only when its own name ends in `-symbolic`, the freedesktop convention; a theme icon keeps the old rule (a `-symbolic` name asked for, or a `-symbolic` file found). Scope: `resolve` is the one chain the renderer (`icon`, an `image` of a name) and the `apps` service (`exists`) use, so a window's, app's or tray item's icon by name is overridden too. Crate placement: strand-icons stays without dependencies and does not find the config: `set_config_icons(Option<PathBuf>)` is set by `strand run` before any thread looks an icon up. Reloading: `strand run` adds the folder to the watcher's cache sources (`live::config_icons_source`, a depth-0 tree of `CacheKind::Icons`; it need not exist yet), so adding, editing or removing a file there is an icon theme change (`strand_icons::invalidate`, `Renderer::icons_changed`, the apps service told) and no config reload. Building it found that `icons_changed` drew no damage when an icon's new decode replaced an old one of the same size: the frame records hash a decode by its pixmap's address, which the new pixmap may reuse once the old is dropped, so an icon theme switched to one with the same names never repainted at a buffer age of 1; the surfaces drawing icons are now painted whole (`valid = false`). `strand check` never looks an icon name up, so a name only the folder has is not warned about (bug 8's `check::missing_file` looks only at paths) (crates/strand-render/tests/config_icons.rs, strand-icons `tests::the_config_folder_comes_first_for_each_name_and_its_variant`, strand `live::tests::the_config_icons_folder_is_an_icon_cache`, crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::icon_names_of_the_config_icons_folder_are_not_warned).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes (the owner's approval of 2026-10-14): a local file an `image`, `svg` or `lottie` draws is watched, and saving it redraws it with no reload.** This replaces the last sentences of bug 8's paragraph above ("Local files are not watched"). Saving `dot.svg` beside `bar.strand` now draws the new file within a frame or two, as an edit in the `icons/` folder does, with no config reload and no state change. Which files are watched: only those the config draws now, as render reads them. The alternative of collecting literal sources from the program at each compile would miss a computed source (`svg (on ? "a.svg" : "b.svg")`), so instantiate records each bound `source`'s current value as a path (`Instance::asset_files`). That covers a literal or computed source, and a relative path under the config directory. It is kept per binding: a source changing, or its node unmounting (a closed popup's content), changes the set, and the logic thread sends the set with the settings and theme files it already sends (`Job::Referenced`, as `Role::Asset`). How a save is seen: the watcher already watches each referenced file through its parent directory with content hashes, so an editor's temporary-file-and-rename save is one change. A new `Role::Asset` keeps it apart from `Role::Other`, whose files the theme reads. The worker hands asset changes to a sink of their own (`Job::Assets`), as it does cache kinds, so they go to the renderer on the main thread and never to logic or the loader. What is redrawn (`Renderer::assets_changed`): an `image` decode of the path that a live frame draws is kept and drawn until its new decode replaces it, so there is no blank frame while the worker reads it (the icons' path removes decodes and shows one); other decodes of the path go; decodes and file reads in flight are dropped when they arrive and asked for again; an animated image's timeline and its worker's decoders go; an `svg` or `lottie` whose source is the path reads its file again and draws the old one meanwhile, a generation in its raster state making the new one draw though no prop changed; and the surfaces showing any of them paint whole, as `icons_changed`'s do. A file first registered is reported as it registers when it was written since the program took the set that names it (two seconds' slack for coarse file times; `Job::Referenced::at`), as render may have read it before the save landed, a screenshot a command is still writing when a click shows it (review of the integration: such a save was taken as the watch's baseline and the old image stayed until the next save; strand `live::tests::a_drawn_file_written_before_its_watch_is_reported`, which failed before); one written earlier is not read again, so a popup opening does not read its files twice; and logic sends the set right after the step that changed it, not when something next wakes its loop. Limits: images a Lottie file names beside it are read again only with the Lottie file; an `icon` is never a path, its files being the `icons/` folder's or the theme's (crates/strand-render/tests/local_assets.rs, crates/strand-compiler/tests/render.rs::the_drawn_local_files_follow_the_mounted_sources, strand `live::tests::a_saved_drawn_file_reaches_the_asset_sink_without_a_reload`, crates/strand/tests/demo.rs::strand_run_redraws_an_edited_svg_without_a_reload, which fails without the redraw). The paths are absolute whatever the config directory is given as (review of the integration): `strand run target/try/island`, the owner's way of running the island bar, keeps the directory as typed, so a relative source was made relative to it, and `file_of` records nothing for a relative path, so no file was watched; `local_source` and `file_of` now make every path absolute against the process's directory with its `.` components dropped (`check::assets::absolute`, the watcher's `paths::absolute`), and the source render draws is that path (crates/strand-compiler/tests/render.rs::a_relative_config_directory_still_records_absolute_files, which failed before with no file recorded; `check::assets::tests::a_relative_config_dir_gives_the_path_the_watcher_reports`). A `.` inside a source was already the watcher's path: `Path` equality drops it (crates/strand-render/tests/local_assets.rs::a_source_with_a_dot_component_follows_its_file).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a `~` is evaluated with its value (owner-testing.md bug 10, B-b).** The owner's notch faded its dashboard out in 160 ms although its `~` said `grown ? ease(ease_out, 160ms) : ease(ease_in, 1000ms)`. Cause: `Ctx::sources` evaluated each prop's `~` expression once, untracked, when the node mounted, and every later change was sent with that transition; the box mounts when `grown` turns true, so both directions took 160 ms. spec.md 6.6 said only that a `when`'s `~` applies while it wins, which already means the transition after the change for the `when` form; read the same way for an expression, a change takes the transition in effect after it. The memo of each bound prop now evaluates the winning source's `~` with its value (`PropOut::transition`), so a transition that depends on state follows it and the change that switches it gets the new one; a change of the transition alone sends nothing (the emitter skips an unchanged value), so it never restarts a motion. Width and height went through the same path, so they were wrong the same way and only looked right where the mount state's transition was the wanted one. spec.md 6.6 states the rule (crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_conditional_transition_applies_to_the_change_that_switches_it).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: cut text stays cut while its box springs (owner-testing.md bug 13).** In the owner's notch every `ellipsis: end` text whose box the morph squeezed (the crown's window title) flickered between cut and whole. Per frame, on the text worker: a text narrower than its unbounded layout asks for a layout shaped for `round(width)` (`place_text`'s `fit`); a springing width asks for a new one every frame, and the worker delivers it after the frame that asked, so that frame drew a stand-in, which was the unbounded layout, unclipped: the whole title spilling past its box. Frames whose rounded width matched the last (the spring's slow tail, an overshoot's turn) drew the delivered cut layout, so the two alternated. The threshold itself, overshoot and fractional scales were not causes: the cut follows the box's whole logical width, and crossing the fit threshold changes the text once per crossing, as it must. Of the candidate fixes, hysteresis or snapping would only make the flips rarer, and shaping on the render thread would put a font shaper's cost into every animated frame; the stand-in was the fault. Now, while the layout for its width is being shaped, a cut text draws the layout shaped for the widest width no more than its box (the last frame's while it grows), else the narrowest wider one, else the unbounded one, the last two clipped to the box (as an `input`'s overflowing text is); slots already kept as stand-ins (`prune_texts`) hold them. A text whose box keeps its width is unchanged: it draws its own layout, and the one frame a newly narrowed box waits for its layout now shows the unbounded text clipped to the box instead of spilling past it (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::cut_text_stays_cut_while_its_box_springs, crates/strand-render/src/flatten/tests.rs::text_is_aligned_in_its_box).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: new text is laid out by its shaped size (owner-testing.md bug 14).** The music bars at the start of the owner's crown status row slid left and back as the card grew. Cause: text the worker had not shaped was measured by an estimate (`measure_text`: 0.55 em a character) for the frames until its layout arrived, and the readings the grown crown mounts are Material Symbols ligatures (`battery_5_bar`: one glyph of about 16 px, estimated at about 110), so the row was laid out once by the estimates and again a frame later by the shaped sizes; a FLIP glide started on the first of those passes aimed at the estimate. An idle surface already held its frame for such text (`NEW_TEXT_WAIT`), but a surface in motion never does (`BUSY_WINDOW`), and a morph is motion. Of the three remedies (shape before the first layout, do not glide estimate corrections, keep unmeasured text out of layout), the first is the root: a correction from an estimate is no layout change at all once no frame is laid out by one, and keeping text out of layout would still move its siblings a frame late. Laying out now waits up to `ESTIMATE_WAIT` (5 ms) for the worker to deliver the unbounded layout of any text that has none at any scale or width, then lays out again (`Renderer::await_unmeasured`, in `flatten_surface`'s loop, as the inline shaper already did). It waits on the text worker, never on logic, so the render thread still never waits on logic (design.md); shaping a label takes well under a millisecond, a frame that mounts text costs that and one more layout pass, and a worker slower than 5 ms (a family's first load) leaves that frame to the estimate as before. Changed text keeps its old layout meanwhile and widths a box asks for (ellipsis, wrapping) are not waited for: their stand-ins are measured (bug 13) (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::a_mounted_text_moves_its_siblings_once).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a layout with no clock leaves size springs alone (owner-testing.md bugs 9 and 11).** A surface just attached is laid out at once by `configure_surface`, before its first frame, as a preview with its own time, which is zero until it has painted. `Animator::start_sizes` snaps on zero time (as reduced motion does), and size springs belong to the node, not the surface, so that preview set every size under the popup to its target and dropped the spring: an `enter` pose's `width` and `height` on content mounted as its popup opens never played (B-c), and a popup made again mid-spring (sway 1.9 offers `xdg_wm_base` 2, so a popup whose size changes is made again rather than repositioned) jumped to the end of its card's size spring while `x`, a paint prop, went on springing (B-a). A preview with no clock now leaves size springs as they are, those in flight and those waiting to start, and reports the surface's layout as animated so the first frame painted starts them; under reduced motion it still snaps. (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::a_size_in_an_enter_pose_plays_as_its_popup_opens).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a surface's overhang holds still while its sizes spring (owner-testing.md bug 9).** The overhang a surface's buffer keeps for shadows (and fillets) is the reach of its boxes' shadows past its box, taken after each layout; a card whose size springs inside a popup with a shadow that reaches past the popup's box changed it on every frame, and with it the popup's size: Hyprland was sent a reposition each frame and sway 1.9 a new popup (with the snapped springs of the paragraph above). Following the spring buys nothing a viewer sees: the shadow is drawn either way, and a buffer's size is not motion. While a size springs under a surface root, its overhang is now the larger, side by side, of the reach when the spring started and the reach of the layout at rest it springs to, learnt when it starts or retargets, and is kept until every size spring there settles, when it takes the rest reach (one more resize after a shrink). What an overshoot carries past the larger reach is clipped by the buffer, as before the overhang was grown. (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::a_shadowed_card_springs_its_size_without_resizing_its_popup, with the popup repositioned and made again).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a popup's gap is its margin, 0 included (owner-testing.md gap 24).** spec.md did not say how a popup's `margin` places it; placement's doc comment said the margin on the side facing the anchor is the gap, default 6, and the code took a margin of 0 there as unset, so a popup could not touch its anchor while a negative margin (overlapping it, which the owner's notch uses to cover its bar) worked unremarked. A margin is a length, and 0 is a length: reading it as "unset" adds a hidden rule where the plain one removes it. spec.md 5.1 now says the gap is 6 px only while `margin` is unset, `0` touches and a negative margin overlaps the anchor; the other sides are unused and `attach:` makes the gap 0, as before. The fix needs `SurfaceSpec` (strand-scene) to tell an unset margin from 0 and `placement::popup_config` (strand-surface) to read it, so it is left to strand-surface's owner, who built it the same day (the next paragraph).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes (owner-testing.md gap 24): a popup's `margin: 0` on its anchor's side touches the anchor.** spec.md 5.1 (written on `laptop/m6-owner-render`) says a popup's margin on the side facing its anchor is the gap, 6 px only while it is unset, `0` touching, negative overlapping. `placement::popup_config` took a resolved 0 for unset, because `SurfaceSpec::margin` is zero both ways. `SurfaceSpec` gains `margin_set: bool` (true when `margin` resolves to usable insets, `0` included), set by `SurfaceSpec::resolve` beside `margin`, and `popup_config` gives the default 6 only while it is false. Alternatives: `margin: Option<Insets>` types it better but changes every reader (render's overhang cap and content sizing, placement's layer config), where a set-ness flag changes no reader and only the one rule that needs it reads it; a per-side flag is moot, since `margin` expands like CSS and sets all four sides at once. A margin that cannot be used (non-finite, or five values) stays unset, as its value already fell back to zero. Layer surfaces do not read the flag: their unset margin is 0 already (crates/strand-surface/tests/sway.rs::a_popups_margin_on_its_anchors_side_is_its_gap, strand-scene `surface::tests::a_zero_margin_is_set_and_an_absent_one_is_not`).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a graph's history is its own, per mount.** A `graph` keeps one sample per column of its box, sampled at its own rate (`history` over its width) and eased by its own `smooth`, and it draws only the new column (design.md's "graphs and sparklines with built-in history"; "only the new column repaints"). A graph mounted again (a popup opened again: a popup mounts what it holds only while shown) starts empty. Keeping the history with the data source instead was considered and not taken: render sees a graph's values, not where they come from, so a history that outlives the node needs logic to keep a series per source, at a rate and length no single graph decides, read by graphs of other widths: a service-side history, which is a new concept (a series kept for a service field), not a property of `graph`. It is not cheap and not consistent with the graph's own sampling, so the history stays per mount; a service history is a later wave's, on the owner's ruling (owner-testing.md gap 25).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a stack aligns its children together (owner-testing.md gap 27).** The owner's popup holds three siblings meant to sit apart (two ears and a body); a popup, like a `stack`, a `box` and every surface, lays its children out over each other in one cell, and its `align` places them all on both axes; nothing aligns one child. spec.md 6.7 now says so, with the default (a child fills the cell on an axis where it has no size and sits at the start where it has) and the two existing ways to place one child apart: a `row` or `col` filling the cell that places it with `justify` and `align`, or `place: absolute` at `x` and `y`. A per-child `align_self` was not added: it would be a second alignment concept beside `align`, and both existing forms already express it (crates/strand-render/tests/layout.rs::a_stacks_align_places_every_child_on_both_axes).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: text in a list's rows is not waited for.** The estimate wait of owner-testing.md bug 14 cost the design launcher's 2,000-row scroll about half its frames on a loaded machine (crates/strand/tests/demo.rs::the_design_launcher_scrolls_2000_apps, which needs 20 frames while it scrolls: 9 to 13 in 7 of 8 runs at 2500382, against 21 to 34 on its base 9788239; bisected to the commit that added the wait, 17 to 22 against 24 to 29 for the commit before it at the same load). Rows mount on nearly every frame of a scroll, and each such frame waited for their text and then laid the surface out and flattened it again. Of the remedies, skipping a second pass when nothing was unmeasured was already the rule, and caching the stand-in lookup addresses nothing a scroll pays for; the cost is the wait itself on text that mounts as a list scrolls. A list's rows take their width from the list and sit apart from each other, so an estimate there moves at most what shares a row, inside a row scrolling in at the list's edge, as it did before the wait. Laying out no longer waits for text inside a `list` (`await_unmeasured`); it also scans the text slots once per call, only when some text has no layout of its own, and lays out again only when an awaited text arrived (other layouts delivered meanwhile are drawn from the next frame, as when they arrive between frames). `Renderer::estimate_waits` counts the texts waited for. After: 21 to 35 frames, 0 of 8 runs failing (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::rows_mounting_in_a_list_do_not_wait_for_their_text, which failed before with two of a list's rows waited for; a_mounted_text_moves_its_siblings_once unchanged).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: painting one surface does not run out another's hold.** A surface's first frame is held for its text (`wait_until`) and a content-sized surface's frame for the configure at the size its spec asks for (`size_hold`), each until a deadline on the wall clock. The loop paints its surfaces one after another and takes no configure while it paints, so under load the time spent painting others ran the hold out: crates/strand/tests/demo.rs::the_design_launcher_is_centred_and_closes_on_click_away failed in 4 of 31 runs on the laptop (a debug build beside nine other sway tests). Its toast panel was made at the size its estimated text gave it (429 × 197), its shaped text asked for 429 × 185 13 ms later, and the frame held 500 ms for that configure; the loop spent 500 ms painting the bar (190 ms) and the launcher (308 ms), and the toasts painted one frame at 197, 9 ms after the hold ran out and 116 ms before the configure arrived (traced with a temporary log). The runs that failed had the frame's single estimate wait of the next paragraph, which moves the timing; 18 runs without it passed, but its absence is no guarantee. Each paint now moves on every other surface's hold still running when it started by the time it took (`Renderer::pause_holds`): a hold waits for the worker and the compositor, and the loop's own painting is neither. The holds keep their lengths, and one already over is not revived (crates/strand-render/src/renderer/tests.rs::painting_another_surface_does_not_run_out_a_hold, which failed before; the demo test then passed 15 runs of 15). A hold is moved on by at most `MAX_HOLD_PAUSE` (1 s) in all (review of the integration): a hold whose configure never matches (a compositor clamping the size) ran only in the gaps between paints, so while another surface animated with paints longer than its frame interval it never ran out and the panel showed nothing until the animation stopped; one second covers the 500 ms of painting traced above twice over, and a configure that never comes costs a bounded wait (crates/strand-render/src/renderer/tests.rs::back_to_back_paints_move_a_hold_on_at_most_max_hold_pause, which failed before at 4 s for 40 paints of 100 ms).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a frame waits for new text once.** The estimate wait (bug 14's fix) let each layout pass of a frame wait `ESTIMATE_WAIT` for text the worker had not shaped, and a frame takes up to six passes; text arriving a few items at a time, as the owner's dashboard mounted, made each pass that received some wait again for the rest, and one frame waited up to 31 ms (owner-testing.md bug 17). The wait now has one deadline a frame, `ESTIMATE_WAIT` from the frame's first pass, shared by its passes: what has not arrived by then is laid out by its estimate and drawn by its shaped size from the frame it arrives, as before the wait. A first frame is not drawn by an estimate either way: it is held for all of its text (`frame_deadline`). Of the alternatives, a shorter wait would cost text that arrives within it, and not waiting at all for text a later pass mounts (a card's content uncovered as it grows) changed no frame of the owner's card. (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::a_frame_waits_for_its_new_text_once, which failed before, laying the bar out waiting 31 ms on a worker shaping a text every 3 ms). The deadline is the frame's, not one flatten's (review of the integration): it starts at the frame's first wait, not before its first pass, so a heavy pass (a debug build, a big mount frame) does not use it up and leave the text to its estimate, and it is kept on the surface until the frame is painted, so `paint`, which flattens again a surface that moves, waits only for what is left of what `update` waited (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::a_moving_frame_waits_for_its_new_text_once, which failed before at 12 ms). Each surface's frame has its own: one `update` flattening two surfaces whose texts mount together waits for each once, since a surface's texts are asked for only when it is flattened and a shared deadline would leave the second surface's to their estimates.

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a paint offset in flight is drawn whole logical pixels from its rest.** Layout snaps boxes to whole logical pixels; paint offsets (`x`, `y`, a FLIP glide) were drawn as they were, so a box whose `x` springs with its width (the owner's card stays centred as it grows) moved its content by fractions of a pixel every frame, and a spring's tail a hundredth of a pixel short of its rest drew the content a pixel off, then back, after the card looked settled (owner-testing.md bug 17: two frames of 300,000 and 210,000 pixels for nothing). An offset in flight is now drawn whole logical pixels from where it rests, as layout places boxes (`written + round(sprung − written)`), and a glide whole pixels: content moves as one with its box's edge, and a tail between pixels draws its rest. At scale 1.5 a logical pixel is 1.5 device pixels, so a slow offset steps by whole logical pixels; layout lengths already do, and a sub-pixel motion is smooth only for a box with nothing in it. A lifted node's held offset (a drag) follows the pointer as it is (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::a_swelling_card_repaints_its_edges_and_settles_still, which failed before with two frames of 253,400 pixels after the card showed its rest).

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: a box that only moves or resizes damages its edges.** A node's record kept one signature of everything it draws, its geometry included, and a clipping box hashed its clip into every child's; so a card swelling under its content (owner-testing.md bug 17) changed every record under it each frame, and each frame repainted the card whole (about 900,000 device pixels at the owner's size). A record now keeps its geometry apart when it is a plain box (solid fills, borders and rims; no transform, effect, outline, squircle, mask, inner shadow or fillet) and for the clips it is drawn through (`NodeRecord::geom`: rounded boxes, the rest hashed apart), and when only those changed its damage is what their outlines swept: the band between the two boxes along each edge and each corner's square (`RoundBox::changed`), within the node's bounds before and after. Anything else (a transformed or effected clip, a gradient, goo, a shader pass) keeps the whole-record damage; a node with a mask (`mask:` or a transition's) hashes its frame into its children's records, since the mask is drawn across it (review of the integration: a hard inner shadow's ring lies inside the box past the edge band, and a resized masked clip moved its fade over children that were repainted only along its edges; crates/strand-render/tests/damage.rs::a_hard_inner_shadow_repaints_with_its_box and ::a_masked_clip_repaints_its_mask_when_it_resizes, which failed before). Damage stays exact: a partial repaint equals a full one (crates/strand-render/tests/damage.rs::a_swelling_clip_repaints_only_its_edges at scales 1 and 1.5 with and without a background, which failed before, and random_edits now moving, resizing and rounding a clipping box; crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::a_swelling_card_repaints_its_edges_and_settles_still, which failed before with 15.8 million pixels over 37 frames). The owner's card's frame time is a CI timing gate (crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::the_island_card_swells_within_the_frame_budget: median under 8.3 ms and every frame under 16.7 ms of the render thread's whole paint, `GATE_MISS`): a swell frame takes a median of 2.1 to 2.7 ms and at worst 3.4 to 5.5 ms, repainting 141,000 to 176,000 pixels (2.7 to 3.1 ms, 4.5 to 5.9 ms and 454,000 pixels with the three changes of bug 17 undone), on the laptop in an optimised build.

**2026-10-14 · m6-owner-fixes: widgets read the pointer where they are drawn (owner-testing.md bug 16).** The owner's island card (`target/try/island/strand/notch.strand`, `MorphBody`) springs by a paint offset, `x: slack + ear`, and its sliders registered away from the pointer. Hit testing has always used the drawn shape (`flatten` records each node's hit box with the paint offsets of it and its ancestors, and the inverse of any `scale`/`rotate`), but `Router::drag_slider` and `Router::choose` computed the value from `node_rect`, the laid-out box before paint offsets: 50 px off in the island, and off by the squeeze under a `when pressed { scale }` ancestor. spec.md 6.7 says input follows the node's shape; a value read anywhere else is a bug, not a design question.
