The local `scripts/container/ci.sh` runs the same five steps as steps 35 to 39 (`CI_JOB=eval`), after the timing job, so every earlier step keeps its number. `affected` runs scripts/eval/ci.sh, every step (the review's change: the inner loop's root fmt and clippy do not reach eval/, its own workspace, so 3 4 5 alone let its fmt and clippy go unchecked until CI), when eval/ or scripts/eval/ changed, and also for the root Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock, which the plan left out: the sandbox's lock is held to the root's and its profiles to the root's (check-lock.sh, drift.rs), so a root manifest change can break it without touching eval/. A product change does not pull the sandbox in (it builds strand-render outside the root workspace, a slow rebuild for every strand-render edit); a change to any of strand-render's code builds it with `eval-hooks` (`cargo check -p strand-render --features eval-hooks`: nothing else in the root workspace compiles the hooks, so a product edit could break the sandbox's build unseen; the review's change) and prints the command that runs the curated and regression scenarios on it. test-affected.sh holds all of this. Not measured: Swatinem/rust-cache keys its cache on the root workspace's lock alone, so a change to eval/Cargo.lock does not change the key, and the job may restore a cache built from an older lock; cargo rebuilds what changed either way. Measure the job's cache hits on its first GitHub runs.

**2026-10-17 · eval-sandbox review: the driver's wakes follow the shell's loop, and the renderer's own timers read the virtual clock.** The review found the driver unlike the shell in five ways: it applied logic's diff and ran `Renderer::update` every tick, empty or not (the logic thread sends only non-empty diffs, run/logic.rs, and the host updates only when woken); it painted a surface up to eight times in one tick to hand layout facts to logic, kept only the last frame and summed their costs; it never ran `Router::settle` or `set_input_wake` after a diff; it set reduced motion on the renderer alone, where the shell sets `system.reduced_motion`, which logic reads and hands render in its diff; and the tooltip delay and the capped clocks read the wall clock, so on a virtual clock that runs ahead of it a tooltip showed at once, and `at_rest` ignored `Renderer::next_wake`. The tick is now the shell's (eval/src/harness.rs, its module doc): input as `Host::input` (an idle surface left wanting a frame wakes the loop), logic stepped and only a non-empty diff applied (`apply`: `Router::observe`, `Renderer::apply`, `Router::settle`, `set_input_wake`, surface sync), a wake between frames when a waker text is delivered or `next_wake` is due (`text_ready`: `Router::tick`, `Renderer::update`), a frame held for its facts answered first (`frame_deadline` set: an idle surface's container query, `QUERY_WAIT` kept at 30 s since logic always answers in time), one paint per surface (a second is an error naming the tick), a wake when the paint leaves surface changes (`Host::painted`), and what the frame laid out answered after it, landing before the next frame. `reduce-motion` and the twin set `system.reduced_motion`; the diff carries it to render. **Beyond plan section 2's footprint:** `Renderer::set_now(Option<Instant>)` (cfg'd, in renderer/probe.rs) and a private, non-cfg `Renderer::now()` that returns the pinned instant only under `eval-hooks` and is `Instant::now()` otherwise, read by the four call sites that time a tooltip (`tooltip.rs`, its due time and its check) and the capped clocks (`clocks.woke` in `update`, `clocks.frame` in `paint`): the same reasoning as `Router::set_now`'s, a timer the sandbox must run on its clock, and the product build is unchanged (the function inlines to the wall clock). The exit stall, GPU promotion and the busy window stay on the wall clock: their waits are set so they never fire in a run. And `take_inline_shaped()` (cfg'd), the layouts inline shaping delivered at once: in the shell a text worker wakes the loop for each layout it delivers (`text_ready`), and inline shaping has no worker, so the driver wakes for each such layout after an apply or a paint, bounded (16 in a row is an error). Without that wake two curated scenarios lost the frame that places their popup (a popup's `anchor_rect` comes from its parent's boxes in `refresh_specs`, which `configure_surface`'s update runs before the bar's first flatten); with it, a bar that shapes text opens its popup on the bar's first layout, as in the shell. title-pill-cut and island-card-swell had text-less bars, so each bar gains a clock's text (the scenarios say why); a bar with no text and an anchored popup open at boot waits for an unrelated wake in the shell too, which the owner may want to confirm (crates/strand/src/demo/host.rs has no other wake there). Tests: eval/tests/smoke.rs (a tooltip shows 15 to 16 ticks after the pointer at a 250 ms delay, not after 200 ms, and a rest waits for it; a container query answered before the first frame and after the frame that lays the row out wide; `system.reduced_motion` reaching render through logic, from `set` and from `reduce-motion`; a surface paints once a tick), eval/tests/hooks.rs (`take_inline_shaped` counts shaped layouts, not held or released ones), and the curated `container-query` scenario. What the change did: the 60 and 144 Hz matrix is unchanged (552 cells, 40 known, none failing or stale), and the jelly cell still shows no JELLY, now through the input wake (each pointer motion of the drag wakes the loop for the surface its last frame left idle, `update` previews, the drag frame reuses the preview): the product's finding stands with its cause corrected. The GPU leg now paints one frame more than before at the end of a rest, as the shell does (no update decides the surface is clean first); its frame presents at buffer age 0 and stamps the surface's painted time, the CPU's empty frame does not, so the exit fade that starts next takes a first step a frame shorter on the GPU (opacity 5e-6 apart, crossfade k31): the 144 Hz known entries' finding, now seen at 60 Hz. eval/tests/gpu.rs compares the legs' rows with opacity to 1e-4 and says why; `cpu-gpu` was and is within its own tolerances.

**2026-10-17 · eval-sandbox review: what makes a node a mover, what it inherits as authored, and what is in flight.** Three check findings. (1) `way()` made a node a mover whenever any frame laid it out elsewhere, so a wrong layout drawn for a frame made itself the node's way: bystander skipped it and envelope's bounds grew to it. Now a frame laid out off the segment's span (its start and rest layouts) counts only as part of an excursion with a reason: something on its surface at one of its frames lays out anew by itself (`checks::LAYOUT_CAUSES`: an exit or an inert ghost, a size spring, keyframes, a time-driven prop, a drag; or a text drawn by its estimate or a stand-in), or logic's diff or input reached the renderer at the frame it came back on (`Frame::driven`, recorded by the driver: a second step, a container query's answer, the pointer leaving). Without one the excursion neither makes the node a mover nor widens its way, and bystander says the node was laid out elsewhere and back with nothing to move it. (2) An ancestor's authored width or height authored its children's x, y, w and h, so a child drawn off its layout inside a springing card was exempt: a size that springs is laid out each frame and the children's laid boxes follow it, so `harness::inherited` passes on only offset (x, y), opacity, and scale or rotation (all geometry, since a transform moves the drawn box off an unchanged layout); keyframes on a width, tried, do not lay out at all (the card stays 80 wide), so they hold nothing either way. (3) `teleport` counted the ancestors' whole inherited offset as glide left to go, a written `x: 100` included; the row now records `fx`, `fy`, the part in flight, which the driver sums from the ancestors' spring and glide parts (a drag's lift included, which the renderer's own seam-snap `flight` leaves out, so strand-render gains nothing for it), and teleport reads that. A trace from before the two columns still reads, with nothing in flight (A/B against an earlier revision). Tests: eval/tests/checks.rs (an excursion with no reason fails envelope, the same with the ghost or with a driven return passes; a one-frame wrong layout fails bystander and passes with a sibling text drawn by its estimate; a static ancestor offset no longer excuses a 70 px jump), eval/tests/smoke.rs (`inherited` per axis, a dot under a springing card held to its layout with every check passing, the in-flight columns end to end and from an old row).

**2026-10-17 · eval-sandbox hardening: what the trace lacked, and the two fields `eval-hooks` gained for it.** A first set of seeded animation defects, run through the gate and the matrix, showed four kinds of gap: defects the checks could not see because the trace did not carry the evidence, defects caught only by a neighbouring check by luck, correct motion flagged, and effects no scenario exercised. Text was the one the trace could not answer at all: a stand-in layout drawn unclipped past its box, or the narrowest one shaped drawn in a box that holds more, leaves every box where it belongs, and only the glyphs differ. So strand-render's `eval-hooks` (only there, behind the feature) now traces per text `fit`, the line box it asked to be shaped for when its unbounded layout is wider than its box, and `ink`, the glyph bounds of the layout drawn, where drawn and clipped where the frame clips them, in logical px before transforms (probe.rs `NodeTrace`, flatten/node.rs after the text's clip). Nothing else in crates/ changed. The rest came from the driver, whose API already had it: each frame records where each shown surface lies on the output (`origins`, the positioner's arithmetic of strand-surface placement.rs `popup_config`/`popup_request`, now redone on every configure and handed to `Renderer::set_surface_origin`), and, with a new `compositor_poses` header, the pose each painted surface commits (`Renderer::delegated_pose`). That pose is read right after the surface's paint, as the surface manager reads `Painter::surface_pose` with its commit; reading it after the loop handled the paint's surface changes read a removed surface's rest pose for a closing popup's last frame, the sandbox's artefact and not the product's. The trace's row grows to 38 columns; the 34- and 36-column rows of older traces still read.

**2026-10-17 · eval-sandbox hardening: the checks read what the eye sees, and two new checks, `coherence` and `ink`.** *On screen.* A content-sized popup the compositor re-centres as it grows moves left by half its growth, and render draws its content where it was on screen and glides it (renderer/surfaces.rs `glide_origin`): on its surface the content moves, on screen it stays. Read on the surface, that was a bystander moving and a glide retargeted on w, a false positive at scale 1.5. `RunTrace::on_screen` moves every row and input region with its surface since it was first placed, and folds a committed surface pose in (opacity into every row's, scale and offset into every visual box and the root's scale, the axes it moves authored), and every check reads that. *`coherence`* holds four rules within one frame: `inherit` (a node's drawn offset beyond its own parts is its parent's: a paint offset carries its subtree, design.md's FLIP), `pivot` (scale, rotate and a morph's scale turn a node about its box's centre, through its ancestors' transforms and the delegated pose, flatten/node.rs's transform group), `morph start` (a shared morph's first frame is one share, at most 0.5 as `vanish`'s pop-in allows, of the way from the box its name was last drawn at to its own, on all four edges, anim/morph.rs) and `stacking` (a node in flight never goes below an overlapping sibling while their layout keeps its order). Each was a seeded defect only a neighbour caught, by a margin. Their exemptions are general: `inherit` leaves out a node moved by its own keyframes, time-driven props, lean or jelly, whose offsets the trace's parts do not carry (the first matrix run flagged every keyframed node); `stacking` flags only the node that goes below while in flight, so a drag lifting a node above its neighbours and a FLIP swap of laid places are not pops (the first run flagged both). *`ink`* holds `spill` (ink within its box ± 2 px of overhang) and `over-cut` (an ellipsised text never draws less of itself from one frame to the next as its line box widens). Over-cut was first "fills its box to within a glyph", which failed title-pill-cut: an ellipsis cuts at a word boundary, so a correct cut can fall a word short. Its monotone form counts the frame before only where that frame's ink stopped short of its box's edge: ink reaching the edge may be a wider layout clipped there, which a wider box cannot draw again (title-pill-cut-late's out-and-back failed without that).

**2026-10-17 · eval-sandbox hardening: false positives fixed in `teleport`, `vanish` and `twin`.** `teleport`'s travel was `|e − s|`, nothing for a spring sent out and back within one segment, so its every step was a jump; it is now the span of the node's way (`way()`: start, rest and every layout a frame counted), cached per node and axis. Its retarget arm (a glide whose drawn box jumped with its layout) applies on x and y only: a glide moves a box and never sizes it, and a size layout snaps under a glide is layout's (design.md "What can't interpolate"). `vanish`'s blank fired on a closing popup's last frame, which draws nothing because nothing in it shows; a frame is blank now only when something inside its surface's root shows (the root is the surface, whose own paint the trace cannot tell). Blanks are keyed per surface and segment, where `first_per_node` had merged every blank of a run into one. Pop-in holds each time an element comes onto a surface, so a popup opened again must play its pose again, and a new `pose back` rule holds bug 7 for delegated poses: from the frame a surface's root plays its exit to its last, the pose it commits never comes back toward rest (gives of 0.01 opacity and 0.005 scale, quantisation). `twin` left time-driven nodes out with keyframes; but a run rests only once nothing shown follows a running clock, so at a settled rest both runs' clocks stand at t = 0 (time.rs `TimeContext::frozen`), and a time signal that did not stop under reduced motion is a difference it now reports. Each change has a synthetic trace it passes and one it fails in eval/tests/checks.rs; the tests of the changed rules (teleport's travel and retarget, twin's time, the pose taken out of `pivot`'s root) fail with the old rule put back.

**2026-10-17 · eval-sandbox hardening: coverage, and what it proved.** The matrix's `flip-reorder` boxes each hold a child (a glider with children, for `inherit`) and `reduced-motion` turns its subject on `rotate: t * 90deg` (a time signal under reduced motion, for `twin`). New curated scenarios, written from design.md: title-pill-cut-late and title-pill-cut-waker (a late title's stand-ins as its pill grows, out and back, at scale 1 and 1.5), cond-transition (`~ (open ? 160ms : 1s)`, a transition chosen by a condition), time-signals-reduced (waves and `t` stopping under reduced motion, a time-driven node mounted then), closing-pose-delegated (bug 7 with `compositor_poses`) and popup-grow-centred (a content-sized popup re-centred as it grows, at scale 1.5). The gate is 20 scenarios, all passing; the matrix at 60 and 144 Hz is 552 cells, 504 pass, 40 known, 8 n/a, 0 fail and 0 stale, with known.toml unchanged. Temporary mutations of strand-render, reverted, showed each new rule catching its defect in the scenarios: a child not carried by its parent's glide (`inherit`, 264 matrix findings and five gate scenarios), scale about a box's corner (`pivot`, 294), a morph started from the old box's corner (`morph start`, 44), a stand-in drawn unclipped (`spill`), time unfrozen under reduced motion (`twin` and `expect`), and the delegated pose read from the frame cache (`pose back`). `over-cut` and `stacking` are proven on synthetic traces only: no scenario caught the narrowest stand-in mutation while the unclipped one ran with it. A popup opened again after its exit ended showed at rest at once in a probe, without its enter pose (anim/mod.rs `enter` says it springs back from its exit pose); no committed scenario holds it, since it is not yet known whether it is the product's or the driver's re-attach order, and it is left to triage rather than accepted.

## exit-height0

**2026-10-17 · exit-height0: a node that exits to a size stays laid out and clipped at it until it unmounts, an exit ends with its frame, and text under a node clipped to nothing is asked for (the eval sandbox's matrix).** A node leaving with `exit { height: 0 }` sprang its height to 0 and then, on the frame its exit ended, was drawn whole for one frame (`row#subject` at 12 × 15, k34 of `m.exit-height0.60`), and at 144 Hz it was laid out again at 29 px wide at height 0 a few ticks before, its row's later siblings snapping 17 px right. Three causes, each a rule that held for some passes or nodes and not others. (1) An exit ended inside a flatten pass (`Animator::paint` removed it from `exits` as its pose settled), but a frame flattens again after a pass that asked for text (`flatten_surface`'s loop, a pruned stand-in), and the next pass laid the node out without its exit pose's size (`rest_sizes` reads `exits`) and drew it at its own props: the flash. An exit now ends with the frame: the pass that ends it records it as finished, it stays exiting, and `take_finished` (after the frame is painted, `process_finished`) removes it as it unmounts, so every pass of that frame lays it out and draws it at its pose (`finish_now` and `finish_undrawn` go the same way; a finished exit is recorded once). (2) A node clipped its content only while its size sprang (`Animator::sizing`): once the spring settled at 0, the frames before the exit ended drew its content overflowing its zero-height box. A node exiting to a pose that sets its size (laid out at that size by `rest_sizes` until it unmounts) now clips as it does while the size springs. (3) A node that clips its content to nothing does not visit its subtree, so its texts left the frame's text list, their layouts were pruned and layout placed them by their estimates (`iiii` at 29 px, against 12 shaped): the 144 Hz width snap. Such a node now asks for its subtree's texts as a node drawn hidden does (`hidden_texts`, hidden-text), as a text visited outside the clip already does. Fade, slide, `reveal` and `clip:` hid the flash at 60 Hz because the node's own pose or clip drew nothing on that frame. In the matrix the 21 exit-height0 entries (18 cells at both rates, three at 144 Hz) are gone and the matrix passes at 60 and 144 Hz with them removed; `exit-height0+gpu@144` now fails `cpu-gpu` by the first-frame lead already listed for `flip-reorder+gpu@144` (the CPU leg paints nothing while the subject sits collapsed, where the flash used to paint, so the gap's glide leads 2.4 ticks there and one on the GPU) and was listed under that finding; first-frame-lead below fixes that lead, and with both on the branch the cell passes and its entry is gone. Test: `crates/strand-render/tests/morph.rs::a_collapsing_exit_hides_what_it_collapsed_until_it_unmounts` (fails on d0673e18: the box after the row 17 px right on frame 4, and the text drawn again on frame 9 after it collapsed on frame 3; each of the three changes alone leaves it failing).

## first-frame-lead

**2026-10-17 · first-frame-lead: a change starts one refresh of its surface before the first frame that shows it, on either backend.** The eval sandbox's 144 Hz matrix found a motion's first frame moving too far, and differently on the CPU and GPU legs (known.toml's text-estimate-far+stagger@144, flip-reorder+gpu@144 and lean+gpu@144). *Cause.* `Motion::sample` started a pending change `min(at - last, START_LEAD)` before the frame at `at`, `last` being the motion's previous sample or, for a motion made in this frame, the surface's `painted_time` (`Animator::begin`'s `prev`). START_LEAD is one 60 Hz refresh, so after idle frames on a 144 Hz surface the first frame of a glide showed 16.7 ms of progress, 2.4 frames in one (the exiting tags of text-estimate-far+stagger jumped 27 px where the next frames moved 18). And `painted_time` moves only on a paint that draws something: a CPU surface's idle frames at buffer age 1 have no damage and leave it where it was, while a GPU-presented surface paints at age 0 (`Renderer::paint_gpu`), so each of its idle frames moved it, and the same glide led by one frame there and 2.4 on the CPU (flip-reorder+gpu@144 k25: 10.36 px left on the CPU, 13.17 on the GPU). *Rule.* The lead is one refresh of the surface drawing the frame: the change was made since the frame before, so the first frame that shows it moves it as far as each frame after does, which is what START_LEAD's comment already said it was ("one frame lead … one refresh at 60 Hz"). The period is the one each surface already estimates from the gaps between its paints (`Clocks::period`, the shortest gap, at most 1/60 s, decisions.md m4-runtime-w1), and every paint feeds it whatever it draws, so both backends see the same period. `Motion::sample_frame(at, period)` starts a change `min(at - last, period, START_LEAD)` before `at`; `Animator::set_period` (which replaces `set_slack`: the slack is half the same period) sets it before every paint and preview, and every sample a painted frame makes passes it: props and enter and exit poses, glides, sizes, morphs, rolls, reveals and image swaps, lean, jelly, shared morphs, scroll springs and flings, the theme swap's roots and its crossfade's first step. `sample(at)` keeps START_LEAD for callers outside a frame. `painted_time` keeps its meaning (when the surface last painted something): the lead no longer depends on it once it is at most `at - period`, which it always is, so the GPU path is left as it is. START_LEAD stays the ceiling, and stands in for a period not yet known. At 60 Hz nothing visible changes (the lead was the period already, to a third of a microsecond). *Test.* `crates/strand-render/tests/motion.rs::a_glide_after_idle_frames_leads_by_one_refresh_at_any_buffer_age` paints twelve idle frames at 144 Hz at buffer age 1 and at age 0, then a keyed reorder: both draw the same first frames, each within half a pixel of the glide started one 144 Hz frame before (before the fix the CPU's first frame was 12 px along where one frame is 3); `strand-scene`'s `a_change_on_a_faster_surface_leads_by_its_refresh` holds the bounds. One reference image is blessed again for it: media.rs's `graph_history` paints at T0 and 16 ms later, so its surface's period is 16 ms and its value spring now leads by that rather than 16.667 ms; 21 anti-aliased pixels along the line's edge change, by at most 19 levels. *Sandbox.* The three entries are gone from known.toml, and so is exit-height0+gpu@144's, which exit-height0 above listed under this lead. Measured on d0673e18 without exit-height0, exit-height0+reveal@144's flash entry went stale under this fix too: with the reveal's mask and the height spring each leading by one frame, the mask hides the exit's last frame at 144 Hz as it did at 60 (exit-height0 removes that entry as fixed). On d0673e18 alone `run.sh eval matrix --hz 60,144` was 552 cells, 508 pass, 36 known, 8 n/a; on the branch with exit-height0 it is 552 cells, 544 pass, 0 known, 8 n/a, no failures and nothing stale. cpu-gpu-crossfade's exit and enter fades are the same frame by frame on both legs.

## late-text-dip

**2026-10-17 · late-text-dip: a text not shaped yet takes no room, so a text later than the frame's waits moves its siblings once, to where they end (eval-sandbox finding, bug24-flip-open-late1).** A frame waits for text the worker has not shaped (`NEW_TEXT_WAIT` on an idle surface, then `ESTIMATE_WAIT`). A text later than that was laid out by its estimate (0.55 em a character, 1.2 em a line) until it arrived. In bug24-flip-open-late1, where Focus's glyph is shaped one frame late, the estimate wrapped seventeen letters into ten lines in the glyph's 14 px. The row's layout dropped the bars 9 px for that frame, and they were drawn up to 3 px off their level and back. Any text whose estimate is far from its shaped size (a ligature's name, narrow or wide letters) does the same wherever the worker falls behind, for example on a font family's first load. *Rule.* A text with no layout at any scale takes no room of its own until it arrives. It measures its authored width (or `min_width`) and no height. When it has neither, the gap beside it folds as a slot collapsing to zero does (`layout::style`, `unshaped_nothing`). "Neither" means no positive `width`/`height` on that axis, no minimum, pad or grow, and not `place: absolute`. So the frame before the text arrives lays its siblings out as if it were not mounted yet. The frame it arrives in moves them once, gliding from where they were drawn (flip-open). A list's rows keep the estimate: no frame waits for their text (`await_unmeasured`), and a list sizes and scrolls by its rows' heights, so rows of no height would make the scroll jump as each one is shaped. The pass that sizes a content-sized surface (a popup, a toast stack: `refresh_specs`, `TextSizes::estimates`) keeps it too. That size is asked of the compositor, and changing it after the surface shows is a round trip that remakes a popup where `xdg_wm_base` cannot reposition one, dropping its keyboard grab. The surface's first frame waits for its text (`FIRST_FRAME_TEXT_WAIT`), so only the request is guessed. With no room there, `crates/strand/tests/acceptance.rs::the_bar_and_its_calendar_on_two_outputs` failed: the calendar popup was first sized without its labels, then made again at its shaped size, and Escape no longer closed it. Three more changes follow from "takes no room". (1) A box that clips its content and holds only such text is laid out empty, so its text was clipped away and never asked for or shaped: a deadlock. The matrix's enter-fade+clip (twin) and exit-fade+clip (vanish) cells failed on it. A node whose content is clipped to nothing now asks for its texts as a hidden node does (`Flattener::hidden_texts`, hidden-text); exit-height0 above makes the same call for a box collapsed to height 0, and the integrated branch keeps one call for both. (2) A new node that drew nothing, because its text is still being shaped or its box was laid out empty, stays in `unpainted` across a paint (`renderer::text::still_shaping`). So the pass its text arrives in does not glide it in from the empty place it was laid. (3) An `enter` pose with such text under it is held at its pose for up to `FIRST_FRAME_TEXT_WAIT` (`Animator::hold_enter`, as a stagger holds). A fade-in then starts when what it shows is shaped, not with half its content. Without the hold, the matrix's enter-fade and enter-slide cells with late text showed a pop-in. *Why this revises flip-open's alternatives.* flip-open rejected laying unshaped text out at no size because it "would move its siblings twice (its gap first)". That weighed a text that arrives within the wait, where neither reading draws a frame without it. For a late text, a frame without it is drawn either way. With the estimate, the siblings move to a guess and then again (away and back, or past and back). With no room, they stay put and then move once, toward where they end, and folding the gap removes the "gap first" move. Moving one way beats moving away and back, and outside lists the layout no longer needs an estimate. *Limit.* A wrapper box around late text keeps its own pad and gap, so its siblings move in two steps (the wrapper's, then the text's). Both steps go toward the end, and the glides add. *Side effect.* Under a box clipped to height 0 (exit-height0's exit), the text was not visited and its layout was pruned. As the height spring ended, the box was relaid at the text's 29 px estimate. That was the 17 px width snap known.toml listed for exit-height0+stagger@144 and exit-height0+lean@144. (1) keeps that text shaped, so those cells' `teleport` now passed; it was stale and is removed from their entries. Their flash remains. (Measured on d0673e18; exit-height0 above fixes the flash and the snap too, so on the integrated branch those entries are gone.) *Mutants.* In bug24-flip-open.scn the glyph's 14 px is already its width, so the first pass no longer moves the bars. Its mutant therefore runs a new regression scenario, bug24-flip-open-min.scn: a text with `min_width: 8` that shapes far wider. The first pass lays it out at 8 px, the mutant's glide starts there, and the bars jump 70 of 80 px in one tick (`teleport` on `#bars` x). The regenerated patch also drops (2)'s `still_shaping`, together with the state it extends. Under bug25-hidden-text's mutant, the count's text is now laid out with its width and no height. The row shrinks 14 → 12 px for a frame instead of dropping the bars, so the scenario's row gains `id: status` and the mutant expects `bystander` on its height. The bug-25 patch now removes only the two calls, since the clip-to-nothing path in (1) still calls `hidden_texts`. *Tests.* These are in `crates/strand-render/src/renderer/tests.rs`, on a renderer whose worker answer is taken by hand, so the text is late on every machine. `a_late_text_moves_its_siblings_once`: the bars stay on their level and only move toward where they end; before the fix they leave their level. `a_late_text_takes_no_room_until_it_arrives`: the first frame draws the row as it was before the text mounted. `a_box_around_a_late_text_shows_it_whole`: the text is drawn only where it rests, and with `enter { opacity: 0 }` its fade starts on the frame it arrives in; it fails without (3). `text_in_a_box_clipped_to_nothing_is_shaped`: a clipping row around the text shows it. `a_popup_opened_before_its_text_is_shaped_is_sized_by_its_estimate`: a popup's first spec takes its text's estimate; with no room it is the pad alone. bug24-flip-open-late1 passes with its `expect_fail` removed (the bars stay on y 9 throughout, gliding 270 → 250). Matrix at 60 and 144 Hz (`run.sh eval matrix-all --hz 60,144`) on d0673e18 with this fix alone: 552 cells, 504 pass, 40 known, 8 n/a, 0 fail, 0 stale; the scenario gate (curated and regressions) passes all 15. On the integrated branch, with exit-height0 and first-frame-lead: 552 cells, 544 pass, 0 known, 8 n/a.
